Merge is detected (it goes through git), but the other three attention reasons are probed by joining paths under `<directory>/.git`, which is a **file**, not a directory, in a linked worktree. The session's worktree attachment therefore carries `attentionReason: null`, so the shared UI never marks the session as needing attention for a stopped rebase/cherry-pick/revert. The web runtime reports the same states correctly.

This is the #648 defect class in a different function: #648 fixed nothing here — it covers `checkInProgressOperations` / `getGitStatus` (`mergeInProgress` / `rebaseInProgress`); this issue covers `canonicalizeWorktreeState`'s `attentionReason`, a separate code path feeding the session-worktree contract.

## Evidence (verified on main `3304bfbe7`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:4292-4305` (`canonicalizeWorktreeState`, exported at `:4222`): merge is probed portably via `execGit(['rev-parse', '--verify', 'MERGE_HEAD'])` at `:4293`, but rebase is probed at `:4297-4298` with `path.join(directoryPath, '.git', 'rebase-merge' | 'rebase-apply')` and cherry-pick/revert at `:4302-4303` with `path.join(directoryPath, '.git', 'CHERRY_PICK_HEAD' | 'REVERT_HEAD')`. In a linked worktree `.git` is a file (`gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`), so every one of those `stat` calls fails and is swallowed by `.catch(() => false)`.
- The web service does it the portable way: `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:6670-6682` resolves `rebase-merge` / `rebase-apply` / `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` / `REVERT_HEAD` through `resolveGitInternalPath` (`:635`), which follows the worktree gitdir.
- Served by the VS Code bridge at `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:272`; consumers that go dark: `packages/ui/src/sync/session-worktree-contract.ts:80,144,184-185` (attachment `attentionReason` → "Needs attention" / attention reason list), `packages/ui/src/components/layout/Header.tsx:335` (header attention state), `packages/ui/src/components/chat/work-status/WorkStatusPrimaryGroup.tsx:228-235` (attention label), `packages/ui/src/components/views/GitView.tsx:1408`.
- Laptop probe (real function, `vscode` mocked per the existing gitService test pattern, temp repos) — `~/git/fleet/probe-vscode-canon-linked/probe.test.ts`:
  - Main worktree with a conflicted cherry-pick in progress (control): `attentionReason = "cherry-pick"` — detected.
  - Linked worktree (`git worktree add`) with the same conflicted cherry-pick: `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` verified present at the real gitdir (`<base>/.git/worktrees/<name>/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, also what `git rev-parse --git-path CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` returns), branch/status read correctly, but `attentionReason = null`.

OpenChamber's spaces workflow runs sessions in linked worktrees, and VS Code is a primary surface. body:
## Summary

`gitService.ts` passes bridge-supplied branch names, merge/rebase targets, and stash refs to git as bare positional arguments — no `--` separator and no option-like rejection. An argument that starts with `-` is parsed by git as a flag, not as the branch/ref the caller named. The remote-name version of this class was already found and fixed (#593, `gitService.remote-argument-hardening.test.js`, `--` separators in `deleteRemoteBranch`/`removeRemote` and remote validation for fetch/pull/push); the branch/ref call sites were missed.

## Verified this run (laptop probe, main `40372c016`)

Probe test importing the real `gitService.ts` with the VS Code Git API absent (so the raw-git fallbacks run — the same path taken whenever the Git extension API is unavailable or its call fails), mirroring the `gitService.remote-argument-hardening.test.js` harness. 4/4 passed, including the control:

- **Control:** `checkoutBranch(dir, 'feature')` checks out `feature` normally.
- **`checkoutBranch(dir, '-f')` returns `{success: true, branch: '-f'}` and silently discards uncommitted work** — the probe's dirty `README.md` edit was gone afterwards. `git checkout -f` force-checks out HEAD; the caller asked to switch to a branch named `-f` and instead lost local changes, reported as success.
- **`merge(dir, {branch: '--abort'})` aborts an in-progress merge** and returns `{success: true, conflict: false}` as if a merge had completed (probe: `MERGE_HEAD` present before, gone after).
- **`rebase(dir, {onto: '--abort'})` aborts an in-progress rebase** and returns `{success: true, conflict: false}`.

## Unguarded call sites (all in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts`)

- `:786` `checkoutBranch` raw fallback — `execGit(['checkout', branch])`
- `:803-808` `createBranch` raw fallback — `['branch', name, startPoint?]`, neither value guarded
- `:829` `deleteGitBranch` raw fallback — `['branch', flag, branch]`
- `:3927` `merge` — `['merge', options.branch]`
- `:3887` `rebase` — `['rebase', options.onto]`
- `:3312` `countGitStashFiles` — `['stash', 'show', '--name-only', ref]`
- `:3334/:3338` `applyGitStash` — `['stash', 'apply', '--index', ref]` / `['stash', 'apply', ref]`
- `:3345` `dropGitStash` — `['stash', 'drop', ref]` (`popGitStash` composes apply+drop)

All of these values arrive straight from bridge request payloads in `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts` (`:166` checkout, `:123` createBranch, `:131` deleteGitBranch, `:473` rebase, `:492` merge, `:431-436` stash apply/pop/drop) with no validation in between.

Contrast with the guarded sites in the same file: commit hashes are rejected up front by `isValidCommitHash` (`:320`, used at `:4022/:4033/:4061/:4094`), and remotes got `--` separators + option-like rejection under #593.

## Why it matters

- Silent data loss: `checkoutBranch(dir, '-f')` destroys uncommitted changes while reporting success — the exact failure shape the repo's correctness invariants forbid (a destructive operation masquerading as the requested one).
- Wrong-operation success: `--abort` through the merge/rebase entry points performs the opposite lifecycle action and reports it as a completed merge/rebase, corrupting the caller's picture of repo state.
- It is the unfinished half of an accepted hardening pass (#593): the pattern, the test harness, and the fix shape already exist in the repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Option-like values (leading `-`) for branch, startPoint, merge branch, rebase onto, and stash ref are rejected with a clear error (or passed after `--` where git supports it and the value is still resolved as a ref) at every call site listed above — in the gitService functions themselves, not only in the bridge, so non-bridge callers are covered too.
- [ ] `checkoutBranch` can no longer discard uncommitted changes via an option-like branch argument; the `-f` probe case fails loudly and the working tree is untouched.
- [ ] `merge`/`rebase` with an option-like target fail loudly and leave any in-progress merge/rebase state untouched.
- [ ] New regression tests in the style of `gitService.remote-argument-hardening.test.js` cover at least the checkout `-f`, merge `--abort`, and rebase `--abort` cases plus a stash-ref case; legitimate branch/stash operations (including names with slashes/dots) keep working.
- [ ] No behavior change for valid inputs; existing gitService suites still pass.

body:
## Problem

In the VS Code runtime, when the raw git fallback cannot read a status at all, `getGitStatus` returns a fabricated success: no branch, no files, and **`isClean: true`**. A directory that is not a git repository, a corrupt repository, or any other `git status` failure is indistinguishable from a pristine, empty repository — under a `success: true` bridge response. The web runtime throws for the same inputs.

## Evidence (verified on main `78b9639f8`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:578` `getGitStatusRaw` (the fallback used when `getRepository` returns null — VS Code Git API unavailable or the repo not opened) returns at `:586-596`: on **any** non-zero `git status` exit, `{ current: '', tracking: null, ahead: 0, behind: 0, files: [], isClean: true }`. The stderr is discarded, so no caller can tell failure from clean.
- The bridge turns that into success: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:93-98` `api:git/status` returns `{ success: true, data: status }` for whatever `getGitStatus` returns.
- The web service is explicit about the opposite contract: `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js` `readStatus` (`:3018`) throws `fatal: not a git repository…` for a non-repo (`:3022-3024`) and re-throws other failures after logging (end of `readStatus`); the repo's own `AGENTS.md` invariant states it directly: "Never let fetch failure masquerade as authoritative empty success."
- Consumers trust `isClean` as authoritative: e.g. `packages/ui/src/components/views/GitView.tsx:2823-2824` refresh logic keys off `!fresh.isClean && fresh.files.length > 0`, and worktree status projections (`packages/ui/src/lib/worktrees/worktreeStatus.ts:9-11`) derive `isDirty: !status.isClean` from the same shape.
- Laptop probe (real function, `vscode` mocked per the existing gitService test pattern) — `~/git/fleet/probe-vscode-status-inprogress/probe.test.ts`: `getGitStatus` on a plain non-repository temp directory returned, with **no throw**: `{"current":"","tracking":null,"ahead":0,"behind":0,"files":[],"isClean":true}`. (The same probe's repo cases return real branch/files, so the harness itself is sound.)

## Why it matters

A status read that fails — the directory was moved, the repo is corrupt, git errored — currently renders in VS Code as a clean repository with nothing to commit. That hides exactly the situations a user most needs surfaced, silently agrees with "nothing to lose" readings built on `isClean`, and breaks parity with the web runtime, which errors. This is the same silent-empty family as #644/#645, in the status path instead of the diff/commit paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getGitStatusRaw` throws on a non-zero `git status` exit (surfacing stderr), mirroring the web `readStatus` contract — including the plain `fatal: not a git repository…` error shape for a non-repository directory so existing message matching keeps working.
- [ ] `api:git/status` consequently answers `success: false` for a non-repository/corrupt directory instead of `success: true` with a clean status.
- [ ] A real repository's status (clean and dirty) is returned exactly as today, on both the raw fallback and the VS Code Git API path.
- [ ] Regression tests in the existing VS Code gitService bun-test style (mocked `vscode`, temp dirs) prove: non-repo directory rejects; clean repo returns `isClean: true` with its branch; dirty repo returns its files.
- [ ] No change to the web service (already throws) and no change to the `GitStatusResult` shape.

## Summary

The VS Code extension's `getCommitFiles` reports a bad commit as a commit with no files: in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` it returns `{ files: [] }` whenever `git show` exits non-zero — a stale, mistyped, or unresolvable hash (and an empty hash at the service layer) is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty commit. The web git service validates and resolves the hash and lets the failure propagate, and the sibling `getCommitFileDiff` in the same VS Code file already throws for a bad hash. Sibling of #644 (range functions, same silent-empty class, different function and surface).

## Evidence (verified on main `78b9639f8`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:3615-3620` (`getCommitFiles`): runs `git show --numstat --format= <hash>` and `if (numstatResult.exitCode !== 0) { return { files: [] }; }` — stderr discarded, no hash validation before the call.
- The bridge entry does not rescue this: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:587-594` (`api:git/commit-files`) only checks that `hash` is non-empty, then returns `success: true` with whatever the service produced — so a stale hash yields a successful empty file list in the commit view.
- The sibling in the same file does it correctly: `getCommitFileDiff` (`gitService.ts:3667+`) throws `Failed to read file content at commit <hash>` when its reads fail (probe below confirms it throws for a bad hash).
- The web service does it correctly: `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:6701-6703` `resolveCommitHash` rejects a malformed hash (`A commit hash is required`) and rev-parse-verifies it as a commit; web `getCommitFiles` at `:6718` calls it and lets `git.raw` failures throw.
- Other VS Code callers of hashes validate first where it matters — e.g. `resetToCommit` checks `isValidCommitHash` (`gitService.ts:4080+`) — `getCommitFiles` is the outlier.

### Laptop probe (real `getCommitFiles`/`getCommitFileDiff` from `gitService.ts` at `78b9639f8`, vscode module mocked per the existing gitService test pattern; temp repo with two commits; probes at `~/git/fleet/probe-vscode-range-silent/probe2.test.ts` + `probe3.test.ts` on the laptop)

```
GOOD hash files            -> NO THROW: {"files":[{"path":"file.txt","insertions":1,"deletions":1,"isBinary":false,"changeType":"M"}]}
BAD hash files (deadbeefdeadbeef)   -> NO THROW: {"files":[]}   (git exits 128 — indistinguishable from an empty commit)
NONSENSE hash files (no-such-commit) -> NO THROW: {"files":[]}
EMPTY hash files                     -> NO THROW: {"files":[]}
BAD hash file-diff         -> THREW: Failed to read file content at commit no-such-commit
GOOD hash file-diff        -> NO THROW: {"original":"line 1\nline 2\n","modified":"line 1 CHANGED\nline 2\n", …}
ROOT commit files          -> NO THROW: {"files":[{"path":"file.txt","insertions":2,…,"changeType":"A"}]}  (correct — checked so the fix must not break it)
```

## Why it matters

The commit view is a review surface: a hash that went stale (history rewritten, shallow/fetch state changed, a race between the log read and the file read) currently renders as "this commit changed nothing" with a success response, instead of an error the user can act on. The web side established the rule for this exact function — resolve the hash, fail loudly — and the VS Code port's own sibling function already follows it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getCommitFiles` in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` throws (with git's stderr or an equivalent message) when `git show` exits non-zero, instead of returning `{ files: [] }`; an empty/missing hash at the service layer is an error, matching web `resolveCommitHash` semantics.
- [ ] No behavior change for valid commits: a normal commit, a root commit, and a genuinely empty commit (`--allow-empty`) return exactly what they return today (the empty commit still returns `{ files: [] }` — via a successful git call, not the failure path).
- [ ] Regression tests in the existing VS Code gitService test style (bun test, mocked `vscode` module, temp repo) prove: bad hash and empty hash reject; good, root, and empty commits return their current values.
- [ ] The `api:git/commit-files` bridge caller surfaces the throw as a failed bridge response (its existing error path), not `success: true` with an empty list.

Found by the new-issue-creator sweep; dedup: title/keyword searches for `getCommitFiles vscode`, `commit files silently empty`, and `bad hash commit files` return no covering issue (#644 covers the range functions `getGitRangeDiff`/`getGitRangeFiles` only; this is the commit-files sibling in the same file).

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension's range-git functions report failure as "no changes": `getGitRangeDiff` and `getGitRangeFiles` in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` never check the git exit code and return an empty result for a missing or unresolvable ref — indistinguishable from a legitimately empty range. The web git service treats exactly these cases as errors. This is the exit-code half of the defect #640 noted in its evidence ("no exit-code check at gitService.ts:2599-2600") but did not cover in its acceptance criteria — #640 / PR #642 normalized `contextLines` only, and the silent-empty path for bad refs remains on current main.

## Evidence (verified on main `78b9639f8`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:2611-2612` (`getGitRangeDiff`): `const result = await execGit(args, directory); return { diff: result.stdout };` — no exit-code check, stderr discarded.
- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:2596-2598`: an empty `base`/`head` returns `{ diff: '' }` instead of an error.
- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:2641` (`getGitRangeFiles`): `if (result.exitCode !== 0) return [];` — and `:2625-2627` returns `[]` for an empty base/head.
- The sibling in the same file does it correctly: `getGitDiff` throws on a non-zero exit (`gitService.ts:2577-2579`).
- The web service does it correctly: `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:3585` throws `'base and head are required'`, `:3527-3532` `assertRangeRefsResolve` throws `Ref "<ref>" is not available locally. Fetch it before comparing.`, and a failing `git.raw` diff propagates. Same checks in web `getRangeFiles` at `:3721`/`:3724`. Web tests pin the throwing behavior (`service.test.js`, getRangeDiff describe: rejects for a checked-out-branch base and for refs not available locally).

### Laptop probe (real `getGitRangeDiff`/`getGitRangeFiles` from `gitService.ts` at `78b9639f8`, vscode module mocked per the existing gitService test pattern; temp repo, `feature` changes one line vs `main`; probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-vscode-range-silent/probe.test.ts` on the laptop)

```
GOOD main..feature diff        -> NO THROW: {"diff":"diff --git a/file.txt … -line 1\n+line 1 CHANGED …"}
EMPTY-RANGE main..main diff    -> NO THROW: {"diff":""}        (legitimately empty)
BAD-BASE no-such-branch..feature diff -> NO THROW: {"diff":""} (git exits 128 — indistinguishable from empty)
BAD-HEAD main..no-such-head diff      -> NO THROW: {"diff":""}
EMPTY-BASE ""..feature diff           -> NO THROW: {"diff":""}
GOOD main..feature files       -> NO THROW: ["file.txt"]
BAD-BASE no-such-branch..feature files -> NO THROW: []
EMPTY-BASE ""..feature files         -> NO THROW: []
```

## Why it matters

A comparison that silently reads as empty is a correctness hazard: when a base branch was deleted, renamed, or never fetched locally, the VS Code comparison / PR-description flow concludes "no changes" instead of surfacing the failed read. The one in-repo consumer today, `api:git/pr-description` (`packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-special-runtime.ts:400-413`), turns the empty file list into the misleading error "No diffs available for base...head" — the refs, not the diff, are the problem. The web side already established the house rule for this exact function pair: missing refs are an error, not an empty diff.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getGitRangeDiff` throws (with git's stderr or an equivalent message) when the underlying `git diff` exits non-zero, and throws for an empty `base` or `head` — matching web `getRangeDiff` semantics; a legitimately empty range (both refs resolve, no differences) still returns `{ diff: '' }`.
- [ ] `getGitRangeFiles` likewise throws on a non-zero exit and on an empty `base`/`head` instead of returning `[]`; a legitimately empty range still returns `[]`.
- [ ] The existing `origin/<base>` resolution preference in both functions is preserved.
- [ ] Regression tests in the existing VS Code gitService test style (bun test, mocked `vscode` module, temp repo) prove: bad base, bad head, and empty base/head reject for both functions; the good range and the empty range (`main...main`) still return their current values.
- [ ] The `api:git/pr-description` caller keeps working: its existing try/catch around these calls already tolerates a throw, and a bad-ref failure no longer surfaces as "No diffs available for base...head" when the file list read itself failed — or that caller's error message is adjusted accordingly.

Found by the new-issue-creator sweep; dedup: title/keyword searches for `range diff silently`, `getGitRangeDiff vscode`, `range refs resolve vscode`, `empty diff bad ref`, and `RangeFiles empty` return only #640 (contextLines scope, closed by PR #642, whose diff touches only the two `-U` sites) and older web-side context-parsing issues (#464/#465) — none covers the VS Code range functions' exit-code/ref handling.

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension's `getGitLog` judges `maxCount` with a bare `||` fallback — the #463 defect in the VS Code port. #463 fixed the web log endpoint ("maxCount judged by bare parseInt — -5 returns the entire history (unbounded)"), and the web service now guards it in the service layer (`packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:6365`: `Number.isInteger(options.maxCount) && options.maxCount > 0 ? options.maxCount : 50`). The VS Code service never got the guard.

This is a distinct defect from #640 (contextLines in the same file): different function, different bridge route (`api:git/log`), different failure — an unbounded history read instead of a broken diff.

## Evidence (verified on main `a9bfab99e`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:3419` (`getGitLog`): `const maxCount = options?.maxCount || 50;` — the value is interpolated verbatim as `--max-count=${maxCount}` at both call sites in the function (:3424 for `options.all`, :3498 for the ranged log). `||` rescues only falsy values (`0`, `NaN`, `undefined` → 50, which happen to match the web fallback); every truthy non-positive-integer passes through.
- The entry point is an unvalidated cast: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:575-587` (`api:git/log`) destructures `maxCount` from the bridge payload with a TypeScript `as` cast and passes it to `getGitLog` unchanged; the webview caller (`packages/vscode/webview/api/git.ts:668`) forwards the option unchecked.

### Laptop probe (real `getGitLog` from `gitService.ts`, vscode module mocked per the existing `gitService.*.test.js` pattern; temp repos)

```
GOOD(2) total: 2          GOOD(undefined) total: 5 (all)
BAD(-5)  on a 60-commit repo -> total: 60   (unbounded pass-through; the 50 fallback would return 50; GOOD(50) returns 50)
BAD(2.5)      -> THREW: fatal: '2.5': not an integer
BAD(Infinity) -> THREW: fatal: 'Infinity': not an integer
BAD('abc')    -> THREW: fatal: 'abc': not an integer   (reachable via the unvalidated bridge cast)
ZERO(0) / NaN -> total: 5 (the || fallback to 50 — same outcome as the web guard, not part of the defect)
```

## Why it matters

A negative `maxCount` turns a bounded history read into an unbounded one — on a large repository the extension host collects and parses the entire history (the exact harm #463 was filed for on the web side), and a fractional or non-numeric value fails the whole log view with a raw git fatal instead of falling back to the default page size. The house rule from #463/#578 is that this guard lives in the service, not only at the transport boundary; the VS Code port has it at neither layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getGitLog` in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` normalizes `maxCount` the same way as the web service (#463): a positive integer passes through unchanged; fractional, negative, `NaN`, `Infinity`, zero, and non-number values fall back to 50.
- [ ] Regression tests in the existing VS Code gitService test style (bun test, mocked `vscode` module, temp repo) prove: `maxCount: -5` on a repo with more than 50 commits returns exactly 50 entries, fractional/`Infinity` values return the default page instead of throwing, and a valid value (e.g. 2) still returns exactly 2.
- [ ] No behavior change for current callers passing a positive integer or omitting `maxCount`.

Found by the new-issue-creator sweep; dedup: title/keyword searches for `maxCount vscode`, `getGitLog maxCount`, and `git log vscode unbounded` return nothing; #463's scope is the web endpoint/service and does not touch `packages/vscode`. Sibling filed the same run: #640 (contextLines normalization in the same file's diff functions).

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension's git service hands `contextLines` to git unnormalized — the #578 defect in the VS Code port. The web service was fixed in #578 (`packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:39-40`: only a non-negative integer is a valid unified-context count; anything else takes the default of 3, because "a fractional value reaching git as -U2.9 (or NaN as -UNaN) is rejected with exit 129"). The VS Code service has no equivalent guard at either of its two `-U` sites, and its bridge layer does no runtime validation either.

## Evidence (verified on main `a9bfab99e`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:2561` (`getGitDiff`): `if (typeof contextLines === 'number') args.push(\`-U${contextLines}\`)` — `typeof` passes fractional, negative, `NaN`, and `Infinity` values straight through.
- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:2598` (`getGitRangeDiff`): `-U${Math.max(0, contextLines)}` — `Math.max` rescues negatives only; fractional/`NaN`/`Infinity` still reach git verbatim (`Math.max(0, NaN)` is `NaN`).
- The entry point is an unvalidated cast, not a schema: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:277-286` (`api:git/diff`) destructures `contextLines` from the bridge payload with a TypeScript `as` cast and passes it to `getGitDiff` unchanged. The webview caller (`packages/vscode/webview/api/git.ts:398`) forwards `options.contextLines` unchecked. Today's UI callers send the constants 3 or 1,000,000, so this is a latent service-boundary defect of exactly the class #578 fixed in the service (not only the routes) on the web side — any future or non-UI caller that computes a context count (halving, ratios, persisted settings) breaks the diff view instead of getting the default.

### Laptop probe (real `getGitDiff`/`getGitRangeDiff` from `gitService.ts`, vscode module mocked per the existing `gitService.*.test.js` pattern; temp repo, line 10 of 20 changed)

```
GOOD(3) first hunk: @@ -7,7 +7,7 @@ line 6
GOOD(0) first hunk: @@ -10 +10 @@ line 9
BAD(2.5)      getGitDiff -> THREW: error: --unified expects a numerical value
BAD(NaN)      getGitDiff -> THREW: error: --unified expects a numerical value
BAD(-5)       getGitDiff -> THREW: error: --unified expects a non-negative integer
BAD(Infinity) getGitDiff -> THREW: error: --unified expects a numerical value
RANGE GOOD(3) len: 193, hunk @@ -7,7 +7,7 @@
BAD(2.5) getGitRangeDiff -> diffLen=0   (silently empty diff — no exit-code check at gitService.ts:2599-2600)
BAD(NaN) getGitRangeDiff -> diffLen=0   (silently empty)
BAD(-5)  getGitRangeDiff -> diffLen=140 (Math.max(0, -5) = 0 rescues negatives here)
```

So the two functions fail differently: `getGitDiff` throws (the Diff view errors), and `getGitRangeDiff` silently returns an empty diff (the comparison view looks like "no changes" — the worse failure).

## Why it matters

A diff that silently reads as empty is a correctness hazard: a reviewer can conclude a file/range has no changes when the read actually failed. The web side already established the house rule (#578: normalize in the service, not only at the transport boundary); the VS Code port — which serves the same UI through the bridge — never got it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getGitDiff` and `getGitRangeDiff` in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` normalize `contextLines` the same way as the web service (#578): a non-negative integer passes through unchanged (including 0 and large values such as 1,000,000); fractional, negative, `NaN`, `Infinity`, and non-number values fall back to the default of 3.
- [ ] Regression tests in the existing VS Code gitService test style (bun test, mocked `vscode` module, temp repo) prove: each bad value above yields the same diff as the default-3 call for both functions, and valid 0 / 3 values still produce their exact hunks.
- [ ] No behavior change for the current UI callers (contextLines 3 and 1,000,000).

Found by the new-issue-creator sweep; dedup: title/keyword searches for `contextLines vscode`, `gitService context`, `VS Code git diff context`, and `578 vscode` return only #578 itself, whose scope is the web service (`packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js`) and which does not touch `packages/vscode`.

body:
## Summary

`GET /api/managed-servers` (design #612 phase 2, #525) lists a registry entry as a live OpenCode server whenever **any** process is alive at the recorded pid. It never verifies that the live process is still the OpenCode server that was recorded. When a recorded server dies and the OS recycles its pid onto an unrelated long-lived process, the read reports a phantom server — with the dead server's port and `startedAt` — for as long as that unrelated process lives. External consumers of the v1 contract (the audience #612/#525 built this read for) will treat the phantom as a real OpenCode server and try to use its port.

## Evidence (verified on main `a9bfab99e`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-servers.js:84-86` — the builder's only liveness gate is the injected probe: `.filter((server) => isPidAlive(server.pid))`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/lifecycle.js:395-402` — the `isPidAlive` the lifecycle defines is signal-0 only (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, EPERM counts as alive), and `lifecycle.js:1943-1949` passes it verbatim into `buildManagedServersResponse`.
- The header comment in `managed-servers.js:9-11` says liveness is "a signal-0 probe of a pid the registry already recorded, **the same check the orphan reaper uses**". That is not the reaper's check:
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-process-registry.js:119-128` — `commandIdentifiesOurServer` requires the live command to contain `opencode` and `serve` and, when the port is known, the recorded port.
  - `managed-process-registry.js:296-300` — the reaper reads the process's command first: "Can't verify identity (or it's not our server) → leave it alone."
  - `lifecycle.js` (the `isOwnedOpenCodePid` comment) — "A recorded pid can be reused by an unrelated process, so it is signalled only when its command still matches." Every other consumer of a recorded pid in this codebase verifies identity before acting on it; the new read is the only one that does not.
- The phantom is sticky, not a transient race: the reaper prunes a registry file only when the entry was reaped or the pid is dead (`managed-process-registry.js`, `drop = wasReaped || !isPidAlive(entry.pid)`). A recycled pid that stays alive keeps its registry file, so the phantom survives restarts of the reading instance too.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-managed-pid/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the current `managed-servers.js` from main `a9bfab99e` and using lifecycle's exact signal-0 `isPidAlive`: a registry entry whose pid belongs to a live `sleep 30` process (not an OpenCode server) and whose port is 4096 is returned as a server:

```json
{ "pid": 3466231, "port": 4096, "directory": null, "version": null,
  "status": "unknown", "startedAt": "2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z", "sessionCount": null }
```

i.e. the unrelated process is listed as a managed server ("PHANTOM LISTED" in the probe output). A dead pid is correctly filtered — the gap is identity, not liveness.

## Why it matters

- The read's whole purpose is stable discovery for external tooling (#525, design #612): a consumer that finds a "server" at a recorded port may connect to whatever now owns that port (or nothing), misattribute sessions, or keep a dead server in its model indefinitely.
- It contradicts the contract's own rule, stated in the same module, that unknown fields are explicit and nothing is fabricated: a recycled-pid entry fabricates a server.
- The codebase already solved this exact problem twice (reaper identity check, `isOwnedOpenCodePid`); the new surface regressed it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A registry (or draining) entry whose recorded pid is now held by a process that is not the recorded OpenCode server does not appear in `GET /api/managed-servers`. Identity is verified the way the existing code verifies it (live command matches `opencode` + `serve` and, when known, the recorded port — cf. `commandIdentifiesOurServer` / `isOwnedOpenCodePid`), or an equivalent recorded-identity check.
- Where identity cannot be verified (e.g. a platform without a command read), the entry is not presented as a live server on signal-0 alone; the chosen behaviour is explicit in code and tests.
- The hosting instance's own entry is unaffected: a ready/starting/draining own server whose pid matches its own recorded process still appears with its completed fields.
- The `managed-servers.js` header comment is corrected so it no longer claims the read uses the reaper's check (or is made true by the fix).
- Tests cover: recycled pid (live process, mismatched command) excluded; genuine recorded server included; dead pid still excluded. Existing `managed-servers.test.js` and lifecycle suites stay green.

body:
## Problem

`GET /api/model-routes/stats` judges its `hours` query parameter loosely — the exact defect class #604 fixed for the sibling pool-health route, on the route #604 did not touch.

`packages/web/server/lib/routing/model-route-stats.js:211` passes the raw query value straight through:

```js
res.json(await queryRouteStats(resolveDbPath(), { hours: req.query?.hours }));
```

and `queryRouteStats` converts it with a bare `Number(...)` at `model-route-stats.js:94`:

```js
const windowHours = Math.min(336, Math.max(0.1, Number(hours) || 24));
```

So malformed spellings are **reinterpreted** instead of falling back to the 24-hour default:

| `?hours=` | Resulting window | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `1e3` | 336h (1000 clamped) | 24h default |
| `0x10` | 16h | 24h default |
| `2.0` | 2h | 24h default |
| ` 2 ` (padded) | 2h | 24h default |
| `+2` | 2h | 24h default |
| `01` | 1h | 24h default |
| `-5` | 0.1h (floor) | 24h default |

## Evidence

Verified this run on main `3e888c38e` (file unchanged since `ddfbc4922`) with a laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-stats-hours/probe.mjs`) that seeds a minimal `route_attempt` table and calls the real `queryRouteStats`:

```
"1e3" -> windowHours 336, targets 1   (the 100-hour-old attempt is counted)
"0x10" -> windowHours 16
"2.0" -> windowHours 2
" 2 " -> windowHours 2
"+2" -> windowHours 2
"01" -> windowHours 1
"-5" -> windowHours 0.1
"24" -> windowHours 24
"1.5" -> windowHours 1.5   (canonical fraction — must stay valid)
undefined -> windowHours 24
```

Honest boundary: `2junk` already falls back to 24 today (`Number('2junk')` is `NaN`, and `NaN || 24` is 24) — the defect is the reinterpreted spellings above, not trailing junk.

`#604`'s fix added a canonical-decimal parser (`CANONICAL_DECIMAL_QUERY` / `parseCanonicalDecimalQuery`, `pool-health.js:217-225`) and applied it only to the pool-health route's `hours`/`activeMinutes`. The stats route shares the same `hours` parameter name, the same 0.1h–336h clamp range, and the same telemetry database, but was left on the loose conversion. The internal callers (`queryAttemptCountsPerTarget`, `queryActiveSessionsPerTarget` in the same file) receive already-parsed numbers from `computePoolHealth` and are not the problem — the fix belongs at the stats route boundary, mirroring #604.

There is also no route-level test for this endpoint: `model-route-stats.test.js` exercises `queryRouteStats` with a numeric `hours: 1` only; `registerModelRouteStatsRoutes` has no test at all.

## Why it matters

This endpoint is routing telemetry external consumers and the UI read to judge pool burn and failures. A mistyped or crafted `hours` silently changes the aggregation window (up to the 14-day clamp, or down to the 6-minute floor) instead of falling back to the documented 24h default — the same "judge the spelling as written" contract the server adopted across #463–#592 and #604. Consistency matters here precisely because the two sibling routes now disagree: `GET /api/model-routes/health?hours=1e3` falls back, `GET /api/model-routes/stats?hours=1e3` silently aggregates 14 days.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/model-routes/stats?hours=1e3`, `0x10`, `0b101`, `2.0`, ` 2 `, `+2`, `01`, and `-5` all fall back to the 24-hour default window (`windowHours: 24` in the response).
- [ ] Canonical values keep working exactly as before: `24` → 24, `1.5` → 1.5, `0.5` → 0.5, values above 336 still clamp to 336, values below 0.1 still floor to 0.1, and a missing `hours` still defaults to 24.
- [ ] The parsing follows the #604 canonical-decimal shape (reuse or mirror `parseCanonicalDecimalQuery` from `pool-health.js`); `computePoolHealth`'s internal numeric callers are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the stats route (or its parsing) for the reinterpreted spellings above plus the canonical cases, in the style of #604's `registerPoolHealthRoutes query parsing` suite.
- [ ] Targeted routing tests pass (run on the laptop or CI, not the sandbox).

title: fix(ci): live daily branch-cleanup protects open-PR heads but not open-PR bases — deleting a stacked PR's base would close it (also in code and opencode)

body:
## Finding

PR #581 (commit `933934e9`) added `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`. Its protected set is built only from open-PR **head** branches. A branch that is the **base** of an open PR is not protected: if that base branch is solely behind the default branch and inactive for 14 days, the workflow will delete it — and deleting a PR's base branch closes the PR. The workflow is live and daily in this repo.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:75` on current main (`763c773b`): `gh pr list --state open --limit 1000 --json headRefName --jq ".[].headRefName"` — `baseRefName` is never fetched, and `is_open_pr_head` (lines 78-88) is the only PR-based protection, alongside the default-branch skip.
- A candidate otherwise only needs: newest commit older than the inactivity window (default 14 days) and `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<branch> origin/<default>` (solely behind — zero unique commits). A stacked PR's base that has been merged/fast-forwarded into main satisfies both.
- Live, daily: repo variable `BRANCH_CLEANUP_LIVE=true` (verified via `gh variable list` this run, set 2026-10-27T18:31:22Z) and the schedule at line 5 is `cron: "27 14 * * *"` (daily).
- Latent today, verified this run: every currently open PR in this repo (626, 625, 619, 618, 617, 503, 401, 216) has `baseRefName=main`, and the default branch is already skipped — so no open PR is at risk until someone stacks a PR on a non-main base, which is a normal workflow in this fleet (queue branches are routinely stacked).
- Same pattern, same file and lines, verified on current main of the sibling repos via the GitHub contents API this run — one finding, one issue (do not file per-repo duplicates):
  - developing-today/code: `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:75` — heads only
  - developing-today/opencode: `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:75` — heads only
- Precedent: the identical finding in dezren39/nix was filed as dezren39/nix#985 and completed.

## Why it matters

The workflow's design promise is "deleting a candidate is provably lossless". That holds for the branch's commits, but not for the PR graph: deleting a stacked PR's base closes that PR and loses its review thread and CI state, in a fully automated daily run with no human in the loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- The protected set in `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` (developing-today/openchamber) includes open-PR base branches as well as heads (e.g. fetch both `headRefName` and `baseRefName`, and skip either), with the failure mode preserved: if the open-PR list cannot be read, the run fails before any deletion.
- The same protection is applied to `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` in developing-today/code and developing-today/opencode in the same set of changes, and each change references this issue.
- Dry-run output names base-protected branches distinctly (e.g. `SKIP open-pr-base: <branch>`), so the protection is observable in the step summary.
- No change to the other candidate rules (default-branch skip, inactivity window, solely-behind test, 50-deletion cap).

body:
## Finding

PR #581 (commit `933934e9`) added `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`, and its checkout step is the only mutable-tag action reference in this repo's workflows — in a workflow that runs with `contents: write` and can delete branches.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:33` on current main (`763c773b`): `uses: actions/checkout@v4`.
- Every other checkout in this repo is SHA-pinned to the same release: 34 references to `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1` across the other workflows (verified by grep on current main this run). `branch-cleanup.yml:33` is the sole exception.
- The workflow's permissions (`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:20-22`) are `contents: write` + `pull-requests: read`, and scheduled runs are LIVE: repo variable `BRANCH_CLEANUP_LIVE=true` (verified via `gh variable list`, set 2026-10-27T18:31:22Z) and the schedule is daily (`cron: "27 14 * * *"`, line 5). A re-pointed `v4` tag would execute in that privileged context.
- Same pattern, same file and line, verified on current main of the sibling repos via the GitHub contents API this run — one finding, one issue (do not file per-repo duplicates):
  - developing-today/code: `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:33` — `actions/checkout@v4`
  - developing-today/opencode: `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:33` — `actions/checkout@v4`
- Precedent: the identical finding in dezren39/nix was filed as dezren39/nix#984 and completed — the fix there was to pin to the repo-standard SHA, not to bump the mutable tag.

## Why it matters

This repo's convention is full-SHA pinning for actions, precisely so a moved or compromised tag cannot inject code into a privileged workflow. The one workflow that escaped the convention is also one of the few with write access to the repository contents and a live daily schedule.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` in developing-today/openchamber checks out with the full SHA pin used by the repo's other workflows (`actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1`), or a newer SHA verified the same way — not a mutable tag.
- The same pin is applied to `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml:33` in developing-today/code and developing-today/opencode in the same set of changes, and each change references this issue.
- No other behavior of the workflow changes (dry-run latch, candidate rules, cap).
- A grep for `actions/checkout@v` (bare tag) across `.github/workflows/` in each of the three repos returns no hits afterwards.

body:
## Finding

PR #553 (fix(notes): format the whole note on first render, head 16b49479, fixes #534) changed `NoteEditor`'s live-preview so a decoration pass finishes the Markdown parse before decorating and rebuilds when the background parser publishes a new tree. It shipped with **no test change**, and the regression it fixes — a note whose tail keeps raw Markdown markers because the background parser had only reached partway — is still not deterministically pinned on current main.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/553 (commit 16b49479) — files changed are only `packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/NoteEditor.tsx` (+23/-3) and its `DOCUMENTATION.md`; no test file.
- Current main (763c773b, verified via gh api contents): `NoteEditor.tsx:91` — `const tree = ensureSyntaxTree(state, state.doc.length, PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS) ?? syntaxTree(state);` with `PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS = 200` at :66, plus the ViewPlugin rebuild on `syntaxTree(update.state) !== syntaxTree(update.startState)`.
- `NoteEditor.test.tsx` on current main has exactly 2 tests, both mounting the same 45-character body (`'## Release\n- push the **tag**\n- check \`changelog\`'`). A body that small parses completely on first pass, so neither test can distinguish the fixed code from the old partial-tree behaviour — the original bug was caught by that test being *flaky* under load (#534), not by a deterministic partial-parse case.
- No open or recently closed issue covers this: search for `NoteEditor` / `ensureSyntaxTree` returns only the closed #534.

## Why it matters

The fix rests on two mechanisms — the 200 ms `ensureSyntaxTree` budget (with fallback to the partial tree on timeout) and the tree-change rebuild in the plugin's `update()`. If either regresses (e.g. the rebuild condition is dropped in a refactor, or the timeout fallback becomes the norm for near-cap 3000-character notes), the first-render bug returns and the existing tests stay green, because they never present a partial tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deterministic test mounts (or drives) a note whose initial syntax tree is partial — e.g. a near-3000-character note, or a stubbed/delayed parse — and asserts the tail's markers are hidden / bullets drawn on first render without any keystroke.
- The test fails when run against the pre-#553 `buildDecorations` (partial `syntaxTree(state)` only, no tree-change rebuild) and passes on current main.
- Existing `NoteEditor.test.tsx` tests keep passing.

title: fix(security): login rate-limit env vars are judged by bare Number(...) || default — a negative value locks out after one failure, 1e3 disables the limit

body:
## Problem

The two login rate-limit env vars in `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-auth.js` are the only env numbers in the server judged by bare `Number(...) || default`, with no finiteness, positivity, or integer check. A negative value locks every login out after a **single** failed attempt and reports a negative limit in the rate-limit headers; an exponent spelling (`1e3`) silently raises the budget to 1000 attempts per window, effectively disabling the login rate limiter; a fractional value (`2.9`) is carried through as a fractional limit.

## Evidence (verified on main `ddfbc4922`)

`packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-auth.js:34` and `:37`:

```js
const RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = Number(process.env.OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS) || 10;
const RATE_LIMIT_NO_IP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = Number(process.env.OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_NO_IP_MAX_ATTEMPTS) || 3;
```

- `||` only rescues falsy results (`NaN`, `0`, unset). `-5` is truthy, so it becomes the limit verbatim; `1e3` parses to `1000`; `2.9` stays `2.9`. `checkRateLimit` (:131) then locks the key as soon as `record.count >= maxAttempts` — with `-5` that is true after the first recorded failure — and `admitLoginAttempt` (:878-880) publishes the value in `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.
- Reproduced on the laptop this run (`~/git/fleet/probe-cursor-ondemand/probe-ratelimit.mjs`, real `createUiAuth` + `handleSessionCreate` with a wrong password, mocked req/res):
  - `OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=-5` → attempt 1: `401, limit=-5, remaining=-5`; attempt 2: **`429` (locked out after one failure)**.
  - Unset (default) → `401, limit=10, remaining=10`, then 9, 8 — the intended behaviour.
  - `OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1e3` → `limit=1000, remaining=1000` — 1000 attempts inside the 5-minute window before any lockout.
- Every sibling env reader in the same server — including one in this very file — validates: `readSessionTtlMs` (ui-auth.js:19-24) requires finite and `> 0` and rounds; `createUploadMaxBytes` / `guestUploadMaxBytes` / `createCommandTimeoutMs` / `createGitReadCacheTtlMs` (fs/routes.js:126-146, guests/upload.js:11-15) all require `Number.isFinite(raw) && raw > 0` (or `>= 0`) and floor. These two constants are the outliers (grep for `Number(process.env` across `packages/web/server` returns no other unguarded site).
- No test covers the env parsing: `ui-auth.test.js` / `session-cookie.test.js` contain no `RATE_LIMIT` reference (grep empty), and the constants are module-level, so the misjudged values are baked in at import.

Dedup: searches for "ui-auth rate", "login rate limit", "OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT" and the earlier "rate limit env" phrasing across open + closed issues returned nothing. No issue tracks these env vars.

## Why it matters

This is the brute-force budget for password and passkey sign-in (the two share one budget per client, ui-auth.js:873). An operator who writes a plausible-looking value — `1e3` for "a thousand", a stray negative, a fraction — either disables that protection without any warning or locks every user out after one typo'd password, and the server starts cleanly in both cases, reporting the nonsense value in its own `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Every other numeric env knob in the server falls back to its default on exactly these inputs; the security control should be the last place to judge its configuration loosely, in a codebase that has spent #463-#604 making numeric judgement strict everywhere else.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and `OPENCHAMBER_RATE_LIMIT_NO_IP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` are read through a validated helper in the style of the file's own `readSessionTtlMs` / the fs env readers: only a finite, positive, whole number is honoured (floored or required integral); anything else (`-5`, `0`, `2.9`, `1e3` if exponent spelling is rejected, `abc`, empty) falls back to the defaults 10 and 3 respectively. Whether canonical exponent spellings are honoured is the fixer's call, but negative and fractional values must never become the limit.
- [ ] With a rejected value, login behaviour is the default behaviour: 10 (or 3 for the no-IP bucket) failed attempts before lockout, and `X-RateLimit-Limit` reports the default.
- [ ] Tests pin the parsing for both vars: a valid value (e.g. `5`) is honoured; `-5`, `2.9` and a non-numeric value fall back. (The constants are module-level today, so the helper should be exported and unit-tested the way `readSessionTtlMs` already is.)
- [ ] Default (unset) behaviour is byte-identical to today, and no other rate-limit semantics change (window, lockout, cleanup, shared password/passkey budget).

## Related

- #604 and the #463-#592 series — the server-wide strict numeric judgement this pair of constants escaped.

title: fix(quota): Cursor on-demand window fabricates 100% used / $0.00 remaining when the payload omits the remaining amount

body:
## Problem

The web Cursor provider's individual-plan `on_demand` window **fabricates 100% used / $0.00 remaining when the usage payload carries a spend limit but no remaining amount**. `buildWindows` in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js` defaults a missing remaining to `0`, so "not reported" becomes "fully spent". The same function's `plan_limit` window makes the milder version of the mistake: its percent is correctly `null` when remaining is absent, but its value label still claims `$0.00 remaining`.

## Evidence (verified on main `ddfbc4922`)

`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js:268-277` (in `buildWindows`, starting :231):

```js
const onDemandLimit = toNumber(spendLimitUsage.individualLimit) ?? toNumber(spendLimitUsage.pooledLimit);
if (onDemandLimit && onDemandLimit > 0) {
  const remaining = toNumber(spendLimitUsage.individualRemaining) ?? toNumber(spendLimitUsage.pooledRemaining) ?? 0;
  windows.on_demand = toUsageWindow({
    usedPercent: clampPercent(((onDemandLimit - remaining) / onDemandLimit) * 100),
    ...
    valueLabel: `${centsLabel(remaining) ?? '$0.00'} remaining of ${centsLabel(onDemandLimit)}`
  });
}
```

- The branch is gated only on the limit (`individualLimit`/`pooledLimit` > 0). The trailing `?? 0` turns an absent `individualRemaining` **and** absent `pooledRemaining` into a definite 0, so `usedPercent` computes to exactly 100 and the label reads `$0.00 remaining of $X`.
- The function's own sibling code judges a missing remaining as unknown, not zero: `percentFromSpend` (:222-228, used for `billing_cycle`) returns `null` when `remaining === null`, and the `plan_limit` branch (:261-266) sets `usedPercent: null` when remaining is absent. Only `on_demand` invents the zero.
- `plan_limit` (:256-267): when `planUsage.limit` is present but `planUsage.remaining` is absent, the window is still created with `valueLabel: "$0.00 remaining of $X"` (`centsLabel(null) ?? '$0.00'`), even though its percent is `null` — the label alone tells the user their plan limit is exhausted.
- Reproduced on the laptop this run (`~/git/fleet/probe-cursor-ondemand/probe.mjs`, stubbed fetch against the real `fetchQuota`): payload `{ planUsage: { totalPercentUsed: 42, totalSpend: 2300 }, spendLimitUsage: { individualLimit: 2000 } }` (no remaining fields) → `on_demand = {"usedPercent":100,"remainingPercent":0,...,"valueLabel":"$0.00 remaining of $20.00"}`. Control with `individualRemaining: 1500` → `usedPercent 25`, label `$15.00 remaining of $20.00` (correct). Second probe (`probe2.mjs`): `planUsage: { ..., limit: 2000 }` with no `remaining` → `plan_limit = {"usedPercent":null,...,"valueLabel":"$0.00 remaining of $20.00"}`.
- No test pins this: `cursor.test.js` never sends a `spendLimitUsage` payload on the individual path at all (grep for `spendLimitUsage`/`individualRemaining` in the web suite returns nothing; the only `on_demand` assertions are the enterprise GetTeamSpend path, which correctly requires a measured spend).

Dedup: searches for "cursor on_demand remaining", "spendLimitUsage" and "cursor remaining" across open + closed issues returned nothing. The Cursor issues already tracked are different defects: #495/#506/#574 (windowSeconds), #517/#569 (unclamped percents), #585-adjacent Meta work. None covers a missing remaining being read as zero.

## Why it matters

An on-demand window that reports 100% used and $0.00 remaining when the API simply didn't send a remaining figure tells the user their paid on-demand budget is exhausted when nothing in the payload says so — the same fabrication class as #608 (Wafer's invented 0% used), in the opposite direction: invented exhaustion can push a user to stop working or buy credit they still have. Any Cursor payload/plan shape that returns a spend limit without a remaining field (or renames it) flips this window to permanently-exhausted, silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `buildWindows` (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js`), when neither `individualRemaining` nor `pooledRemaining` is present, the `on_demand` window does not report a fabricated percent or remaining: `usedPercent` is `null` (mirroring `percentFromSpend` / the `plan_limit` branch) or the window is omitted, and no `$0.00 remaining` label is produced from an absent remaining.
- [ ] The `plan_limit` value label no longer claims `$0.00 remaining` when `planUsage.remaining` is absent (omit the remaining claim or the window; a reported remaining of genuinely 0 still labels `$0.00 remaining`).
- [ ] Behaviour with a reported remaining is unchanged, including a reported `individualRemaining: 0` (real exhaustion still reads 100% used) and the pooled fallback order (individual first, then pooled).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.test.js` (first `spendLimitUsage` coverage on the individual path): limit present with no remaining fields → no fabricated 100%/$0.00; limit + remaining 1500/2000 → 25% and `$15.00 remaining of $20.00`; remaining reported as 0 → 100%.
- [ ] Existing Cursor quota tests pass; the enterprise `on_demand` path (GetTeamSpend) is untouched.

## Related

- #608 — the same fabrication class in the Wafer provider (invented 0% used when a percent field is absent).
- #517 — Cursor percent clamping in this same file (different defect: reported values out of range, not absent values read as zero).

body:
## Problem

The VS Code port of the Wafer quota provider **fabricates `usedPercent: 0` when the API payload omits `current_period_used_percent`**, even when the same payload carries `remaining_included_requests` / `included_request_limit` that contradict it. This is the #608 defect in the port (`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`); #608's scope and acceptance criteria are web-only (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/wafer.js`), so the port is not covered by it — the same web/port split as #506, #492 and #546.

## Evidence (verified on main `f77bcc12e` by code reading)

`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:3296-3298` (in `fetchWaferQuota`, starting :3241):

```ts
const usedPercent = hasOverage
  ? Math.max(0, usedPercentRaw ?? 0)
  : Math.max(0, Math.min(100, usedPercentRaw ?? 0));
```

- `usedPercentRaw` is `toNumber(payload?.current_period_used_percent)` (:3280) — `null` when the field is absent. The `?? 0` in both branches turns "unknown" into a definite 0.
- The port's no-data guard (:3285) only errors when remaining, limit, overage *and* percent are all null, so a percent-less payload with counts — e.g. `{ remaining_included_requests: 40, included_request_limit: 100 }` — passes through and reports `usedPercent: 0` / `remainingPercent: 100` next to the value label `40 / 100 left` (:3303-3311). 60 of 100 requests are used; the window says none are.
- The lines are identical to the web provider's `wafer.js:82-84`, which #608 reproduced on the laptop with exactly that payload (web window: `{"usedPercent":0,"remainingPercent":100,...,"valueLabel":"40 / 100 left"}`).
- No test pins this in the port: `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.test.ts` contains no Wafer cases at all (grep for `wafer`/`Wafer` returns nothing), while the web suite's Wafer tests always supply `current_period_used_percent`.

Dedup: searches for "wafer vscode" and "wafer" return #608 (web-only scope), #484 (web test coverage, closed) and other providers' clamp issues. No issue tracks the port's missing-percent fabrication.

## Why it matters

Same harm as #608, on the VS Code surface: a quota window that reports 0% used while 60% of the allowance is gone reassures the user with a number the provider invented. Any upstream payload change that drops the percent field (or a plan tier that never sends it) flips the VS Code Wafer window to permanently-zero usage, silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `fetchWaferQuota` (`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`), when `current_period_used_percent` is absent, `usedPercent` is derived from remaining/limit when both are present (`(limit - remaining) / limit * 100`, clamped to [0, 100], with the overage branch's deliberate >100 allowance preserved only when a real percent or overage count supports it), and is `null` — not 0 — when neither a percent nor a derivable pair exists. This mirrors whatever shape #608 lands in the web provider.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.test.ts` (first Wafer coverage there): percent absent with remaining 40 / limit 100 → usedPercent 60; percent absent with only `overage_request_count` present → usedPercent null; percent present (including the overage >100 and negative-clamp cases) unchanged.
- [ ] Existing VS Code quota tests pass.
- [ ] Do NOT change the deliberate overage behaviour for a *present* percent above 100 (pinned by the web test at `wafer.test.js:40`).

## Related

- #608 — the same defect in the web provider (fix in flight there does not touch this file).

Same class as #332 (auto-model-routing), #339 (install / notes-todos-plans / desktop-browser) and #601 (projects / scheduled-tasks / walkthrough) — a translated docs mirror is missing a whole subsection that the English page has — but on a page none of those issues cover, and at heading level 3, which is why earlier sweeps missed it: #601's sweep counted `## ` sections, and on this page every mirror has the same `## ` count as English.

Verified on main `f77bcc12e` by comparing headings at every level (`#`/`##`/`###`) for every docs page against its 11 translated mirrors in `packages/docs/content/docs/{de,es,fr,ja,ko,nl,pl,pt-br,tr,uk,zh-cn}/`. After this page, no other page has a heading deficit at any level outside the pages #339/#601 already cover.

## Evidence

**`providers.mdx` — "Custom / Other providers" (`###`, English :18–29) is missing in 9 of 11 mirrors.**

- English `packages/docs/content/docs/providers.mdx` is 63 lines with headings at :6 (`#`), :10 (`## Connect a provider`), :18 (`### Custom / Other providers`), :35, :42, :55, :59.
- nl (`nl/providers.mdx:18`) and tr (`tr/providers.mdx:18`) carry the subsection; de, es, fr, ja, ko, pl, pt-br, uk and zh-cn do not — each is 50 lines and jumps straight from "Connect a provider" to "Pick a model" (e.g. `de/providers.mdx:10` → `:22`).
- The missing subsection is the only documentation of custom / OpenAI-compatible providers on this page: choosing **Other / Custom**, entering provider ID / display name / base URL / API key (or `{env:VAR_NAME}`) / model ids, optional reasoning levels and request headers, saving to OpenCode config + auth, editing an existing custom provider, and the warning that without credentials models may appear but chat calls will fail (English :20–29).
- The mirrors also lose the English step-2 clause "or choose **Other / Custom** for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint" (:13) — e.g. de step 2 ends at "…der noch nicht verbunden ist." — so in those locales the page never mentions custom providers at all.

## Why it matters

Readers of 9 translated locales never learn that OpenAI-compatible gateways, campus LLMs, Ollama or LiteLLM can be connected at all — a whole provider class, not a detail. The mirrors otherwise track the English page section-by-section, so this reads as a subsection added to English and never carried over (the same failure #332/#339/#601 record for other pages, one heading level down).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `providers.mdx`: the 9 mirrors missing it (de, es, fr, ja, ko, pl, pt-br, uk, zh-cn) gain a translation of "Custom / Other providers", placed where the English page has it (inside "Connect a provider", before "Pick a model"), so every mirror has the same heading set as English at every level (1 `#`, 5 `##`, 1 `###`). nl/tr are not touched.
- [ ] The translated step 2 of "Connect a provider" in those 9 mirrors restores the "Other / Custom" alternative the English step 2 names.
- [ ] Translations follow the terminology each mirror already uses on the same page, and no other sections or pages change.
- [ ] After the change, a heading-count sweep at every heading level over all docs pages shows no deficit outside the pages already tracked by #339/#601, and `docs:validate` passes.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `providers.mdx`, "Custom Other providers" and "translated mirrors": the only hits are #601 (projects, scheduled-tasks, walkthrough only — its sweep counted `## ` headings, which this `###` deficit does not change) and #339 (install, notes-todos-plans, desktop-browser only, now closed). Neither lists providers.

body:
## Phase 3 of design #612 — contract documentation + consumer conformance fixture

Design: #612 ("one observability contract for external consumers"). This phase lands **after** phases 1 (#524, session-activity v1 fields) and 2 (#525, `GET /api/managed-servers`) have fixed their payload shapes; it documents the contract they share and gives external consumers a conformance probe so the next consumer never has to re-derive the shapes from source (which is how #524's probe ended up reporting "shape couldn't be confirmed").

## Scope

- One external-consumer document (in the server route docs / endpoint documentation location the phase 1–2 work establishes) covering:
  - Both reads: `/api/session-activity` and `/api/managed-servers` — full field lists, types, and the meaning of every `null`.
  - The five contract rules from #612: additive-only + `version`, explicit unknowns, empty-vs-unknown (`watcherReady`, registry `status: "unknown"`), allowlist projection with no auth material, authoritative sources only.
  - The caveat that `model`/`provider` in session activity is **observed** (latest assistant message) not configured, and that activity is a pollable snapshot, not a stream guarantee.
- A conformance fixture a paired client can run against a live server: probes both endpoints and asserts the pinned key sets per entry, presence of `version` + `serverTime`, `watcherReady` semantics (an empty-but-ready activity read is valid; a not-ready read is marked), registry secret-field absence (no password/token/fingerprint/args keys anywhere in the payload), and that a stopped server is absent or marked within one poll cycle.
- The fixture lives with the server tests (or the documented consumer location, if phase 1–2 established one) and runs without a real OpenCode session for the empty-state assertions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The document names both endpoints, every field, and each field's unknown representation; a reader can build the babysitter's poller from the document alone.
- [ ] The conformance fixture passes against a server with no active sessions (empty-but-ready state) and asserts the secret-field absence by key set, not by today's two field names only.
- [ ] The fixture's assertions match the payloads #524 and #525 actually landed (if a landed shape differs from #612, the design issue is updated to match reality — the document describes what shipped, not what was proposed).
- [ ] No production behaviour changes in this phase: docs + fixture/tests only.

body:
## Problem

The Wafer quota provider (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/wafer.js`) **fabricates `usedPercent: 0` when the API payload omits `current_period_used_percent`**, even when the same payload carries `remaining_included_requests` / `included_request_limit` that contradict it. The window renders as completely unused (0% used, 100% remaining) next to a value label that says otherwise.

## Evidence (verified on main 029f69675)

`wafer.js:82-84`:

```js
const usedPercent = hasOverage
  ? Math.max(0, usedPercentRaw ?? 0)
  : Math.max(0, Math.min(100, usedPercentRaw ?? 0));
```

`usedPercentRaw` is `toNumber(payload?.current_period_used_percent)` (:67) — `null` when the field is absent. The `?? 0` in both branches turns "unknown" into a definite 0. The provider's own no-data guard (:71) only errors when remaining, limit, overage *and* percent are all null, so a percent-less payload with counts passes through and gets the fabricated 0.

Reproduced on the laptop this run (probe worktree at HEAD 029f69675, following `wafer.test.js`'s harness — credentials stubbed via `configureOpenCodeCredentials`, global `fetch` stubbed) with payload `{ remaining_included_requests: 40, included_request_limit: 100 }` (no percent field):

```
ok: true
windows: {"5h":{"usedPercent":0,"remainingPercent":100,"windowSeconds":18000,...,"valueLabel":"40 / 100 left"}}
```

60 of 100 requests are used, the label says "40 / 100 left", and the same window reports 0% used / 100% remaining.

Sibling behaviour: the Copilot provider derives usedPercent from remaining/entitlement and falls back to the API percent, leaving `null` when neither exists; `toUsageWindow` itself maps a null/non-finite usedPercent to `remainingPercent: null` (unknown), which is the honest rendering. #484 added wafer tests for the overage clamp but no test covers a missing percent — every existing wafer test supplies `current_period_used_percent`.

Dedup: searches for "wafer usedPercent" / "wafer" return only #484 (test coverage, closed) and other providers' clamp issues. No issue tracks the missing-percent fabrication.

## Why it matters

A quota window that reports 0% used while 60% of the allowance is gone is worse than no window: the headline, bars and remaining figures all reassure the user with a number the provider invented. Any upstream payload change that drops the percent field (or a plan tier that never sends it) flips Wafer to permanently-zero usage, silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `current_period_used_percent` is absent, `usedPercent` is derived from remaining/limit when both are present (`(limit - remaining) / limit * 100`, clamped to [0, 100], with the overage branch's deliberate >100 allowance preserved only when a real percent or overage count supports it), and is `null` — not 0 — when neither a percent nor a derivable pair exists
- [ ] Regression tests in `wafer.test.js`: percent absent with remaining 40 / limit 100 → usedPercent 60; percent absent with only `overage_request_count` present → usedPercent null; percent present (including the existing overage >100 and negative-clamp cases) unchanged
- [ ] Existing wafer tests pass
- [ ] Do NOT change the deliberate overage behaviour for a *present* percent above 100 (pinned by the existing test at wafer.test.js:40)

body:
## Summary

`GET /api/model-routes/health` is the last server route that still judges its numeric query parameters with a bare `Number(...)`: `hours` and `activeMinutes` are converted loosely, so non-canonical spellings are silently reinterpreted as different windows instead of falling back to the defaults — `?hours=1e3` becomes a 1000-hour request (clamped to 336), `?hours=0x10` becomes 16 hours, `?activeMinutes=0b101` becomes 5 minutes, and whitespace / sign / trailing-`.0` spellings (` 2 `, `+2`, `2.0`) are all accepted as the number they happen to convert to. Every other numeric query parameter in this server has been strictified to judge the spelling as written (#463/#464/#465 for git `context`/`maxCount`, #554 for GitHub/GitLab `page`/`number`/`limit`, #578 for diff context in the service, #592 for `bindingRevision`, and the strict regex in `/api/fs/find-in-files`' `limit`); this route is the sole survivor of that sweep (grep-verified this run).

Verified on main `28c5b0c10` (2026-10-27).

## Evidence

- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/pool-health.js:220-221` — the route conversion, the only remaining `Number(req.query…)` in `packages/web/server` outside the dead canonical branches #602 tracks in the GitHub routes:
  ```js
  hours: req.query?.hours ? Number(req.query.hours) : undefined,
  activeMinutes: req.query?.activeMinutes ? Number(req.query.activeMinutes) : undefined,
  ```
- The converted values are only clamped/fallback-guarded downstream (`pool-health.js:84-85`: `hours = min(336, max(0.1, positiveOr(requestedHours, 24)))`, `activeMinutes = min(1440, positiveOr(requestedActiveMinutes, 15))`), so a junk spelling that converts to a positive number is honoured, not rejected: the clamp hides `1e3` as a plausible-looking 336-hour window rather than the 24-hour default a malformed value gets everywhere else (`2junk` → `NaN` → default).
- The sibling stats route's helper has the same asymmetry in miniature: `queryRouteStats` clamps its window to 336 hours (`model-route-stats.js:83`) while `queryAttemptCountsPerTarget` (`model-route-stats.js:189`) applies only the 0.1 floor — today only `computePoolHealth`'s own clamp keeps the two windows consistent.
- The route conversion is untested: `pool-health.test.js` calls `computePoolHealth` with numbers directly (e.g. `hours: 24`, `hours: Number.NaN` at :140) and never exercises `registerPoolHealthRoutes`' string parsing.

### Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-poolhealth/probe.mjs`, this run — the route's exact conversion + the compute clamp/fallback from main)

```text
"24"       -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 24
"1e3"      -> hours 336  | activeMinutes 1000   (1000h, clamped)
"0x10"     -> hours 16   | activeMinutes 16
"0b101"    -> hours 5    | activeMinutes 5
" 2 "      -> hours 2    | activeMinutes 2
"+2"       -> hours 2    | activeMinutes 2
"2.0"      -> hours 2    | activeMinutes 2
"2.9"      -> hours 2.9  | activeMinutes 2.9
"01"       -> hours 1    | activeMinutes 1
"2junk"    -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 15     (NaN -> default)
"-5"       -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 15     (not positive -> default)
"0"        -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 15
"Infinity" -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 15
undefined  -> hours 24   | activeMinutes 15
```

## Why it matters

- Pool health is an advisory surface other tooling reads (#524's external-babysitter use case is the same family): a caller that builds the query string loosely (or a hand-typed URL with `hours=1e3`) silently gets a different telemetry window than it spelled, with no signal — the exact failure mode the #463–#592 strict-parsing fixes removed from the git, GitHub, GitLab and filesystem routes one by one.
- Leaving one loose route in place re-teaches the pattern: the next route copied from this one inherits `Number(req.query…)` as the house style, against the repo's now-established convention that a numeric parameter's spelling is judged as written and anything else falls back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hours` / `activeMinutes` query spellings are judged strictly: a canonical decimal spelling (fractional hours/minutes such as `1.5` may stay valid — the compute layer deliberately supports sub-hour windows down to 0.1h) is honoured; exponent (`1e3`), radix-prefixed (`0x10`, `0b101`), signed (`+2`, `-5`), whitespace-padded (` 2 `) and trailing-junk (`2junk`) spellings fall back to the defaults (24h / 15m) instead of being reinterpreted.
- [ ] The defaults and clamps are unchanged: missing/invalid → 24h and 15m; honoured values still clamp to 336h / 1440m and the 0.1h floor.
- [ ] `pool-health.test.js` (or a route-level test) pins the route's string parsing: at least one reinterpreted spelling per parameter (`1e3`, `0x10`) now yields the default window, and a canonical spelling still yields its window.
- [ ] No change to `computePoolHealth`'s numeric contract (its direct callers and tests pass numbers), the stats route, or the response shape.

title: refactor(github-routes): eight read handlers carry an always-true canonical flag — the retired legacy branches (incl. loose Number number parsing) are dead code

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

body:
## Summary

Eight read handlers in `packages/web/server/lib/github/routes.js` still carry a dual-path `canonical` flag that can only ever be `true`, so every non-canonical branch in them is dead code — including the loose `Number(...)` issue-number parsing that the strict-parsing series (#554) removed from the live paths. The dead branches preserve the pre-bound behaviour (no read-context validation, non-strict network/metadata handling, failures answered as empty results) in the source, where a future re-registration or copy-paste could resurrect it.

Verified on main `67d7e88ed`.

## Evidence

- The handlers are registered **only** at canonical paths: `canonicalGitHubRoutePath` (routes.js:26) returns just `/api/source-control/github<suffix>`, and the registrations are at :1688 (`/pr/status`), :1974 (`/repo/upstream`), :2067 (`/repo/branches`), :2469 (`/issues/list`), :2651 (`/issues/get`), :2743 (`/issues/comments`), :2821 (`/pulls/list`), :3028 (`/pulls/context`). There is no array-path or legacy registration for these handlers.
- Their legacy twins are registered separately as a retirement stub at :308-313: every `/api/github` suffix in `retiredLegacyGitHubGetRoutes`/`retiredLegacyGitHubPostRoutes` (:27-31, which lists exactly these routes) answers `410 SOURCE_CONTROL_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` and never reaches the handlers.
- The test suite pins that split: `routes.auth.test.js` expects 410 for `/api/github/pr/status` (:195, :261), `/api/github/pulls/list` (:411, :436, :731), `/api/github/pulls/context` (:733), `/api/github/repo/upstream` (:939), `/api/github/repo/branches` (:1157), `/api/github/issues/list` (:1159) and `/api/github/issues/comments` (:1161); `routes.mutations.test.js:1034` likewise.
- Inside the handlers each computes `const canonical = req.path.startsWith('/api/source-control/')` (:1694, :1977, :2072, :2474, :2655, :2747, :2826, :3035) — always `true` given the registrations above — and branches on it ~50 times, e.g.:
  - `issues/get` :2656 and `issues/comments` :2748: `canonical ? readPositiveIntegerQuery(req, 'number') : requestedNumber ? Number(requestedNumber) : null` — the `Number(...)` side (fractions like `2.9` pass) is unreachable, but reads as live loose parsing; it already had to be analysed and excluded during the #554 audit.
  - `trustedContext = canonical ? await validateReadContext(...) : null` with `if (canonical && !trustedContext)` 501 guards (:1695-1698 and siblings) — the unvalidated path cannot run.
  - Downstream strictness flags and fallbacks that are always on: `strictNetworkErrors: canonical`, `requireGitHubIssue(...)` vs raw `result?.data` (issues/get), `if (!canonical) { ... }` empty-result fallbacks and `canonical ? null : reposToQuery[0]` repo fallbacks (issues/list :2551-2558), `defaultBranch = canonical ? null : 'main'` (repo/upstream :2012).

## Why it matters

- **Misleading security surface:** a reader auditing origin/binding checks or number parsing (as #592/#554 required) cannot tell from the handler code that the unbound, loosely-parsed path is unreachable; the audit has to re-derive it from the registration tables every time.
- **Resurrection risk:** the dead branches are complete working implementations of the retired behaviour. Re-registering one handler on an additional path, or copying a handler as the template for a new route, silently restores unbound reads with no read-context validation.
- **Maintenance cost:** every change to these handlers must be made and reviewed in two variants, one of which no test can reach through the public routes (the suite's legacy-path tests all stop at the 410 stub).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In the eight handlers listed, the `canonical` flag and its unreachable non-canonical branches are removed; the canonical behaviour is the only behaviour (read-context validation always runs, strict helpers always used, strict network/metadata flags always on).
- [ ] No route registration changes: canonical paths behave exactly as before, and every legacy `/api/github` path still answers 410 `SOURCE_CONTROL_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` (existing tests in routes.auth.test.js / routes.mutations.test.js pass unmodified).
- [ ] The loose `Number(requestedNumber)` expressions in issues/get and issues/comments are gone; `number` is read only via `readPositiveIntegerQuery`.
- [ ] The GitHub route test suites (routes.test.js, routes.auth.test.js, routes.aliases.test.js, routes.mutations.test.js) pass, with no test deleted to make them pass.
- [ ] Scope is this file's eight handlers only: the auth routes' dual registration (`githubAuthRoutePaths`, :1326+) is genuinely live on both paths and is not touched, and the mutation executor's canonical path is unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for "retired legacy GitHub", "dead code github routes", "canonical dead branch" and "non-canonical": no covering issue. #554/#558 fixed the live loose parsing in these routes and #592 covers bindingRevision; neither mentions the unreachable branches.
