body:
## Problem

`NoteEditor`'s formatted (live-preview) view is racy on first render: the decorations that hide Markdown markers are built from whatever part of the syntax tree happens to be parsed at that moment, and nothing rebuilds them when parsing completes. The visible symptom is the tail of a note rendering as raw Markdown — inline-code backticks stay visible and a later list item keeps its `-` instead of a bullet — until the user interacts with the editor.

This makes the editor's own test flaky and turns that flake into unrelated CI failures.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-27, main `efdd08b70`)

- `packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/NoteEditor.test.tsx` — repeated targeted runs:
  `bun test packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/NoteEditor.test.tsx`
  Batch 1: 1 fail / 5 runs. Batch 2: 4 fails / 8 runs. (Plus the same failure in PR #533's CI, where the diff was dictionary-only.)
- Failing assertion (test line 57):
  ```
  expect(content()).not.toContain('`')
  Received: "Release• push the tag- check `changelog`"
  ```
  Note what the received text shows: the heading mark and `**` ARE hidden and the first list item DID get its bullet, but the second list item still shows `-` and the inline code still shows its backticks — i.e. the decoration pass saw only a prefix of the parsed tree.
- Root-cause shape in `packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/NoteEditor.tsx`:
  - Line 82: `buildDecorations` iterates `syntaxTree(state)` — the tree parsed so far; it does not use `ensureSyntaxTree` / `forceParsing`.
  - Lines ~139-152: the `livePreview` ViewPlugin rebuilds decorations only on `docChanged || viewportChanged || selectionSet || focusChanged`. A background parse completing is none of those, so stale (partial) decorations persist until the next user interaction.
  - Contrast with the sibling editor in the same package, `packages/ui/src/components/ui/CodeMirrorEditor.tsx:170,461,518,594`, which explicitly calls `forceParsing(...)`, and `packages/ui/src/lib/codemirror/documentSymbols.ts:93`, which uses `ensureSyntaxTree`.

## Why it matters

- Product bug, not just a test bug: on a real first render the note can show raw backticks / dashes — exactly what this component exists to hide (see its header comment: markers "are hidden except on the lines the cursor is on") — until the user clicks or types.
- CI noise: this flake already failed the tests job on PR #533, a pure i18n dictionary change, forcing a "pre-existing failure" investigation in that run.

## Acceptance criteria

- The decoration pass sees a complete tree for the visible document (e.g. via `ensureSyntaxTree`/`forceParsing`, bounded), OR decorations are rebuilt when parsing completes — first render is fully formatted with no user interaction.
- `bun test packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/NoteEditor.test.tsx` passes 20 consecutive runs locally.
- The second test (active line shows its markers; stored text untouched) still passes — the fix must not hide markers on the cursor's line.
- No new anti-slop / lint / type-check findings on the changed files (`bun run check:changed` per repo rules).

## Suggested fix direction

In `buildDecorations` (or the plugin's update path), ensure the syntax tree is parsed to the end of the visible ranges before iterating — following the in-repo precedent in `CodeMirrorEditor.tsx` (`forceParsing`) or `documentSymbols.ts` (`ensureSyntaxTree` with a bounded timeout). Keep any timeout bounded so a very long note cannot block typing; if the bounded parse still cannot complete, the rebuild-on-parse-complete path is the fallback.

body:
## Bug

`resolveOutboundProxyEnv` in `packages/web/server/lib/outbound-proxy.js` claims to read the standard proxy variables "either case", but an **empty (or whitespace-only) uppercase variable shadows a set lowercase one**, because `readVariable` uses `??` (nullish) fallback:

```js
const readVariable = (env, name) => String(env[name] ?? env[name.toLowerCase()] ?? '').trim();
```

An empty string is not nullish, so the lowercase variable is never consulted. Empty uppercase proxy variables are common in practice: container images, CI templates and corporate shell profiles frequently export `HTTP_PROXY=`/`NO_PROXY=` blank while a tool or user sets the lowercase form.

## Evidence (verified on main `501f17168`, Node probe importing the real module)

```js
import { resolveOutboundProxyEnv } from './packages/web/server/lib/outbound-proxy.js';

resolveOutboundProxyEnv({ HTTP_PROXY: '', http_proxy: 'http://proxy:3128' })
// => null   (proxy silently ignored)

resolveOutboundProxyEnv({ HTTP_PROXY: '   ', http_proxy: 'http://proxy:3128' })
// => null   (whitespace-only upper case also shadows)

resolveOutboundProxyEnv({ HTTPS_PROXY: 'http://p:1', NO_PROXY: '', no_proxy: 'corp.example' })
// => { HTTPS_PROXY: 'http://p:1', NO_PROXY: 'localhost,127.0.0.1,::1' }
//    (the user's `corp.example` bypass entry is silently dropped)
```

## Why it matters

- Case 1/3: the server silently runs without the configured proxy — quota/catalog/upstream calls fail or bypass the required egress path with no warning.
- Case 2 is worse: a configured proxy *is* applied, but the user's `no_proxy` bypass list is lost, so internal/corporate hosts that must stay direct are routed through the proxy.

## Suggested fix

Treat an empty/whitespace-only value as unset when falling back to the other case, e.g. read the uppercase value, trim it, and only fall back to lowercase when the trimmed result is empty (apply the same to the lowercase-first direction if one is added). Keep the existing loopback bypass behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- `resolveOutboundProxyEnv({ HTTP_PROXY: '', http_proxy: 'http://proxy:3128' })` returns the proxy env using `http://proxy:3128`.
- `resolveOutboundProxyEnv({ HTTPS_PROXY: 'http://p:1', NO_PROXY: '', no_proxy: 'corp.example' })` keeps `corp.example` in the returned `NO_PROXY`.
- Whitespace-only uppercase values behave the same as empty ones.
- Existing tests in `packages/web/server/lib/outbound-proxy.test.js` pass, plus new regression cases for the three probes above.

body:
## Nice-to-have (found by fleet pilot #1188, 2026-10-26)

OpenChamber spawns one OpenCode server per project/workspace on
**dynamic localhost ports** (seven observed in one evening: 4747,
13420, 34437, 34707, 37249, 37621, 40967), each requiring auth. That's
fine for the UI, but any external tool (a babysitter, a monitor, a
debugger) that needs to find "the server for project X" has to scrape
process tables or state files — there is no stable discovery surface.

## Request

A registry read in the OpenChamber web API: per managed server —
project id/path, port, server version, status (starting/ready/
stopped), started-at, and session count. (Auth material deliberately
NOT included; the point is discovery, and consumers that need more
should come through OpenChamber's own API/proxy as paired clients.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One call returns the live server list in the shape above,
      matching `ss`/process ground truth at probe time.
- [ ] Stopped servers disappear (or are marked) within one poll
      cycle — no zombie entries.

Filed by Muse (operator) 2026-10-26. Priority low: the babysitter
program treats OpenChamber's API as its integration layer, so this is
ergonomics for every future external tool, not a blocker.

## Feature request (from the fleet babysitter program)

An external babysitter (developing-today/code#1185) watches
OpenChamber sessions and judges progressing vs stalled. Its detector
(derived from 187 real claim episodes, developing-today/code#1192)
needs, per session, a small set of pollable fields:

- session status (working / idle / waiting / error),
- **last-activity timestamp** (last message or tool event),
- current model + provider (which pool the session is drawing on),
- whether a tool call is currently in flight.

`/api/session-activity` exists but returned `{}` during a probe with
no active sessions, so its live shape couldn't be confirmed. If the
fields above are already there when sessions are active, this issue
is just documentation; if any are missing, they're the ask.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a session active, `/api/session-activity` (or a documented
      per-session endpoint) exposes status, last-activity, model +
      provider, and in-flight state, verifiable by a paired client.
- [ ] The response shape is documented where API consumers will find
      it (server route docs / endpoint comment).

Filed by Muse (operator) 2026-10-26; the babysitter's stall detector
is blocked on the last-activity field specifically.

body:
## Problem

The VS Code port of the Cursor quota provider (`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`, `fetchCursorQuota`) passes the plan explicit percent to `toUsageWindow` unclamped — the same defect filed for the web provider as #517, in the port that #517 explicitly left as a separate follow-up (its packet scope excluded "VS Code port totalPercentUsed site (separate follow-up per #509->#510 precedent)").

Site (on main 2813c128a):
- `quotaProviders.ts:2537-2538` — `const usedPercent = toNumber(planUsage.totalPercentUsed);` passed raw into the `billing_cycle` window

## Evidence (verified this run)

Temporary `bun test` probe on main 2813c128a (scratch `OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR` with a `quota/cursor.json` credential, global `fetch` stubbed, probe deleted after the run), payload `GetCurrentPeriodUsage` → `{ planUsage: { totalPercentUsed: 150 } }`:

- `billing_cycle` window reported `usedPercent: 150`

The same file's enterprise Cursor path (built by `cursorEnterpriseWindows`, covered for windowSeconds by #506) derives its percents from clamped request counts; only this explicit-percent plan path leaks. Sibling paths in the same file clamp both bounds (copilot at :1806-1812, ollama-cloud at :2350/:2361).

## Why it matters

`usedPercent` is the headline figure the extension renders. A drifting upstream payload is shown verbatim — 150% used — instead of the clamped value every sibling path produces.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fetchCursorQuota` clamps the plan-path `usedPercent` to [0, 100].
- Regression tests: 150 → 100, -20 → 0, an in-range value (e.g. 42) unchanged, missing/null stays null.
- Do NOT clamp inside `toUsageWindow` itself: the wafer overage branch deliberately allows >100 (see #517 packet scope).
- Existing VS Code quota tests pass, including the enterprise windows covered by #506.

## Suggested fix

Apply the same `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value))` clamp used by the copilot/ollama-cloud paths in this file (or a shared `clampPercent` helper if one is introduced for #515/#518/#519) at the site above.

body:
## Problem

The Cursor quota provider (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js`) clamps its *computed* percentages but passes the API's *explicit* percentages through unclamped, so an out-of-range payload leaks into the usage UI: `usedPercent: 150` / `200`, or a negative `usedPercent: -20` with `remainingPercent: 120`.

## Evidence (verified on main 2813c128a)

Node probe following `cursor.test.js`'s own harness (future-expiry `CURSOR_TOKEN`, global `fetch` stubbed by URL fragment, exported `fetchQuota`), with `planUsage: { totalPercentUsed: 150, autoPercentUsed: -20, apiPercentUsed: 200, totalSpend: 2300, limit: 10000, remaining: 5000 }`:

- `billing_cycle.usedPercent = 150` (from `totalPercentUsed`)
- `auto.usedPercent = -20`, `remainingPercent = 120` (from `autoPercentUsed`)
- `api.usedPercent = 200` (from `apiPercentUsed`)
- Control in the same payload: `plan_limit.usedPercent = 50` — the limit/remaining fallback in the same function *is* clamped, proving the explicit paths are the inconsistent ones

Unclamped read sites in `cursor.js`:
- `percentFromSpend` (~:207-209): `const explicit = toNumber(planUsage?.totalPercentUsed); if (explicit !== null) return explicit;` — while its own fallback at :213 is `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, …))`
- `buildWindows` (~:230-238): `autoPercent = toNumber(planUsage.autoPercentUsed)` and `apiPercent = toNumber(planUsage.apiPercentUsed)` passed straight to `toUsageWindow` — while `plan_limit` (:245-258), `on_demand` (:297-309) and the enterprise windows in the same file all clamp both bounds

Sibling providers clamp both bounds (kimi, minimax-shared `coercePercent`, nanogpt, neuralwatt, opencode-go `clampPercent`). #495/#506 track Cursor's `windowSeconds` defect (a different field); #507/#509/#512/#515/#516 cover other providers — no issue tracks Cursor's explicit-percent clamping.

Note: the VS Code port has a related explicit-percent site (`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` ~:2537, `toNumber(planUsage.totalPercentUsed)`) — a separate code copy that, per the #509 → #510 precedent, should be tracked/fixed as its own follow-up.

## Why it matters

Quota bars and remaining-percent labels are rendered from these values. Cursor's explicit percentages are the primary billing-cycle figure users see; a drift above 100 or below 0 renders as an impossible bar and an over-100 remaining figure, silently — and the inconsistency inside one file means the fallback windows look right while the headline window is wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cursor web explicit percentages clamp to [0, 100] at the read site: `totalPercentUsed` in `percentFromSpend`, and `autoPercentUsed` / `apiPercentUsed` in `buildWindows`
- [ ] Regression tests in `cursor.test.js`: 150 → 100, -20 → 0, 200 → 100, in-range values (42) unchanged, missing stays absent/null

body:
## Finding

PR #502's new schedule editor silently deletes stored `daysOfWeek` entries it cannot read when a weekday is toggled — including entries OpenCode reads perfectly well — instead of preserving them or letting the server name the problem, which is the design the same PR uses everywhere else.

## Evidence

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/502 (merged) — `packages/ui/src/lib/routing/routeSchedules.ts`, still present verbatim on current main.
- `dayNumber` (routeSchedules.ts) is `WEEKDAYS.find((weekday) => weekday === day) ?? DAY_NUMBERS.get(String(day))` — exact, case-sensitive, untrimmed lookup, numbers only as numbers. `windowWeekdays` drops every entry it cannot map: *"an entry the editor cannot read is left out."*
- `toggleWeekday` rebuilds `daysOfWeek` from `windowWeekdays(window)` alone and writes that list back, so one toggle rewrites the stored list without the dropped entries. No warning, no read-only marking.
- OpenCode's own parser (`developing-today/opencode`, `packages/core/src/model-route-schedule.ts`, `dayOfWeek`) accepts far more: it trims and lowercases (`"Mon"`, `"MONDAY"`, `" mon "` all read as Monday) and accepts numeric strings (`"5"` reads as Friday). Those stored forms are valid, live config — OpenCode applies the schedule on those days today.
- The PR's own test pins the lossy read: `windowWeekdays({ daysOfWeek: ['monday', 'tues', 5, 'Mon', 9] })` → `[1, 2, 5]` — `'Mon'` (valid to OpenCode) is dropped alongside `9` (invalid everywhere).
- Contrast with the same PR's stated design for entries it cannot read: `readScheduleList` keeps an unreadable schedule *"as stored, so a save writes it back unchanged and the server names its problem"*, and the server validator (`validateScheduleWindow` in `packages/web/server/lib/routing/model-routes.js`) is loud — it refuses a save naming the bad day entry. The toggle path bypasses that loud path by erasing the entry before the server ever sees it.

## Why it matters

A hand-written (or tool-written) config using `"Mon"` or `"5"` works today. Opening that pool's schedule in Settings shows Monday/Friday unselected (the checkbox state also comes from `windowWeekdays`), and toggling any weekday saves a list with those days silently removed — the schedule then no longer applies on days it applied on before, with no error and no record of what was lost. This is the same silent-narrowing class OpenCode PR #524 fixed in the core parser (reject the whole window rather than drop an unreadable day entry), reintroduced at the editor layer.

Cross-repo note: the affected pattern is this repo's editor only; OpenCode's parser is the reference behaviour and needs no change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Toggling a weekday on a window whose `daysOfWeek` contains an entry the editor cannot map (e.g. `9`, or a misspelling) never silently removes that entry: either the window is treated as unreadable/read-only like an unreadable schedule entry, or the unmapped entries are preserved verbatim in the written list, or the save is refused with the entry named.
- [ ] Day forms OpenCode accepts are read correctly by the editor: case-insensitive names (`"Mon"`, `"MONDAY"`), surrounding whitespace, and numeric strings (`"5"`) display and toggle as their weekday.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both: a toggle over a mixed list (`['Mon', 'fri', 9]`) loses nothing silently, and the OpenCode-valid forms map to the right weekdays.
- [ ] Existing `routeSchedules` tests updated where they pinned the dropping behaviour.

## Problem

The VS Code quota port's Cursor enterprise path reports time-until-reset as `windowSeconds`, while every other provider and every consumer of that field treat it as the window's duration. This is the #495 defect in the VS Code port — #495's scope and grep were the web provider only (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js`), so the port was not covered, exactly as #492 was the port instance of the web-only #489.

`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`:

- `:2491` (`cursorEnterpriseWindows`): `const windowSeconds = resetAt ? Math.max(0, Math.floor((resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000)) : null;`
- That value is passed to both windows the builder creates: `billing_cycle` (:2496) and `on_demand` (:2501).

So a monthly Cursor enterprise cycle reports a `windowSeconds` that shrinks every day as reset approaches — and drops to 0 once the fixture/payload end passes — instead of the cycle's length. The port's own plan path in the same file does it correctly: `:2538` passes `windowSeconds: null` for its `billing_cycle` window (the copilot precedent for an unknown duration).

## Why it matters

Consumers trust the duration semantics:

- `packages/ui/src/components/chat/work-status/usageHeadline.ts` (`pickUsageHeadline`) picks the headline quota as the row with the *shortest* `windowSeconds`, on the documented reasoning that a short window says more about whether the next turn will land. A Cursor enterprise row therefore looks like an ever-shortening window: near cycle end it outranks genuine short windows (5h buckets) purely because reset is near, and it is never treated as the duration-less monthly row it is.
- `resetAt` / `resetAfterSeconds` already carry the time-until-reset information (via the port's own `toUsageWindow` at `quotaProviders.ts:496-505`, which derives `resetAfterSeconds` from `resetAt`), so nothing is lost by reporting the duration honestly.

## Evidence (verified this run on main a181e1299)

- Read `quotaProviders.ts:2489-2503` verbatim: `cursorEnterpriseWindows` derives `windowSeconds` from `resetAt - Date.now()` and passes it to both windows it builds.
- `grep -rn "resetAt - Date.now" packages/vscode/src/` — the other matches (:315, :492, `exeDevQuota.ts:34`, `opencodeGoQuota.ts:48`) all assign to `resetAfterSeconds`-style fields, which is the correct use; only :2491 assigns the difference to `windowSeconds`.
- The enterprise test block in `quotaProviders.test.ts` (`describe('Cursor quota provider (VS Code parity)')`, :1861-1975) asserts `usedPercent` and `valueLabel` for the enterprise windows but never `windowSeconds`, so no test pins the current behaviour.
- The enterprise payload already carries the real cycle bounds in fixtures (`quotaProviders.test.ts:1883`: usage payload has both `billingCycleStart` and `billingCycleEnd`), so a true duration is derivable when both are present. Note the port's `resetAt` source is `planInfo.billingCycleEnd ?? usage.billingCycleEnd` (:2490); the start must be read from the matching source (`planInfo.billingCycleStart ?? usage.billingCycleStart`) so start and end come from the same payload.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cursor enterprise windows (`billing_cycle`, `on_demand`) no longer report time-until-reset as `windowSeconds`.
- Where the cycle start and end are both known (from the same payload source), `windowSeconds` is the actual cycle duration in seconds; where they are not, it is `null` (matching the port's own plan path at :2538).
- `resetAt` / `resetAfterSeconds` behaviour is unchanged.
- A test in the Cursor block of `quotaProviders.test.ts` pins `windowSeconds` for a fixed `billingCycleStart`/`billingCycleEnd` pair (and the `null` case) for the enterprise builder.

## Suggested fix

In `cursorEnterpriseWindows`, derive `windowSeconds` from the billing-cycle start/end when both are available, otherwise pass `null`. Keep the change inside `quotaProviders.ts` plus its test. This mirrors the fix direction already recorded for the web provider in #495 / follow-up task 1157; the two fixes are independent (different files, different test suites) and neither blocks the other.

title: fix(security): [::1] loopback origin alias is dead code — host.split(':') mangles bracketed IPv6 hosts

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

In `packages/web/server/lib/security/request-security.js`, `getRequestOriginCandidates` intends to treat the three loopback spellings as aliases of one another: when the request `Host` is `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, the `localhost` origin (same port) is added to the allowed set, and vice versa. The `[::1]` half of that logic is dead code — it can never fire — so a server reached over IPv6 loopback rejects the very alias origins the code means to allow.

## Evidence (verified on main `ad113995c`)

`request-security.js:142-149`:

```js
const [hostname, port] = host.split(':');
const normalizedHost = typeof hostname === 'string' ? hostname.toLowerCase() : '';
const portSuffix = typeof port === 'string' && port.length > 0 ? `:${port}` : '';
if (normalizedHost === 'localhost') {
  origins.add(`${protocol}://127.0.0.1${portSuffix}`);
  origins.add(`${protocol}://[::1]${portSuffix}`);
} else if (normalizedHost === '127.0.0.1' || normalizedHost === '[::1]') {
  origins.add(`${protocol}://localhost${portSuffix}`);
}
```

`'[::1]:3000'.split(':')` is `['[', '', '1]', '3000']`, so `hostname` is `'['` and `port` is `''`: `normalizedHost` never equals `'[::1]'`, and the port suffix is lost as well. The same happens for a port-less `[::1]` host (`['[', '', '1]']`).

Direct probe against `createRequestSecurityRuntime` (this run):

| Origin | Host | Result | Expected per the code's intent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http://localhost:3000` | `127.0.0.1:3000` | allowed | allowed |
| `http://localhost:3000` | `[::1]:3000` | **rejected** | allowed |
| `http://127.0.0.1:3000` | `[::1]:3000` | **rejected** | allowed |
| `http://[::1]:3000` | `[::1]:3000` | allowed (exact host match) | allowed |

## Why it matters

- Fail-closed papercut with a real user surface: anyone who opens the UI via `http://[::1]:<port>` (or whose tooling resolves `localhost` to `::1` first and sends that as `Host`) gets origin-check rejections (403s on origin-gated requests/WebSocket upgrades) for `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` origins that the sibling `127.0.0.1` host accepts.
- The dead branch misleads future editors into believing IPv6 loopback is handled.
- The fix pattern already exists in the same codebase: `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/session-cookie.js` (`hostPort`, lines 29-41) parses bracketed IPv6 authorities correctly — hostname/port extraction here should match that behaviour instead of a naive `split(':')`.

## Suggested fix

Parse the `Host` authority bracket-aware (reuse or mirror the `session-cookie.js` approach): for `[...]` hosts, the hostname is everything up to `]`, and the port is the digits after `]:`. Keep behaviour for plain hosts unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `Host: [::1]:3000`, origins `http://localhost:3000` and `http://127.0.0.1:3000` are allowed by `isRequestOriginAllowed`; with `Host: [::1]` (no port) the port-less aliases are added.
- [ ] Existing behaviour is unchanged for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, LAN, and non-loopback hosts, and foreign origins (e.g. `https://evil.example.com`) stay rejected in every host spelling.
- [ ] New tests in `packages/web/server/lib/security/request-security.test.js` cover the bracketed-IPv6 host cases (with and without a port), alongside the existing loopback-alias tests.
- [ ] No widening beyond loopback aliases: the allowed set for a `[::1]` host is exactly the set a `127.0.0.1` host of the same port produces, plus the exact host origin.

Single-repo: the request-security origin logic exists only in openchamber.

title: fix(quota): Cursor provider reports time-until-reset as windowSeconds, not the window duration

body:
## Problem

The Cursor quota provider reports time-until-reset as `windowSeconds`, while every other provider and every consumer of that field treat it as the window's duration.

`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js`:

- `:220` (`buildWindows`): `const windowSeconds = resetAt ? Math.max(0, Math.floor((resetAt - Date.now()) / 1000)) : null;`
- `:290` (`buildEnterpriseWindows`): the identical line.

So a monthly Cursor cycle reports `windowSeconds` of ~2,592,000 on day 1 and ~86,400 on the last day — the value shrinks with time left, not with the length of the billing window. It is the only provider that derives the field this way: a grep for `resetAt - Date.now` across `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/**` matches only these two Cursor lines. Providers that do not know a duration report `null` instead (e.g. `copilot.js` passes `windowSeconds: null` for its monthly premium-interactions window).

## Why it matters

Consumers trust the duration semantics:

- `packages/ui/src/components/chat/work-status/usageHeadline.ts:57-75` (`pickUsageHeadline`) picks the headline quota as the row with the *shortest* `windowSeconds`, on the documented reasoning that "a 5-hour bucket says more about whether the next turn will land than a monthly one", and keeps rows *without* a duration only as a last resort. A Cursor row therefore looks like an ever-shortening window: near cycle end it outranks genuine short windows (5h buckets) purely because reset is near, and it is never treated as the duration-less monthly row it is.
- `packages/ui/src/components/usage/UsageGiftResetButton.tsx:22-25` and the z.ai gift-reset attachment in `providers/zai.js` compare `windowSeconds` against exact durations (5h, 7d), the same duration contract.

`resetAt` / `resetAfterSeconds` already carry the time-until-reset information (via `toUsageWindow` in `utils/formatters.js`), so nothing is lost by reporting the duration honestly.

## Evidence (verified this run on main 8711e6d56)

- Read `cursor.js:214-262` and `:288-326` verbatim: both builders compute `windowSeconds` from `resetAt - Date.now()` and pass it to every window they build (`billing_cycle`, `auto`, `api`, `plan_limit`, `on_demand`).
- `grep -rn "resetAt - Date.now" packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/` — only `cursor.js:220` and `cursor.js:290`.
- `cursor.test.js` never asserts `windowSeconds` (grep finds no occurrence), so no test pins the current behaviour.
- The usage payload already carries the real cycle bounds in fixtures (`cursor.test.js:25`: `billingCycleStart` and `billingCycleEnd`), so a true duration is derivable on the plan path when both are present.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cursor windows no longer report time-until-reset as `windowSeconds`.
- Where the cycle start and end are both known, `windowSeconds` is the actual cycle duration in seconds; where they are not, it is `null` (the copilot precedent for an unknown duration).
- `resetAt` / `resetAfterSeconds` behaviour is unchanged.
- A test in `cursor.test.js` pins `windowSeconds` for a fixed `billingCycleStart`/`billingCycleEnd` pair (and the `null` case), for both the plan and enterprise builders.

## Suggested fix

In both builders, derive `windowSeconds` from the billing-cycle start/end when both are available (the usage payload's `billingCycleStart`/`billingCycleEnd`), otherwise pass `null`. Keep the change inside `cursor.js` plus its test.

title: eval: bun2nix for the node_modules derivation — verdict: not needed for the #449 failure class

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/low

labels.name: area/nix

labels.name: effort/xs

body:
## Question

During the #449 investigation (fixed-output hash flipping between CI and local builds), Drew asked whether a better tool exists for the node2nix-style step — specifically bun2nix (nix-community) versus the current hand-rolled bun-install fixed-output derivation.

## What the #449 evidence showed

- The two flavors' trees were diffed file by file: all 73,147 files byte-identical. The fetched content was NEVER the problem.
- The entire variance was one symlink created (or not) by bun's isolated installer at install time inside the local build: `node_modules/.bun/browserslist@4.28.1+…/node_modules/.bin/update-browserslist-db` — a cyclic peer pair whose bin link creation is environment-sensitive.
- Identical bun binary (same store path) in every environment; the flip tracked the build machine, not the sources, the lockfile, or the fetch path.

## Verdict

bun2nix would NOT have prevented #449. Its wins are per-package SRI-verified fetching (fetchurl per package from bun.lock's integrity hashes) and an offline, cache-based install. That eliminates fetch-path variance — a class we proved was not involved here (contents were always identical). The install step still runs bun's linker in a derivation, so the environment-sensitive bin-link behavior would remain, and the same normalization (dropping the store-internal .bin links/dirs, as landed in #488) would still be needed on top.

Where bun2nix would genuinely help: supply-chain integrity per package, incremental rebuilds (one changed package refetches instead of a 1.9 GB whole-tree FOD), and removing the single giant hash as a point of fragility. Those are real but separate benefits, and migration is a substantial change (generated bun.nix to keep in sync, fetchBunDeps wiring, patchedDependencies flow to re-validate).

## Recommendation

Do not migrate for the #449 class — it is fixed by output normalization. Revisit bun2nix only if per-package integrity or incremental dependency builds become goals in their own right; if that day comes, this issue is the starting evidence that the install-time normalization must be carried over.

Priority: low / informational. No action scheduled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The verdict and recommendation recorded in this issue are the deliverable: no bun2nix migration is started for the #449 failure class.
- [ ] If bun2nix is ever revisited (per-package integrity or incremental dependency builds becoming goals in their own right), the revisit starts from this issue's evidence and carries over the install-time normalization landed in #488 (dropping the store-internal .bin links/dirs).

title: fix(quota): google transformModelData converts an unparseable resetTime to NaN instead of null — the one quota path bypassing toTimestamp

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

`transformModelData` in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/google/transforms.js` (line 74–76) converts the models payload's `resetTime` with a raw `new Date(...).getTime()`:

```js
const resetAt = modelData?.quotaInfo?.resetTime
  ? new Date(modelData.quotaInfo.resetTime).getTime()
  : null;
```

For any unparseable `resetTime` string this yields `NaN`, which flows verbatim into the usage window (`toUsageWindow` in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/utils/formatters.js` copies `resetAt` into its result untouched). Its sibling in the same file, `transformQuotaBucket` (line 47), uses the shared `toTimestamp` helper (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/utils/transformers.js`), which returns `null` for unparseable input — so the two Google transform paths disagree on the same bad input: one produces `null`, the other `NaN`. The unguarded `new Date(...).getTime()` at transforms.js:75 is the only one in the quota tree; the other call site (formatters.js `calculateResetAfterSeconds`) checks `Number.isFinite` before using the value.

`transforms.js` also has no test file (the google provider's `api.js`, `auth.js`, `oauth.js` and `transforms.js` are covered only indirectly through `index.test.js`, which never passes a `resetTime`).

## Evidence (verified on main a763f5d57, 2026-10-26)

Direct import of the transforms module in node:

- `transformModelData('gemini-x', { quotaInfo: { remainingFraction: 0.5, resetTime: 'not-a-date' } }, 'gemini')` → `windows.daily.resetAt` is `NaN` (`Number.isNaN(...) === true`), `resetAfterSeconds: null`.
- `transformQuotaBucket({ modelId: 'gemini-x', remainingFraction: 0.5, resetTime: 'not-a-date' }, 'gemini')` → `windows.daily.resetAt` is `null`.

A `NaN` reset timestamp is worse than `null` for in-process consumers: comparisons and arithmetic against it silently produce `NaN`/`false` instead of taking the "no reset time" path, and it only becomes `null` by accident if the result happens to cross a JSON boundary.

## Why it matters

The Google provider merges bucket data and model data into one usage map (`providers/google/index.js:57–79`); a malformed or unexpected `resetTime` from the models endpoint currently poisons that model's window with `NaN` instead of degrading to "no reset time known", which is the behaviour every other path in the file (and the shared helper) implements.

## Acceptance criteria

- `transformModelData` returns `resetAt: null` for an unparseable `resetTime`, matching `transformQuotaBucket` and `toTimestamp` semantics (including numeric epoch seconds/milliseconds handling if the payload ever carries a number).
- No code path in the google provider can emit a non-finite `resetAt`.
- A new `transforms.test.js` (or equivalent coverage) pins both transforms: valid ISO reset time, unparseable reset time → `null`, missing `quotaInfo`/`resetTime`, and the scoped-name prefixing behaviour.
- Existing google provider tests still pass.

title: fix(quota): openai.js is a stale duplicate of codex.js — same endpoint and aliases, hardcoded windows, NaN-prone reset conversion, publicly exported but unregistered and untested

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Problem

`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/openai.js` (85 lines) is a stale duplicate of `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/codex.js`. Both fetch the same endpoint (`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`) for the same credential aliases (`['openai', 'codex', 'chatgpt']`), but `openai.js` has drifted behind every fix `codex.js` received:

- **Hardcoded window keys**: `openai.js:51-66` keys windows literally `'5h'` and `'weekly'` regardless of the payload, while `codex.js` derives the label from the actual `limit_window_seconds` via `resolveWindowLabel`. A primary window that is not 5 hours is mislabeled by `openai.js`.
- **Naive reset conversion**: `openai.js:56,64` computes `reset_at * 1000` directly — an ISO-string `reset_at` yields `NaN` (verified: `'2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' * 1000 === NaN`). `codex.js` uses `toTimestamp`, which handles epoch seconds, epoch ms, and ISO strings. Notably `openai.js:7-8` imports `toNumber` and `toTimestamp` but never uses them — the migration to the shared helpers was started and abandoned.
- **Missing behavior `codex.js` has**: no `ChatGPT-Account-Id` header from `entry.accountId`, no 401 `rejected_by_access_enforcement` handling (it reports a generic `API error: 401` where `codex.js` explains the Sign-in-with-ChatGPT case), no `credits` / `spend_control` windows, no `accountLabel`, no `isConfigured` export, no per-credential `fetchQuotaForCredential`.
- **Unregistered but publicly exported**: the provider registry in `providers/index.js` has no `openai` entry (only `codex`), so the routes never use it — yet `fetchOpenaiQuota` is re-exported from `providers/index.js:518` and from the module's public surface `packages/web/server/lib/quota/index.js:15`. A grep of `packages/` finds no in-repo consumer of `fetchOpenaiQuota` outside those two re-export barrels.
- **No tests**: there is no `openai.test.js`; `codex.test.js` covers only the `codex.js` implementation.

Verified on main `46f89f696` this run (file reads, registry read, consumer grep). Dedup: no open or closed issue mentions `openai.js` duplication.

## Why it matters

Two implementations of one provider contract invite exactly the drift already visible: anyone who wires up (or imports) the exported `fetchOpenaiQuota` gets silently worse data — mislabeled windows, `NaN` reset times, and a misleading 401 message — while fixes keep landing only in `codex.js`. The dead duplicate also costs review and dead-code-ratchet attention on every quota change.

## Acceptance criteria

body:
## Finding

PR #474 (merged, commits `8e18868cc4`..`fd9bade6d7`) added per-credential quota — one labeled result per stored credential — to fix "a second stored sign-in never appeared anywhere". The new dispatcher entry point is exported and used by the CLI, but no server caller uses it, so the web Usage page still only ever shows the active credential. The module documentation describes per-credential quota as available on "web and CLI", which the web route does not deliver.

## Evidence (verified on current main `46f89f696`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/index.js:461` — `fetchQuotaForProviderInstances` returns one labeled result per usable stored credential; exported at `packages/web/server/lib/quota/index.js:13`.
- Its only caller in the repo is the CLI: `packages/web/bin/lib/commands-quota.js:245,250`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/quota/routes.js:96-100` — `GET /api/quota/:providerId` (the route the Usage page reads) still calls the single-result `fetchQuotaForProvider`, which answers with the active credential only.
- `packages/ui/src/types/quota.ts` — `ProviderResult` has no `credentialId` / `credentialLabel` / `credentialActive` / `accountLabel` fields, and the Usage page renders one result per provider, so even a multi-result response would have nowhere to show the labels.
- `packages/web/server/lib/quota/DOCUMENTATION.md:89` — "per-credential and per-instance quota below are web and CLI only for now", i.e. the docs claim web coverage the route does not provide. (Provider *instances* are partially served on web: they list via `/api/quota/providers` and their active credential answers through `fetchQuotaForProvider`; it is the per-credential multiplicity that stops at the CLI.)

## Why it matters

The motivating case in PR #474 — a second ChatGPT/Codex account whose usage never appeared — remains invisible in the primary surface (the running server's Usage page); it only appears if the user runs the new `openchamber quota` CLI. The dead export also invites the next change to build on a path no production caller exercises.

## Acceptance criteria

Either wire it through, or correct the documented scope — wiring preferred:

- `GET /api/quota/:providerId` (or a successor route) returns the per-credential results from `fetchQuotaForProviderInstances` for providers that support it, keeping the single-result shape for the rest.
- `ProviderResult` in the UI gains the credential label/active/account fields, and the Usage page renders one labeled row/block per credential for a multi-credential provider.
- Tests: a route-level or dispatcher test asserting two stored credentials for one provider produce two labeled results through the web route, plus the existing CLI tests keep passing.
- If the decision is CLI-only for now, `DOCUMENTATION.md` is corrected to say so and the dead "web" claim is removed.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #474.

title: PR #401 (happy-dom 18→21) is incomplete: no bun.lock update (every CI job fails at frozen-lockfile install) and the obsolete 18.0.1 bun patch is left behind

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review)

Open Dependabot PR #401 — "chore(deps-dev): bump happy-dom from 18.0.1 to 21.0.4 in /packages/ui" — is an incomplete dependency update: it changes one version string and leaves the lockfile and this repo's happy-dom patch behind, so it cannot pass CI or be merged as written, and a directly related part of the same change (the patch removal) is left undone.

## Evidence

- The PR's entire diff is `packages/ui/package.json` +1/−1 (`"happy-dom": "18.0.1"` → `"21.0.4"`), verified via the PR files API: no `bun.lock`, no root `package.json`, no patch file.
- Its CI (run 40106401928) fails on all four jobs — type-check, lint, tests, build — at the same first step, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: "error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen / note: try re-running without --frozen-lockfile and commit the updated lockfile" (verified in the failed-run logs). `bun.lock` on main still pins `happy-dom@18.0.1` (bun.lock:2271).
- Root `package.json:204-207` still carries `patchedDependencies: { "happy-dom@18.0.1": "bun-patches/happy-dom@18.0.1.patch" }` (mirrored at bun.lock:416-418). The patch's own header says it is a "Backport of the fix shipped in happy-dom 20.12" (a MutationObserverListener strong-reference fix in `bun-patches/happy-dom@18.0.1.patch`) — happy-dom 21 includes that fix upstream, so the version-keyed patch entry and patch file are obsolete on 21 and must be removed as part of this same update, not left dangling.
- happy-dom is load-bearing for the UI test suite: dozens of `packages/ui` tests do `import { Window } from 'happy-dom'`, and v21 is a major bump (per the PR's own release notes, v21.0.0-era changes disable CSS and iframe loading by default) — so the update also needs a real test run once the lockfile is regenerated, not just a green install.

Scope note: this is an openchamber-only finding. The patch/`patchedDependencies` setup exists only here; developing-today/opencode pins its own happy-dom (20.11.1) in its own lockfile and is not part of PR #401.

## Why it matters

As written the PR is unmergeable (every CI job dies at install), and if the lockfile were regenerated without removing the patch, the repo would carry a stale version-keyed patch for a version it no longer uses — the exact kind of leftover that breaks the next person's install in a harder-to-read way.

## Acceptance criteria

- PR #401 (or its replacement) includes a regenerated `bun.lock` resolving happy-dom 21.0.4, so `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes.
- The `happy-dom@18.0.1` entry is removed from `patchedDependencies` (root `package.json` and lockfile) and `bun-patches/happy-dom@18.0.1.patch` is deleted, after confirming the MutationObserver fix it backports is present in the installed happy-dom 21 code.
- The `packages/ui` test suite is run against happy-dom 21 and any fallout from the major bump (e.g. CSS/iframe loading defaults) is fixed or explicitly reported on the PR.
- All four PR checks (type-check, lint, tests, build) pass.

**1. `install.mdx` — the whole "Nix" section is missing in all 11 mirrors.**
English has 5 sections (Desktop, Web + PWA, VS Code, Mobile, Nix at install.mdx:40); every mirror has 4 and ends at Mobile (de/install.mdx is 38 lines vs 51 English). The missing section is the only install path for NixOS/Nix users: `nix run github:openchamber/openchamber`, the `#gui` desktop app, `packages.openchamber`/`openchamber-desktop`, the `nixosModules.openchamber` systemd module, and the note that the in-app updater is off for Nix builds.

English has 6 sections (Notes, Todos, Plans, Deleting and undo at :36, Agents at :40, Related). de/es/fr/ja/ko/nl/pl/pt-br/tr/zh-cn have 4 (they jump from Plans to Related). uk has 5 — it translated "Deleting and undo" but still lacks "Agents".

**3. `desktop-browser.mdx` — "Size and appearance" missing in 8 mirrors.**
English has 6 sections (Size and appearance at :58, between "Let the agent drive" and "Developer tools"). de/es/fr/ja/ko/pl/pt-br/zh-cn have 5; nl/tr/uk have all 6.

- [ ] `notes-todos-plans.mdx`: the 10 mirrors missing both gain "Deleting and undo" and "Agents"; the uk mirror gains "Agents" — every mirror reaches 6 `## ` sections.

body:
Follow-up to the provider fix in #216 (commit 90c100f35).

OpenCode does not watch `disabled_providers`: it keeps listing a provider written there until the location reloads. #216 makes Disable take the provider out of every catalog the config store holds, and asks OpenCode to reload only the locations of the Settings project and of the app's directory, because a read of any other location starts it with its MCP servers.

What is left:

- Another location that is running, such as a second project or worktree a session works in, still lists the provider until OpenCode starts it again. In the window that made the change the store's list hides it there too. After an app reload that list is unknown (`null`) until Settings > Providers is opened, so the picker of such a location offers the provider again, and a turn on it fails with `provider.no-route`.
- Nobody has checked what `POST /api/location/reload` does to a turn that is running in the reloaded location. The reference OpenCode checkout was not available.

Possible fixes: read `GET /api/provider/disabled` once per runtime at startup, which is one small read, so every window filters from the first catalog; or reload every running location from the server, if OpenCode can list them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A provider disabled in Settings does not appear in pickers for any running location after an app reload, without first opening Settings > Providers.
- [ ] The chosen mechanism (a startup `GET /api/provider/disabled` read per runtime, or a server-side reload of running locations) is verified not to disrupt a turn running in an affected location — or that risk is explicitly documented on this issue.
- [ ] A regression test covers the reload-then-picker case for a second location.

title: Pool health (PR #303): plan projection double-counts when a pattern target and a model it covers share a plan

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Finding

PR #303's plan projection double-counts usage when two targets linked to the same plan overlap — one a pattern (`openai/*`) and one a concrete model the pattern covers (`openai/gpt-x`). The plan's projected usage is inflated, which can flip a plan from ok to warn/over and trigger a spurious Lower weight suggestion.

## Evidence

- PR #303 (head `5ed7a623b2a518994cc379cca3e125cc0dd3eee0`), `packages/web/server/lib/routing/pool-health.js`: `usageForPlan(planID)` sums `usageOf(ref)` over every ref linked to the plan, and `usageOf` sums every `route_attempt` row the ref covers (`keyNamesTarget`). A row for `openai/gpt-x` is covered by both `openai/*` and `openai/gpt-x`, so it is added twice. (The session counter in the same file avoids this with a `Set` of session ids per target; the usage sum has no equivalent dedupe across refs.)
- Reproduced by running the PR head's own `computePoolHealth` against a seeded `route_attempt` table with exactly 20 attempts on `openai/gpt-x` in 24h and a 24-request/24h plan quota:
  - Only `openai/*` linked: `projected: 20, ratio: 0.83`.
  - Both `openai/*` and `openai/gpt-x` linked to the same plan: `projected: 40, ratio: 1.67, status: 'over'` — double the real usage, from the same 20 attempts.
- The PR's own tests cover the two halves separately — sibling concrete targets combined (`pool-health.test.js`: 'combines sibling targets on the same plan') and a pattern target alone ('counts a pattern target across the concrete models it matches') — but never a pattern and a concrete target it covers linked to one plan.

## Why it matters

Linking both a provider pattern and a specific model on it to one plan is a natural way to describe a subscription. Those users get projections up to 2x too high for the overlapping models, false 'over' states, and Lower weight prompts (see also #307) pushing them to rebalance pools that are actually within quota.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plan usage is computed over the union of covered `route_attempt` rows: each row counts once toward a plan, however many linked refs cover it.
- [ ] A regression test in `pool-health.test.js` links a pattern and a concrete model it covers to one plan and asserts the projection equals the single-ref projection for the same traffic.
- [ ] Sibling concrete targets and the pattern-only case keep their current, correct projections (existing tests still pass).

body:
## Finding

PR #303's Pool health panel offers its **Lower weight** button for pattern targets (e.g. `openai/*`), but the weight it saves can never take effect: the button writes `weights: { "openai/*": 0.5 }`, and OpenCode never looks that key up.

## Evidence

- PR #303 (head `5ed7a623b2a518994cc379cca3e125cc0dd3eee0`), `packages/web/server/lib/routing/pool-health.js`: the `lower-weight` suggestion is computed for any target whose plan projection is warn/over in a weighted/round-robin pool with more than one target — pattern targets are not excluded. Reproduced by running the PR head's own `computePoolHealth` against a seeded `route_attempt` table: a weighted pool `targets: ['openai/*', 'anthropic/b']` with `openai/*` linked to a plan at 20/24 projected requests returns `suggestion: 'lower-weight'` for `openai/*`.
- `packages/ui/src/components/sections/routing/ModelPoolsSection.tsx` (PR #303): `lowerTargetWeight` persists `weights[targetRef]` with the pattern ref as the key. OpenChamber's own save validation accepts it — `validateModelRoute` in `packages/web/server/lib/routing/model-routes.js` passes because `keyNamesTarget('openai/*', 'openai/*')` is an exact match — so the save succeeds silently.
- OpenCode side (developing-today/opencode, `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts:251,283-284` on main `af59c305`): a pattern target is expanded to concrete leaves and each leaf is attached with `leafKey = ${providerID}/${id}` (the concrete model); the weight is read as `current.weights?.[key]` with that concrete key. A `weights` entry keyed `openai/*` matches no leaf, so every expanded model keeps weight 1.
- OpenChamber's existing UI already encodes this rule: `packages/ui/src/lib/routing/poolAdvanced.ts:9` — "A pattern such as `openai/*` names several models, so it cannot carry its own budget or weight" — and `PoolAdvancedFields` offers weight fields only for concrete targets. The new panel bypasses that restriction.

Net effect: the user clicks Lower weight, the panel reloads and the dead entry keeps halving on each click (0.5, 0.25, …), while routing is unchanged and new sessions do not lean away from the target.

## Why it matters

The panel's one corrective action silently does nothing exactly for the pattern targets that fan out to the most models — the highest blast-radius case the panel exists for (#294/#301 line of work).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pattern target never gets a `lower-weight` suggestion (server-side in `computePoolHealth`), or the action writes weights for the concrete models the pattern currently expands to — one of the two, with the choice stated in the PR.
- [ ] A regression test in `pool-health.test.js` (and the panel test if the UI changes) covers a weighted pool whose warn/over target is a pattern: no dead `weights['provider/*']` entry can be produced.
- [ ] If a config already carries a pattern-keyed weight, saving pools does not silently keep a weight OpenCode ignores — it is flagged or dropped with a note.

body:
Follow-ups for the Pool health panel (Settings, Routing, Model pools), found while building it:

1. **Projections cover only `requests` and `messages` quotas.** A plan whose window is in `tokens`, `usd` or `percent` shows no projection. `route_attempt` has token counts, so a token projection is possible. Cost and percent need prices or the provider's own meter.
2. **The projection is an estimate from recent traffic.** It multiplies the last 24 hours' attempt rate across the plan's linked targets by the window length. It cannot see usage from outside OpenCode or how much of the window was used before the 24 hours. The panel says so; a reading from the provider would replace it where one exists.
3. **The panel reads once.** It loads when Settings opens and after a plan link changes. A refresh button or a slow poll while it is open would keep the session counts current.

## Acceptance criteria

Scope note (2026-10-26 intake): items 1 (tokens projection) and 3 (refresh) were built by PR #303 — see the intake comment. The remaining acceptance criteria are:
- [ ] Where a provider supplies its own meter/reading, the panel shows that reading instead of the traffic estimate, and labels which source a projection came from.
- [ ] `usd` and `percent` quota windows either get a projection or the panel explicitly states why they have none (today they silently get none).
- [ ] The existing requests/messages/tokens projections and the refresh behaviour from PR #303 keep working (existing pool-health tests pass).

title: test(themes): port-opencode-theme integration suite is run by nothing — not collected by the test runner, dedicated script referenced nowhere, sibling-checkout precondition undocumented

labels.name: kind/test

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/human

labels.name: meta/enriched

body:
## Problem

`scripts/port-opencode-theme.integration.ts` (151 lines, 7 tests) is the only integration suite for the OpenCode theme porter (`scripts/port-opencode-theme.ts`, 264 lines; exposed as `themes:port:opencode`), and it is run by nothing:

- The root `test` script runs `scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs scripts`, whose collector regex is `\.(test|spec)\.(js|cjs|mjs|jsx|ts|tsx)$` (`scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs:29`) — `port-opencode-theme.integration.ts` ends in `.integration.ts`, so it is never collected.
- Its dedicated script, `themes:port:opencode:test` (`package.json:89`), is referenced nowhere else: no workflow under `.github/workflows/`, no docs, no other script (verified by grep this run).
- Sibling suites in `scripts/` (`build-builtin-extensions.test.mjs`, `bump-version.test.mjs`, `check-changed.test.mjs`, `release-workflow.test.mjs`, …) are all collected by the root test run — this one silently is not, so the porter can regress (syntax/diff color mapping, contrast ≥ 4.5 checks, round-trip compaction, idempotent publication, CLI behavior) with no failing check anywhere.

## Verified this run (on current main, a19917b0f)

- `bun test ./scripts/port-opencode-theme.integration.ts` with no sibling checkout: **fails before any test runs** — `Cannot find module '../../opencode/packages/ui/src/theme/resolve'`.
- With a sibling checkout named exactly `opencode` next to this repo (`~/git/opencode` → the opencode repo): **7 pass, 0 fail** (~2.5s). The suite is healthy; it is just never executed and its precondition is undocumented.
- The precondition is hard-coded in two shapes: static imports from `'../../opencode/packages/ui/src/theme/resolve'` (and `.../v2/resolve`) at the top of the file, and `sourceDirectory = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../../opencode/packages/ui/src/theme/themes')` — i.e. a sibling directory literally named `opencode`, not an env var or a configurable path. Nothing in the repo tells a contributor (or CI) that this layout is required.

## Why it matters

Theme porting is how OpenCode themes land in this app; the integration suite is the only check that ported themes keep readable contrast, exact syntax colors, and lossless round-trips across *all* upstream theme files. Today a porter change can break every ported theme and every existing check stays green — the same "test run by nothing" class as #135/#137, with the extra twist that even running it manually fails opaquely unless you already know the sibling-layout secret.

## Suggested fix (choose one shape)

- Wire it in with its precondition satisfied: e.g. in the CI job that runs `bun run test` (`oc-review.yml`), check out the opencode repo as a sibling named `opencode` and run `bun run themes:port:opencode:test`; or
- Make the suite self-skipping: have the isolated-test collector pick it up and have the suite skip with a clear message when the sibling checkout is absent (so local `bun run test` exercises it whenever the sibling exists, and CI without the sibling stays green but visibly skips); and
- Document the sibling-layout precondition (README/CONTRIBUTING or a comment at the `themes:port:opencode:test` script) and ideally allow overriding the sibling path via an env var.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The integration suite runs in at least one automated check (CI or the root `test` run) whenever its sibling-checkout precondition is present
- [ ] When the precondition is absent, the outcome is an explicit, visible skip/notice — not silence and not an opaque module-not-found failure
- [ ] The sibling-layout requirement (directory named `opencode` beside this repo, or its override) is documented where a contributor running the porter will find it
- [ ] With the sibling present, the suite still passes 7/7 on current main

body:
## Finding

PR #69 (squash-merged as 6f9efd07c) added a `sessionIndexReads` counter to the sync performance diagnostics. It exists for one test, which proves that streaming a message doesn't make the request-lineage hooks read the cross-directory session index. This issue is to decide whether to keep it.

The test guards the fix for a Copilot finding on #69: the lineage hooks (the request docks and the "From subagent" label) reran on every message-only store update. #69's last commit subscribes them only to session, request and global-session changes.

## What it is (main 043998db2)

- `packages/ui/src/sync/sync-refs.ts:98`: `getAllSyncSessionMap()` calls `countSyncPerformance("sessionIndexReads")`.
- `packages/ui/src/sync/performance-diagnostics.ts:24` and `:68` declare it. `countSyncPerformance` (`:123-130`) returns after a null check unless diagnostics are on, which needs `localStorage.openchamber_sync_perf = "1"` (read at `:103`).
- `packages/ui/src/sync/DOCUMENTATION.md:672` lists it among the diagnostics ("cross-directory session index reads").
- Its one consumer is the test "leaves the cross-directory session index alone while a message streams, and still follows its requests" (`packages/ui/src/sync/__tests__/trimmed-ask-dock.test.tsx:155`), which expects 0 reads (`:166`).

## Options

1. **Keep it.** It costs a null check while diagnostics are off, and profiling can use it to spot session-index reads on hot paths.
2. **Remove it and count another way.** Constraints on a replacement:
   - Module mocking counts toward the anti-slop ratchet (`AGENTS.md:79`).
   - A render counter would not see the cost. The extra work was in `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot reads that returned an unchanged value, which don't re-render.
   - Whatever replaces it must still fail if the lineage hooks go back to reading the index on message-only updates.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either the counter stays and this issue closes with that decision,
- or it is removed together with a replacement for the test at `trimmed-ask-dock.test.tsx:155` that still fails when the hooks rerun on message-only updates, with `DOCUMENTATION.md:672` updated to match.

body:
## Finding

Three housekeeping workflows on this repository — the fork where all current development happens — can never run here: their only jobs are gated on the *upstream* repository name, so every run completes as "skipped" in ~1s and the work silently never happens.

Verified on current main `0e5663f4e`:

- `.github/workflows/label-merge-conflict.yml:21` — job `label`: `if: ${{ github.repository == 'openchamber/openchamber' }}`. No PR on this fork ever gets the `merge-conflict:true` label. Latest runs all skipped, e.g. run 39166607710 (push to main, 2026-10-18T21:10Z, 1s, skipped) and 39166089637 (pull_request_target).
- `.github/workflows/pr-intake.yml:34` — job `collect`: same guard. PR size labels and the large-PR Ideas-discussion check never apply here. Latest runs all skipped, e.g. run 39166756929 (issue_comment, 2026-10-18T21:11Z, 1s, skipped).
- `.github/workflows/stale.yml:18` — job `stale`: same guard. The daily (01:30 UTC) stale sweep never marks or closes anything here; last scheduled run 38521596365 (2026-10-14) skipped in 1s.

`gh run list` for all three workflows shows only `skipped` conclusions on this repository.

## Why this is a leftover, not a settled decision

PR #62 (fixing #61) deliberately left these three alone, noting they are "already repository-gated (`stale`, `pr-intake`, `label-merge-conflict`), so they do not fail on PRs" — that reasoning was about not breaking PR checks, not a decision that the fork should never have merge-conflict labels, PR intake labels, or a stale policy. Since then the fork has become the active repo (all sweeps, bot reviews and releases-in-progress live here), so the guard now disables housekeeping on the only repo that needs it.

Not in scope: `.github/workflows/release.yml:94` also guards on the upstream name, but release publishing is plausibly upstream-only by design (same pattern as the deploy/publish guards in developing-today/opencode) — leave it out unless a maintainer says otherwise.

## Per-workflow blockers (they differ)

- `pr-intake` needs no app secrets: `collect` uses `actions/github-script` with the workflow's declared `permissions:` (`pull-requests: write`, `issues: write` on the intake job). Changing the guard to include `developing-today/openchamber` should be sufficient.
- `stale` and `label-merge-conflict` first generate a token from the `OC_REVIEW_APP_ID` / `OC_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets, which #61 established are **not configured for this fork**. Simply widening their guard would turn silent skips into red failures. They need either the app installed/secrets set for this fork, a fallback to `github.token` (both actions accept it: `actions/stale`'s `repo-token` and the label action's `repoToken`), or the #62-style secret-presence gate that skips with a visible notice.
- `stale` is also a policy decision: enabling it starts the 28-day stale / +7-day close clock on this repo's long-lived phase and handoff issues (e.g. #2, #14–#22). A maintainer should confirm the exempt labels cover those before it is switched on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pr-intake` actually labels PRs on `developing-today/openchamber` (a test PR gets its size label; the workflow run is no longer `skipped`).
- [ ] A decision is recorded for `stale` and `label-merge-conflict`: enabled on this fork (via fork app secrets or a `github.token` fallback), or explicitly kept upstream-only with the guard comment updated to say that is intentional for the fork.
- [ ] If `stale` is enabled, exempt labels are confirmed to cover long-lived tracking/handoff issues before the first scheduled run.
- [ ] No workflow that is enabled starts failing on missing `OC_REVIEW_APP_*` secrets (the #61 failure mode).

Found by the new-issue-creator job (run 2026-10-18 17:30 CDT), verifying run conclusions and job guards on main.

title: Transcript blanks for 57–149 ms twice in a turn

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## What happens

The viewed session's whole transcript disappears for 57–149 ms, twice in one turn. It happens once about a second after the page loads, while a subagent waits for permission, and once when the turn finishes. A screenshot taken in that window shows an empty chat column; a moment later the transcript is back, unchanged.

Seen in the built web UI in headless Chrome (1440×900) against an isolated OpenCode in simulation mode. A root session launched a subagent, which launched its own; the innermost one waited for shell permission. The page was opened while it waited, the permission was granted about 2.3 s after load, and then every level finished.

`main` (`e409366de`) and the nested-subsessions branch (#47) behave the same. #47 does not change this.

## Measurements

Inline-opacity flips on the element that contains the transcript, in milliseconds from page load. Three runs on `main`:

| Run | While waiting: hidden → shown | Turn finishes: hidden → shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1596 → 1679 (83 ms) | 2413 → 2496 (83 ms) |
| 2 | 1559 → 1616 (57 ms) | 2399 → 2482 (83 ms) |
| 3 | 1668 → 1763 (95 ms) | 2447 → 2596 (149 ms) |

Two runs on #47 gave 99 ms and 98 ms for the first hide and 83 ms for both second hides.

## Where the opacity comes from

`@legendapp/list` 3.6.0 renders its `Containers` wrapper with `opacity: isVisible ? 1 : 0`. `isVisible` is `readyToRender` with no fresh-data transition pending. `resetInitialRenderState` clears `readyToRender` until the list has laid out and finished its initial scroll again. Three paths call it:

1. A fresh-data transition: the data goes from empty to non-empty after it once had rows, or `dataKey` changes. `MessageList` passes no `dataKey`.
2. `handleBootstrapInitialScrollDataChange`: the data goes from 0 rows to some after the initial scroll had finished.
3. `handleBootstrapInitialScrollFooterLayout`: the footer size changes the scroll-to-end target while the initial scroll is kept for footer layout.

Which path fires here is not pinned down. Path 3 would fit both moments if the status row under the transcript changes height then; that is unverified.

## Next step

Log `TimelineList`'s `entries.length` and the list footer's height at those two moments. Empty entries point to paths 1 and 2; a footer change with entries present points to path 3.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reproducing the scenario (page opened while a nested subagent waits for permission, then the turn finishes) no longer blanks the transcript: no opacity-0 window on the transcript container at permission-wait or turn-finish.
- [ ] The fix addresses the `resetInitialRenderState` re-trigger (fresh-data transition / bootstrap scroll data change) rather than masking the symptom, and the measured hide durations drop to 0 ms in the issue's measurement setup.
- [ ] Existing MessageList behaviour (initial scroll, fresh-data transitions) still works — relevant existing tests pass.

title: feat(knowledge): auto-publish agent task plans to Project Knowledge with live progress tracking

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
### Context & Background
OpenChamber upstream PR #4582 / commit `e2a724d217` and commit `390dc4a0fe` introduced **Project Knowledge** and the `openchamber_knowledge` tool (`list`, `save`, `delete`, `show`). Project Knowledge includes Notes, Todos, and Plans.
Plans in Project Knowledge are stored as Markdown files with a `## Steps` checklist (e.g. `- [ ] Step 1`, `- [x] Step 2`). The server dynamically calculates completion progress (e.g. `2/4` or `Done`), displays it in the Project Context sidebar, and links sessions to plans ("Implement" and "Improve" actions).

In our fork (`developing-today`), agents use the `plan-tracking` and `routing-review` skills or the `/plan` command to decompose user requests into multi-step execution plans with token/cost estimates. However, these plans currently live only inside the chat message transcript or local scratch files.

### Feature Objective
Connect agent task planning in OpenCode/OpenChamber with Project Knowledge so that:
1. When an agent creates an implementation plan, it automatically (or via tool call) saves the plan directly into Project Knowledge via `openchamber_knowledge.save(kind: 'plan', title, content)`.
2. As the agent finishes each step in the session, it marks the checklist item `- [x] Step` in the saved plan file.
3. The Project Context sidebar automatically updates with live step progress (`1/5`, `2/5`, etc.) and links the working session to that plan.

---

### Specifications

#### 1. Plan Formatting Standard for Agents
Ensure the `plan-tracking` skill and `/plan` prompt enforce upstream's plan format:
- Must have a markdown title `# Plan Title`.
- Must contain a `## Steps` header followed by checkbox items:
  ```markdown
  # Feature X Implementation

  ## Overview
  Brief description...

  ## Steps
  - [ ] 1. Scaffold API routes and schema definitions
  - [ ] 2. Implement backend service and business logic
  - [ ] 3. Create frontend UI components
  - [ ] 4. Add unit and integration tests
  ```
- Note: Upstream's `project-knowledge.js` rejects or warns if a saved plan does not contain a `## Steps` section.

#### 2. Plan Creation & Linking
- When the agent produces a plan, call `openchamber_knowledge` (`action: 'save', kind: 'plan', title: '...', content: '...'`).
- The server writes the plan into the project's plan directory (e.g. `.openchamber/plans/<slug>.md`) and returns the file path.
- Link the current session ID to the newly created plan so that OpenChamber's UI displays the active working session button next to the plan row.

#### 3. Step Checkoff During Execution
- As each step is completed, the agent updates the markdown file (or calls `openchamber_knowledge.save` with updated markdown content) checking off the step (`- [x] Step 1`).
- The frontend Plans section (`packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/PlansSection.tsx`) polls every 10 seconds or responds to file watch events, displaying the updated step counter (`1/4`, `2/4`, `Done`).

#### 4. Fallback & Standalone OpenCode Compatibility
- When running in standalone OpenCode CLI/TUI (without OpenChamber UI server), fallback cleanly to local `.openchamber/plans/` or `.opencode/plans/` markdown files without failing.

---

### Key Files & References
- `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/project-knowledge.js`: `saveKnowledgeItem`, `countPlanSteps`, `OPENCHAMBER_KNOWLEDGE_ACTIONS`
- `packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/PlansSection.tsx`: Plans UI in Project Context sidebar, progress badge rendering, "Implement" / "Improve" button handlers
- `packages/ui/src/components/session/project-context/KnowledgeActions.tsx`: Action menus for knowledge rows
- OpenCode skills: `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/plan-tracking.md`, `routing-review.md`

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Running a planning command or triggering `plan-tracking` produces a plan registered in Project Knowledge.
2. The plan appears under the "Plans" tab in OpenChamber's Project Context sidebar with correct total step counts.
3. Ticking a step during agent execution updates the progress indicator in the sidebar.
4. The plan row displays the active session link allowing one-click navigation between the plan and the chat session.

title: Add durable OpenChamber cursors for local event frames

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: kind/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement

body:
## Context

The global stream currently gives the browser OpenCode event IDs as cursors. OpenChamber-generated or ID-less frames cannot be replayed by OpenCode. While the current process still has a local-frame marker, an unreplayable resume is reset and the client refetches. After an OpenChamber restart, that marker is gone; an old OpenCode cursor may still be accepted upstream, allowing the client to resume past a local frame it missed.

## Goal

Add a versioned OpenChamber cursor and durable replay state so local frames can be resumed across process restarts without silently skipping them. The cursor should carry or resolve to both the OpenChamber stream position and the OpenCode upstream cursor; it must not be mistaken for an OpenCode event ID.

## Acceptance criteria

- Persist the payload and ordering/position of non-reconstructible local frames, anchored to the upstream OpenCode cursor.
- Generate a stable, versioned cursor per stream and validate its stream/scope before replay.
- Commit replay state before sending a frame; make replay duplicate-safe for clients.
- Resume missed local frames after an OpenChamber process restart and continue from the correct OpenCode cursor.
- Bound retention. If the cursor is invalid, expired, or OpenCode cannot honor its cursor, send the existing replay-reset signal and refetch rather than skip data.
- Add tests for restart with missed local frames, retention expiry, invalid/upstream-resync cursors, and the OpenCode-only resume path.
- Document the practical delivery guarantee (replay with deduplication; do not claim exactly-once side effects).

Reconstructible state announcements may be re-emitted from their authoritative state instead of being stored as individual frames.

title: fix(web,vscode): npm-registry metadata caches never evict — the TTL is only checked on re-lookup of the same name, stale entries and their full version lists are retained for the life of the process

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
