body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#660 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): The managed-OpenCode password and OpenChamber agent-token indefinite reuse (reusePassword / reuseToken) is implemented in OpenChamber managed-OpenCode code, so credential-rotation support belongs with that source. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

---

Source: `docs/2026-10-19-reliability-review.md`, Open problems #2, and incident "Two credentials printed into the session".

## Finding
A read-only investigation printed the managed OpenCode server password and OpenChamber's agent tool token from `~/.config/openchamber/managed-opencode/state.json` into session history. OpenChamber reuses both across restarts on purpose (`ensureLocalOpenCodeServerPassword({ reusePassword })`, `createChildEnv({ reuseToken })`), so a restart does not rotate them.

## State on 2026-10-22
`openchamber.log` shows 17 `handoff (binary-changed)` and 1 `start (no-state)` launches. Every handoff reuses the saved password and token, so nothing so far proves rotation. (Values not read for this issue.)

## Fix
A `just` recipe that rotates both, following the steps in `docs/services.md`, and running it.

## Acceptance
- The state file's password and token differ from before; verified by comparing SHA-256 hashes, never printing values.
- OpenChamber and its OpenCode are up afterwards.


## Acceptance criteria

- A `just` recipe, following the rotation steps in `docs/services.md`, rotates BOTH the managed OpenCode server password and the OpenChamber agent tool token in the managed-opencode state file — and it has been run.
- Rotation is verified by comparing SHA-256 hashes of the state file's values before and after; the values themselves are never printed or logged.
- OpenChamber and its managed OpenCode are up and healthy after the rotation.

title: fix(ui): getWebServerSessionActivity still returns the pre-v1 bare-map type after PR #620's envelope change

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/ui
labels.description: Package: ui (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

PR #620 changed `GET /api/session-activity` from the bare phase map `{ [sessionId]: { type } }` to the session-activity v1 envelope `{ version: 1, serverTime, watcherReady, sessions }`. The VS Code webview consumer was migrated to the envelope (PR #637, `SessionActivityV1Snapshot`), but the shared UI client was not: `getWebServerSessionActivity()` in `packages/ui/src/lib/opencode/client.ts` still declares `Promise<Record<string, { type: string }> | null>` and returns the raw response body cast to that type.

Any caller of that method now receives the envelope object where a session map is promised: its top-level keys are `version` (a number), `serverTime` (a number), `watcherReady` (a boolean) and `sessions` — none of them a `{ type }` entry — so iterating the result as a session map yields garbage "sessions" and silently misses every real one. The method currently has no in-repo caller (verified by `git grep` on current main), so this is a latent break in a public client method, not a live UI outage — but the type signature actively lies about the wire format, and the first future caller (the method exists for visibility-restore recovery, per its doc comment) will ship the bug.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/620 (merge commit `96d525e13294f3f9dfcec737879e2464e1def335`, source commit `909d0306`)
- Current main `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/session-runtime.js:383-403` — `getSessionActivitySnapshot()` returns `{ version: 1, serverTime, watcherReady, sessions }`.
- Current main `packages/ui/src/lib/opencode/client.ts:1683` — `getWebServerSessionActivity(): Promise<Record<string, { type: string }> | null>` returns `data as Record<string, { type: string }>` with no envelope unwrapping or validation.
- Current main `packages/vscode/webview/main.tsx:515,575-589` — the migrated consumer types the same endpoint as `SessionActivityV1Snapshot` and reads `.sessions`, showing the intended client-side shape.
- `git grep getWebServerSessionActivity origin/main` returns only the definition — no caller exercises the stale contract today.

Verified against current `origin/main` (`6b7e8155994ec9b5db148782cf430b5c65d32ef0`) at review time; deduped against open + closed issues (searches for "session-activity client envelope" and "getWebServerSessionActivity" return only #524 and #614, the feature/design issues — neither covers the stale UI client method).

## Why it matters

The observability contract v1 (design #612) was adopted precisely so consumers stop guessing the payload shape. Leaving one in-repo consumer typed against the pre-v1 shape reintroduces exactly that guesswork, in the package every UI surface shares. Fixing it now is cheap; discovering it after a caller is wired to it costs a debugging round-trip through a silent data-shape failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- `getWebServerSessionActivity()` (or its replacement) parses the v1 envelope: it validates the shape, returns the per-session entries from `sessions` (each keeping at least `{ type }`), and returns null on a malformed payload instead of casting blindly — OR the method is removed entirely if the maintainers confirm it is dead, with no dangling references.
- The return type matches the wire contract (envelope-aware), consistent with the VS Code webview's `SessionActivityV1Snapshot` handling.
- A test pins the behaviour against an envelope-shaped payload (a session entry is returned keyed by session id; `version`/`serverTime`/`watcherReady` are never surfaced as session entries).

body:
## Problem

The Open Design quota provider exists in this repo but is not live on the running laptop instance, so every fleet quota picture silently omits the provider that sits inside almost every route pool.

Verified 2026-10-27 ~03:11 CDT against the laptop's running OpenChamber (`localhost:3000`):

- `GET /api/quota/providers` → claude, cline-pass, codex, deepseek, google, antigravity, openrouter, github-copilot, github-copilot-addon, opencode-go. **No opendesign.**

## What already exists (do not rebuild)

body:
## What I want

Connect a Linear workspace with a personal API key that stays in 1Password, the same way GitHub and GitLab accounts already can (#176): Settings stores a reference such as `op://Vertex SRE/linear_api_key`, and OpenChamber reads the key with `op read` when it calls Linear. The key is never written to OpenChamber's files.

## What exists today

- **Linear signs in through OAuth only.** `linear/auth.js` stores `accessToken`, `refreshToken` and expiry per workspace, and `linear/oauth.js` refreshes them. There's no way to enter an API key.
- **The client always sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`** (`linear/client.js:106`). Linear's personal API keys go in the header without `Bearer` (`Authorization: <key>`), so a personal key fails as written today.
- **GitHub and GitLab already support vault references** (#176): a `pat` credential holds `tokenReference` instead of a token; `withVaultToken` reads it through the shared resolver (`environment/vault.js`: `op read --no-newline`, memory only, five-minute cache). A refused read never marks the account invalid.

## Proposal

1. **Credential kind.** A Linear workspace credential of kind `apiKey` with `tokenReference` (`op://…`). No refresh token, no expiry.
2. **Client.** For `apiKey` credentials, send `Authorization: <key>` without `Bearer`. OAuth credentials keep `Bearer`.
3. **Identity.** On add, read the key once and run the viewer query, so the workspace gets its id, name and user like an OAuth sign-in. A failed read or query is reported and nothing is saved.
4. **Route.** `POST /api/linear/auth/vault` with `{ tokenReference }`, beside the OAuth routes, mirroring GitHub's `/auth/vault`.
5. **Settings.** In Settings → Linear, next to "Sign in with Linear": "Use an API key from 1Password", a field for the `op://` reference, and the result of the test read. This is new UI, so the wording and placement are a product decision.
6. **Agent actions.** `linear.status` shows the source (`oauth` or `vault`) and never the key. Adding a vault credential stays user-only, like every sign-in (#169).
7. **Enterprise mode.** Unchanged: Linear is a service the user connected, outside the mode today.

## Open questions

- Whether an API-key workspace and an OAuth workspace for the same Linear organization can coexist, or one replaces the other.
- Whether the key's scopes are checked on add (a read-only key can list issues but cannot update them or post the session comment).

Tracked in #152.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Linear workspace credential of kind `apiKey` can be added holding a `tokenReference` (`op://…`); the key itself is never written to OpenChamber's files.
- [ ] For `apiKey` credentials the Linear client sends `Authorization: <key>` without `Bearer`; OAuth credentials keep sending `Bearer`.
- [ ] Adding a vault credential reads the key once and runs the viewer query so the workspace gets its id, name and user; a failed read or query is reported and nothing is saved.
- [ ] `POST /api/linear/auth/vault` accepts `{ tokenReference }` beside the OAuth routes, mirroring GitHub's `/auth/vault`.
- [ ] Settings → Linear offers "Use an API key from 1Password" beside "Sign in with Linear", with the reference field and the result of the test read.
- [ ] `linear.status` shows the credential source (`oauth` or `vault`) and never the key; adding a vault credential stays user-only (#169).

The desktop and web sidebar now has a layout the display menu arranges (#20): attention sections (Approvals, Questions, Errors, Stopped, and the merged Blocked / Needs attention / Pending), movable sections, the open session holding its place until another one opens, what happens after Done or Archive, and the List view options (Chats with the projects under one heading, no project groups, one line per session).

The phone sessions sheet (`packages/ui/src/apps/MobileSessionsSheet.tsx`) is a separate renderer and still shows the classic sections, so on hosted mobile and Capacitor none of this exists yet.

What the phone needs:

- The attention sections, fed by the same live states (`components/session/sidebar/zones/useSidebarLiveStates.ts`) and partition (`zones/sidebarZones.ts`), so a session waiting on an approval or a question shows up the same way on the phone as on the desktop.

- The open session hold and the After Done or Archive choice. On the phone the session list is a sheet that closes when a session opens, so "keep the row until I switch" may need a different meaning there; decide that first.

Today the sheet shows the classic sidebar on purpose, so nothing is broken; this is the parity work that was left out of the first change.

## Acceptance criteria

- The phone sessions sheet (`MobileSessionsSheet.tsx`) shows the attention sections (Approvals, Questions, Errors, Stopped, Blocked/Needs attention/Pending) fed by the same live-states hook and zone partition as the desktop sidebar.
- Section order on the phone comes from the same `sidebarLayout` value (per-surface-kind), with a touch-friendly reorder control.
- The open-session hold and After Done/Archive behaviors have a defined phone meaning (the sheet closes on open) and behave that way.
- The List view options that the desktop timeline supports are mirrored on the phone where the sheet's timeline corresponds.

title: fix(vscode): bridge api:proxy and api:session:message forwards buffer the whole upstream body with no byte cap — deadline-only, while the web twin caps at 16 MiB (#776)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/vscode
labels.description: Package: vscode (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Bug

The VS Code bridge's general API proxy buffers every upstream response body whole, with no byte cap — only the 45-second deadline bounds it, and a deadline bounds time, not bytes:

- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-proxy-runtime.ts:164` `performApiProxyFetch` — the single fetch helper behind the `api:proxy` bridge message (GET at `:414`, other methods at `:431`):
  - `:176` text/JSON branch: `bodyText: await response.text()`
  - `:178` binary branch: `const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer();` then base64 (+33% on top of the whole buffer)
- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-proxy-runtime.ts:499` / `:509` — the `api:session:message` forward (POST `/api/session/:id/prompt`) duplicates the same two unbounded reads inline instead of using the helper.
- The only bound is `API_PROXY_DEADLINE_MS = 45_000` (`:88`), and the comment at `:85-90` says the deadline signal "also bounds the body read in performApiProxyFetch" — it bounds how *long* the read may take. The upstream is a loopback or LAN OpenCode server: it can deliver hundreds of megabytes well inside 45 seconds.

The coalesced-GET path (`READ_COALESCE`, `:414`) additionally holds the one buffered body for every concurrent caller of the same read.

## Precedent in the same package / same system

This is the remaining whole-body read of its class:

- Web twin: closed #776 — the web session-list proxy was time-bound only; its fix landed `SESSION_LIST_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 16 MiB` with a during-read bounded reader (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/proxy.js:45`, `:981`).
- Same bridge, sibling modules already read bounded: `bridge-system-runtime.ts:33` (`readBoundedResponseText`, `UPDATE_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 1 MiB`, `:26`), `bridge-fs-helpers-runtime.ts:538` (models.dev catalog, 16 MiB), `opencodeConfig.ts` / `opencode-upgrade-runtime.ts` import the web shared `readBoundedResponseText` from `packages/web/server/lib/shared/response-body.js`.
- Closed #788 gave this same proxy its deadline; the size half of the bound never followed. Closed #1027 / #1068 capped the bridge's fs proxy/read paths (16 MiB) — `api:proxy` and `api:session:message` are the un-capped remainder.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `26e569d97`)

Probe (laptop, bun, real `handleProxyBridgeMessage` imported from the laptop clone at main `26e569d97`; fetch stubbed to a `Response` carrying one 64 MiB JSON body — 67,108,875 bytes — delivered immediately, i.e. well inside the deadline; probe dir: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-bridge-proxy-cap-20261101/` on the laptop):

```
api:proxy GET            status 200, bodyText chars: 67,108,875 (whole body)
api:session:message      status 200, bodyText chars: 67,108,875 (whole body, POST /api/session/abc/prompt)
api:proxy GET (binary)   status 200, bodyBase64 chars: 89,478,488 (= whole 64 MiB, base64)
RSS delta with the bodies held: +154 MiB
```

No size judgement exists anywhere in the path: no `content-length` check, no streaming cap, no post-read length check — the first moment the size is known is after the whole body (and, for binary, its base64 copy) is already in extension-host memory.

## Why it matters

Every OpenCode API call the VS Code webview UI makes flows through this proxy, including session and message pages — legitimately the largest payloads in the system, and exactly the shape #776 capped on the web side. A corrupted, compromised, or simply enormous upstream answer (a very large session page is a real shape, not an adversarial invention) is buffered whole — twice for binary (buffer + base64 string) — per request in the extension host, whose memory pressure destabilises the whole editor. The cap is a memory guard, not a product limit: it should sit generously above a legitimate large page, the way the web twin's 16 MiB does.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both branches of `performApiProxyFetch` (text and binary) and the inline reads in the `api:session:message` forward read the upstream body bounded **during the read** by a named cap (e.g. a `PROXY_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` in `bridge-proxy-runtime.ts`, reusing the `readBoundedResponseText`-style streaming reader the sibling bridge modules already carry), sized generously above a legitimate large session/message page — triage pins the exact value against the web twin's 16 MiB precedent.
- [ ] An over-cap upstream answer fails that bridge request with a clear proxy error payload (502-style, like the existing fetch-failure shape at `:182-189`) and cancels the upstream body; the webview is never handed a silently truncated body as if complete, and no whole over-cap buffer (or its base64 copy) is materialised.
- [ ] In-cap behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged: text vs binary branch selection, header collection, read coalescing, the owned-session overlay, and the session:message timeout/abort behaviour.
- [ ] Tests in `bridge-proxy-runtime.test.ts` style pin: over-cap text body rejected without full buffering, over-cap binary body rejected, an exactly-at-cap body succeeds unchanged, and the existing proxy/coalescing/abort tests pass.

Found by: new-issue-creator-openchamber, 2026-11-01 run. Deduped against open + closed issues: #788 (deadline only, closed), #776 (web twin, closed), #1027 / #1068 (bridge fs paths, closed) — no issue covers a byte cap for the `api:proxy` / `api:session:message` response bodies.

title: fix(web): plan size cap is bypassed by unsharePlan, updatePlan's expectedRaw check, and legacy migration — all read plan files whole in the module #1133 capped

labels.name: source/creator

body:
## Bug

The project-plan size cap landed for #1133 — `PLAN_FILE_READ_MAX_BYTES = 1 MiB` in `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/plan-progress.js:24`, enforced in `readPlanFile` (`runtime.js:747-767`: stat judged up front, bounded read, 413 on over-cap) and in the listing (`tooLarge` flag, file never read) — is bypassed by three sibling operations in the **same module** (`packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js`) that still read plan files whole with no stat judgement and no bounded read:

- `unsharePlan` (`runtime.js:1077`) — `raw = await fsPromises.readFile(from, 'utf8')` on the shared plan file, used only to derive the title via `parsePlanMarkdown(raw).title` before the file is moved into the user's own plans. Reachable over HTTP: `POST /api/project-context/:projectId/plans/:planId/unshare` (`routes.js:296`). A shared plan the listing marks `tooLarge` and `readPlan` refuses with 413 can still be unshared — buffering the entire file to read its first line.
- `updatePlan`'s conflict check (`runtime.js:827-833`, `checkExpectedRaw`) — `await fsPromises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8') !== expectedRaw.data` reads the whole current plan file (shared or personal) whenever an `expectedRaw` is supplied. That is a live path: the OpenChamber control surface passes it through at `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/project-knowledge.js:170`.
- Legacy migration (`runtime.js:374` / `:379`, `migrateFromLegacyConfig`) — reads a legacy-referenced plan file whole (`targetPath`, falling back to the recorded absolute path) and copies it into the plans directory, again with no size judgement. (Code-read evidence; the two HTTP-reachable legs above are probe-verified.)

The shared plans folder is a team folder (`resolveSharedPlansDir` — e.g. a repo's `docs/plans`), so the over-cap file does not need to come from OpenChamber's own writer (which clamps plan bodies at `PROJECT_PLAN_BODY_MAX_LENGTH = 200_000` chars, `runtime.js:29`): any large markdown a teammate, sync tool, or editor places there is enough.

## Evidence (verified on main `aa631af77`)

Probe (laptop, real `createProjectContextRuntime` from main `aa631af77`, counting `fsPromises` wrapper in the style of the existing `runtime.test.js` over-cap tests; probe dir: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-plan-residual-caps-20261101/` on the laptop). One shared plan file of 67,108,900 bytes (64 MiB, ~64× the cap):

```
capBytes: 1048576, fileBytes: 67108864
control readPlan:        413 "Plan file is too large to read (67108900 bytes; limit is 1048576 bytes)", bigReadCalls: 0, bigBytesRead: 0
unsharePlan:             succeeded (title "Big Plan", file moved), bigReadCalls: 1, bigBytesRead: 67108900, RSS +67 MB
updatePlan+expectedRaw:  409 "Plan changed; reload before saving" — but only after bigReadCalls: 1, bigBytesRead: 67108900
```

So the cap's guarantee — an over-cap plan is never buffered whole — holds only for the read path. The move and save-conflict paths buffer it anyway.

## Why it matters

The 1 MiB cap exists so a stray large file in a shared plans folder cannot blow up server memory or stall the event loop on a routine context operation. Unsharing a plan and saving one with a conflict check are exactly routine operations — a user cleaning up the very over-cap file the UI flags as `tooLarge` triggers the unbounded read the cap was meant to prevent. The fix should make the cap a property of the module, not of one function.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `unsharePlan` on a plan file over `PLAN_FILE_READ_MAX_BYTES` does not buffer the whole file: it either refuses with the same too-large error `readPlan` raises (413 / `mutationError`), or derives the title from a bounded prefix read and still completes the move — peak memory bounded by ~the cap either way. The chosen behaviour is covered by a test.
- [ ] `updatePlan`'s `expectedRaw` conflict check does not read a file over the cap whole: an over-cap current file is refused (or compared via a bounded/streaming comparison) without a whole-file buffer; at-cap and under-cap conflict behaviour (match saves, mismatch 409) is unchanged.
- [ ] The legacy-migration plan copy (`migrateFromLegacyConfig`) judges the referenced file's size before reading it whole; an over-cap legacy plan is not buffered (skip the link, or copy by stream) and the migration still completes for the remaining items.
- [ ] Regression tests in `runtime.test.js` style (counting `fsPromises`): over-cap shared plan — `unsharePlan` performs no whole-file read of it; `updatePlan` with `expectedRaw` performs no whole-file read of it; normal-size share/unshare/update flows unchanged.
- [ ] No change to `readPlan`/listing behaviour or to the 1 MiB cap value.

Found by: new-issue-creator-openchamber, 2026-11-01 run. Deduped against open + recently closed issues: this is the residual surface of closed #1133 (its fix capped `readPlan` + listing in this same module; the three operations above were not in its scope and remain uncapped on current main).

title: fix(ui): guest binary file editor buffers the whole file before its 20 MB cap is judged — loadCanvasBytes arrayBuffers uncapped /api/fs/raw and the mount gate is null-permissive

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Bug

A guest extension's **binary** file editor loads the file's bytes through a path where the 20 MB editor cap (`GUEST_FILE_EDITOR_CONTENT_MAX = 20_000_000`, `packages/sdk/src/file-editor.ts:21`) is only checked **after** the whole file has been downloaded and buffered in the renderer — and the mount gate that is supposed to spare the read is permissive while the file's size is still unknown.

## Evidence (verified on main `aa631af77`)

- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx:4890-4904` — `loadCanvasBytes` fetches `/api/fs/raw` and returns `new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer())`. No `Content-Length` check, no streaming cap: whatever the server sends is buffered whole before anyone judges its size.
- `/api/fs/raw` is uncapped **by design** — `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js` (raw handler, ~:1360-1460) streams any file with range support for media playback; the size caps live on the sibling routes (`MAX_READ_BYTES = 16 MiB` at `routes.js:221` for `/api/fs/read`, `MAX_SERVE_BYTES = 100 MiB` at `routes.js:214` for preview). So the raw response itself will happily deliver hundreds of megabytes to `arrayBuffer()`.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/files/GuestFileEditor.tsx:71-79` — the editor's own guard `bytes.byteLength > GUEST_FILE_EDITOR_CONTENT_MAX` runs only **after** `loadBytes()` resolves, i.e. after the full buffering it was meant to prevent. Its doc comment says "the editor never loads" for an over-cap file; in fact it always loads, then refuses.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx:2863-2864` — the mount gate meant to spare the read, `canMountCanvas`, is `artifactSize === null || artifactSize <= GUEST_FILE_EDITOR_CONTENT_MAX`. `artifactSize` starts as `null` on every selection (`:3023`, `setArtifactSize(null)`) and is filled asynchronously by a separate stat effect (`:3020-3034`); nothing awaits that stat before `GuestFileEditor` mounts and its effect fires `loadBytes()`. If the stat is slow, fails (the effect swallows errors, `:3030` `.catch(() => {})`), or `files.statFile` is unavailable on the host (`readFileStat` returns `null`, `:1845-1857`), the gate never engages at all.

### Probe (laptop, real `registerFsRoutes` from main `aa631af77`, express + real fs)

Probe dir: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-canvas-raw-cap-20261101/` (laptop)

```
READ status: 413 {"error":"File too large to read"}        // /api/fs/read, same 64 MiB file
RAW status: 200 content-length: 67108864                   // /api/fs/raw
RAW arrayBuffer byteLength: 67108864 overEditorCap: true rssDeltaMB: 221
```

A 64 MiB file — over 3× the editor cap — is delivered whole by the exact endpoint + `arrayBuffer()` call `loadCanvasBytes` uses, growing the process by ~221 MB before the post-read check in `GuestFileEditor` can fire.

## Why it matters

Opening a large binary file (disk image, recording, archive, database) that a guest binary editor claims can freeze or OOM the renderer/web tab, even though every layer involved believes the 20 MB cap protects it: the server route is uncapped on purpose, the mount gate is null-permissive and racy, and the final check is post-buffering. The cap needs to be judged **before** the bytes move — from the stat the view already fetches, and/or the `Content-Length` the raw response already carries — and the read needs a streaming bound so an unknown or lying size cannot buffer whole.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `loadCanvasBytes` (or its caller) refuses a file over `GUEST_FILE_EDITOR_CONTENT_MAX` **before** buffering it: e.g. judge the `/api/fs/raw` response's `Content-Length` up front and/or read the body with a streaming cap that aborts past the limit, so peak renderer memory stays bounded by ~the cap regardless of file size.
- [ ] The binary canvas does not mount (and `loadBytes` is never called) while the selected file's size is unknown-and-unjudged: `canMountCanvas` no longer treats `artifactSize === null` as mountable for binary editors, or mount waits for the stat the view already performs; a failed/unavailable stat falls back to the pre-read `Content-Length`/streaming judgement above, not to an unbounded read.
- [ ] The over-cap outcome stays the existing user-visible one (`onTooLarge` → the file-editor too-large message), now reached without downloading the file.
- [ ] Regression tests: a binary-editor load for a file whose raw response declares (and/or streams) more than `GUEST_FILE_EDITOR_CONTENT_MAX` bytes rejects as too-large with bounded bytes consumed; an at-cap file still loads byte-identically; the text-editor canvas path is unchanged.
- [ ] `/api/fs/raw` itself keeps streaming uncapped for media/range playback — the fix belongs on the editor load path, not the shared route.

Found by: new-issue-creator-openchamber, 2026-11-01 run. Deduped against open + recently closed issues (closest: #1026/#1027 capped the server `/api/fs/read` and the vscode bridge raw path; neither covers the UI binary-editor load path or its mount gate).

title: fix(web): walkthrough pull-request diff read has no byte cap — GitHub diff response returned whole while the sibling file reader caps at 5 MiB

body:
## Problem

The walkthrough pull-request diff read has no size bound at all, while every sibling read in the same module is capped.

`packages/web/server/lib/walkthrough/pull-request.js`:

- `readGitHubPullRequestDiff` (:106-118) requests the PR diff via octokit with `accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff` and returns `response.data` as the patch string after only a prefix assertion (:116). No byte check, no limit constant, no error path for an oversized diff.
- The sibling full-file reader in the same file caps at `MAX_FULL_FILE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024` (:123) and throws `413 file-too-large` when a single file exceeds it (:162-164). The GitLab twin (`packages/web/server/lib/gitlab/resources.js` `changeRequestFileContents`) enforces the same 5 MiB / 413 contract, and its patch path is at least item-bounded by `readCollection` (2,000-item ceiling). The GitHub patch path has neither a byte bound nor an item bound.
- The local-diff machinery the walkthrough also uses is byte-capped (`MAX_FILE_DIFF_WORKING_TREE_BYTES = 50 MiB`, `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:3971`).

## Verified evidence (main `0d3f15d95`, 2026-11-01)

Laptop probe against the real module (dependency-injected octokit, the module's own test seam — probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-pr-diff-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`; module file byte-identical between the laptop clone and sandbox main, md5 `94b89c65b3b002869c27e03fdc3a9c9d`):

- Fixture diff of 67,240,009 bytes → `getPullRequestDiff` returned `patch` of 67,240,009 bytes, no error.
- Same probe, sibling reader: a 6 MiB file → `getPullRequestFileContents` rejected with `413 file-too-large`.

## Why it matters

The patch is not consumed once: `GET /api/walkthrough/pr-diff` (`packages/web/server/lib/walkthrough/routes.js:100-118`) sends the whole string to the client, and walkthrough generation parses and prompts over it. The module explicitly supports reading fork PRs (network check in `resolvePullRequestRepo`), so the diff size is controlled by whoever authored the PR under review — a vendored-dependency rewrite or generated-file churn produces a multi-hundred-MB diff that the server buffers whole, re-serializes to the browser, and feeds to hunk parsing. One oversized PR under review can OOM the managed server that every session depends on. This is the same unbounded-read class as #802/#1254, in the one walkthrough read those designs did not name.

## Acceptance criteria

- `readGitHubPullRequestDiff` enforces a named byte cap on the returned patch (a generous multiple of `MAX_FULL_FILE_BYTES` is fine — legitimate PR diffs are far smaller than the failure mode), rejecting over-cap diffs with a coded error consistent with the module's existing shape (`statusCode` + `code`, mirroring `file-too-large`).
- The GitLab `changeRequestPatch` join (`packages/web/server/lib/gitlab/resources.js`) gets the same total-byte bound on the assembled patch, not only the per-item collection bound.
- Tests in `pull-request.test.js` (and the GitLab resources tests): at-cap diff returned byte-identically; over-cap diff rejected with the coded error; empty-diff behaviour (`allowEmpty`) unchanged.
- No change to the network/account authority checks in `resolvePullRequestRepo`.

title: fix(web): generated agent-tool plugin buffers the callback response whole with no byte cap — response.text() in the OpenCode-side tool source, and no deadline for non-answer actions

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## Problem

The generated OpenChamber agent-tool plugin (the code OpenChamber writes into a session so OpenCode can call back into OpenChamber) reads the callback response with **no byte cap and, for non-answer actions, no deadline of its own** — `await response.text()` buffers the whole body in the OpenCode process before it is parsed or validated.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `506365c5c`)

`packages/web/server/lib/agent-tool/runtime.js`, in the generated tool source (`createToolEntry`):

- `:512-513` — endpoint/token come from `OPENCHAMBER_AGENT_TOOL_URL` / `OPENCHAMBER_AGENT_TOOL_TOKEN` (the callback address is built at `:745` as `http://<callbackHost>:<port>/api/openchamber/agent-tool`).
- `:526-538` — the `fetch` signal is `context.signal` (session abort) for ordinary actions; only the render `awaitAnswer` variant composes a wait signal (`ANSWER_WAIT_SETUP`, `:348ff`) and lifts Bun's idle timeout for the wait (`ANSWER_FETCH_TIMEOUT`, `:368ff`). Ordinary actions get no fetch deadline beyond Bun's ~6-minute no-response idle timeout noted in that same comment.
- `:539` — `const content = await response.text()` — the entire response is buffered whole, then `JSON.parse`d and shape-checked (`:540-542`). There is no `Content-Length` pre-check, no streamed bounded read, and no named cap anywhere in the generated source.

Dedup checked this run: open + closed search for the agent-tool response read returns #965 (action-name prototype resolution, fixed), #727/#35 (token rotation / plugin packaging) — nothing covers the response body read. The analogous daemon-client gap was filed and fixed as #774 (mcpx daemon client: no timeout, no response cap).

## Why it matters

This plugin runs inside every managed OpenCode session. A wedged or misbehaving action handler that streams a body without ending it — or simply returns a pathological result — grows memory inside OpenCode for as long as the stream lasts, and the only stop is the user aborting the whole session. Every other OpenChamber-owned client surface that reads a body from a peer process has been given the deadline + bounded-reader treatment (#774, #802 primitives, #845 error-detail reads); the generated plugin is the one caller that still reads raw.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The generated plugin reads the callback response through a bounded read with one named cap constant (sized generously above the largest legitimate action result, e.g. render/knowledge payloads — the cap is a memory guard, not a product limit), refusing an over-cap body during the read rather than after full buffering.
- [ ] Over-cap and endless-body cases resolve to the existing failure envelope (`OpenChamber returned an invalid response`, `ok: false`) — no throw escaping the tool, no partial content returned.
- [ ] Ordinary (non-answer) actions gain a fetch deadline consistent with the codebase's other callback clients, or the issue's fix explicitly documents why session-abort + Bun's idle timeout is the intended bound for them; the `awaitAnswer` wait behaviour (no deadline while waiting, chat-message abort) is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in the agent-tool runtime's existing test home: streamed over-cap response → failure envelope without full consumption; at-cap valid envelope → returned byte-identically; stalled body on an ordinary action terminates at the deadline if one is added.

body:
## Problem

Two UI fetches of public-internet catalogs have a deadline but **no byte cap** — the body is buffered and parsed whole via `response.json()`, so a bloated, compromised, or fast-streaming oversize answer is fully allocated in the renderer before any check can run. The deadline only stops a *stall*; it does nothing about a large body delivered quickly inside the timeout window.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `506365c5c`)

1. **models.dev metadata, direct fallback** — `packages/ui/src/stores/useConfigStore.ts`:
   - `:45-46` — sources are the server proxy `/api/openchamber/models-metadata` and the direct public URL `https://models.dev/api.json`.
   - `:736` — `fetchModelsDevMetadata` tries the proxy first, then the direct URL.
   - `:739-740` — an `AbortController` gives an 8 s deadline.
   - `:766` — `const data = await response.json();` — no byte cap, no `Content-Length` check, no bounded reader.
   - The server side of the *same catalog* is capped: `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/models-metadata.js:10` `MODELS_DEV_CATALOG_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024`, read through `readBoundedResponseText` at `:27` (#1006). The UI's direct fallback bypasses that cap entirely — exactly when the proxy has failed and the client is on the less-trusted path.
2. **Gitmoji catalog** — `packages/ui/src/hooks/useGitmojiList.ts`:
   - `:21-23` — `GITMOJI_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`, source is a public `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL.
   - `:81-87` — `fetch(..., { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...) })` then `await response.json()` — deadline from #851, still no byte cap.

Dedup checked this run: open + closed search for the UI models.dev / gitmoji byte-cap gap returns only #851 (deadline-only fix for gitmoji), #1006 (server-side reads), and #931 (Mermaid remote source, a different loader that already has a cap). No issue covers these two UI reads.

## Why it matters

The renderer is the long-lived UI process on every surface (web, desktop webview, VS Code webview, mobile). An oversize catalog answer — upstream incident, hostile mirror, or a captive-portal/proxy injecting a huge body — costs unbounded memory in that process during a routine background refresh, with no error surfaced except an OOM/freeze. The server already decided this catalog is worth a 16 MiB cap; the client fallback should not silently un-decide it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both reads go through a bounded body read with a named cap constant per catalog (models.dev mirroring the server's 16 MiB `MODELS_DEV_CATALOG_MAX_BYTES`; gitmoji a named cap sized generously above the real catalog), and an over-cap body is refused *during* the read, not after full buffering.
- [ ] Over-cap behaves like today's fetch failure: models.dev falls through to the next source / empty map with the existing warning; gitmoji falls back to the cached/empty list with the existing warning. No new user-facing error surface.
- [ ] Regression tests: a streamed over-cap body is rejected without being consumed whole; an at-cap (or representative real-size) body parses and returns the same result as today for both loaders.
- [ ] The existing deadlines (8 s / 10 s) and the proxy-first source order are unchanged.

title: fix(electron): Linux .desktop entry files are read whole with no size cap — readLinuxDesktopEntries buffers every scanned entry file in the main process (icon sibling filed as #1257)

body:
## Summary

The Electron shell's Linux installed-app discovery reads every `.desktop` entry file **whole, with no size cap**, in the main process. `readLinuxDesktopEntries` scans the XDG applications directories — including the user-writable `~/.local/share/applications` — and buffers each `.desktop` file entire before parsing the handful of keys it needs. A real desktop entry is a few hundred bytes to a few KiB; nothing in the read enforces that, so one bloated or hostile `.desktop` file (a broken installer, a renamed text file, a log dropped with a `.desktop` suffix) is loaded into the main process entire on every installed-apps refresh. This is the entry-file sibling of #1257, which capped nothing yet but covers the **icon** files these entries point at; the entry files themselves were missed.

## Evidence (verified on main `81d7fff6e`)

- `packages/electron/linux-app-discovery.mjs:135` — inside `readLinuxDesktopEntries` (:127-145): `parseDesktopEntry(await fsp.readFile(filePath, 'utf8'), filePath)` — no `stat`, no size check, for every `.desktop` file `collectDesktopFiles` (:108-125) recurses into under the scanned dirs.
- `packages/electron/linux-app-discovery.mjs:54-67` — `linuxApplicationDirs` scans `~/.local/share/applications` (XDG data home) plus every `XDG_DATA_DIRS` applications dir, `/usr/local/share/applications`, `/usr/share/applications`: the first is user-writable, the rest are package/tooling-writable.
- Reachable in the main process: `packages/electron/main.mjs:3852` — `getLinuxDesktopEntries()` calls `readLinuxDesktopEntries()` (cached only for a TTL, so the scan re-runs), feeding `buildLinuxInstalledApps` (`linux-app-discovery.mjs:286`, `:505`).
- Same shape, second module: `packages/electron/linux-desktop-entry.mjs:64-72` — `readFileOrNull` is a bare `fsp.readFile(filePath)`; its `findForeignEntry` caller (:87) reads **every** `.desktop` file in the user's applications directory whole during the AppImage desktop-entry reconcile (`main.mjs:104` imports `reconcileAppImageDesktopEntry`). (Its other callers read OpenChamber's own entry/icon, which are own-file reads.)
- Contrast in the same module: the icon read these entries feed was filed as #1257 precisely because it buffers an uncontrolled file whole; the favicon sibling was capped at 512 KiB in #817. The parser here needs only the `[Desktop Entry]` keys (`parseDesktopValues`, :69-87) — the first entries in the file.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (module copied byte-identical from main `81d7fff6e`, md5 `a101269ea7a5f93361f38bf6445c3eac`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-desktop-entry-read-20261101/probe.mjs`, node): a temp applications dir holding one normal entry plus a 67,108,935-byte `.desktop` file (valid header, `Name=Huge App`, one 64 MiB `Comment=` value) passed to the real `readLinuxDesktopEntries({ applicationDirs: [dir] })` — returned **both** entries parsed (`Huge App`, `Small App`) with process RSS **+70 MB**. There is no size at which this read refuses or skips.

## Why it matters

Installed-app discovery runs in the Electron main process — the process whose event loop drives every window — and it re-runs on a cache TTL, not just at startup. One oversized `.desktop` file in any scanned directory turns each refresh into a multi-hundred-megabyte string allocation (the read, the line split in `parseDesktopValues`, and the retained value strings), stalling the desktop app and risking an OOM of the main process. Desktop entries are metadata stubs; nothing legitimate needs more than a small fraction of a megabyte, which is why the sibling icon/favicon reads cap at 512 KiB–1 MiB.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readLinuxDesktopEntries` (`linux-app-discovery.mjs`) skips a `.desktop` file over an explicit named byte cap (suggest 512 KiB–1 MiB, in line with `MAX_FAVICON_BYTES` / the #1257 icon cap) **before** buffering it — judged from stat/handle, not after a whole read; at/under-cap entries parse byte-identically to today, and an over-cap entry simply does not appear (matching the existing unreadable-file behaviour at :141-142, which already skips per-file failures).
- [ ] `findForeignEntry`'s per-file read in `linux-desktop-entry.mjs` gets the same cap (over-cap file treated as no match), or a code comment records why that directory's files are exempt.
- [ ] Regression coverage (the electron unit/smoke path covering `linux-app-discovery.mjs`, e.g. `linux-app-discovery.test.mjs`) pins: over-cap `.desktop` file → skipped, other entries in the same directory still returned; at-cap entry → parsed normally; malformed/missing behaviour unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `linux-app-discovery`, `desktop entry read size`, `readLinuxDesktopEntries`: #1257 (open) covers the **icon** files (`iconFileToDataUrl`, `imageFileToDataUrl`) only — its acceptance criteria do not touch the entry-file scan read; #817 (closed) bounded the remote favicon fetch; #137 (closed) wired the linux-desktop smoke scripts into CI; #833 (closed) added spawnSync timeouts in this package. No issue covers the `.desktop` entry-file reads in `linux-app-discovery.mjs` or `linux-desktop-entry.mjs`.

body:
## Summary

The Electron shell's installed-app icon reads buffer the icon file **whole, synchronously, with no size cap**, in the main process. On Linux the icon path comes from a scanned `.desktop` file's `Icon=` entry — which may be an **absolute path to any file on disk** — so any `.desktop` file in a scanned applications directory (including the user-writable `~/.local/share/applications`) can name an arbitrarily large `.png`, and one `desktop_fetch_app_icons` IPC call reads it entire, base64-inflates it by ~4/3, and ships it to the renderer. The Windows terminal-icon helper in `main.mjs` has the same uncapped shape. The sibling favicon path was already bounded for exactly this reason (#817: 512 KiB cap, refused before buffering); the local-file icon reads were missed.

## Evidence (verified on main `013a7d48c`)

- `packages/electron/linux-app-discovery.mjs:463-469` — `iconFileToDataUrl` is `` `data:image/png;base64,${fs.readFileSync(filePath).toString('base64')}` ``: no `stat`, no size check, sync read in the Electron main process. Its only gate is the `.png` extension test.
- `packages/electron/linux-app-discovery.mjs:389-393` — `resolveLinuxIconFile` returns an absolute `Icon=` path verbatim when it exists (`if (path.isAbsolute(raw) && pathExistsSync(raw)) return raw;`), and `:102` shows the value is parsed straight from the `.desktop` file's `Icon` key by `parseDesktopEntry`; entries are scanned from the XDG applications directories at `:127-135`.
- Reachable from the renderer: `packages/electron/main.mjs:5109` — the `desktop_fetch_app_icons` IPC case calls `fetchLinuxAppIcons(...)` on Linux, which flows through `buildLinuxInstalledApps` (`linux-app-discovery.mjs:505`, icon resolution at `:522`/`:529`/`:537`) into the uncapped read.
- Same shape, second site: `packages/electron/main.mjs:4118-4125` — `imageFileToDataUrl` is the identical uncapped `fs.readFileSync(...).toString('base64')`, used for the Windows Terminal icon (`:4176`, `:5102`; path from the installed Windows Terminal package's `Images` folder, `:4097-4108`). Narrower (package-controlled path), same missing guard.
- Contrast in the same package: the page-controlled favicon fetch is capped at `MAX_FAVICON_BYTES = 512 * 1024` (`main.mjs:1119`) and bounded *before* buffering in `favicon-fetch.mjs` (#817); the macOS icon path converts through `sips -Z 32`, so its output is a 32px PNG by construction (`main.mjs:3798-3803`).
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at `6eb0a10a9`; `linux-app-discovery.mjs` and `main.mjs` md5-identical to main `013a7d48c`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-linux-icon-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`, node): a 64 MiB file with a PNG signature, named by a stubbed `.desktop` entry's absolute `Icon=` path, passed to the real `buildLinuxInstalledApps(['File Manager'], …)` — returned an `iconDataUrl` of **89,478,510 characters** (≈ the whole 67,108,864 bytes, base64-inflated), with process RSS **+150 MB** for the one icon. There is no size at which this read refuses.

## Why it matters

`desktop_fetch_app_icons` runs in the Electron main process — the process whose event loop drives every window. A bloated or hostile icon (a broken icon pack, an installer that drops a `.desktop` file pointing at a renamed archive/movie file with a `.png` suffix, or a genuinely huge legitimate icon) turns one routine "which apps are installed" refresh into a synchronous multi-hundred-megabyte read plus a ~1.33× base64 copy plus an IPC-sized string, stalling the whole desktop app and risking an OOM of the main process. Icons are display thumbnails; nothing legitimate needs megabytes, which is why the favicon sibling caps at 512 KiB.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `iconFileToDataUrl` (`linux-app-discovery.mjs`) refuses an icon file over an explicit named byte cap (suggest 512 KiB–1 MiB, in line with `MAX_FAVICON_BYTES`) **before** reading it — stat-gated, returning `null` over the cap so the existing no-icon fallback applies; at/under-cap icons return byte-identical data URLs.
- [ ] `imageFileToDataUrl` (`main.mjs`, Windows terminal icon) gets the same named cap and over-cap `null` behaviour, or a code comment records why its package-controlled path is exempt.
- [ ] Regression coverage (the electron smoke/unit path that covers `linux-app-discovery.mjs`) pins: over-cap icon → `null` / no data URL and the file is not read whole; at-cap icon → data URL returned; missing/non-PNG behaviour unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `iconFileToDataUrl`, `app-discovery`, `linux icon`, `desktop icon size cap`: #817 (closed) bounded the **favicon fetch** (remote URL, `favicon-fetch.mjs`) only; #833 (closed) added spawnSync timeouts in this package; #137 (closed) wired the linux-desktop smoke scripts into CI. No issue covers the local-file icon reads in `linux-app-discovery.mjs` or `main.mjs`.

body:
## Scope — phase 1 of design #1254

Land one shared bounded file-read primitive in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/` and change no call-site behaviour. This phase is the generalisation of the family's one correct in-tree embodiment: `packages/web/server/lib/skills-catalog/scan.js` `readSkillMdFile` (open-once with `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX, handle stat, non-regular refusal, cap+1 bounded read loop, `{ tooLarge }` result) — the design contract rules 1–5 of #1254 are its semantics, stated once.

Deliverables:

- `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`: parameterised cap; async and sync spellings answering identically (sync via `readSync` on an opened fd — no stat-by-path shortcut); opens once and judges from the handle (non-regular files refused distinctly from over-cap); enforces the cap during the read (at most cap+1 bytes read), so a file that grows after the stat is over-cap; uniform coded over-cap result/error carrying path, size and limit; missing-file outcome distinct from over-cap and non-regular.
- Conformance tests beside the module covering the matrix: missing / exactly-at-cap / cap+1 / grows-after-stat (content replaced or extended between open and read) / FIFO-or-device (non-regular) / symlink to a non-regular file / sync-vs-async agreement across the matrix.
- `packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` records the contract (rules 1–5 of #1254) and the named exclusions: truncation is not a policy (diagnostics/local-files.js offset sampling stays), response bodies stay #802's `response-body.js`, the server's own state files stay #976's durable store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The primitive exists in `lib/shared/`, async + sync, importing nothing beyond platform APIs, and no existing module changes behaviour in this phase.
- [ ] The conformance matrix above passes, including the grows-after-stat and non-regular cases the stat-then-read sites (snippets.js, plugins.js:423) currently fail by construction.
- [ ] `shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` documents the contract and exclusions; `bun run check:changed` passes.

Design: #1254 (full doc: `files/designs/openchamber-bounded-file-reads.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace). Phase 2 (migration of the landed web gates) is the sibling sub-issue and sequences after this phase.

body:
## Scope — phase 2 of design #1254

Migrate the web server's landed size gates onto the shared bounded file-read primitive landed in phase 1 (the sibling sub-issue of #1254), module by module — each module is an independently landable step. This phase sequences **after** phase 1 lands.

The five landed gates (refs main `013a7d48c4`):

- `packages/web/server/lib/skills-catalog/scan.js` — `readSkillMdFile`, `SKILL_MD_MAX_BYTES` 4 MiB, `{ tooLarge }` result + skip-with-warning policy, git-show fallback on non-regular (the primitive's own source embodiment; becomes its first consumer)
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/snippets.js` — stat-then-read gate, `SNIPPET_FILE_MAX_BYTES` 4 MiB, uncoded throw (gains the coded result; message surface unchanged to callers)
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugins.js` — stat-then-read gate at :423, `MAX_PLUGIN_FILE_BYTES` 1 MiB, coded `PLUGIN_FILE_TOO_LARGE` / HTTP 413 surface preserved
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/` — the entry-HTML stat gate (2 MB) inside `inspectGuestPackage` (its `package.json` read is open issue #1149, **not** this phase)
- `packages/web/server/lib/git/` — the file-diff working-tree bounded reader (`readFileDiffWorkingTreeFile`, 50 MiB, `file_too_large`, HTTP 413; staged / symlink / deleted paths keep their existing behaviour)

Per module: the private gate is replaced by the shared primitive; the module keeps its cap value, its error code and HTTP surface, its caller policy (`refuse` vs `skip`), and its fs-injection/test seams where they exist. The stat-then-read race and FIFO/device hole in snippets/plugins close by construction (primitive rule 2/3); every other observable behaviour is identical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five modules read through the primitive; no private stat-gate or private bounded-read loop remains in them.
- [ ] Each module's existing tests pass unmodified except where a test asserted the private implementation; cap values, error codes (`PLUGIN_FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `file_too_large`), HTTP statuses and the skills git-show fallback are unchanged.
- [ ] A test per migrated stat-then-read module (snippets, plugins) proves the grows-after-stat / non-regular cases now refuse instead of buffering.
- [ ] `bun run check:changed` passes.

Out of scope: VS Code modules (design #1254 phase 3, deliberately unfiled), the open per-site issues (#1150, #1143, #1149, #1247, #1151, #1156, #1157, #1158 — their own queue lifecycle), diagnostics/local-files.js (offset sampling, named exclusion of the contract).

Design: #1254 (full doc: `files/designs/openchamber-bounded-file-reads.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace).

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension's npm packument lookup reads the registry response whole with a bare `response.json()` and no byte cap — the exact read #1006 capped on the web side. The registry is **user-configured** (npm's standard resolution: `npm_config_registry` env / `.npmrc` `registry=`, including scoped registries), so the endpoint is whatever registry or mirror the user's npm config names, not necessarily `registry.npmjs.org`. The only bound is a 5-second abort, which limits time, not bytes: a fast local or nearby registry/mirror can deliver hundreds of megabytes inside it, all buffered and `JSON.parse`d in the extension host.

## Evidence (verified on main `013a7d48c`)

- `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:1528` `lookupNpmPackage`: fetch with `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` (`:1533`), then `const data = await response.json()` at `:1536` — no bounded reader, no `content-length` check, no post-read size check anywhere in the function. Reached from the exported `queryPluginRegistry` (`:1575`) via `getNpmInfo`, i.e. whenever the config UI resolves plugin npm specs.
- The web twin in the same repo was fixed under #1006: `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/npm-registry.js:122` reads through `readBoundedResponseText(response, NPM_PACKUMENT_MAX_BYTES)` with `NPM_PACKUMENT_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` (`:16`) and returns a typed `network` error over the cap. Both copies resolve the request through the same shared `resolveNpmRegistryRequest` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/npm-registry-config.js`), so the surfaces differ only in the body read.
- Precedent for this exact twin pattern: #1051 filed the VS Code upgrade-status latest-version read for the same reason (bare `response.json()` against the user-configured registry; web twin capped under #1040) and it was fixed.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at `6eb0a10a9`; `lookupNpmPackage` verified byte-identical to main `013a7d48c` — the file's other diffs are the #1154 changes above it; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-npm-packument-20261101/probe.mjs`, run with bun): `npm_config_registry` pointed at a local server streaming a **64 MiB packument** (chunked, no `content-length`; the pad carried in a version key so the parsed result retains it). The real `queryPluginRegistry(['bigpkg'])` returned `kind: 'npm-ok'` with `versions[0]` of length **67,108,864** — the server served all **67,108,931 bytes** and the extension-host process RSS went **88 MB → 236 MB (+148 MB)** for one lookup. Under the web twin's 16 MiB cap this body is refused before parsing.

## Why it matters

Plugin resolution runs in the VS Code extension host, the process that also hosts the chat UI; a bloated or hostile registry/mirror response (a compromised mirror, a misconfigured private registry returning an error document of arbitrary size, or just an unusually large packument) converts one routine plugin-info lookup into a multi-hundred-megabyte allocation with no error surface — the lookup simply succeeds more slowly, or the host is OOM-killed. The web surface decided in #1006 that 16 MiB is the legitimate envelope for this exact document; the VS Code copy was missed when that cap landed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lookupNpmPackage` in `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts` reads the registry body through a bounded reader against an explicit named cap (suggest the same `NPM_PACKUMENT_MAX_BYTES` 16 MiB the web twin uses, shared or mirrored with the keep-in-sync note this codebase uses for twin constants); a body past the cap is never buffered or parsed whole.
- [ ] Over-cap resolves to the existing typed failure shape (`{ ok: false, status: 'network', error: … }`), matching the web twin's over-cap behaviour — not a throw and not a silent success; 404 and ordinary packuments behave byte-identically to today.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: a streamed over-cap packument is refused after the cap (not consumed whole), an at-cap packument returns its `latest`/versions, and the 404 path is unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `lookupNpmPackage`, `packument`, and `npm registry`: #1006 (closed) capped the **web** packument read only; #1040/#1051 cover the latest-version reads (web + vscode); #967 (closed) covers both npm caches' eviction, not the body read; #1061/#1062 cover vscode models.dev and update-check reads. No issue covers `opencodeConfig.ts`'s packument lookup.

body:
## Summary

#1109 capped the **client → proxy** direction of the realtime-proxy and persistent-pty WebSocket proxies (server `maxPayload` + a post-assembly handler check), and its final acceptance criterion asked for the upstream direction to be checked in the same pass. That check never landed: on current main, both proxies create their **upstream** `ws` client connections with **no `maxPayload`** and their `upstream.on('message')` handlers forward with **no size check at all** — no cap, and no code comment recording why upstream frames would already be bounded. A single frame up to the `ws` default of **100 MiB** from the upstream (a remote desktop runtime for the realtime proxy; OpenCode for the persistent-pty proxy) is therefore assembled whole in the long-lived web server's memory and forwarded whole to the client.

## Evidence (verified on main `013a7d48c`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/realtime-proxy.js:225` — `new WebSocket(resolved.target.toString(), { headers, origin, handshakeTimeout })`: no `maxPayload`, so the `ws` client default (100 MiB) applies. Its `upstream.on('message')` handler at `:306` forwards any assembled frame straight to `client.send(data)`; the only reaction is the post-send `closeIfPeerTooSlow(client)` bufferedAmount check. Contrast the client direction in the same file: server `maxPayload: REALTIME_PROXY_WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (1 MiB, `:24`/`:216`) plus a handler-level size check that closes the pair with 1009 before forwarding.
- `packages/web/server/lib/persistent-pty/runtime.js:65` — `new WebSocket(buildUpstreamUrl(...), { headers, origin })`: no `maxPayload`, no handshake timeout option. Its `upstream.on('message')` handler at `:100` is a bare `client.send(data, { binary: isBinary })` with no size check. Contrast the client direction in the same file: server `maxPayload: PERSISTENT_PTY_WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (64 KiB, `:29`/`:60`) plus the handler check at `:84-93` that closes with 1009 before a frame is forwarded or queued.
- Sibling upstream clients in the same codebase do set it: dev-tunnel's upstream `new WebSocket(target, { …, maxPayload: MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES })` (`packages/web/server/lib/dev-tunnel/client.js:115`) and the relay tunnel-host's local socket (`maxPayload: MAX_PENDING_WS_BYTES`, `packages/web/server/lib/relay/tunnel-host.js:516`).
- **Laptop probe vs the real modules** (fork at `6eb0a10a9`; both files md5-identical to main `013a7d48c`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-upstream-ws-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`, run with bun): a fake upstream that sends **one 16 MiB frame** as soon as the proxy connects —
  - realtime-proxy: the client received **all 16,777,216 bytes in 1 message** (16× the proxy's own 1 MiB client-direction cap) and the connection stayed **OPEN** (`readyState: 1`, no close code).
  - persistent-pty: the client received **all 16,777,216 bytes in 1 message** (256× the proxy's own 64 KiB client-direction cap) and the connection stayed **OPEN**.

## Why it matters

These proxies front the event/terminal streams of every session in the one long-lived server process. The realtime proxy's upstream is a desktop runtime reached over the network (its target must match the configured runtime origin, so it is a distinct, remotely operated peer), and the persistent-pty upstream is the managed OpenCode process — neither is code this server controls frame-by-frame. #1109 bounded the queues and the inbound frame size precisely so one frame cannot allocate 100 MiB before any cap reacts; the reverse direction retains exactly that hole, and because the fix for #1109 added a Bun-proof handler check only on the client path, under Bun the upstream path has no layer that ever refuses an oversize frame.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both upstream client connections (`realtime-proxy.js`, `persistent-pty/runtime.js`) are created with an explicit, named `maxPayload` sized for their legitimate upstream traffic (event/terminal streams — if a larger allowance than the client-direction cap is justified, the rationale is recorded in the code next to the constant), **and** the `upstream.on('message')` handlers check the assembled size before forwarding (the Bun precedent from #1109/#1082: `maxPayload` alone is not enforced by the bundled `ws` under every runtime), closing the pair with 1009 and forwarding zero bytes for an over-cap frame.
- [ ] Regression tests in `realtime-proxy.test.js` / `realtime-proxy-terminal.test.js` and `persistent-pty/runtime.test.js` pin: a single upstream frame over the cap reaches the client as zero bytes and closes the pair; a frame at/under the cap forwards byte-identically; the existing client-direction caps, pending-queue and handshake behaviours are unchanged.
- [ ] If investigation shows a direction genuinely cannot be capped (e.g. a legitimate unbounded upstream frame shape), that justification is recorded in a code comment at the upstream construction instead — silence is the defect being filed here.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `maxPayload` and `upstream maxPayload`: #1109 (closed) covered the two **servers** (client → proxy) and listed this upstream check as its last acceptance item, but the merged fix added no upstream `maxPayload`, handler check, or justification — this issue is that residual. #1082 (closed, dev-tunnel server), #1108 (closed, message-stream server) and #1059 (open, persistent-pty pre-open queue/handshake) do not cover the upstream client connections of these two proxies.

body:
# Shared project config (`.openchamber/project.json`) is read whole with no size gate — on both the web server and the VS Code bridge

## Summary

The shared project setup file — `.openchamber/project.json` inside any opened
project's checkout (`SHARED_CONFIG_RELATIVE_PATH`) — is read into memory whole
and `JSON.parse`d with no size check on either surface. The file is
repo-controlled: it is committed in the checkout, so any project a user opens
(or is invited to open) decides how large it is. Every project-setup read
buffers all of it before the parser's field sanitizers ever run.

## Evidence (main `ea768d031`)

Web server:

- `packages/web/server/lib/projects/project-config.js:1025` —
  `readSharedProjectConfig` does a bare
  `raw = await fsPromises.readFile(sharedConfigPathOf(projectPath), 'utf8')`
  with no `stat` and no size check anywhere in the function.
- `packages/web/server/lib/projects/project-setup.js:239` —
  `parseSharedProjectConfig(raw)` runs `JSON.parse(raw)` with no length gate;
  the sanitizers (`sanitizeSetupCommands`, `sanitizeProjectActions`, …) only
  clamp fields *after* the whole document has been buffered and parsed.
- Reached from `GET /api/projects/:projectId/config`
  (`packages/web/server/lib/projects/routes.js:95`, `readProjectSetup`) and
  from the merged view built on every project-setup update.

VS Code bridge (same file, same pattern):

- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-project-setup-runtime.ts:144` — `readShared`
  does a bare `raw = await fs.promises.readFile(sharedConfigPathOf(projectPath), 'utf8')`.
- `packages/vscode/src/project-setup.ts:258` — the twin
  `parseSharedProjectConfig`, likewise ungated.
- `SHARED_CONFIG_RELATIVE_PATH = '.openchamber/project.json'` on both sides
  (web `project-setup.js:206`, vscode `project-setup.ts:79`).

The writers prove the legitimate file is tiny: both serializers emit only the
sanitized, length-clamped fields, so a real shared config is a few KB at most.
Sibling clone-/project-controlled config reads have already been capped for
exactly this reason (#1150 `opencode.json`, #1132 AGENTS.md at 1 MiB, #1149
guest `package.json`); this reader was missed because it lives in the projects
module, not the opencode module.

## Reproduction (verified this run, laptop probe vs the real modules)

Fixture: a checkout whose `.openchamber/project.json` is
`{"version":1,"pad":"<128 MiB of x>"}` (134,217,750 bytes — a valid v1
document; unknown fields are ignored by the parser).

- Web: `createProjectConfigRuntime(...).readProjectSetup('path_<base64url>')`
  returned `shared.status: 'ok'`; process RSS grew **+258 MB** for the single
  read.
- VS Code: `createProjectSetupStore(...).read('path_<base64url>')` likewise
  returned `shared.status: 'ok'` — the bridge parsed the 128 MiB file whole
  instead of rejecting it.

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-shared-project-config-cap-20261101/`
(`probe.mjs`, `probe-vscode.ts`) on the laptop, against
`~/git/openchamber-fork` at `ea768d031`.

## Why it matters

Opening an untrusted or simply bloated checkout is a routine action, and the
project-setup view is read whenever a project's setup is displayed or edited.
One oversized committed file multiplies memory on the server (and in the
VS Code extension host) on every such read — the same unbounded-read class
the fleet has been closing file by file.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both readers stat the shared file before reading and refuse anything over
  a named cap (suggest 1 MiB, mirroring #1150/#1132) — e.g. a
  `SHARED_PROJECT_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES` constant per surface, kept in sync like
  the other mirrored constants in these modules.
- Over-cap behaviour preserves the module's contract that a broken shared
  file is reported, never silently treated as empty: return
  `{ status: 'invalid', reason: …too large… }` (web) / the equivalent
  `SharedProjectConfigRead` invalid result (vscode), rather than throwing or
  returning `missing`.
- Missing file still returns `missing`; at-cap and ordinary files parse
  byte-identically to today.
- Tests on both surfaces: over-cap → invalid/too-large without reading the
  body, at-cap → ok, missing → missing (mirroring the
  `project-setup.test` / bridge project-setup test patterns already in tree).

Filed by the fleet issue creator (`new-issue-creator-openchamber`) after
dedup against open and recently closed issues (no existing issue mentions
the `.openchamber/project.json` read; #1150 covers `opencode.json` only).

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension's skill supporting-file read is the twin of web #1139 — same ungated helper, different host process. `readSkillSupportingFile` in `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:3318-3322` joins the path inside the skill dir, checks only `fs.existsSync`, and returns `fs.readFileSync(fullPath, 'utf8')` at `:3321` — no stat, no cap. Its caller is the bridge skill-files GET in `packages/vscode/src/bridge-config-runtime.ts:852`, which returns the entire content to the webview (`{ content: fileContent }`).

Skill directories are external content: skills are discovered in project `.opencode/skills/` (whatever repository is open), the user config skills dir, and catalog/clone-installed locations — the same trust class as the SKILL.md files capped after #1103. A supporting file inside a skill (a reference doc, a data file, an accidentally included bundle or log) can be any size on disk; nothing OpenChamber writes bounds it, and the read is synchronous, so it also blocks the extension host while it buffers.

#1139 covers only the web server's copy (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js` + `skill-routes.js`). This VS Code copy in `opencodeConfig.ts` was not in its scope, the same way the VS Code git-log twin (#1121) was filed separately from the web original (#1120) and the VS Code bridge AGENTS.md read (#1151) separately from web #1132.

## Evidence (verified on main `b5548ca01`)

- `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:3318-3322` — `readSkillSupportingFile`: path join + `existsSync` + bare `readFileSync` at `:3321`; size is never consulted (the module's only `statSync` calls check `isFile()`/`isDirectory()`).
- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-config-runtime.ts:852` — the bridge GET: resolves the discovered skill's sources, calls `readSkillSupportingFile(skillDir, relativePath)`, and returns the whole string as the response data. The sibling PUT path (`:859+`) writes through `writeSkillSupportingFile` from a webview-supplied body, so what the API itself writes is body-bounded — what a clone or another tool leaves in the skill dir is not.
- The SKILL.md in the same directory tree is the subject of the VS Code parser filing (twin of #1143) and the catalog scan was capped in #1103 (`skillsCatalog.ts`); supporting files under the same skill dirs are covered by neither — different helper (`opencodeConfig.ts` `readSkillSupportingFile`), different bridge handler.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at main `b5548ca01`, `opencodeConfig.ts` md5 `ae854d42748f32de502cedd1cf7db7cc` identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-opencodeconfig-caps-20261101/probe.mjs`): a 134,217,728-byte supporting file was returned by the real `readSkillSupportingFile` in full (`length === 134217728`), RSS 810 MB → 938 MB around the call; a 5-byte control read normally (`"hello"`).

## Why it matters

Opening a skill's supporting file in the Settings/skills UI is a routine read over third-party content. One oversized file in any discovered skill — a vendored reference dump, a generated data file, a hostile clone — is buffered whole in the extension host on every view, and the synchronous read stalls the editor for its duration. The house pattern is established (stat-gate with a named cap, as in the web fix for #1139): stat before reading, refuse past a named cap with a clear error shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readSkillSupportingFile` (or its bridge GET caller) stat-gates before reading: a file past an explicit named cap is never read whole; the bridge GET answers with a clear error shape the webview can surface.
- [ ] At-cap and ordinary supporting files behave byte-identically (`{ content }` response), and a missing file still returns the existing not-found error.
- [ ] The cap is a named constant sized for hand-maintained skill supporting docs, consistent with the web fix for #1139 (precedents: 1 MiB AGENTS.md in #1132/#1151).
- [ ] Regression tests pin: over-cap file refused without a whole-file read; at-cap file reads byte-identically; the PUT/DELETE skill-file bridge paths are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `readSkillSupportingFile` VS Code terms: the only hit is #1139 (open), which covers `shared.js` `readSkillSupportingFile` and the web `/api/config/skills/:name/files/*` route — same helper name, different module, different process (web server vs extension host), distinct fix site. #1103 covers the SKILL.md catalog scan, not supporting files. Established twin pattern: #1120/#1121, #1132/#1151.

## Summary

The VS Code extension's shared markdown parser is the twin of web #1143 (with #1144's snippet surface folded in, because the VS Code module routes snippets through the same parser). `parseMdFile` in `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:1980-1981` is a bare whole-file read:

```ts
const parseMdFile = (filePath: string): { frontmatter: Record<string, unknown>; body: string } => {
  const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
```

No stat, no cap. Every OpenCode config-entity read in the extension that goes through it inherits the hole:

- `opencodeConfig.ts:2007` — `readMdAgent` behind the exported `getAgentConfig` (`:2054`; bridge handler `bridge-config-runtime.ts:287`) — agent `.md` in the project `.opencode/agents/` or the user config dir
- `opencodeConfig.ts:2396` — `getCommandConfig` (bridge `:360`) — project `.opencode/commands/`
- `opencodeConfig.ts:2944, 3287, 3436, 3596` — skill `SKILL.md` parsing in discovery (`getSkillSources`/`discoverSkills`), create and rename paths
- `opencodeConfig.ts:412` — `loadSnippetFile`, called by `loadSnippetRegistry` (`:435`) behind the exported `listSnippets` (`:2822`) and `expandSnippets` (`:2857`; bridge `:601`/`:605`) — every `.md` in the project's `.opencode/snippets/` + `.opencode/snippet/` and the global snippet dirs, re-read on each list/expand call

These files are project/clone-controlled content: opening a repository puts its `.opencode/agents/*.md`, `.opencode/commands/*.md`, skill `SKILL.md` files and `.opencode/snippets/*.md` on these paths, and nothing OpenChamber writes bounds their on-disk size (the API write sides are body-limited; a clone, another editor, or a generated file is not). The read is synchronous, so it also blocks the extension host for the whole read.

#1143 covers only the web server's parser (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js` `parseMdFile`/`parseMdFileAsync`) and #1144 only the web snippet module (`snippets.js`, which has its own private parser there). In the VS Code module one `parseMdFile` serves all four surfaces, so one filing covers the extension's parser; it was not in either web issue's scope. Twin-filing precedent: #1121 (VS Code git log), #1151 (VS Code AGENTS.md).

## Evidence (verified on main `b5548ca01`)

- `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:1980-1981`: bare `readFileSync`; the module's only `statSync` calls check `isFile()`/`isDirectory()` — size is never consulted before the parse.
- Callers above span agents, commands, skills and the snippet registry; the snippet registry is rebuilt from disk on every `listSnippets`/`expandSnippets` call (`:2822`/`:2857`), including the message-send expansion path in the webview.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at main `b5548ca01`, `opencodeConfig.ts` md5 `ae854d42748f32de502cedd1cf7db7cc` identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-opencodeconfig-caps-20261101/probe.mjs`): a project `.opencode/snippets/bigone.md` with a normal frontmatter block plus 134,217,728 bytes of body was returned by the real `listSnippets(projectDir)` in full (`content.length === 134217728`, RSS 681 MB → 810 MB around the registry load); a small sibling snippet listed normally (`content === "hello"`).

## Why it matters

Listing agents, commands, or skills for an opened project is a routine Settings/discovery action in the editor, and the snippet registry is re-read on every list and every message-send expansion. One oversized markdown file in a cloned repo is buffered whole (plus the parsed copies) in the extension host on every such call; the synchronous parse stalls the editor while it reads. The fix belongs at the choke point: one gate in `parseMdFile` covers every caller instead of repeating per-surface fixes, mirroring the web fix shape for #1143/#1144.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseMdFile` size-gates before reading (stat-then-read with a re-check, or a bounded read) against an explicit named cap sized generously for hand-maintained agent/command/skill/snippet documents; an over-cap file is never buffered whole.
- [ ] Over-cap behaviour is defined per caller class and pinned: discovery/registry walks (skills, snippets) skip the over-cap file and keep loading the rest (the snippet registry already logs per-file failures at `:447-449`); single-entity reads (agent/command) fail with a clear too-large error instead of a whole-file read; no caller silently returns truncated content as if it were the whole file.
- [ ] At-cap and ordinary files parse byte-identically through every caller (frontmatter, body, legacy detection), and missing-file behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: an over-cap .md is refused/skipped without a whole-file read through the parser's callers, and a normal multi-entity load (agents + commands + skills + snippets) is unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `parseMdFile` VS Code terms: #1143 (open) covers `shared.js` `parseMdFile`/`parseMdFileAsync` and its web agent/command/skill/loop callers; #1144 (open) covers the web `snippets.js` parser; #1103 covered the skills-catalog scan on both surfaces (`skills-catalog/scan.js` + vscode `skillsCatalog.ts`) — a different module from `opencodeConfig.ts`. Nothing covers the VS Code `opencodeConfig.ts` parser or its agent/command/skill/snippet callers.

The module's only `statSync` calls check `isFile()`/`isDirectory()`; size is never consulted before any config read.

The files it reads are project- and clone-controlled: `readConfigLayers` (`:711`, exported as `readConfig` at `:750`) loads the user, project and custom `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc` layers for a working directory; `readProjectConfigFiles` (`:1941`) walks ancestors of the opened directory reading each config it finds (feeding the websearch project-override detection at `:1921-1922`); the plugin and MCP paths read the project config through the same helper (`:1369`, and the layer reads behind `listMcpConfigs`/`getMcpConfig`). These helpers back the VS Code bridge's config messages (`bridge-config-runtime.ts`), so routine Settings/agent/MCP views in the editor re-read them. Nothing OpenChamber writes bounds what can be on disk in a cloned project's `opencode.json` — a generated file, a vendored dump, or a hostile clone supplies it — and because the read is synchronous, an oversized config also stalls the extension host for every other extension while it reads.

#1150 covers only the web server's copy (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js`). This VS Code copy in `opencodeConfig.ts` was not in its scope, the same way the VS Code git-log twin (#1121) was filed separately from the web original (#1120) and the VS Code bridge AGENTS.md read (#1151) separately from web #1132.

## Evidence (verified on main `b5548ca01`)

- `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts:665-667` — `readConfigFile`: `existsSync` check, then bare `fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')`; no stat, no size constant for config files anywhere in the module.

- `GET /api/config/snippets/:name` (`config-entity-routes.js:423`, via `findSnippetByName` at `snippets.js:153`)
