Project snippets are clone-controlled content: whatever repository is open supplies `.opencode/snippets/*.md`, and nothing OpenChamber writes bounds their on-disk size (the create/update routes write from a 50 MB-limit JSON body in `core-routes.js`, but a clone, another editor, or a generated file is not bound by that). The reads are synchronous, so an oversized snippet also stalls the server event loop on every list/get/expand call — including each message send that expands snippets.

## Evidence (verified on main `3657243fa`)

- `snippets.js:38-39`: bare `readFileSync`; no `stat`/`statSync` anywhere in `snippets.js` (grep-verified).
- `snippets.js:109-128` (`loadSnippetRegistry`): iterates every `.md` in every load dir and parses each whole; `:206-207`, `:210`, `:236-237`: list, get and expand all rebuild the registry per call.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork files md5-identical to main: `snippets.js` `94661947fe8c30d10d138ed01eed1a22`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-snippets-cap-20261101/`): a project `.opencode/snippets/bigone.md` with a normal frontmatter block plus 134,217,728 bytes of body was returned by the real `listSnippets(projectDir)` in full (`content.length === 134217728`, RSS +133 MB around the call); a small sibling snippet listed normally.

Snippets are a casual, always-on surface: the composer lists them and every send can trigger an expansion, which re-reads the entire snippet registry from disk. One oversized `.md` in an opened project's `.opencode/snippets/` — a vendored dump, a generated file, a hostile clone — is buffered whole, synchronously, in the long-lived server process on every one of those calls, multiplying with the number of oversized files present. ## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseMarkdownFile` (or `loadSnippetFile`) stat-gates before reading against an explicit named cap sized generously for hand-written snippets: an over-cap snippet file is never read whole.
- [ ] An over-cap file is skipped with a warning (the registry's existing per-file failure logging shape) and the remaining snippets still list, get and expand normally; a single over-cap file must not fail the whole registry or the expand call.

- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/snippets.test.js` pin: an over-cap snippet is skipped without a whole-file read, sibling snippets still load, and a normal registry lists/expands byte-identically.

## Dedup

`inspectGuestPackage` reads a guest package's `package.json` whole with no size gate — in the same module that already stat-gates the two neighbouring reads. `packages/web/server/lib/guests/catalog.js` defines `GUEST_ASSET_MAX_BYTES` (2,000,000) as "Byte cap for one guest asset on the serve path and for the entry HTML read during package inspection, judged from stat before any read", and the entry-HTML check honours it (`guestBuiltScriptsReady` stats the entry and refuses over-cap before `readFile`). The manifest read at `catalog.js:176` does neither: it is a bare `await fs.readFile(path.join(packageRoot, 'package.json'), 'utf8')` whose result is then JSON-parsed whole.

The package root is attacker/clone-controlled content: `inspectGuestPackage` is reached from folder installs, git-clone installs and zip installs (`install.js:106`, `install.js:318`), from the update check (`updates.js:243`), and from `loadGuestFromPackageRoot` (`catalog.js:336`), which `listInstalledGuests` runs for every installed guest — so one installed guest with an oversized `package.json` is buffered whole on every catalog list, not just at install time. Closed #744 capped the *git-show* copy of a package.json on the update path; this local-file read was never gated, and #1116 capped the asset serve path and the entry-HTML read in this same module, leaving the manifest as the one ungated inspection read.

## Evidence (verified on main `fe0d11935`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/catalog.js:37` — `export const GUEST_ASSET_MAX_BYTES = 2_000_000;` with the stat-before-read comment at :32-36; `fileSizeOrNull` helper at :39.
- `catalog.js:155-159` — entry HTML: size is statted and over-cap returns false *before* `fs.readFile(entryPath)`.
- `catalog.js:176` — manifest: `raw = await fs.readFile(path.join(packageRoot, 'package.json'), 'utf8');` — no stat, no size comparison anywhere in `inspectGuestPackage`.
- Callers: `install.js:106` (install from prepared source), `install.js:318` (path install), `updates.js:243` (update check), `catalog.js:336` (`loadGuestFromPackageRoot`, used per installed guest by `listInstalledGuests`).
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at main `fe0d11935`, `catalog.js` md5 `1740e03012a9d1b424e2d05cc7f8a787` identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-guest-manifest-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`): a guest package whose `package.json` (134,217,880 bytes) carries a valid manifest with a 128 MiB `panel.name` was inspected with `ok: true` and the returned `guest.name.length === 134217728` — the whole file was read and parsed, 67× the module's own 2,000,000-byte cap for the neighbouring reads.

## Why it matters

Guest packages are third-party content by design — installed from folders, cloned repos and zips — and their manifest is the first file the host reads from them. An oversized `package.json` (hostile, generated, or a vendored dump committed by accident) is buffered and parsed whole in the long-lived web server at install time, at every update check, and on every catalog listing for as long as the guest stays installed. The fix is the shape this module already uses twice: judge the size from stat against the existing named cap before reading.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `inspectGuestPackage` stats `package.json` before reading and never buffers more than the cap allows: an over-cap manifest is answered without a whole-file read (the existing `{ ok: false, code: 'invalid-manifest' }` shape, or an explicitly recorded alternative).

body:
Found while implementing #1139 (task 5312, 2026-11-01): the skill-files routes build the path with `decodeURIComponent(req.params.filePath)`. On Express 5 the `*filePath` wildcard param arrives as an array of segments (`["references","guide.md"]`), so decodeURIComponent coerces it to `references,guide.md` — a path that never exists.

Evidence (laptop, main-derived branch for #1139): debug log in the GET handler printed `DEBUG PARAMS {"name":"capped-skill","filePath":["references","over-cap.md"]} filePath= references,over-cap.md`, and nested GETs returned 404 `File not found` for files that exist on disk. Single-segment files work only because a one-element array stringifies cleanly.

Scope: `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/skill-routes.js` PUT handler (~line 786) and DELETE handler (~line 821) still use the bare pattern. The GET handler (~line 690) is fixed in the #1139 PR by joining segments first, following the house precedent in `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js` (`Array.isArray(rawPath) ? rawPath.join('/') : (rawPath || '')`).

Acceptance:
- PUT and DELETE for a nested supporting-file path (e.g. `references/guide.md`) operate on that exact file on disk.
- Single-segment paths behave byte-identically to today.
- Regression tests pin nested PUT + DELETE (and the existing nested GET) in skill-routes.test.js.

body:
## Summary

The skill supporting-file read buffers the whole file with no size gate. `readSkillSupportingFile` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js:972-978`) resolves the path inside the skill dir, checks only `fs.existsSync`, and returns `fs.readFileSync(fullPath, 'utf8')` — no stat, no cap. Its caller is `GET /api/config/skills/:name/files/*filePath` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/skill-routes.js:706`), which returns the entire content as JSON (`res.json({ path, content })`).

Skill directories are external content: skills are discovered in project `.opencode/skills/` (whatever repository is open), the user config skills dir, and catalog/clone-installed locations — the same trust class as the SKILL.md files capped after #1103. A supporting file inside a skill (a reference doc, a data file, an accidentally included bundle or log) can be any size on disk; nothing OpenChamber writes bounds it, and the read is synchronous, so it also blocks the server event loop while it buffers.

## Evidence (verified on main `b95d6ad80`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js:972-978` — `readSkillSupportingFile`: `assertPathWithinSkillDir` + `existsSync` + bare `readFileSync`; size is never consulted (the only `statSync` in `shared.js` is an unrelated `isFile` check at `:213`).
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/skill-routes.js:696-715` — the GET route: resolves the discovered skill's sources, calls `readSkillSupportingFile(sources.md.dir, filePath)` at `:706`, and returns the whole string in the JSON response. The sibling PUT route (`:783+`) writes through the same helper from a JSON body, so what the API itself writes is body-bounded — what a clone or another tool leaves in the skill dir is not.
- The SKILL.md in the same directory tree got a size gate discussion in #1103 (skills-catalog scan + vscode twin); supporting files under the same skill dirs were not covered there — different helper (`shared.js`), different route (`skill-routes.js`).
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork files md5-identical to main: shared.js `3e550113ee1e39a499598ca9b3845f3f`, skill-routes.js `7e136f2eb98d7758fec5364b49e01a42`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-skill-support-read-20261101/`): a 134,217,728-byte supporting file was returned by the real `readSkillSupportingFile` in full (`length === 134217728`), RSS +129 MB around the call; the 6-byte control read normally.

## Why it matters

Opening a skill's supporting file in the Settings/skills UI is a routine read over third-party content. One oversized file in any discovered skill — a vendored reference dump, a generated data file, a hostile clone — is buffered whole (plus JSON copies) in the long-lived server process on every view, and the synchronous read stalls every session for its duration. The house pattern is established (#1107/#1086 stat-gate, #1132 named-cap precedent): stat before reading, refuse past a named cap with a clear error shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readSkillSupportingFile` (or its GET caller) stat-gates before reading: a file past an explicit named cap is never read whole; the GET route answers with a clear non-200 too-large error shape.
- [ ] At-cap and ordinary supporting files behave byte-identically (`{ path, content }` response), and a missing file still returns the existing 404.
- [ ] The cap is a named constant sized for hand-maintained skill supporting docs (precedents: 1 MiB AGENTS.md in #1132, 2,000,000 chars for guest file ops), documented where the skill file API is described.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: over-cap file refused without a whole-file read; at-cap file reads byte-identically; the PUT/DELETE skill-file routes are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for skill supporting-file read/size terms: #1103 covers the SKILL.md catalog scan (`skills-catalog/scan.js` + vscode `skillsCatalog.ts`), not `shared.js` `readSkillSupportingFile` or the `/api/config/skills/:name/files/*` route. #1138 (filed this run) covers plugin files via a different helper. No issue covers this read.

## Summary

The plugin-file read path buffers the whole file with no size gate. `readPluginDirFile` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugins.js:417-427`) does a bare synchronous `fs.readFileSync(target.absolutePath, 'utf8')` at `:425` — there is no `stat`/`statSync` anywhere in `plugins.js`, and no named cap. It backs two routes in `plugin-routes.js`: `GET /api/config/plugins/file/:id` (`:286`, returns the whole content as JSON) and the `PUT /api/config/plugins/file/:id` existence/content check (`:321`, reads the whole existing file before every update).

Plugin files live in `.opencode/plugins/` (project scope, inside the working directory — i.e. whatever repository the user has open, including a fresh clone) and the user config `plugins/` dir. Their on-disk size is not bounded by anything OpenChamber writes: files arrive via clones, other editors, code generators, or OpenCode itself. The read is also synchronous, so an oversized file both allocates its full size (plus the JSON string copies on the GET response) and blocks the server's event loop for the duration.

## Evidence (verified on main `b95d6ad80`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugins.js:425` — `content: fs.readFileSync(target.absolutePath, 'utf8')`; the module contains no `statSync`/`stat` call at all (grep-verified), so size is never consulted before the read.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugin-routes.js:286` — GET handler returns `res.json(file)` with the whole content; `:321` — PUT handler re-reads the whole existing file via the same helper before overwriting.
- Scope resolution (`plugins.js:208-222`): project scope is `path.join(workingDirectory, '.opencode', 'plugins')` — project-controlled content, not an OpenChamber-managed store; the files OpenChamber's own API writes are small hand-edited plugin sources, so a generous named cap does not constrain legitimate use.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork files md5-identical to main: plugins.js `e7eed97be944e4afc7356cbaadcc0651`, plugin-routes.js `f5032930829aa4cd683c987460a15a4b`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-plugin-read-cap-20261101/`): a project `.opencode/plugins/big.js` of 134,217,728 bytes was returned by the real `readPluginDirFile` in full (`content.length === 134217728`), RSS rose 158 MB → 287 MB (+129 MB) around the single call; the 19-byte control file read normally.

## Why it matters

This is the same read/write asymmetry the fleet has been closing across the web server (#1132 AGENTS.md GET, #1127 fs/write pre-read, #1086 hook read — the last fixed on current main): a file whose size OpenChamber does not control is buffered whole on a routine UI path (opening a plugin file in Settings, and every plugin-file save via PUT). A bloated or hostile plugin file in any opened project — a bundled/minified artifact dropped into `.opencode/plugins/`, an accidentally committed build output — inflates and stalls the one long-lived server process that hosts every session. The fix follows the house pattern from #1107/#1086: stat before reading, refuse past a named cap with a clear error shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readPluginDirFile` (or its callers) stat-gates before reading: a file past an explicit named cap is never read whole; the GET route answers with a clear non-200 too-large error shape and the PUT route's pre-read does not buffer an over-cap existing file either.
- [ ] At-cap and ordinary plugin files behave byte-identically on GET and PUT (content, fileName, scope), and a missing file still returns the existing 404/null behaviour.
- [ ] The cap is named and documented where the plugin file API is described, sized for hand-edited plugin sources (the precedent caps are 1 MiB for AGENTS.md in #1132 and 2,000,000 chars for guest file ops).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugins.test.js` / `plugin-routes.test.js` pin: over-cap file is refused without a whole-file read, at-cap file reads byte-identically.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for plugin-file read/size terms: no issue covers `readPluginDirFile` or the `/api/config/plugins/file` routes' read size. #1132 (behavior AGENTS.md GET cap) and #1127 (`/api/fs/write` pre-read) are different files/routes with the same shape; #1103 covers SKILL.md catalog scans, not plugin files.

title: fix(web): project plan reads buffer the whole file with no size gate — list and readPlan read shared plans entire while writes clamp at 200,000 chars

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

Project plans have a size contract on the write side and none on the read side. The project-context runtime clamps every plan it writes to `PROJECT_PLAN_BODY_MAX_LENGTH` (200,000 chars, `runtime.js:29`, applied at `:800` and `:878`), but plan files are **not** only written through that API: shared plans live in the team's shared plans folder and are, by the module's own design, written by other tools — `listSharedPlans` says "Plans written by other tools have no manifest entry, so the title comes from the file each time" (`runtime.js:468-472`), and `plan-progress.js:34-38` notes "agents tick steps with their own file tools, so no write event announces it". Every read of such a file buffers it **whole, with no size gate**:

- The plan **list** (`readContext` → `listSharedPlans` / `progressOfLink`) goes through the summary cache in `plan-progress.js`, which stats the file (`:50`) and even records `stat.size` for its cache key (`:59`, `:64`) — but never compares that size to any cap before `readFile` at `:62`. Listing therefore materializes every oversized plan file entire, just to extract a title and a checklist count.
- `readPlan` (`runtime.js:735`) reads the plan file whole at `:747` (shared) and `:766` (personal) and returns the entire `raw` string to the caller. Its callers include the HTTP route (`project-context/routes.js:219`), the Project Knowledge tool (`openchamber-control/project-knowledge.js:165/:171/:191`), and session knowledge (`session-knowledge/runtime.js:239`), so an oversized plan is buffered whole on ordinary list/open/knowledge reads, repeatedly.

## Evidence (verified on main `ea75c0ade`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js:29` — `PROJECT_PLAN_BODY_MAX_LENGTH = 200_000`, enforced only on writes (`:800` update, `:878` create).
- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/plan-progress.js:50-62` — `summaryOf` stats the file, checks the cache by `mtimeMs`/`size`, then `await fsPromises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8')` with no size comparison.
- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js:747` and `:766` — `readPlan`'s two bare `readFile(planPath, 'utf8')` calls; the result's `raw`, `body`, and `title` are all derived from the whole string and `raw` is returned to callers.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork files `runtime.js` sha256 `b873af71583b…` and `plan-progress.js` sha256 `0400ebbf47d2…` identical to sandbox main `ea75c0ade`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-plan-read-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`): a 128 MiB `big.md` in a temp shared-plans folder. `readContext` listed it (`title: "Big Plan"`, progress `{done:0,total:1}`) with **RSS +131 MB** for that one list; `readPlan('shared:big.md')` returned **`raw` of 134,217,764 chars — ~671× the 200,000-char write cap**.

## Why it matters

The Plans tab re-reads the list while it is open, and agents — the actors most likely to write a plan file outside the API, per the module's own comments — work in exactly the shared folder these reads serve. One oversized plan file (a generated dump saved as `.md`, a bad merge, a tool writing to the wrong path) makes every list refresh and every knowledge read buffer the whole file in the long-lived web server, for every connected client, with the cache offering no protection on first read or after any edit. The stat the summary cache already performs makes the gate cheap: the size is in hand before the read.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The plan summary path (`plan-progress.js` `summaryOf`) refuses or truncates before reading: a plan file over an explicit named cap (the 200,000-char write contract, a byte-denominated sibling, or a recorded rationale) is never buffered whole for a title/progress summary; its list entry degrades explicitly (e.g. no progress / marked too-large) instead of failing or silently succeeding, and one oversized plan must not fail the whole list.
- [ ] `readPlan` applies the same gate on both branches (shared `:747`, personal `:766`): an over-cap file is answered without a whole-file read (clear too-large error shape its HTTP/knowledge callers can surface, or an explicitly recorded alternative), while a missing file still returns `null`.
- [ ] Plans at or under the cap behave byte-identically: list titles/progress, `readPlan` `raw`/`body`/`title`, and create/update flows are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/` (runtime / plan-progress test style) pin: an over-cap shared plan is not read whole by the list or by `readPlan`, and an at-cap plan lists and reads unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + recently closed issues for plan/project-context read-size terms: no issue covers these reads. The write-side clamp is this module's own; the AGENTS.md read cap (#1132) and `/api/fs/write` pre-read (#1127) are different files in different modules. Own-store JSON reads dispositioned in earlier creator runs do not apply: shared plan files are explicitly written by other tools and agents, outside the API that clamps.

title: fix(web): behavior AGENTS.md GET reads the file whole with no size gate — PUT caps the same file at 1 MiB, the read side buffers any size

body:
## Summary

The Behavior / global `AGENTS.md` endpoints enforce their size contract on only one side. `PUT /api/behavior/agents-md` refuses any content over `MAX_BEHAVIOR_PROMPT_SIZE` (1 MiB) with a 413 — the module's own statement that this file is at most 1 MiB — but `GET /api/behavior/agents-md` reads the file from disk **whole, with no stat or size check**, and returns it entire. The PUT handler's conflict check does the same unbounded read a second time. The file lives at a fixed path in the OpenCode config directory and can be edited, generated, or replaced outside the UI (it is the user's global agent instructions file, routinely hand-edited and synced), so anything that makes it large — a bad merge, a generated file, a tool writing to the wrong path — makes every Behavior-page load buffer the whole file in the web server, and the UI then holds it as an editor string.

## Evidence (verified on main `bf3927b77`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/routes.js:658` — `const MAX_BEHAVIOR_PROMPT_SIZE = 1024 * 1024; // 1 MB`, enforced only on write at :679-680 (413 over the cap).
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/routes.js:667` — GET handler: `const content = await fs.promises.readFile(AGENTS_MD_PATH, 'utf8');` — no `stat`, no size comparison, after only an `access()` existence check at :663.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/routes.js:689` — PUT handler's `expectedContent` conflict check repeats the same unbounded `readFile(AGENTS_MD_PATH, 'utf8')`, so even a *refused* oversized save attempt first buffers the whole existing file.
- `AGENTS_MD_PATH` is `path.join(OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR, 'AGENTS.md')` (:657), where `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` is env-overridable (`lib/opencode/shared.js:23-25`) and the file is a plain user-managed text file — nothing outside these two handlers bounds what can be on disk there.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at main `bf3927b77`, `routes.js` md5 `e2373fcad698d07a0b48a6c1c68152cb` identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-agents-md-cap-20261101/probe.mjs`): pointed `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` at a temp dir holding a 128 MiB `AGENTS.md`, registered the real `registerOpenCodeRoutes`, and invoked the GET handler. Result: status 200, `exists: true`, **`contentCharsReturned: 134217728`** — the entire file, 128× the cap the PUT side enforces — RSS **+134 MB** for one load.
- Sibling precedent in the same server: theme JSON reads stat-gate at a named cap before reading (`lib/opencode/theme-runtime.js` `maxThemeJsonBytes`), and #1104 covers the VS Code twin's theme read. Nothing pins the behavior routes' read size.

## Why it matters

The cap asymmetry means the 1 MiB contract protects the write path while the read path — the one taken on every Behavior-page load, by every connected client — has no protection at all against the file the contract is about. `AGENTS.md` is exactly the kind of file that grows outside the app's control: it is hand-edited, dotfile-synced, and written by other tools in the OpenCode ecosystem. A single oversized file degrades the long-lived web server for all sessions, not just the editor, and the fix is the shape this codebase already uses elsewhere: check the size the cap already names before reading.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/behavior/agents-md` stats the file before reading and never buffers more than the route's contract allows: an over-cap file is answered without a whole-file read (a clear error / too-large response shape the UI can surface, or an explicitly recorded alternative), while a missing file still returns `{ content: '', exists: false }`.
- [ ] The PUT handler's `expectedContent` conflict check applies the same gate: an over-cap existing file is never read whole during a save attempt.
- [ ] Files at or under `MAX_BEHAVIOR_PROMPT_SIZE` behave byte-identically: GET returns the full content with `exists: true`, PUT saves and conflict detection work exactly as today.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: an over-cap on-disk `AGENTS.md` is not read whole by either handler, and an at-cap file loads and saves unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `agents-md` / behavior-route terms: no issue covers these reads (#25 is the unrelated fork-release handoff). The theme-read caps (web `theme-runtime.js`, #1104 for the VS Code twin) cover different files in different modules. Own-store JSON reads dispositioned in earlier creator runs do not apply: this is a user/tool-managed text file whose size contract the same module already states at 1 MiB.

body:
## Summary

`POST /api/fs/write` reads the existing target file **whole, with no stat or size gate at all**, purely to short-circuit a save whose content is unchanged. The handler resolves and authorizes the path, then immediately calls `fsPromises.readFile(writePath, 'utf8')` and compares the result to the request's `content`. The target is any file inside an opened workspace — including files that arrive with a cloned repository — so a workspace containing one very large file makes every save attempt against that path buffer the entire file into the web server as a UTF-8 string first, however small the new content is. Every sibling path in the same file gates before it reads; this one does not even stat.

## Evidence (verified on main `bf3927b77`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js:1601` — `const existing = await fsPromises.readFile(writePath, 'utf8').catch(() => null);` followed at :1602 by `if (existing === content) return res.json({ success: true, … })`. The write handler (`app.post('/api/fs/write', …)` at :1565) performs `realpath` + root checks before this line but **no `stat` call and no size comparison anywhere** before the read.
- Siblings in the same file all gate first: the read route stats and refuses `stats.size > MAX_READ_BYTES` (16 MiB, :221) at :1316-1323 before `readFile`; the preview route refuses `stats.size > MAX_SERVE_BYTES` (100 MiB, :214) at :1532 before `readFile`; the upload route caps at `createUploadMaxBytes()` (100 MiB default). The write route's pre-read is the one ungated whole-file read left in `fs/routes.js`.
- The comparison only ever needs to distinguish "same bytes" from "different": when the existing file's byte length differs from the new content's byte length the contents cannot be equal, so the unbounded read is never necessary — a stat (or a bounded prefix/length check) settles most cases without buffering anything.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at main `bf3927b77`, `routes.js` md5 `cfd0acb750d4da603dbc242f3238301c` identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-fs-write-preread-20261101/probe.mjs`): registered the real `registerFsRoutes` with real `fs` in a temp workspace holding a 256 MiB file, then invoked `POST /api/fs/write` with 1-byte content `'x'`. Result: the handler's `readFile` returned **268,435,456 bytes** for the target (1 call), RSS **+280 MB**, status 200, and the file was then written down to 1 byte — the whole-file read bought nothing, because the contents differed in length alone.
- `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.test.js` covers the write route's authorization/atomicity with small fixtures only; nothing pins the pre-read's behaviour against a large existing file.

## Why it matters

The web server is the long-lived process hosting every session. The Files editor saves through this route, and workspaces routinely contain large artifacts (recordings, datasets, build outputs, vendored binaries) that came with a cloned repo — content the user did not author and may not know is there. One save against such a path (or an agent-driven write through the same API) costs the file's full size in memory, as a decoded string, on top of the request body — repeatedly, on every save attempt, because the shortcut re-reads from scratch each time. The fix is the file's own established shape: gate on size before reading, the way the read and preview routes already do in this module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/fs/write` never buffers an existing file larger than the new content can possibly equal: when the existing file's size differs from the request content's byte length, the identical-content shortcut is skipped without a whole-file read (stat-first, or an equivalent bounded comparison).
- [ ] An existing file whose size exceeds an explicit named cap (the module's `MAX_READ_BYTES` precedent, or a recorded rationale for another value) is never read whole by this route; the save proceeds to the atomic write path (or refuses with a clear error) without retaining the old bytes.
- [ ] Behaviour is unchanged for ordinary files: an identical-content save still returns `{ success: true }` without rewriting (mtime/inode preserved), a changed save still writes atomically via temp + rename, and a missing target still writes fresh.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.test.js` pin: a large existing file is not read whole on save (e.g. `readFile` never consumes it / is not called with the target when sizes differ or the cap is exceeded), and the identical-content no-rewrite shortcut still fires for a small unchanged file.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `fs/write`, `api/fs/write` and write-route read terms: no issue covers this pre-read. #1026 (closed) capped `GET /api/fs/read`; the preview gate and the upload cap cover their own routes in the same file. The fixed-SaaS / own-store whole-file reads dispositioned in earlier creator runs do not apply: this target is a workspace file whose size is set by whatever repository or artifact the workspace contains.

title: fix(vscode): getGitLog maxCount has no ceiling — normalizeMaxCount passes any positive integer to --max-count (web twin #1120)

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Summary

The VS Code port of `getGitLog` has the same missing ceiling as the web twin filed as #1120: `normalizeMaxCount` in `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts` accepts any positive integer and passes it straight to `--max-count`, so a huge `maxCount` makes the extension host buffer a repository's entire history whole for one `api:git/log` bridge call.

#641 fixed this function for invalid values (negative / fractional / `Infinity` fall back to 50); it never bounded a huge **finite** value — the exact gap the web side's diff-context fix (#1079) later closed with a safe-integer check plus a named clamp, and that #1120 now tracks for the web log route.

## Evidence (verified on main `c58095af0`)

- `packages/vscode/src/gitService.ts:3649-3654` — `normalizeMaxCount`: `if (maxCount === undefined || !Number.isInteger(maxCount) || maxCount <= 0) return 50; return maxCount;` — no ceiling. The result is interpolated as `--max-count=${maxCount}` at `:3668` (plain path) and `:3742` (`--all` path), and the output is consumed whole via `execGit` (stdout string → parsed entries array → bridge response).
- Entry point: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-git-runtime.ts:573-583` — `api:git/log` takes `maxCount` from the webview payload and forwards it unmodified to `gitService.getGitLog`.
- Legitimate values are the same as the web UI's: 25 / 50 / 100 plus load-more increments (`packages/ui/src/components/views/git/HistorySection.tsx:23-27`); no caller needs an unbounded count.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (laptop fork at `c58095af0`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-log-maxcount-20261031/probe.test.js`, using the module's own `gitService.log-max-count.test.js` harness shape — mocked `vscode` module, real `getGitLog`, real git): on a 55-commit repo, the default returned **50**, while `maxCount=1000000000` returned **all 55** on both the plain path and the `all: true` path.
- The existing test file pins only the #641 invalid cases: `gitService.log-max-count.test.js` covers -5 / 2.5 / Infinity / NaN / 0 / 'abc' → 50, and valid 2 / omitted → pass-through/default. No huge-finite case exists.

## Why it matters

The extension host is a long-lived process shared by every VS Code window surface; the bridge payload is webview-supplied, so the count is not trusted input. One call with a huge count forces git to emit the whole history and the host to hold it as a stdout string, a parsed array, and a serialized bridge response — on a large repository that is unbounded memory and latency for a request whose legitimate maximum is a few hundred. The fix shape is already established twice in this repo: clamp to a named ceiling (web `MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES`, #1079; the ceiling #1120's triage picks for the web log route — the two surfaces should agree on the value).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `normalizeMaxCount` clamps a positive integer past a named, documented ceiling instead of returning it unchanged; the ceiling matches the value chosen for the web twin (#1120) so both surfaces behave identically for the same request.
- [ ] Invalid values keep today's exact behaviour (-5 / 2.5 / Infinity / NaN / 0 / non-number → 50; omitted → 50), and ordinary values (1, 2, 25, 50, 100) pass through unchanged on both the plain and `--all` paths.
- [ ] `gitService.log-max-count.test.js` gains a huge-finite case (e.g. 1,000,000,000 on the 55-commit fixture) proving the returned total is the ceiling-clamped result, not the whole history, on at least the plain path and ideally `--all` too.
- [ ] No change to the web server's git routes/service (owned by #1120).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `maxCount`, `normalizeMaxCount`, `git log max-count`: #641 (closed) is this function's invalid-value fix and pins only those cases; #463 (closed) is the web original; #1120 (open, filed this run) is the web twin — its scope explicitly excludes this VS Code port and flags it for a separate twin filing, following the house twin pattern (#1054/#1057, #1040/#1051).

title: fix(web): git log maxCount has no ceiling — a huge positive value passes both guards and returns the entire history buffered whole

body:
## Summary

`GET /api/git/log`'s `maxCount` has no ceiling at either layer. The route parser accepts any all-digits value and returns `Number(text)` unchecked, and the service guard accepts any positive integer — so `?maxCount=1000000000` reaches git as `--max-count=1000000000`, and the server buffers the repository's entire history whole (the raw `git log` string, the parsed entries array, and the JSON response) for one request.

This is the one sibling the earlier fixes missed: the diff-context parser directly above it in the same file was given a safe-integer check **and** a 100,000 clamp in the #1079 fix, precisely because "a merely huge one asks git for an absurd -U value". The log parser got neither.

## Evidence (verified on main `c58095af0`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/git/routes.js:49-54` — `parseLogMaxCount`: `/^\d+$/` then `return maxCount > 0 ? maxCount : undefined` — no `Number.isSafeInteger` check, no clamp.
- `packages/web/server/lib/git/routes.js:36-44` — the sibling `parseDiffContextLines` in the same file: `Number.isSafeInteger(contextLines) ? Math.min(contextLines, MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES /* 100_000 */) : 3`, with a comment explaining why digits alone are not enough (#1079).
- `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js:6647` — the service guard is `Number.isInteger(options.maxCount) && options.maxCount > 0 ? options.maxCount : 50`: it stops negatives, fractions and `Infinity`, but any huge finite integer passes through to `--max-count=${maxCount}` (`service.js:6652`, `:6733`, `:6740`). The result is consumed whole: `git.raw(logArgs)` returns the full string, records are parsed into an `entries` array, and the route answers `res.json(log)`.
- Legitimate callers need nowhere near this: the UI offers 25 / 50 / 100 (`packages/ui/src/components/views/git/HistorySection.tsx:23-27` `LOG_SIZE_OPTIONS`), the graph view starts at 100, load-more steps +25, and every other caller passes 1, 2, 25 or 50.
- **Laptop probe vs the real modules** (laptop fork at `c58095af0`, `routes.js`/`service.js` md5-identical to sandbox main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-log-maxcount-20261031/probe.mjs`): the real `parseLogMaxCount` (extracted verbatim from `routes.js`) returns `1000000000` for `'1000000000'`, `Infinity` for a 309-digit string, and `9007199254740992` for `'9007199254740993'` (an unsafe integer, silently rounded). The real `getLog` on a 60-commit repo returns 50 entries for `maxCount=50`, **all 60 for `maxCount=1000000000`**, and 50 for `Infinity` (the service's `isInteger` check catches only that one case).

## Why it matters

The route's own comment states the threat model: a value that means "unlimited" must never reach git (#463 closed the negative case). A huge positive is unlimited in practice — git stops only at the end of the history — but it sails through both guards because each layer assumes the other bounds the magnitude. On a large repository, one unauthenticated-shape request (the endpoint is a plain query parameter on a directory the user has open) makes the long-lived server hold the whole history three times over. The diff-context fix established the house answer for exactly this shape in the same file: safe-integer judgement plus a generous named ceiling that clamps instead of failing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseLogMaxCount` (route) judges with `Number.isSafeInteger` and clamps to a named, documented ceiling (mirroring `MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES`' shape; the ceiling is generous vs the UI's 25/50/100 + load-more steps), so a 309-digit value and any over-ceiling value can no longer pass through as `Infinity`, an unsafe integer, or an absurd count.
- [ ] The service-layer guard in `getLog` applies the same ceiling (defence in depth, matching how context lines are normalised in both layers — routes + `normalizeContextLines` in the service), so direct service callers cannot bypass it.
- [ ] Ordinary values behave byte-identically: 1, 2, 25, 50, 100 and load-more increments return exactly as today; invalid spellings (`-5`, `2.5`, `10junk`, `0`, absent) still take the existing undefined/default path.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: the route cases in `routes.test.js` gain the 309-digit and over-ceiling cases, and `service.test.js`' `getLog maxCount guard (#463)` block gains a huge-finite case proving the returned count is the ceiling, not the whole history.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `maxCount`, `git log max-count`, `parseLogMaxCount`: #463 (closed) fixed the bare-`parseInt` / negative case at the route, #641 (closed) was its VS Code port, #1079 (closed) fixed the same missing safe-integer + clamp for the *diff context* parser in the same file. None bounds a huge **positive** `maxCount`: the existing route test (`routes.test.js:1478`) pins only malformed/negative/small cases, and the service test (`service.test.js:239`) pins only -5 / 0 / 2.5 / absent / 7.

title: fix(web): guest asset route buffers every served package file whole with no size gate — one oversized asset in any installed guest is loaded whole into the server on every request

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/extensions

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The guest asset route buffers every served package file whole in the web server's memory, with no size gate anywhere on the path. `GET /api/guests/:id/{*filePath}` resolves the file, then does a bare `fs.readFile(filePath)` and `res.send(body)` — for HTML it additionally stringifies and rewrites the whole buffer. Guest packages are third-party code, and folder ("path") installs point straight at a directory on disk with no size limits at all (the ZIP limits — 20 MB archive / 40 MB expanded — do not apply), so a single oversized `.js`, `.png`, `.svg`, `.css` or `.json` asset in any installed guest is loaded whole into the long-lived server process on every request for it.

## Evidence (verified on main `3bb1e72a8`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js:860` — the route; `:886` `raw = await fs.readFile(filePath)` with no preceding size check; the HTML branch then does `raw.toString('utf8')` plus two token/style injections (further whole-buffer copies) before `res.send(body)`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/catalog.js:89` `resolveGuestServedFile` / `:60-71` `resolveGuestAssetPath` — the resolver stats the candidate only for `isFile()`; `stat.size` is never consulted. Servable types (`catalog.js` `MIME_BY_EXT`): html, js, css, svg, json, png.
- The house pattern this route misses exists in the same feature: guest file operations stat before reading and refuse over `GUEST_FILE_CONTENT_MAX` (2,000,000 chars) — `packages/web/server/lib/guests/files.js:186-194`. The guest request/service paths bound their reads through `response-body.js` (#770). Only the static asset serve is unbounded.
- Install-side bounds do not cover this: `guests/DOCUMENTATION.md:47` — ZIP limits are 20 MB / 500 files / 40 MB expanded, but "Folder installs store their realpath" with no per-file or total size limit, and a folder guest's files can also grow after install.
- **Laptop probe vs the real route module** (fork files md5-identical to main: routes.js `d470f3e3b8e6b2eff96f1bf47c2a1370`, catalog.js `934a39b91a51c5bf223c0b26ea569496`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-guest-asset-cap-20261031/`): a folder-installed guest whose `panel/big.js` is 134,217,728 bytes was served by the real `registerGuestRoutes` with **200 and all 134,217,728 bytes**, and the server process RSS rose **78 MB → 332 MB** around the single request (readFile buffer + `res.send` copies). The small control asset (`panel/main.js`, 20 bytes) served 200 normally.
- Secondary, same surface: `catalog.js:137` `guestBuiltScriptsReady` also reads the entry HTML whole with no size gate during package inspection (called from `inspectGuestPackage` for panel/background/attach/page/status/editor entries).

## Why it matters

Guests are explicitly third-party, capability-gated code — the asset route exists to serve their files from the OpenChamber origin to the sandboxed rail. Every other guest read path in the codebase is bounded during the read (file ops, request proxy, surface frames); this one trusts the on-disk size of whatever a guest package contains. A bloated or hostile asset — or an ordinary asset that grew, e.g. an unoptimized PNG or a bundled JS with sourcemaps inlined — is re-buffered whole on every panel load, multiplying memory in the one process that hosts every session. The fix can follow the in-feature precedent: stat-gate before reading (refuse past a named cap), and/or stream non-HTML responses the way `/api/fs/raw` streams (`fs/routes.js` createReadStream) instead of buffering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The asset route refuses (or streams, for non-HTML types) a file past a named, documented size cap instead of buffering it whole: the size is judged from the stat the resolver already performs, before any `readFile`; an over-cap asset gets a clear non-200 answer and the server's memory stays flat.
- [ ] HTML handling keeps working under the cap: token injection and style injection behave byte-identically for in-cap pages; the cap is sized/documented in `guests/DOCUMENTATION.md` §37 (the asset-route paragraph) with its rationale.
- [ ] `guestBuiltScriptsReady`'s entry-HTML read gets the same gate (or the issue records why the serve-route gate covers it).
- [ ] Regression tests pin: an over-cap asset is refused with the file never read whole (or streamed without a whole-buffer read); an at-cap asset serves byte-identically; the existing catalog/routes behaviours (404 shapes, tools-only guests serving icons but not HTML/JS, token propagation) are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for guest size/read caps: #1085 (open) covers guest OAuth *network* reads; #744 (closed) covered the guest update check's `git show` capture; #770 (closed) bounded guest *service* responses; #704 (closed) was the upload-cap number parsing. None covers the static asset serve route (`/api/guests/:id/{*filePath}`) or `guestBuiltScriptsReady`. The fs preview/read caps (#1026 and siblings) are different routes over project files, not guest packages.

body:
## Finding

The store-only Antigravity quota tests added by PR #921 do not isolate the second accounts-file path, so on a developer machine they can silently read the developer's real `antigravity-accounts.json` instead of being store-only — and they leak the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` override they install.

## Evidence

- PR #921 (merged, merge commit `4998e715a80c6cdca752dd29e69da58e7d89332f`): https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/921 — CodeRabbit Minor comment `4423345816` on `antigravityStoreQuota.test.ts:13` raised this; it was never answered and the merged test file still has the shape below.
- Current main `3bb1e72a84b5a8428726326715a1a3ba4de8a32c`:
  - `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:274` `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR = path.join(os.homedir(), '.local', 'share', 'opencode')`, and `:286-288` `ANTIGRAVITY_ACCOUNTS_PATHS` contains **both** `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/antigravity-accounts.json` and `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR/antigravity-accounts.json`.
  - `packages/vscode/src/antigravityStoreQuota.test.ts:12-13` only redirects `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` to a scratch dir before importing the providers; the home-directory path is untouched, so a real `~/.local/share/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json` is the second path `resolveAntigravityAuth()` reads.
  - The test's premise is "no accounts file, every sign-in lives only in the store": with a real file present, the file wins (file-first ordering), so the store-only test can pass for the wrong reason and the API-key test's `Not configured` assertion can fail.
  - `:25-27` the `after()` hook removes the scratch dir but never restores the original `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` value.

## Why it matters

These tests are the only pin for the #911 credential-store port. On any machine that actually uses Antigravity (the machines most likely to run them), they can silently test the file path instead of the store path — a green run that proves nothing — or fail spuriously, training developers to ignore them. CI is isolated, which is why this did not surface there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both accounts-file paths are isolated for these tests (e.g. the home-directory data path is also redirected to the scratch tree, via whatever seam the module exposes), so no real `antigravity-accounts.json` can be read.
- [ ] `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (and any other environment the file changes) is restored to its original value after the tests.
- [ ] A test or guard demonstrates the isolation: with a canary accounts file at the home-directory path, the store-only cases still resolve from the store only.
- [ ] The existing store-only and API-key cases still pass.

title: fix(vscode): Antigravity accounts-file entry with an unusable refresh token blocks the credential-store fallback (PR #921)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Finding

In the VS Code Antigravity quota path, an accounts-file entry whose stored refresh token is truthy but unusable — e.g. `||`, or `|project|managed` (empty token segment before the first `|`) — blocks the credential-store fallback that PR #921 added, so a valid store-only sign-in reads as `Not configured`.

## Evidence

- PR #921 (merged, merge commit `4998e715a80c6cdca752dd29e69da58e7d89332f`): https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/921 — CodeRabbit Minor comment `4423345822` on `quotaProviders.ts:1468` raised exactly this; it was never answered and no later commit in the PR addresses it (final head `026629ac9e` fixed only the separate Codex P2, comment `4423533572`).
- Current main `3bb1e72a84b5a8428726326715a1a3ba4de8a32c`, `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`:
  - `:407-420` `parseGoogleRefreshToken('||')`: the string is non-empty, splits to an empty first segment, and returns `refreshToken: null`.
  - `:1157-1182` `resolveAntigravityAuth()` only checks `account?.refreshToken` (the raw string) before returning an auth object, so for `||` it returns an object whose `refreshToken` is `undefined`.
  - `:1471-1473` `fetchAntigravityQuota()` consults the credential store only `if (!auth)` — the unusable file object is truthy, so the store is never read.
  - `:1496` the result then falls to `Not configured` via `!auth.refreshToken`.
  - `:889` the configured-provider listing uses the same truthiness (`resolveAntigravityAuth() || resolveAntigravityStoreAuth(auth)`), so the listing can call the provider configured while the fetch says `Not configured`.
- The web provider does not have the fetch-path form of this defect: `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/antigravity/index.js` collects file and store candidates independently and tries both.

## Why it matters

#911 / PR #921 exist because current opencode-antigravity-auth sign-ins live in the credential store, not the accounts file. A stale or separator-only accounts entry — exactly the kind of leftover a migrated user can have — silently re-breaks that fix in the extension: the Antigravity row disappears as `Not configured` even though a valid OAuth login is in the store, and the configured listing disagrees with the fetch result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fetchAntigravityQuota` falls back to the credential store whenever the accounts-file resolution yields no usable refresh token (no object, or an object with no `refreshToken`), not only when it yields no object.
- [ ] A test pins the divergence: accounts file with a `||` (or empty-token-segment) refresh token plus a valid store OAuth login → quota fetches with the store token and reads as configured.
- [ ] The configured-provider listing agrees with the fetch path for that shape (an unusable file entry alone does not count as configured; file-unusable + store-valid does).
- [ ] Existing Antigravity quota tests (file-first ordering, store-only, API-key-is-not-a-login, store-read-failure) still pass.

title: fix(web): realtime-proxy and persistent-pty WebSocket servers have no maxPayload — a single frame up to the ws default 100 MiB bypasses both proxies' post-assembly caps

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The two remaining proxy WebSocket servers are created with **no `maxPayload`**, so the `ws` default of **100 MiB per message** applies — while both modules advertise byte caps that are only checked *after* the `ws` layer has assembled the whole frame in the web server's memory. A single oversize frame therefore bypasses every cap in both files: it is assembled whole, forwarded whole to the upstream, and only then (realtime-proxy) or never (persistent-pty) does any bound react. This is the same single-frame hole #1082 filed for the dev-tunnel; #1082's dedup note explicitly named these two servers as separate follow-ups, and this issue is that follow-up.

## Evidence (verified on main `587994193`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/realtime-proxy.js:202` — `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, no `maxPayload`. Its caps are post-assembly: `MAX_PENDING_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (`:8`) is accounted in the `message` handler at `:268` after the frame exists; `MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` (`:10`) only closes the pair *after* `upstream.send(data)` at `:258-262` when the peer's `bufferedAmount` is already over.
- `packages/web/server/lib/persistent-pty/runtime.js:47` — `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, no `maxPayload`, and no size check anywhere in the forwarding path (`:74-80`): a client frame of any size is passed straight to `upstream.send`. Terminal input frames are small keystroke/paste chunks by design; nothing needs a 100 MiB allowance.
- The bundled `ws@8.21.0` default is `maxPayload: 100 * 1024 * 1024` (`node_modules/ws/lib/websocket-server.js:74`). Sibling servers set it explicitly: `terminal/runtime.js:199` (64 KiB), `dictation/runtime.js:126` (512 KiB), `guests/surface.js:585` (256 KiB), dev-tunnel tracked in #1082, message-stream tracked in #1108.
- **Laptop probe vs the real modules** (fork at `587994193`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-proxy-maxpayload-20261031/`): with a recording upstream that accepts and counts bytes —
  - realtime-proxy: one single **16 MiB** frame (64× its pending cap) — the upstream received **all 16,777,216 bytes**; the pair was closed 1013 only *after* the whole frame had been assembled and forwarded.
  - persistent-pty: one single **16 MiB** frame — the upstream received **all 16,777,216 bytes** and the client connection stayed **OPEN** (no close, no error).

## Why it matters

Both proxies sit in the long-lived web server process that hosts every session. #962 (realtime-proxy) and #1059 (persistent-pty) bounded the *queues* — bytes accumulated across many messages — but at frame granularity the bound still does not exist: one message of up to 100 MiB is assembled whole by `ws`, then buffered whole again by the upstream socket write, before any cap in either file can fire. The fix is one explicit named constant per server, sized to each surface's legitimate frames (terminal input for the pty proxy; the proxied event/terminal streams for the realtime proxy, whose own pending cap already declares 256 KiB the intended budget).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `realtime-proxy.js`'s `WebSocketServer` is created with an explicit, named `maxPayload` consistent with its declared budgets (at most `MAX_PENDING_BYTES`, or a named constant with the rationale recorded); a frame past it is refused by the `ws` layer (close 1009) instead of being assembled and forwarded.
- [ ] `persistent-pty/runtime.js`'s `WebSocketServer` is created with an explicit, named `maxPayload` sized for terminal input (large pastes included) with the rationale recorded; a frame past it is refused with 1009.
- [ ] Regression tests pin both: a single frame over the cap reaches the upstream as zero bytes and closes the client with 1009; a frame at/under the cap forwards byte-identically; the existing #962/#1059 queue and handshake behaviours are unchanged.
- [ ] The upstream (server→client) direction is checked in the same pass: the `ws` client connections these proxies create toward OpenCode/remotes get the matching treatment, or the code records why upstream frames are already bounded elsewhere.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `maxPayload`: #1082 (open) covers the dev-tunnel server only and names `realtime-proxy.js:202` and `persistent-pty/runtime.js:47` in its dedup note as worth the same check but out of its scope; #1108 (open) covers the message-stream server. #962 (closed) bounded the realtime-proxy's cross-message queue and #1059 (open) covers the persistent-pty pre-open queue and handshake deadline — both account bytes *after* assembly, so neither covers the single-frame assembly bypass verified here.

title: fix(web): message-stream WebSocket server has no maxPayload — a receive-only server assembles client frames up to the ws default 100 MiB and discards them

body:
## Summary

The message-stream WebSocket server (the global + directory event stream every UI client connects to) is created with **no `maxPayload`**, so the `ws` default of **100 MiB per message** applies — on a server that is **receive-only**: no code in the event-stream module ever reads a client message. Every data frame a connected client sends is assembled whole in the long-lived web server's memory by the `ws` layer and then discarded. There is no legitimate client frame to size for: the UI's event pipeline never sends a data frame on this socket (resume state travels in the `lastEventId` query parameter), so the entire 100 MiB allowance is pure exposure.

## Evidence (verified on main `587994193`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/event-stream/runtime.js:74-76` — `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, no `maxPayload`. The bundled `ws@8.21.0` (bun.lock) default is `maxPayload: 100 * 1024 * 1024` (`node_modules/ws/lib/websocket-server.js:74`).
- No consumer exists for client frames: `grep "'message'" packages/web/server/lib/event-stream/*.js` (excluding tests) returns nothing — neither `global-ws-bridge.js`, `directory-ws-bridge.js`, nor `runtime.js` registers a message handler. Outbound traffic is bounded separately (`MESSAGE_STREAM_WS_MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES` 16 MiB in `protocol.js:8`, a send-side `bufferedAmount` guard), but nothing bounds the receive side.
- The UI client sends nothing: `packages/ui/src/sync/event-pipeline.ts` contains no socket `.send(` call; `createMessageStreamWsRuntime`'s connection handler reads only `lastEventId` and `directory` from the query string (`runtime.js:111-112`).
- Sibling servers all set the bound explicitly: `terminal/runtime.js:199` (64 KiB), `dictation/runtime.js:126` (512 KiB), `guests/surface.js:585` (256 KiB). This server — and the two proxy servers named in #1082's dedup note — are the ones that were missed.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (fork at `587994193`, `event-stream/runtime.js` md5 `0274bb7575945cc63cf3f6cd4522a988` identical to main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-eventstream-maxpayload-20261031/`): the real `createMessageStreamWsRuntime`'s server reports `wsServer.options.maxPayload = 104857600`. A real client then sent single frames of 16 MiB and 64 MiB: in both cases the connection stayed **OPEN** (client `readyState` 1, no close, no 1009) and the server process's RSS grew ~32 MiB / ~97 MiB around the sends — each frame was assembled whole before being dropped. A 1 KiB control frame behaved identically (connection open), as expected today.

## Why it matters

This is the highest-traffic WebSocket surface in the product — every open UI holds one of these connections for the life of its session, on the same long-lived server process that hosts every other session. The send path was carefully bounded (16 MiB buffered guard, replay byte limits, heartbeat), but the receive path accepts a 100 MiB in-memory assembly per message, per connection, for data the server provably never reads. A buggy or hostile authenticated client (or a reconnect loop replaying an oversized frame) can repeatedly spike the server's memory with frames that serve no purpose. Because no legitimate client frame exists, the fix can be strict — this is the cheapest of the remaining `maxPayload` gaps to close safely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The message-stream `WebSocketServer` in `event-stream/runtime.js` is created with an explicit, named `maxPayload` sized for a receive-only protocol (e.g. 1 KiB, or another small named constant with the rationale recorded in `event-stream/DOCUMENTATION.md`); a frame past it is refused by the `ws` layer (close 1009) instead of being assembled.
- [ ] Regression tests in `event-stream/runtime.test.js` (or a sibling test file) pin: a single frame over the cap closes the connection with 1009; normal connection/ready/replay flow is unchanged.
- [ ] The fix pass confirms no client (web, desktop, mobile, relay) sends a data frame on either message-stream path (`/api/global/event/ws`, directory stream) — if one is found, the cap is sized above its largest legitimate frame and that frame is named in the docs.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `maxPayload`: only #1082 (open, dev-tunnel server — its dedup note explicitly scopes itself to the tunnel and names other servers as separate follow-ups) and #1017 (closed, dictation reorder buffer — different mechanism). No open or closed issue covers the event-stream server's missing `maxPayload`. Related: #1059 (open) covers the persistent-pty proxy's pre-open queue, not this server.

body:
## Summary

The VS Code extension reads the active color theme's JSON file whole, with no size check, before parsing it for the webview's Shiki highlighting. `packages/vscode/src/shikiThemes.ts:175-192` — `readThemeJsonByLabel` resolves the theme file from an installed extension's `contributes.themes` entry and at :186 runs `const bytes = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(uri)`, then decodes and JSONC-parses the whole buffer. It never calls `vscode.workspace.fs.stat` — the same API the codebase already uses to gate reads elsewhere (e.g. `bridge-fs-helpers-runtime.ts` `readUriAsAttachment` stats and rejects over 20 MB before reading; `gitService.ts` stat-gates the file-diff working-tree read after #1065/#1057).

The theme file's size is controlled by whichever extension provides the user's selected theme — normally a small JSON, but nothing bounds it: a bloated or hostile theme extension, or a theme file that is not really a theme (a large JSON-shaped blob), is buffered, decoded, and char-by-char JSONC-stripped (`stripJsonc`, shikiThemes.ts:9+) in the long-lived extension host. The call runs on the ordinary panel path: `ChatViewProvider.ts:221` and `SessionEditorPanelProvider.ts:284` both call `getWebviewShikiThemes()` when a panel resolves, and it reads the theme twice per call (light + dark variants, shikiThemes.ts:220-223).

## Evidence (verified on main `cdb34837a`)

- `shikiThemes.ts:186`: bare `vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(uri)`; no `stat`, no byte cap anywhere in `readThemeJsonByLabel` or its callers.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (laptop clone at main `cdb34837a`, probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-shiki-theme-cap-20261031/probe2.mjs`, `vscode` module stubbed): a contributed theme whose file is a 128 MiB JSON body was returned in full — the resulting payload's `colors.pad` string measured **134,217,728 characters** — and the stub's `fs.stat` was called **0 times**, confirming nothing size-checks the file before or after the read. (The probe's RSS sampling under bun was unreliable and is not cited; the functional result — the entire 128 MiB value present in the returned payload, twice over for light+dark — is the evidence.)
- A real theme needs kilobytes: built-in and marketplace themes are small JSON files, so a cap in the low megabytes loses nothing legitimate.

## Why it matters

The extension host is the process every other bridge feature lives in; inflating it with an unbounded read of an extension-supplied file is the same failure shape as the bridge fs:read cap (#1068/#1074) and the models.dev catalog cap (#1061/#1067), both fixed by stat-gating or bounding the read. This is the remaining un-gated `workspace.fs.readFile` on a file whose path and contents come from package metadata rather than from the user picking that exact file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readThemeJsonByLabel` size-gates the theme file before reading (stat via `vscode.workspace.fs.stat`, rejecting over an explicit cap sized generously for theme JSON — or a bounded read with a post-read byte check before decode/parse, matching the gitService pattern); an over-cap theme resolves to `null` for that variant (the existing fallback behaviour), never a buffered whole file.
- [ ] Behaviour for ordinary themes is byte-identical: light/dark resolution, the one-side fallback, and the `(Light)`/`(Dark)` name suffixing are unchanged.
- [ ] A regression test (extending the vscode test suite for shikiThemes, with a stubbed `vscode` fs) pins: an over-cap theme file is not read into the payload, and a normal theme still resolves.
- [ ] No new dependency; the gate uses the `vscode.workspace.fs` API already used in this file's package.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `shiki`, `theme readFile cap`, `theme size`: no hits. #1068/#1074 (bridge fs:read) and #1061/#1067 (models.dev catalog) cover different reads in different modules.

body:
## Summary

The skills-catalog scan reads every `SKILL.md` from a cloned catalog repository whole, with no size gate, on both surfaces:

- `packages/web/server/lib/skills-catalog/scan.js:183` — `skillMdContent = await fs.promises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8')` on the sparse-checkout disk path, inside a worker that scans up to 10 files in parallel (`maxParallel = 10`, scan.js:~170).
- `packages/vscode/src/skillsCatalog.ts:350` — `content = await fs.promises.readFile(toFsPath(skillMdPath), 'utf8')`, same scan in the extension host.

The catalog source is a repository the user chooses to browse (any GitHub owner/repo or host) — its contents are not trusted, and a `SKILL.md` can be arbitrarily large: it only needs to sit in a directory in the repo. All the scan uses from the file is its YAML frontmatter (`parseSkillMd` reads name/description); the body is discarded after parsing.

Both implementations already cap the fallback path and not the primary one: when the disk read fails, `git show HEAD:<path>` runs through `runGit`, whose `maxBuffer` is 4 MiB (web `skills-catalog/git.js:11,57`; vscode `skillsCatalog.ts:16,119`) — so a >4 MiB `SKILL.md` fails the fallback closed but is buffered without limit on the fast path, exactly backwards.

## Evidence (verified on main `cdb34837a`)

- `scan.js:183` and `skillsCatalog.ts:350`: bare `readFile` of a clone-controlled path; no `stat` size check anywhere in either scan loop before the read.
- **Laptop probe vs the real web module** (laptop clone at main `cdb34837a`, probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-skills-scan-cap-20261031/probe2.mjs`): a catalog repo containing one skill whose `SKILL.md` is 128 MiB of padding after a normal frontmatter block was scanned through the real `scanSkillsRepository()` (a PATH-level git shim substituted only the clone transport with a local repo; sparse checkout, `ls-files`, the disk read, and `parseSkillMd` all ran as the real code). Result: `ok: true`, the skill returned with its frontmatter description — and the probe process **peak RSS rose ~157 MiB over baseline** (14.4 MiB → 171.8 MiB) for that one file. With the web scan's 10 parallel workers, ten such files multiply the peak.
- The same pattern was fixed for project-icon discover (#1053: stat-gate before read) and the fs preview route stats before reading (`fs/routes.js`); the catalog scan is the remaining clone-content read without a gate.

## Why it matters

Browsing a skills catalog is a casual, repeatable action — a user pastes a repo someone recommended and the server (or the VS Code extension host) clones and scans it. One oversized `SKILL.md` inflates the long-lived server process by roughly the file's size (×10 workers on the web path) every time the catalog is browsed or its cache expires (#998 fixed the vscode cache's retention, not the read size). The scan needs only the frontmatter, so nothing about the feature requires buffering a whole arbitrary file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Web scan (`scan.js`): each `SKILL.md` is size-gated before the disk read (stat-then-read with a re-check, or a bounded streaming read) with an explicit cap sized generously for a skill document; an over-cap file yields a per-skill warning (e.g. `SKILL.md too large`) and no buffered body, and the rest of the catalog still scans.
- [ ] VS Code scan (`skillsCatalog.ts`): the same gate on the disk read, with the same warning behaviour; the extension host never buffers an over-cap `SKILL.md`.
- [ ] The `git show` fallback stays capped (it already is, at 4 MiB via `runGit`) and the two paths agree on outcome for an over-cap file: warning, not silent success-with-full-body or a scan failure.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: an over-cap `SKILL.md` in a scanned repo produces the warning and a completed scan of the remaining skills, on the web scan (and the vscode scan where its test harness allows), and a normal catalog scans byte-identically.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `SKILL.md cap`, `skills scan readFile cap`, `skills-catalog SKILL.md`: no hits. #968/#998 cover the catalog caches' eviction, not the scan's read size; #1053 covers project-icon discover, a different module.

title: fix(web): Linear OAuth broker JSON reads have a deadline but no byte cap — readJsonWithDeadline buffers the whole body from the operator-configured broker

body:
## Summary

The Linear OAuth broker JSON reads have a deadline but no byte cap. `packages/web/server/lib/linear/oauth.js:54-56` — `readJsonWithDeadline` is a bare `return await response.json()`. That one helper feeds every broker read:

- `oauth.js:142-143` — `readJsonResponse` (broker `/start` and `/poll` answers)
- `oauth.js:168` — `registerBrokerTransaction` (POST `{brokerUrl}/start`)
- `oauth.js:231` — `pollBrokerState` (POST `{pending.broker.url}/poll`)
- `oauth.js:127` — the token-endpoint read in `postForm` goes through the same helper

The broker URL is operator-configured, not a fixed SaaS endpoint: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/auth.js:524-532` — `getLinearBrokerUrl()` takes `OPENCHAMBER_LINEAR_BROKER_URL` or the stored `linearBrokerUrl` setting before falling back to the default. A deadline does not bound bytes: a fast or local broker can deliver hundreds of megabytes well inside the 5 s broker deadline (`LINEAR_BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS`, oauth.js:21), and `response.json()` buffers and parses all of it in the server process before any field is looked at.

The codebase already has the bounded reader for exactly this shape — `packages/web/server/lib/shared/response-body.js:13` (`readBoundedResponseText` / `readBoundedResponseBytes`) — and the user-configured-instance reads in GitLab (#1015/#1021) and the guest-declared endpoint reads (#1085) were capped with it. The Linear broker reads were missed; #775 gave these fetches their deadlines but no cap.

## Evidence (verified on main `cdb34837a`)

- `oauth.js:54-56`: `readJsonWithDeadline` returns `await response.json()` — no size check, no `content-length` gate, no bounded reader.
- `auth.js:524-532`: broker URL from env/setting — an operator-supplied endpoint, so its body size is not controlled by Linear.
- **Laptop probe vs the real module** (laptop clone at main `cdb34837a`, probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-linear-broker-cap-20261031/probe.mjs`): a local HTTP stand-in broker answered POST `/start` with a 128 MiB JSON body (`redirectUri` + one large `pad` string); the real `startAuthorization()` completed the flow while the probe process's **peak RSS rose ~496 MiB over baseline** (151.7 MiB → 647.4 MiB peak) — the body was buffered and parsed whole, several times the body's own size in memory, despite being a response whose only used field is a short URL string.
- The poll path repeats this every 1.5 s while a user waits on authorization (`pollAuthorizationBroker`, oauth.js:263+), so a hostile or wedged broker gets repeated chances to inflate the server.

## Why it matters

The broker is the component a self-hoster points OpenChamber at to complete Linear OAuth. A compromised, misconfigured, or merely buggy broker — or anything that can answer on the configured URL — can grow the OpenChamber server process by hundreds of megabytes per response with a single fast loopback/LAN answer, no slow-loris needed, and the authorization poll repeats the exposure. Every other operator-configured endpoint family in this server has been given a byte cap for this reason; this one is the remaining outlier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Broker (`/start`, `/poll`) and token-endpoint JSON reads in `linear/oauth.js` go through a bounded read (e.g. `readBoundedResponseText` from `lib/shared/response-body.js`) with an explicit cap sized for a small OAuth JSON payload; a body over the cap fails as a `LinearOAuthError` (broker: `LINEAR_BROKER_FAILED`, token: `LINEAR_OAUTH_FAILED`) instead of being parsed.
- [ ] The deadline semantics from #775 are unchanged: a body read cut off by the deadline still surfaces as the existing timeout errors.
- [ ] Regression tests in `linear/oauth.test.js` pin: an over-cap broker `/start` body is rejected without parsing, an over-cap `/poll` body is rejected, and a normal small broker flow still completes.
- [ ] Well-formed small responses behave byte-identically: redirect-URI validation, poll complete/failed handling, and token parsing are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `linear byte cap`, `linear response.json cap`, `broker response cap`: no hits. #775 (closed) added the deadlines to these same fetches and did not add a byte cap; the GitLab (#1015/#1021) and guest OAuth (#1085) caps cover different modules.

body:
## Summary

`packages/web/server/lib/event-stream/delta-coalescer.js` contains a **raw NUL byte (U+0000) embedded literally in the source** as the value of `KEY_SEPARATOR` (delta-coalescer.js:33, used at :155 to join key parts). The byte sits at file offset 1763 — inside the first 8000 bytes — so Git's binary heuristic classifies the whole file as binary. The separator value itself is a sound choice (NUL cannot appear in the ids being joined); the defect is only that it is written as a literal control byte instead of the escape sequence `'\0'` / `'\^@'`.

## Evidence (verified on main `17966b1d3`)

- Byte scan of the repo: `delta-coalescer.js` is the **only** tracked `.js`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mjs`/`.json`/`.md` file containing a NUL byte (scan over `git ls-files`, 1 NUL at offset 1763).
- Line 33 is `const KEY_SEPARATOR = '<NUL>';` (shown as `'^@'` under `cat -v`); line 155 joins key parts with it.
- **Git experiment** (scratch repo in /tmp, the real file committed, then one constant changed): `git diff` prints `Binary files a/delta-coalescer.js and b/delta-coalescer.js differ` — no textual diff at all.
- GNU grep on the working tree likewise reports `binary file matches` and suppresses line content for this file, which is how the byte was found: a routine `grep -rn` over `lib/event-stream/` flagged the file as binary.
- GitHub's web UI uses the same NUL heuristic, so PR diffs touching this file render as binary there too.

## Why it matters

The delta coalescer is on the hot streaming path (it was performance-tuned in #3660 and its env parsing fixed in #725) — exactly the kind of file whose changes most need line-by-line review. Today any change to it is unreviewable in `git diff` and in the GitHub PR view, and invisible to text searches that skip binary files: a regression — or anything worse — could land in this file without appearing in a diff. The fix is a one-line, behaviour-identical change of the literal byte to an escape sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `KEY_SEPARATOR` in `delta-coalescer.js` is written as an escape sequence (`'\0'` or `'\^@'`) with the identical runtime value; no raw control byte remains in the file (`grep -P '\x00'` / byte scan finds none).
- [ ] `git diff` on a subsequent edit to the file renders a textual diff, and the file no longer scans as binary.
- [ ] Existing `delta-coalescer.test.js` tests pass unchanged (the joined keys are byte-identical, so coalescing behaviour cannot change).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `delta-coalescer`, `NUL`, and `binary`: no issue covers this. #725 fixed the coalesce-window env parsing in the same file but did not touch the separator literal.

## Summary

The tunnel auth cookie parser throws `URIError` on any malformed percent-encoded cookie value — including values in cookies that have nothing to do with the tunnel session. `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/tunnel-auth.js:26` runs a bare `decodeURIComponent(value || '')` inside `parseCookies` (tunnel-auth.js:11-28) with no `try/catch`.
