body:
## Summary

Two more Linear store readers read their files whole, synchronously, with no size gate and no non-regular-file protection — the residual class fixed for the Linear *auth* reader in #1615, in two sibling files that issue does not touch:

- `packages/web/server/lib/linear/mapping.js` — `readStoredLinearMapping` (:102) does `fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')` (:109) for `linear-mapping.json` (the workspace → project-path mapping, `mappingFile()` :15-17), and `setStoredLinearMapping` (:125) repeats the same ungated sync read (:133) as the base for every mapping write.
- `packages/web/server/lib/linear/status.js` — `readRecords` (:147) does `fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')` (:154) for `linear-session-status.json` (which sessions already got their Linear status comments, `statusFile()` :21-23). It runs inside `postLinearSessionStatus` (:268) on the session-status posting path.

Neither reader uses the house standard: `readBoundedFile` / `readBoundedFileSync` in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` (:73 / :117) — open once with `O_NONBLOCK`, judge from the opened handle, refuse non-regular files, buffer at most cap + 1 byte. #1615 covers only `lib/linear/auth.js`'s `readJsonFileStrict` (and the lenient reader it backs); the mapping and session-status readers are separate code in separate files and are covered nowhere.

Because these reads are **synchronous**, the failure mode is worse than the async sibling stores (#1607–#1614): a blocked read does not hang one request or one store lock — it freezes the managed server's only event-loop thread.

## Verified this run (laptop probe against the real modules, main 68c9f11c54)

Code read on `origin/main` 68c9f11c54f25fcff7e2f7c69a71d16725ac9e1f (laptop `git show origin/main:`, cross-checked with `gh api`), plus a probe on the laptop (probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-linear-mapstatus-20261104/`) running the real `mapping.js` / `status.js` / `auth.js` extracted verbatim from `origin/main` (only `status.js`'s unrelated network import `issues.js` was stubbed in the harness; the code under test is byte-identical), each case run ×2 with identical results:

- **Oversized, mapping:** a 33 MiB `linear-mapping.json` (schema-shaped object with a 33 MiB pad value) was read and parsed whole by `readStoredLinearMapping` — settled normally, no size rejection.
- **Oversized, status:** a 33 MiB `linear-session-status.json` (one 33 MiB session-id key with a valid record) was read and parsed whole on the real `postLinearSessionStatus` path (planted valid auth + `linearSessionComments` settings; the call completed with its normal `not-started` answer after the read).
- **FIFO, both:** with either file replaced by a FIFO, the reader printed its pre-read marker and never returned — the process had to be killed by an external 10 s timeout in both runs. The sync `readFileSync` blocks in `open()`, so nothing else in the server can run meanwhile.
- **Control:** ordinary small files of both shapes read back exactly.
- No bounded cases exist in the suites: `mapping.test.js`, `status.test.js` and `status-runtime.test.js` contain no oversized / FIFO / non-regular / bounded test (grep-verified).

## Why it matters

- **Availability, server-wide:** one non-regular or runaway file at either path freezes the whole managed server (sync read on the event loop), not just the Linear surface — `readStoredLinearMapping` runs on the Linear mapping read/write routes (exported via `lib/linear/index.js`), and `readRecords` runs whenever a session-status comment is considered.
- **Memory:** the validators run only *after* the whole file is in memory, so they bound what is kept, not what is read; an oversized file is buffered and parsed whole on every read/write of the mapping and on every status post attempt.
- **Semantics that must not flip:** today a missing or empty file reads as the empty mapping / `{}` records, and a malformed file throws `LinearMappingError` / `LinearSessionStatusError` with code `MALFORMED`. An over-cap or non-regular file must follow the malformed path — never read as empty: `setStoredLinearMapping` writes from the read base, so a false empty read would let the next mapping save silently erase every workspace's project mapping (the same false-first-run hazard #1615 and #1614 pin for their stores).

## Why the caps are safe (write-side clamps)

- `linear-session-status.json`: records are pruned to `MAX_SESSION_STATUS_RECORDS = 500` on every write (`status.js:9`, `pruneSessionStatusRecords` :181, applied in `writeRecords`); each record is a session id key plus an organization id and three booleans — a legitimate file is well under 100 KB.
- `linear-mapping.json`: workspaces keyed by organization, each holding a default project path and a team → path record of filesystem paths — bounded by the number of Linear workspaces/teams a user connects; a legitimate file is in the KB range.
A named cap per file (1 MiB already gives >10× headroom over the status file's computed maximum) loses nothing legitimate; document the computation in code the way the sibling fixes do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three read sites (`mapping.js` `readStoredLinearMapping` and the read inside `setStoredLinearMapping`; `status.js` `readRecords`) read through a bounded, handle-judged read (`readBoundedFileSync` in `lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, or equivalent): at most cap + 1 byte is ever buffered, and a FIFO / directory / other non-regular file at either path is refused promptly instead of blocking the server's event loop.
- [ ] Each cap is a named constant documented in code with its headroom over the legitimate maximum from the write-side clamps above.
- [ ] Existing semantics preserved exactly: missing/empty file still reads as the empty mapping / `{}`; malformed, over-cap, and non-regular files throw the existing `MALFORMED` errors — an over-cap file never silently reads as a valid empty state, so a mapping write can never be based on a false empty read.
- [ ] Regression tests in `mapping.test.js` and the status suites: oversized file refused without being parsed whole, FIFO/non-regular target refused without hanging, at-cap and ordinary files read unchanged, missing file unchanged.
- [ ] No other Linear behaviour changes; `auth.js` (covered by #1615), the write paths, pruning, and atomic writes are untouched.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues and `gh search issues` for `linear mapping file`, `readStoredLinearMapping`, `Linear session status`, `linear-mapping.json`, `linear mapping readFileSync`: no covering issue. #1615 covers `lib/linear/auth.js`'s readers only (linear-auth.json + the shared settings.json); #1598 covered the Linear *teams list* page cap, a different surface. The mapping and session-status file readers are covered nowhere.

body:
## Problem

`packages/web/server/lib/relay/key-store.js` reads the host relay identity file whole, with no size gate and no regular-file check:

- `key-store.js:68-71` — `readStore` does `raw = await fsPromises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8')` on `<data-dir>/relay-identity.json` (the `0600` file holding the relay signing and encryption keypairs, private JWKs included — see the header at `:1-14`).
- Every operation funnels through this read: `getOrCreate` calls `readStore` up to twice per call (`:127`, `:131`), and `reset` calls it again (`:151`).
- All of those operations are serialized behind one promise queue (`:61-66`): the push relay and the private relay both ask for the signing key at boot through this store (comment at `:58-60`).
- A legitimate identity file is two JWK pairs — a few KB at most. There is no cap at any layer.

Unlike the house standard: `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` (`readBoundedFile`, `:41-70`) opens with `O_NONBLOCK`, judges the handle's stat (rejecting non-regular files), and reads in chunks up to an explicit cap (default 8 MiB). Sibling stores in this series: #1607, #1608, #1609, #1610, #1490. This store was noted as checked-not-filed in the 2026-11-04 17:50 CST creator run and is filed now with probe evidence.

## Verified this run (main `9cef4f4c1e95`)

Code read ×2 independent routes (`gh api` raw read and laptop `git show` on `origin/main`), plus a laptop probe against the real `createRelayKeyStore` extracted from `origin/main` (probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-relay-keystore-ungated-20261104/` on the laptop):

- Oversized ×2: a 33.5 MB `relay-identity.json` (valid shape, 33,554,432-char pad inside the signing JWK) was parsed whole and the stored pair returned — no size rejection.
- FIFO: with `relay-identity.json` replaced by a FIFO, `getOrCreate('signing', …)` never settled within the 3 s probe window. Because every caller serializes behind the one queue (`:61-66`), that one stuck read wedges both relays' key access, including boot.

## Why it matters

- Availability at boot: the identity read sits on the serialized path both relays use to obtain their signing key; a non-regular file at the identity path hangs key access indefinitely instead of failing with the store's otherwise-strict error discipline (the file's own header, `:12-14`, insists corrupt/unreadable files throw rather than read as first run — a hang is neither).
- Memory: an oversized identity file is buffered and parsed whole with no bound.
- The strictness already in this file (throw on corrupt, never silently mint a replacement key) makes the missing gate conspicuous: size/type judgement is the one input validation the read does not do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The identity read judges the file before/while reading: non-regular files (FIFO, device, directory) fail promptly with the store's strict error style instead of hanging the serialized queue, and content past an explicit named cap is refused rather than buffered whole.
- [ ] The cap is sized to the legitimate shape (two JWK pairs) and named in code, mirroring `readBoundedFile`'s discipline or reusing it.
- [ ] Existing semantics preserved exactly: ENOENT reads as `{}` (first run), corrupt JSON / schema-mismatched content throws the existing `Relay identity file is corrupt` error, legacy settings migration and `reset()` behaviour unchanged (`key-store.test.js` behaviour).
- [ ] Regression tests cover: oversized identity file refused, FIFO/non-regular path refused promptly (no hang), and a normal identity file still loads and round-trips through `getOrCreate`/`reset`.

Filed by the new-issue-creator fleet run (agent `new-issue-creator-openchamber`), 2026-11-04. Sibling filings in the same ungated-read series: #1607, #1608, #1609, #1610, #1490.

body:
Found by the #1530 phase-2 inventory (design #1528). Surface: `packages/web/server/lib/github/pr-status.js`, per-head pull list.

## The read

`pr-status.js:791` (`findByBranch`-style resolution) calls `safeListPulls` with `{ state, head: '<owner>:<branch>', per_page: 100 }` and treats the returned page as the whole set: `pickPreferred` picks an open match from it, and the historical pick sorts the page by number and takes the newest. There is no page 2, no Link/`total_count` check, and no completeness flag on this path.

Contrast with the same file's repo-level list (`getRepoPulls`, :443/:459), which carries `complete: prs.length < 100` and whose consumers (:748, :765, :876) only treat a miss as authoritative when the list was complete — that path is dispositioned (signals). The per-head path has no equivalent guard, so >100 PRs ever opened from one head (across states, `state: 'all'` when history is included) can hide the relevant PR and the status resolves to "no PR" on a prefix.

## What done looks like

- The per-head read either paginates under a named cap with the collections discipline, or returns a completeness flag its consumers honour the way `getRepoPulls` consumers do (a miss on an incomplete list is not authoritative).
- A test pins the over-page case (matching PR past page 1).

## Acceptance criteria

- The per-head read in `pr-status.js` either paginates under a named cap with the collections discipline, or returns a completeness flag its consumers honour the way `getRepoPulls` consumers do (a miss on an incomplete list is not authoritative).
- A test pins the over-page case (matching PR past page 1).

# fix(ui): sessionGoalActions fitObjective cuts can split a surrogate pair — the UI twin of server #1909 slices the distilled, ignoreLimit, head and tail cuts unguarded, and the result is written to the goal objective file

## Evidence (main d5955751ce22c273c1987149b586c43064871499)

`packages/ui/src/lib/sessionGoalActions.ts`, `fitObjective` (:77-91) — every cut is a raw slice with no surrogate-pair guard:

- :82 — ignoreLimit branch: `raw.slice(0, limit)` with `limit = SESSION_GOAL_CHAR_LIMIT_MAX` 1,000,000 (`sessionGoalLimits.ts`).
- :86 — distilled branch: `distilled.slice(0, limit)`.
- :90 — head/tail fallback: `` `${raw.slice(0, half)}${TRIM_MARKER}${raw.slice(-half)}` `` — the head can end in a lone high surrogate and the tail can start with a lone low surrogate.
- A fourth unguarded cut follows in `setSessionGoal`: the inline objective at :284, `objective.slice(0, useUIStore.getState().sessionGoalObjectiveCharLimit)`, applied to the fitObjective result when the objective file write fails.

The result is persisted, not transient: `setSessionGoal` (:250) passes the fitted objective to `writeGoalObjectiveFile(sessionId, objective)` (:275), which stores it as the goal's objective file, and the inline form rides session metadata on every event. The UI cut runs **first**: once the UI has cut the text to (or below) the limit, the server stores what it receives — the server-side pair guards (#1909/#1970 in `session-goal/create.js` `fitObjective`, #1949 in `objectives.js` `clampContent`) never re-cut it, so a lone surrogate produced here is baked into the stored objective as U+FFFD at the first UTF-8 encoding. The UI has a pair-safe precedent in `components/chat/message/parts/toolDiffPreview.ts:33-34`, but `fitObjective` does not use one, and `sessionGoalActions.test.ts` has no fitObjective straddle test.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the verbatim real function, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-uifitobjective-surrogate-20261108/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun), running `fitObjective` copied verbatim from sessionGoalActions.ts at main d5955751c with only its external dependencies stubbed (store limit, `distillGoalObjective`, toast/i18n, and the real `SESSION_GOAL_CHAR_LIMIT_MAX` = 1,000,000).

- Fallback head/tail at limit 1,000 (`SESSION_GOAL_CHAR_LIMIT_MIN`), distiller returning null, U+1F600 straddling both cuts: result contains lone surrogates at both ends, exactly **2 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- Distilled branch at limit 1,000, distilled text straddling the cut: result ends in a lone high surrogate, **1 U+FFFD** after encode.
- ignoreLimit branch: 999,999 chars + U+1F600 straddle at 1,000,000: result ends in a lone high surrogate, **1 U+FFFD** after encode.
- Controls clean both times: ASCII over-limit fallback returns a clean excerpt; an under-limit objective containing an emoji is returned unchanged.

## Why it matters

Goal objectives are exactly the kind of long pasted text (plans, specs, composer prompts — the function's own comment names these) that contains emoji and other astral characters. The condensation exists to preserve the objective's intent for the auditor; instead, a straddling character corrupts both preserved ends and the corruption is written to the objective file, where every later read, audit and restore sees U+FFFD instead of the user's character.

## Acceptance criteria

- All four UI cuts — `fitObjective`'s ignoreLimit slice, distilled slice, and head/tail fallback slices in sessionGoalActions.ts, plus the inline `objective.slice(0, …)` in `setSessionGoal` — never produce a lone surrogate: a cut landing inside a surrogate pair moves to the pair boundary (drop the partial character), matching the server behaviour from #1909/#1970.
- Regression tests in `sessionGoalActions.test.ts` (or equivalent) cover each branch with an astral straddle: no lone surrogate, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode, trim marker intact on the fallback branch, results within the applicable limit; ASCII and under-limit controls unchanged.
- Existing UI tests still pass.

## Evidence (main d5955751ce22c273c1987149b586c43064871499)

`packages/ui/src/lib/messages/messageMarkdown.ts`:

- `excerptMarkdown` (:6-12) truncates over-limit text to a head + marker + tail: `text.slice(0, head)` and `text.slice(-tail)`, where `head`/`tail` are computed from the limit and the `'\n\n[Content omitted]\n\n'` marker (:8-10). Neither cut has a surrogate-pair guard: a cut landing between the halves of an astral character leaves the head ending in a lone high surrogate (U+D800–U+DBFF) and/or the tail starting with a lone low surrogate (U+DC00–U+DFFF).
- The excerpt is model-facing, not display-only:
  - `packages/ui/src/lib/goalWriter.ts:227/:233` — conversation turns excerpted at `USER_FIELD_LIMIT` 1,500 (:207) and `ASSISTANT_FIELD_LIMIT` 2,000 (:208) and sent to the goal-writer model.
  - `packages/ui/src/lib/sessionTitle.ts:94-99` — turns excerpted at 4,000 for title generation; `formatContextMessage(item, 2000)` at :95.
  - `formatContextMessage` (:89-95) and `formatMessageText` (:54, :76, :80) route code quotes, file quotes, chat quotes, PR comments and terminal output through the same excerpt; the result is quoted into new messages and session exports (`exportSession.ts:85`, `guests/actions.ts:88`).
- The server twin of this exact pattern was already fixed as a bug: `session-assist/context.js` excerpt (#1911) now routes its cuts through `dropSplitHead`/`dropSplitTail`. The UI helper has no equivalent, and there is no `messageMarkdown.test.ts`.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the verbatim real function, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-uiexcerpt-surrogate-20261108/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun), running `excerptMarkdown` copied verbatim from messageMarkdown.ts at main d5955751c.

- At every real limit (1,500 / 2,000 / 4,000, plus 100): a U+1F600 straddling the head cut → result contains a lone surrogate and exactly **1 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip; a U+1F600 straddling the tail cut → same (lone low surrogate at the tail start, 1 U+FFFD).
- Controls clean both times: pure-ASCII over-limit inputs return exact-limit excerpts with no lone surrogates and no U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

Chat and quoted context routinely contain emoji and other astral characters. When a long turn or quote is excerpted for the goal writer, the title generator, or a quoted-context message, a straddling character is corrupted to U+FFFD at the first JSON/UTF-8 encoding and one real character is lost from each affected end — the model (and any reader of the quoted message/export) sees damaged text at exactly the head and tail the excerpt exists to preserve.

## Acceptance criteria

- `excerptMarkdown` never returns a lone surrogate: a head cut landing inside a surrogate pair drops the partial character (backs off to the pair boundary) and a tail cut landing inside a pair advances past the low surrogate, matching the server's `dropSplitHead`/`dropSplitTail` behaviour (#1911).
- New tests (a `messageMarkdown.test.ts` or equivalent) cover: an astral character straddling the head cut and one straddling the tail cut at a real limit (1,500 or 4,000) — no lone surrogate, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode, marker intact; ASCII over-limit controls keep the exact limit length apart from a dropped partial character; under-limit inputs returned unchanged.

# fix(ui): useUIStore clamps can split a surrogate pair — context-tab labels (120), custom fonts (100) and vim mappings (10,000) are sliced with no pair guard and persisted by the zustand persist partialize

## Evidence (main d5955751ce22c273c1987149b586c43064871499)

All sites are in `packages/ui/src/stores/useUIStore.ts`, and every value below is persisted: the store's `partialize` includes `contextPanelByDirectory`, `customUiFont`, `customMonoFont` and `fileEditorVimMappings`, so a split pair is written to the persisted UI-store document and re-read on every launch.

1. **Context-panel tab labels** — `normalizeContextTabLabel` (:315-328) returns `trimmed.slice(0, CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH)` with `CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 120` (:231) and no pair guard. It normalizes `label` and `sessionTitleFallback` both when a tab is created (`createContextPanelTab`, :389-390) and when persisted tabs are rehydrated (`sanitizeContextPanelTabs`, :496-497). Labels derive from session titles and file names, which routinely contain emoji and other astral characters.
2. **Custom fonts** — `setCustomUiFont` (:2897) and `setCustomMonoFont` (:2901) store `family.slice(0, 100)` with no pair guard.
3. **Vim mappings** — `setFileEditorVimMappings` (:3536) stores `value.slice(0, 10_000)` with no pair guard; its own comment (:3535) says "Same cap as the settings registry field".

The server twins of sites 2 and 3 were already fixed: issue #2028 routed the settings-helpers font (100), vimMappings (10,000) and shortcut cuts through a pair-safe clip. The UI store cuts **first**, before any value reaches the server sanitizer, so the client-side persisted copy still carries the lone surrogate — the same client/server twin shape as #2029 (UI gitlabReferences vs server previewBody) and #2031 (client PWA clamps vs server endpoint). Site 1 has no server twin at all.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs verbatim real code, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-uistore-surrogate-20261108/probe.ts` on the laptop. `normalizeContextTabLabel` and the 120 constant were extracted verbatim from `useUIStore.ts` (:231, :315-328) with `sed`; the font and vim cuts are the setters' exact one-line expressions (`family.slice(0, 100)`, `value.slice(0, 10_000)`). Run under `bun`.

- Label straddle (119×`a` + U+1F600 + tail): result length 120, **ends with lone U+D83D**, exactly **1 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- Font straddle (99×`f` + U+1F600 + tail): length 100, ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD.
- Vim-mappings straddle (9,999×`v` + U+1F600 + tail): length 10,000, ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD.
- Controls clean both times: ASCII over-limit inputs return exact-length cuts with no surrogates; an under-limit label (`hi 😀`) returns the pair intact.

## Why it matters

These are user-visible, persisted strings: a context tab whose label came from an emoji-bearing session title, a pasted font-family name, or a long vim-mappings blob can be stored ending in a lone high surrogate. The persisted JSON carries it as `\ud83d`, and every later display/encode renders U+FFFD — a corrupted character baked into the user's saved UI state, re-applied on each launch because `sanitizeContextPanelTabs` re-clamps with the same unguarded function instead of repairing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `normalizeContextTabLabel`, `setCustomUiFont`, `setCustomMonoFont` and `setFileEditorVimMappings` in `useUIStore.ts` never store a value ending in a lone high surrogate: a cut landing inside a surrogate pair drops the partial character (the pair-safe clip pattern already used elsewhere in the UI, e.g. `clipPairSafe` in the PWA paths and `OpenChamberVisualSettings`).
- Regression tests cover each of the four cuts: an astral character straddling the cap (stored value ends on a pair boundary, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode), ASCII over-limit controls (exact length apart from the dropped partial character), and under-limit inputs unchanged.
- A rehydration case is covered: a persisted context tab whose label straddles 120 comes back through `sanitizeContextPanelTabs` pair-safe.

# fix(web): spaces output tails can split a surrogate pair — space-setup's keptOutputOf slices the last 32,768 chars with no pair guard and the result is persisted in the space record; exec-http's tail() and the Docker place tails have the same unguarded slice(-N)

## Evidence (main d5955751ce22c273c1987149b586c43064871499)

Primary, persisted site — `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-setup.js`:

- `keptOutputOf` (:63-71) keeps the tail of a setup command's combined stdout/stderr: lines are capped at `MAX_KEPT_OUTPUT_LINES` 200 (:38), then the joined text is cut with `kept.slice(-MAX_KEPT_OUTPUT_CHARACTERS)` at :70, where `MAX_KEPT_OUTPUT_CHARACTERS = 32 * 1024` (:39). There is no surrogate-pair guard: when the cut lands between the halves of an astral character, the kept text **begins** with a lone low surrogate (U+DC00–U+DFFF).
- The result is not transient: `runOne` returns it as `output` (:103/:110), and on failure `runAll` persists it via `remember(spaceId, { state: 'failed', ..., ...outcome })` (:128) into the space record (`records.update`). It is served back to clients by `outputOf` (:175) through `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/journey.js:1063`.

Sibling sites with the identical unguarded tail pattern in the same subsystem:

- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/exec-http.js:27` — `export const tail = (text) => String(text ?? '').trim().slice(-ERROR_TAIL_CHARACTERS)` (2,000). Used to build `SpaceError` messages in `space-server.js:101/:131/:170`, `gatekeeper-channel.js:97/:126/:137`, and imported by `code-in.js`, `code-out.js`, `host-git.js`, `space-opencode.js`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/places/docker-setup.js:40` — `tailOf` slices `-OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS` (4,000); its result is carried as the `output` of the `docker_setup_failed` `SpaceError` (:118).
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/places/docker-tools.js:91` — `result.stderr.trim().slice(-ERROR_TAIL_CHARACTERS)` in an install-failure message.
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/places/docker-disk.js:132` — `result.stderr.trim().slice(-500)` in a `{ state: 'failed', message }` result.

Guarded siblings in the same codebase show the intended pattern: `bounded-output-accumulator.js` routes its tail through `dropSplitTailHead`, `guests/service.js` guards its `slice(-maxChars)` tail, and `routing/history.js` uses `dropSplitTail` for tail excerpts. The spaces tails above have no equivalent.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real modules, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-spaces-tail-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `keptOutputOf` from `space-setup.js` and the real `tail` from `exec-http.js` at main d5955751c.

- `keptOutputOf` straddle (one char + U+1F600 + filler sized so the 32,768-char tail cut lands inside the pair): output length 32,768, **first code unit U+DE00 (lone low surrogate)**, exactly **1 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- `tail` straddle (input length 2,002, cut at 2,000 lands inside U+1F600): output length 2,000, **first code unit U+DE00**, exactly **1 U+FFFD** after UTF-8 encode.
- Controls clean both times: pure-ASCII over-limit inputs return exact-length tails with no surrogates and no U+FFFD; an under-limit `hello 😀` input returns the pair intact.

## Why it matters

Setup commands run project/agent code, whose output routinely contains emoji and other astral characters (test reporters, build tools, CLI spinners-as-text). When a failing command's output is long enough, the one diagnostic the user is shown — persisted in the space record and re-served on every later read — starts with a corrupted character (U+FFFD baked in at the first JSON/UTF-8 encoding), and the first real character of the kept window is lost. The Docker/exec-http error tails corrupt the same way in the messages users copy into bug reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- `keptOutputOf` (space-setup.js), `tail` (exec-http.js), `tailOf` (docker-setup.js), and the inline tails in docker-tools.js:91 and docker-disk.js:132 never return text whose first code unit is a lone low surrogate: a cut landing inside a surrogate pair drops the partial character (advances past the low surrogate), matching the existing `dropSplitTail`-style helpers.
- Regression tests cover: an astral character straddling each tail cut (result starts on a pair boundary, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode), ASCII over-limit controls (exact length preserved apart from the dropped partial character), and under-limit inputs returned unchanged.
- The persisted failed-setup output path (`runAll` → record → `outputOf`) is covered by at least one of those tests, so the stored record is verified, not just the helper.

body:
## Defect

The managed OpenCode `stderrTail` diagnostic is produced by byte tails that never align their start to a UTF-8 boundary, so a log line whose character straddles the tail start is destroyed and the diagnostic begins with U+FFFD.

Sites:

1. `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-opencode-state.js` — `readLogTail` (:197-205) computes the tail as `readLogSince(logPath, Math.max(offset, size - maxBytes))`: it jumps to an arbitrary byte offset in the middle of the log file. `readLogSince` (:138-176) meticulously holds back a *trailing* incomplete UTF-8 sequence (`incompleteUtf8TailLength`, :110-126) so a split character is re-read whole on the next poll — but nothing aligns the *leading* edge, so a start offset inside a character decodes that character's continuation bytes to U+FFFD. `readLogSince`'s offset contract cannot fix this from inside: for `readLogTail` the caller chose the start.
2. `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/lifecycle.js` — `getBoundedTextTail` (:119-123) re-cuts the already-decoded string at a raw byte offset: `Buffer.from(String(value)).subarray(buffer.byteLength - maxBytes).toString()`. It is applied to the `readLogTail` result and to the child's accumulated `stderrTail` at :284, :617 and :728 (`MANAGED_STDERR_TAIL_MAX_BYTES` = 32 KiB, :116), so even a clean `readLogTail` result can be split again here.

The aligned house pattern exists in `guests/clone.js:249-262` and `terminal/runtime.js:151-153` (drop leading continuation bytes after a byte tail cut).

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main b8b7f08b8)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-runcommand-bytetail-20261108/probe3.mjs`, importing the real `readLogTail` from the laptop primary; log file = 100×`a` + `€` (3 bytes) + N×`b`, `readLogTail(path, 0, 64)`. Run twice, identical both times:

- Tail start at the €'s 2nd byte (N=62): `len=64, 2× U+FFFD` at the head — the € is destroyed.
- Tail start exactly at the € (N=61): `€` preserved whole, 0× U+FFFD.
- ASCII control (same byte lengths): 0× U+FFFD, clean.

Site 2 is the verbatim subarray pattern on code inspection: `Buffer.from(s).subarray(len - 32768).toString()` starts mid-character whenever byte `len - 32768` is a continuation byte, by construction.

Dedup: no open or closed issue mentions `readLogTail` alignment (REST issue search, 2026-11-08). #1794 bounded `readLogSince`'s reads and added the trailing hold-back in the same file; #1687 fixed per-poll split corruption in the drain path. Neither touches the tail-start jump or `getBoundedTextTail`.

## Why it matters

`stderrTail` is the diagnostic surfaced when the managed OpenCode fails to start, exits early, or is adopted/restarted — the first thing a user or a fleet agent reads to learn why. OpenCode logs carry non-ASCII content (paths, localized errors, model output), and a 32 KiB tail start lands inside a multi-byte character with probability proportional to that content; when it does, the tail opens with U+FFFD garbage and the character is lost from the record (`state.lastManagedOpenCodeProcess`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `readLogTail`'s returned text never starts with U+FFFD produced by its own start offset: align the start forward past leading continuation bytes (or read from an aligned offset), without changing `readLogSince`'s offset/trailing-hold-back contract for its streaming callers.
- `getBoundedTextTail` in lifecycle.js aligns its byte cut the same way.
- Regression tests: a log file with a multi-byte character straddling the `size - maxBytes` start yields a tail with no leading U+FFFD and loses at most that one character; the same for `getBoundedTextTail` over a long string (export it for tests if needed, following the module's existing test-export pattern); aligned and ASCII controls unchanged.
- Existing opencode lifecycle / managed-state tests still pass.

## Defect

`packages/web/server/lib/spaces/run-command.js` keeps byte windows of child output with no UTF-8 boundary alignment, in two places, and the kept bytes are decoded with `Buffer.concat(...).toString('utf8')` at close (:303-304). When a window cut lands inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, the tail starts with that character's continuation bytes and decodes to U+FFFD — the character itself is destroyed in the only output the caller ever sees.

Sites:

1. The `keepTail` window, :231-238 — `chunks[0] = chunks[0].subarray(held - maxOutputBytes)` (:236) trims the oldest chunk at a raw byte offset.
2. The `keepAtExit` stderr read-back, `readErrorFile` :253-256 — `fs.readSync(errorFile.fd, kept, 0, kept.length, size - kept.length)` reads the last `maxOutputBytes` of the stderr file starting at a raw byte offset; the bytes are pushed into `stderrChunks` and decoded the same way.

Production callers: `code-out.js:959` and `:1790` run `git apply` / `git apply --check` with `keepTail: true` (the :1790 call also `keepAtExit: true`, so it exercises site 2), tail 64 KiB (`APPLY_OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES`, code-out.js:65); `code-out.js:1159` parses a keepTail result; `space-setup.js:103` keeps a 256 KiB tail (`OUTPUT_WINDOW_BYTES`, :37) of setup command output shown to the user. These tails are failure diagnostics for non-ASCII path names and localized git output — exactly the content that carries multi-byte characters.

The house pattern already exists twice in the same codebase: `guests/clone.js:249-262` drops leading continuation bytes after its byte tail cut ("The byte cut can land inside a multi-byte character; drop leading continuation bytes so the tail starts on a UTF-8 boundary instead of decoding its first character as U+FFFD"), and `terminal/runtime.js:151-153` aligns its scrollback suffix the same way. `run-command.js` is the unaligned remainder.

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main b8b7f08b8)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-runcommand-bytetail-20261108/probe.mjs` + `probe2.mjs`, importing the real `runCommand` from the laptop primary, child = `node -e` writing 100×`a` + `€` (3 bytes) + N×`b`, `maxOutputBytes: 64`, `keepTail: true`. Run twice, identical both times:

- Window start at the €'s 2nd byte (N=62): stdout `len=64, first code points [U+FFFD, U+FFFD, U+0062], 2× U+FFFD` — the € is destroyed.
- Window start at the €'s 3rd byte (N=63): `1× U+FFFD` at the head.
- Window start exactly at the € (N=61): `€` preserved whole, 0× U+FFFD.
- Window start exactly after the € (N=64): clean `b` head, 0× U+FFFD.
- ASCII control (same byte lengths): 0× U+FFFD, clean.
- The `keepAtExit: true` stderr path reproduces identically: straddle → 2× U+FFFD, offset-by-2 → 1× U+FFFD.

Dedup: no open or closed issue mentions `keepTail` or a run-command byte tail (REST issue search, 2026-11-08). #1811/#1966 fixed the same defect in `guests/clone.js` only; #1553/#1567 were per-chunk decode defects, a different mechanism.

## Why it matters

`keepTail` exists precisely so a failing `git apply --check` over tens of thousands of paths still returns its diagnostic tail (module doc, run-command.js:129-132). When the tail's first character is a split multi-byte character — common in non-ASCII file names, which are also the paths most likely to appear in apply failures — the diagnostic starts with U+FFFD garbage and the character is unrecoverable. Same for space-setup output shown to the user.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both window sites (the `keepTail` chunk trim and the `readErrorFile` read-back) start their kept bytes on a UTF-8 boundary, e.g. by dropping leading continuation bytes `(byte & 0xc0) === 0x80` as in `guests/clone.js`, or by decoding through a boundary-aware tail helper.
- Kept-byte accounting stays consistent: the window still holds at most `maxOutputBytes` bytes (holding slightly fewer after alignment is fine, as in the sibling fixes).
- New regression tests in `run-command.test.js` (or the existing spaces test files): a multi-byte character straddling the window start yields no U+FFFD and loses at most that one character, for both the `keepTail` stdout/stderr path and the `keepAtExit` stderr-file path; ASCII and boundary-aligned controls unchanged.
- Existing spaces tests still pass.

# fix(web,ui): client PWA manifest clamps can split surrogate pairs — index.html fallback manifest builder and usePwaManifestSync cut names/titles with no pair guard

## Summary

The client-side PWA manifest path cuts install names and recent-session titles at fixed lengths with plain `slice`, with no surrogate-pair guard. When an astral character (emoji, rare CJK) straddles a cut, the value ends with a lone high surrogate, which becomes U+FFFD when the manifest is serialized/UTF-8-encoded — so the installed app's name, short_name, or recent-session shortcut label ends in a replacement character.

This is the client twin of the server-side clamps: #2021 covered `normalizePwaAppName` in `settings-helpers.js` (settings file) and #2023 covers the server endpoint `pwa-manifest-routes.js`. Neither covers the browser-side copies below. The settings UI copy of the same 64-char name clamp is already pair-guarded — `clipPwaInstallName` in `packages/ui/src/components/sections/openchamber/OpenChamberVisualSettings.tsx:91-95`, whose comment names exactly this hazard — so the house pattern exists; these sites are the unguarded remainder.

## Evidence (main b8b7f08b8)

- `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePwaManifestSync.ts:27` — `normalizeRecentTitle` returns `normalized.slice(0, 48)`. Its output is persisted to `localStorage` under `openchamber.pwaRecentSessions` (`usePwaManifestSync.ts:88-90`, `JSON.stringify(recentShortcuts)`) and drives the manifest rebuild.
- `packages/web/index.html:37-43` (inline bootstrap script) — `normalizePwaName` returns `normalized.slice(0, 64)`; the result is persisted to `localStorage` (`openchamber.pwaName`, incl. from the `?pwa_name=` query override) and used as the fallback manifest `name`.
- `packages/web/index.html:45-50` — `truncate(value, maxLength)` is a plain `value.slice(0, maxLength)`, used at:
  - `:172` — recent-session titles re-truncated at 48 in `parseRecentSessionShortcuts`,
  - `:199` — shortcut `name`/`short_name` truncated at 32 in `buildShortcuts`,
  - `:221` — manifest `short_name` truncated at 30 in `buildManifest`.
- The fallback manifest built from these values is serialized with `JSON.stringify` into a Blob (`setManifestFromBlob`, index.html) whenever the `/manifest.webmanifest` endpoint is unavailable — the exact path where the corrupted names ship.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real code, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-pwa-client-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` on the laptop — it loads the verbatim inline script from `packages/web/index.html` (browser globals stubbed) and the verbatim `normalizeRecentTitle` from `usePwaManifestSync.ts`, with U+1F600 (😀) straddling each cap:

- `normalizePwaName` (63 ASCII + 😀): len 64, ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode
- `truncate` at 48 (47 ASCII + 😀): len 48, ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD
- `buildManifest` short_name at 30 (29 ASCII + 😀): ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD
- `buildShortcuts` name at 32 (31 ASCII + 😀): ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD
- `normalizeRecentTitle` at 48 (47 ASCII + 😀): len 48, ends lone U+D83D, 1 U+FFFD; the stored localStorage value read back through `parseRecentSessionShortcuts` carries the same lone surrogate
- Controls clean: ASCII over-limit strings clamp with no U+FFFD; a pair that fits exactly inside the cap survives intact

## Why it matters

Session titles are user/model-generated and routinely contain emoji; PWA install names are user-chosen. On the fallback-manifest path (endpoint down, auth proxy, offline install), the installed app and its recent-session shortcuts get names ending in "�" — a visible corruption of the exact surfaces #2021/#2023 were filed to protect, through the copies those issues don't cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `normalizeRecentTitle` in `usePwaManifestSync.ts` never returns a string ending in a lone surrogate (drop a straddling pair's high half, matching the guarded sibling pattern).
- [ ] `normalizePwaName` and `truncate` in `packages/web/index.html` are pair-safe at every call site (64 name, 48 title, 32 shortcut, 30 short_name).
- [ ] A regression test (or probe-pinned unit test where the harness allows) covers an astral character straddling each cap, plus ASCII and exact-fit controls.
- [ ] Server-side behavior in #2023 is untouched; this issue closes the client copies only.

## Summary

The UI's GitLab reference mapper, `body()` in `packages/ui/src/components/references/gitlabReferences.ts:43-46`, cuts issue and merge-request bodies at `BODY_LIMIT` 20,000 (`:35`) with a plain `value.slice(0, BODY_LIMIT)` and no surrogate-pair guard. A body whose astral character (e.g. an emoji) straddles the cut is shown in the reference preview ending in a lone high surrogate, which renders/encodes as U+FFFD.

This is the exact twin of the server-side `previewBody` in `packages/web/server/lib/github/reference-search.js`, which produced the identical `{ body, bodyTruncated }` shape at the identical 20,000 limit and was fixed pair-safe for #1957 (`reference-search.js:359-361` now drops a split high surrogate). The UI mapper was missed by that fix. Same-file precedent: #1820 (commentTotal) was also a defect in this mapper.

## Evidence (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch5-20261108/probe-gitlab.test.ts` on the laptop, importing the real `gitlabReferences.ts` from the laptop primary at main e7f1ff4c, with a body of 19,999 ASCII chars + U+1F600 + tail:

| path | result length | last code unit | lone surrogates | U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pullReferenceFromChangeRequest` (MR body) | 20,000 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| `fetchGitLabReferencePage` (issue body) | 20,000 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| ASCII control (25,000 chars) | 20,000 | U+0061 | 0 | 0 |

`bodyTruncated` is correctly `true` in the straddle case; only the pair guard is missing.

## Why it matters

The reference preview is how users read GitLab issue/MR bodies before inserting them into a session; a long body with an emoji or other astral character at the 20,000-char boundary displays a corrupted final character, and the lone surrogate propagates anywhere the preview text is copied or encoded. The server mapper for the same shape was already judged worth fixing (#1957); the surfaces should agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- `body()` in `gitlabReferences.ts` drops a split high surrogate at the 20,000 cut (same guard as `reference-search.js` `previewBody`), so no returned body ends in a lone surrogate; `bodyTruncated` semantics unchanged.

# fix(web): settings sanitizer clamps can split surrogate pairs — custom fonts, vim mappings, shortcut overrides and usage model groups in settings-helpers.js slice with no pair guard, persisted to settings

## Summary

`createSettingsHelpers`' write sanitizers in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-helpers.js` cut several user-supplied strings at fixed lengths with a plain `slice`, with no surrogate-pair guard. A value whose astral character (e.g. an emoji) straddles the cut is persisted ending in a lone high surrogate, which encodes as U+FFFD on every later read/display — the stored setting is silently corrupted.

This is the same defect class as #2021 (`normalizePwaAppName`, fixed in 243347229 by dropping a split high surrogate). That fix guarded only the PWA name helper in this same file; the cuts below — all reached through `sanitizeSettingsUpdate`, the sanitizer the settings write path runs before merging into the persisted settings (`applySettingsChanges` in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-runtime.js:1188`, also `config-actions.js:373`) — remain unguarded.

## Unguarded cuts (main e7f1ff4c)

- `customUiFont`: `settings-helpers.js:493` — `candidate.customUiFont.slice(0, 100)`
- `customMonoFont`: `settings-helpers.js:496` — `candidate.customMonoFont.slice(0, 100)`
- `fileEditorVimMappings`: `settings-helpers.js:595` — `candidate.fileEditorVimMappings.slice(0, 10_000)`
- shortcut overrides: `settings-helpers.js:155` (via `sanitizeSettingsUpdate:995`) — `key.slice(0, 128)` and `combo.slice(0, 128)` (constants :98-99)
- usage model groups: `settings-helpers.js:1136` — group `id.slice(0, 64)`; `:1137` — group `label.slice(0, 128)`; `:1166` — renamed-group `label.slice(0, 128)`
- `openCodeUpdateToastDismissedVersion`: `settings-helpers.js:901` — `version.slice(0, 128)` (constant :97)

## Evidence (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch5-20261108/probe-settings.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `createSettingsHelpers` from the laptop primary at e7f1ff4c and driving `sanitizeSettingsUpdate` with straddling inputs (N−1 ASCII chars + U+1F600 + tail):

| field | cut | result length | last code unit | lone surrogates | U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| customUiFont | 100 | 100 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| customMonoFont | 100 | 100 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| fileEditorVimMappings | 10,000 | 10,000 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| shortcutOverrides key | 128 | 128 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| shortcutOverrides value | 128 | 128 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| usageModelGroups group id | 64 | 64 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| usageModelGroups group label | 128 | 128 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| usageModelGroups renamed label | 128 | 128 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |
| openCodeUpdateToastDismissedVersion | 128 | 128 | U+D83D | 1 | 1 |

ASCII controls at the same limits are clean (0 lone surrogates, 0 U+FFFD), so the defect is the split pair, not the clamp itself.

## Why it matters

These values are written to the persisted settings file and read back on every settings load: a custom font family name, a vim-mappings blob, a keyboard shortcut, or a model-group label that happens to straddle the cap is stored corrupted (the astral character is destroyed and replaced by U+FFFD on encode). Group ids are also lookup keys for `modelAssignments`/`renamedGroups`, so a split id can silently orphan its assignments.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every cut listed above drops a split high surrogate at the boundary (the pattern already used in this file for `normalizePwaAppName` after #2021, and in `project-config.js`'s `clampLength` after #1976), so no sanitized value ends in a lone surrogate.
- Regression tests in the settings-helpers test suite cover at least one straddle per cut family (fonts, vim mappings, shortcut key+value, group id/label/renamed label) plus ASCII controls.
- Existing settings-helpers tests still pass.

## Problem

Every name clamp in the served PWA manifest splits surrogate pairs. `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/pwa-manifest-routes.js` cuts three values with fixed UTF-16 code-unit slices and no pair guard:

- `:46-48` — `normalizeShortcutTitle` cuts recent-session titles at 48 (`normalized.slice(0, 48)`), applied to every session title at `:162`.
- `:172` — each shortcut's `short_name` cuts that title again at 32 (`session.title.slice(0, 32)`).
- `:223` — the manifest's own `short_name` cuts the app name at 30 (`appName.slice(0, 30)`), served at `:231`.

Session titles are real user/agent content where emoji are routine, and titles past 48 code units are the norm, not the exception. A title whose cut lands inside an astral character is served in `manifest.webmanifest` ending in a lone high surrogate (U+FFFD after encoding) — as the shortcut name on the installed app's launcher menu. The UI twin `normalizeRecentTitle` in `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePwaManifestSync.ts:27` cuts the same titles at 48 the same unguarded way when building the shortcuts signature.

## Evidence (main b1d5d2164)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/pwa-manifest-routes.js:46-48, 162, 172, 223, 231` — the three cuts above; none checks whether the cut lands on a high surrogate.
- The values are served verbatim: the handler ends with `res.send(JSON.stringify(manifest))`, and the recent-session shortcuts are included for authorized callers.
- Pair-safe precedents in-repo: `client-auth/pairing.js:32-34` `clipPairSafe`; `projects/project-config.js:45-47` `clampLength`; `session-knowledge/runtime.js` `truncate`.
- Dedup: title + keyword search over open and closed issues (manifest / pwa / surrogate) — no existing filing for these cuts; #1291 covered this route's *response-body byte cap* for the session list fetch, a different defect. Distinct from the `settings-helpers` `normalizePwaAppName` filing this run: that clamp (64, persisted settings) feeds this route, but all three cuts here are this module's own, and the 48/32 cuts apply to session titles that never pass through it.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real route handler, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch4-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), registering the real `registerPwaManifestRoute` with stub dependencies (authorized caller, stub OpenCode session list, the real `normalizePwaAppName`) on main b1d5d2164:

- Query override name `'c' × 29 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'dddd'`: manifest `name` intact (length 35), but `short_name` length 30 ending lone `U+D83D`, 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.
- Session title `'a' × 47 + '😀' + 't' × 10`: shortcut `name` length 48 ending lone `U+D83D`, 1 U+FFFD.
- Session title `'b' × 31 + '😀' + 'x' × 20`: shortcut `name` length 48 clean (pair intact — control for the 48 cut), but its `short_name` length 32 ending lone `U+D83D`, 1 U+FFFD — isolating the 32 cut as the culprit there.

## Why it matters

The manifest is the installed app's public face: its `short_name` labels the app icon and its shortcuts label the launcher long-press menu with the user's most recent sessions. Any recent session with a long, emoji-bearing title — ordinary for agent-named sessions — can put a corrupted name in front of the user every time the manifest is fetched, and the 5-second-cached shortcuts re-serve it. Three cuts in one small module, all with the same one-line-class fix, make this a single tidy repair.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three cuts in `pwa-manifest-routes.js` (48 shortcut title, 32 shortcut `short_name`, 30 manifest `short_name`) are pair-safe: when a cut lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary, while ASCII values still cut at exactly 48 / 32 / 30.

title: fix(web): Cursor quota token refresh settles outside fetchQuota's try — a stalled refresh rejects with a raw TimeoutError instead of the 'Request timed out' result (#782 residual, PR #1845)

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Finding

The quota deadline contract (issue #782, closed) is: every provider HTTP call carries a 15 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, and a stalled endpoint answers that provider's normal failure result — `ok: false` with `error: 'Request timed out'` — instead of hanging or escaping as a raw abort. On current main (`1a560de055f96f8a0d69a87fe3252c1d5ed5c23f`) the Cursor token-refresh call breaks that contract, because of where it is awaited:

- `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js:161` — `refreshAccessToken`'s fetch DOES carry `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)`, so a stalled refresh settles in 15 s. Good.
- `cursor.js:388-400` — but `fetchQuota` awaits the token resolution **outside** its try block:
  - `:389` `const accessToken = await resolveAccessToken();` (which calls `refreshAccessToken` whenever the access token needs refresh, `cursor.js:185,179-183`)
  - `:400` `try {` — the usage/plan/credits calls live inside
  - `:460-467` — the catch is what converts `error?.name === 'TimeoutError'` to `'Request timed out'` in the returned `buildResult`.

So a stalled refresh rejects `fetchQuota()` with the raw `TimeoutError` DOMException:

- Direct callers get a rejection, not a result — `fetchCursorQuota` is exported as-is (`providers/index.js` `export const fetchCursorQuota = cursor.fetchQuota;`), and every other Cursor failure path returns a `buildResult`.
- Through the dispatcher (`providers/index.js` `fetchQuotaForProviderUncoalesced` catch), the rejection is converted with `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Request failed'` — i.e. the runtime's abort wording ("The operation was aborted due to timeout"), not the documented `'Request timed out'` every other provider/call produces.

Closed PR #1845 (the branch-disposition surfacing of the #782 fix) had this right: its cursor hunk moved `await resolveAccessToken()` **inside** the try with the comment "Token refresh runs inside the deadline too: a stalled refresh is the …" and added a test `times out a stalled token refresh instead of hanging` expecting `result.error` to be `'Request timed out'`. When the deadline work landed on main through another route, the refresh fetch's signal came along but the try relocation and that test did not. Main's only Cursor deadline test (`cursor.test.js:422-433`) drives a usage call throwing `TimeoutError`; the refresh path is uncovered.

The same outside-try placement also means any other `refreshAccessToken` throw (e.g. its deliberate `'Cursor session expired'` / `'Session expired - please sign in to Cursor again'` errors) rejects `fetchQuota` instead of returning a failure result — moving the await inside the existing try fixes the whole class in one move, matching #1845's shape.

## Why it matters

The quota route's error vocabulary is user-visible (the UI renders the provider error string) and is the documented contract in `quota/DOCUMENTATION.md` ("Every provider HTTP call carries an abort deadline… answers that provider's normal failure result, `ok: false` with `Request timed out`"). One call path silently opting out — only when a user's access token happens to need refresh at the moment the endpoint stalls — is exactly the kind of inconsistency the #782 sweep existed to eliminate, and it is currently untestable-by-omission: no test can fail for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stalled Cursor token refresh makes `fetchQuota()` **return** `{ ok: false, configured: true, error: 'Request timed out' }` (the same shape as a stalled usage call), never a rejection with a raw `TimeoutError`.
- [ ] A regression test in the shape of #1845's dropped case: refresh endpoint never answers / throws `TimeoutError`, result error is `'Request timed out'`; the existing usage-call deadline test (`cursor.test.js:422-433`) still passes.
- [ ] Refresh failures generally (e.g. the session-expired throws) return a failure result from `fetchQuota` rather than rejecting, OR the issue records an explicit decision that only the timeout conversion is in scope.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1845 (CLOSED unmerged; its cursor hunk at diff lines 333-376 and refresh-timeout test at diff lines 429-438 of the run's saved diff), origin issue #782 (CLOSED).
- Main `1a560de0`, verified by two independent reads (parent + first-pass reviewer): `cursor.js:161` refresh signal; `:185` `resolveAccessToken`; `:389` await outside try; `:400` try; `:460-467` TimeoutError conversion inside the catch only; `providers/index.js` dispatcher catch building `error.message`; `cursor.test.js:422-433` deadline test covers a usage call only.
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): searches for cursor refresh / "Request timed out" return only #782 (closed parent) and unrelated #822/#759 — this residual is not filed.
- Filed by pr-diff-review lane B, run 2026-11-08 13:18 CST. Evidence: `hidden_files/pr-review-b-2026-11-08-1318/` (pr-1845.diff, review-closed-b.md).

## Problem

The session-assist runtime splits surrogate pairs when it clamps the generated recap and suggestion, and the corrupted text is persisted to the session metadata store. In `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/runtime.js:256-257`:

```js
let recap = targets.recap && typeof structured?.recap === 'string' ? structured.recap.trim().slice(0, RECAP_CHAR_LIMIT) : '';
let suggestion = targets.suggestion && typeof structured?.suggestion === 'string' ? structured.suggestion.trim().slice(0, SUGGESTION_CHAR_LIMIT) : '';
```

Both are fixed UTF-16 code-unit cuts (`RECAP_CHAR_LIMIT` 320 at `:29`, `SUGGESTION_CHAR_LIMIT` 500 at `:30`) with no pair guard. Recap and suggestion text is small-model output about the user's own work — emoji and extended CJK are ordinary content. If an astral character straddles offset 320 (recap) or 500 (suggestion), the value ends with a lone high surrogate, which becomes U+FFFD when encoded or rendered. The clamped values are written at `:286` via `persistSessionAssist(sessionId, directory, { recap, suggestion, … })` into OpenChamber's session metadata store, so the corruption is durable and shown every time the assist is displayed for that turn.

## Evidence (main 1a560de05)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/runtime.js:256-257` — both slices, no surrogate-pair guard; limits at `:29-30`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/runtime.js:286-291` — the clamped `recap`/`suggestion` are persisted via `persistSessionAssist`.
- Distinct from #1911: that filing covers `session-assist/context.js` `excerpt` (the prompt-side context cuts). This is the output-side clamp in `runtime.js`, a different function whose result is stored, not sent to the model.
- Pair-safe precedents in-repo: the sibling `session-assist/context.js:23` already drops a split head surrogate; `session-knowledge/runtime.js` `truncate`; `client-auth/pairing.js:32-34` `clipPairSafe`.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

- Recap `'a' × 319 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'tail'`: persisted recap length 320, last code unit lone `U+D83D`, exactly 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.
- Suggestion `'b' × 499 + '😀' + 'tail'`: persisted suggestion length 500, last code unit lone `U+D83D`, exactly 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.
- The generation, script checks, and persistence all completed normally — the only defect is the split pair in the stored values.

## Why it matters

The recap is the user's reminder of what a turn accomplished, and the suggestion is the proposed next step; both are rendered from the metadata store long after generation. A recap or suggestion whose cut lands inside an emoji is stored corrupted and renders as U+FFFD permanently for that turn. The input side of this same module was already made pair-safe (#1911, `context.js`); the output side that actually persists user-visible text was not.

body:
## Finding

Merged PR #1837 bounded `tracked-items/persistence.js` `load()` at 8 MiB (closing #1662), but left four verified residuals on current main (`1a560de055f96f8a0d69a87fe3252c1d5ed5c23f`). All four were verified against current main by two independent reads (parent + first-pass reviewer) on 2026-11-08.

### 1. The shared bounded-read inventory row is now wrong in two facts

`packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md:353` still says of tracked-items `load`:

> bound status: `none — covered-by-open-issue #1662` … cache restore: missing → [], wrong version/shape → [], **a parse error throws**

Both halves are stale: the code IS bound (`persistence.js:9` `MAX_FILE_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`, `:20` `readBoundedFile(filePath, MAX_FILE_BYTES)`) and #1662 is CLOSED; and a parse error no longer throws — `persistence.js:29-33` catches `JSON.parse` failure and silently returns `[]`. The module's own header (`persistence.js:11-14`, "a missing, unreadable or malformed file restores nothing") and `tracked-items/DOCUMENTATION.md:22` match the NEW behaviour, so the shared row is the wrong document. Contrast PR #1827, which updated its inventory row in the same PR.

The silent-`[]` change also has a real consequence: the sole caller only logs corruption on a throw (`tracked-items/service.js:317-319`, `log.warn '[tracked-items] could not restore state'` in its `catch`), so a corrupt cache now restores empty with no log signal at all, and the next routine `save()` (service.js:160) overwrites the malformed file. The old throw path at least surfaced the corruption first.

### 2. The FIFO / non-regular case — the headline hazard of #1662 — has no real test

`packages/web/server/lib/tracked-items/persistence.test.js:27-30` on main:

```js
it.skip('returns empty array when file is a FIFO', () => {
  // FIFO test skipped - mkfifo not available in Bun environment
  expect(true).toBe(true);
});
```

A skipped placeholder asserting `true`. The behaviour exists (`not-regular` → `[]`, `persistence.js:22`) but nothing exercises it — sibling bounded-read PRs merged the same weekend (#1827) pin FIFO cases with a real `mkfifo` via `execFileSync` + `it.runIf(platform !== 'win32')`. The same test file (`:153-164`) also leaves an unused helper `fsMkfifo` whose `const { mkfifo } = await import('node:fs/promises')` imports an export that does not exist — dead code that could never have worked.

### 3. `load()` ignores the injected `fs` the factory advertises

`createTrackedItemsPersistence({ dataDir, fs = fsPromises })` (`persistence.js:16`): `save()` honours the injected `fs` (`:44-45`, `fs.writeFile` / `fs.rename`), but since #1837 `load()` reads through the module-level `readBoundedFile`, which opens via the real `fs.promises.open` (`shared/bounded-file-read.js`). A caller injecting a fake/virtual fs reads from real disk and writes to the fake — split-brain — and read edge cases cannot be simulated through the seam. The PR's own tests mask this by passing the real fs as the "mock" in every case.

### 4. Latent: `load()` can `throw` a plain result object, not an Error

`persistence.js:21-25`: any `!result.ok` whose reason is not missing/not-regular/too-large hits `throw result;` — a plain `{ ok, reason, code, path }` object with no `message` and no stack. This is unreachable today (`readBoundedFile` returns exactly those three reasons and throws real Errors itself for unexpected I/O), but any future fourth reason added to the shared reader would be thrown here as a bare object, and the caller logs `error?.message ?? error`.

## Why it matters

The bounded-read campaign's inventory doc is the fleet's map of which readers are safe; a row that is wrong about both bound status and error semantics misdirects the next audit. The untested FIFO branch is the exact failure mode (startup restore wedging on a FIFO) that #1662 was filed for. The fs-seam split makes the persistence layer untestable in the way its own factory promises.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` tracked-items row corrected on both halves: bound-complete at 8 MiB via `readBoundedFile`, and cache-restore semantics state parse error → `[]` (or the code is changed back to throw — pick one and make code + both docs agree; if silent `[]` stays, note the lost corruption log signal or restore one).
- [ ] The FIFO case is exercised by a real test in the #1827 pattern (real `mkfifo`, POSIX-gated), or the skip + dead `fsMkfifo` helper are removed with the reason recorded; no `it.skip` placeholder asserting `true` remains.
- [ ] `load()` honours the injected `fs` (threaded into the read) or the `fs` parameter is removed from the factory and callers/tests updated — load and save must use the same filesystem; a test with a genuinely fake fs proves it.
- [ ] The non-Error `throw result` path is removed or converted to a real `Error` carrying the result fields.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1837 (merged, merge commit `96b7efc7c81a2899a2cb03d5cf01b5b6747e3ddd`), closing #1662 (CLOSED).
- Files on main `1a560de0`: `packages/web/server/lib/tracked-items/persistence.js:9,16,20-25,29-33,44-45`; `packages/web/server/lib/tracked-items/persistence.test.js:27-30,153-164`; `packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md:353`; `packages/web/server/lib/tracked-items/service.js:160,317-319`; `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` (three result reasons only).
- Dedupe (2026-11-08): searches for tracked-items persistence / FIFO / parse return only #1662 (closed, the bounding issue itself) and unrelated #117 — none of these four residuals is filed.

body:
## Problem

The guest settings save path cuts every settings value at 2,000 code units with no surrogate-pair guard, and the corrupted value is persisted to the guest auth store. In `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js`, `saveSettings` (`:437-456`) sanitizes each declared settings value with `value.trim().slice(0, 2000)` (`:451`) and persists the result via `patchGuestAuth(guest.id, { settings }, authPath)` into the on-disk guest auth store, where it is returned by every later read and handed to the guest integration (e.g. a ClickUp list ID field declared in the guest manifest's `integration.settings`). If an astral character (emoji, extended CJK) straddles offset 2,000, the stored value ends with a lone high surrogate, which becomes U+FFFD when encoded — on disk, permanently, not just in one response. The same `saveSettings` operation is also exposed to the `openchamber` agent tool (`../openchamber-control/integration-service-actions.js`, per the comment at `routes.js:230-233`), so the cut is reachable from both the HTTP route (`PUT /api/guests/:id/settings`) and the agent surface.

## Evidence (main 1a560de05)

- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js:451` — `settings[key] = value.trim().slice(0, 2000);` — a fixed code-unit cut with no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js:453` — `const stored = await patchGuestAuth(guest.id, { settings }, authPath);` — the clamped values are the persisted ones.
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/routes.js:205-208` — `declaredSettings` takes the allowed keys from the guest manifest's `integration.settings`, so any declared text setting is affected.
- Pair-safe precedents in-repo: `client-auth/pairing.js:32-34` `clipPairSafe`, `projects/project-setup.js:32-36`, `agent-memory/runtime.js` `clampLength` — all back off a split high surrogate because the clamped value is persisted.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch2-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real exported `registerGuestRoutes` (fake app capture) and its returned `saveSettings` against a path-installed guest fixture whose manifest declares a `list-id` setting, on main 1a560de05:

- Value `'s' × 1999 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'zzzz'`: `saveSettings` returns status 200; the value read back from the auth store (`getGuestAuth`) has length 2000, last code unit lone `U+D83D` (JSON tail `"sss\ud83d"`), exactly 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.
- ASCII control (`'b' × 2500`): status 200, stored length 2000, no lone surrogate, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

Guest settings are user-entered configuration that integrations act on — names, list/workspace identifiers, free-text preferences pasted from other tools, where emoji and non-BMP characters occur naturally. A value that ends exactly at the cap with an astral character on the boundary is silently stored corrupted; because the store is the source of truth for both the UI and the agent tool, the mangled value is what the integration receives on every subsequent call, with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The settings cut in `guests/routes.js` `saveSettings` never splits a surrogate pair: when the 2,000 cut lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary (back off the lone high surrogate), while ASCII values still cut at exactly 2,000.
- [ ] A test pins the boundary case with a named oracle: a declared settings value with an astral character straddling offset 2,000 persists with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding), through the same operation the route and the agent tool share.
- [ ] Existing guests tests pass unchanged.

Related (different files/functions, same defect class): #1993 (client-auth labels), #1991 (agent-memory titles), #1990 (project-setup clamps).

## Problem

Both guest-account length cuts in `packages/web/server/lib/guests/oauth.js` split surrogate pairs, and the corrupted account name is persisted to the guest auth store. The account label for a connected guest integration is cut at `GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX` (200, `packages/sdk/src/contract.ts:395`) in two places, neither with a pair guard:

1. `readAccountLabel` (`oauth.js:235`) cuts the provider-returned account name (e.g. a Jira `displayName`) with `current.trim().slice(0, GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX)`.
2. The basic-auth fallback in `saveGuestAccessToken` (`oauth.js:383`) cuts the pasted username with `pastedUsername.slice(0, GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX)` when the provider probe returns no account name.

Both results land in `patchGuestAuth(..., { account, ... })` (`oauth.js:384-392` and the OAuth exchange path `:475-487`), i.e. in the on-disk guest auth store, and are shown as the connected account identity in the guest UI. An astral character straddling offset 200 leaves a lone high surrogate at the end, which becomes U+FFFD when encoded or rendered — permanently, since the stored value is what every later read returns.

## Evidence (main 1a560de05)

- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/oauth.js:235` — `return typeof current === 'string' ? current.trim().slice(0, GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX) : '';`
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/oauth.js:383` — `const account = probed.account || (api.authorization === 'basic' ? pastedUsername.slice(0, GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX) : '');`
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/oauth.js:384-392` — `saveGuestAccessToken` persists `account` via `patchGuestAuth`; `:475-487` the OAuth exchange persists the probed account the same way.
- `packages/sdk/src/contract.ts:395` — `GUEST_ACCOUNT_MAX = 200`.
- Pair-safe precedents in-repo: `client-auth/pairing.js:32-34` `clipPairSafe`, `projects/project-setup.js:32-36`, `agent-memory/runtime.js` `clampLength` — all back off a split high surrogate because the clamped value is persisted.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch2-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real exported `saveGuestAccessToken` with the Jira basic-scheme guest fixture from `oauth.test.js` and a stubbed `fetch`, on main 1a560de05:

- Provider `displayName` = `'d' × 199 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'zzzz'`: returned and persisted `account` length 200, last code unit lone `U+D83D` (JSON tail `"ddd\ud83d"`), exactly 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode; the value read back from the auth store (`getGuestAuth`) is identical.
- Provider `displayName` empty, pasted username = `'u' × 199 + '😀' + 'zzzz'` (basic fallback, `oauth.js:383`): persisted `account` length 200, lone `U+D83D` at the end, 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.

## Why it matters

The account string is the identity a user sees for a connected guest integration ("connected as …"). Provider display names routinely contain emoji and non-BMP characters, and a 200-code-unit name with an astral character at the boundary is stored with a replacement character baked in. The corruption is silent — connect succeeds — and durable: it lives in the auth store until the user disconnects and reconnects with a different name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Neither account cut in `guests/oauth.js` splits a surrogate pair: when the 200 cut lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary (back off the lone high surrogate), while ASCII values still cut at exactly 200. One shared pair-safe clip for both sites is preferred.
- [ ] Tests pin both sites with a named oracle: a provider display name straddling offset 200 and a basic-auth username straddling offset 200 each persist an `account` with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding).
- [ ] Existing `guests/oauth.test.js` tests pass unchanged.

## Problem

The UI passkey label normalizer splits surrogate pairs, and the corrupted label is persisted to the passkey store. `normalizeLabel` in `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:45-51` trims, collapses whitespace, and then cuts with `normalized.slice(0, 120)` — a fixed UTF-16 code-unit cut with no pair guard. Every passkey label passes through it: the registration label captured in `beginRegistration` (`:456`, fallback 'This device'), the rename path `renamePasskey` (`:360`, via `normalizeOptionalLabel` → `customLabel`), and the read-side sanitize of stored records (`:121-122`). If an astral character (emoji, extended CJK) straddles offset 120, the stored label ends with a lone high surrogate, which becomes U+FFFD when the value is encoded or rendered. `renamePasskey` persists via `persistStore` to the passkey store file, so the corruption is durable: the device row in the passkey list shows a permanently mangled name.

## Evidence (main 1a560de05)

- `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:45-51` — `normalizeLabel`: `return normalized ? normalized.slice(0, 120) : fallback;` — no surrogate-pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:53` — `normalizeOptionalLabel` delegates to the same cut; `:360` rename stores its result as `customLabel`; `:367` persists the store.
- `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:456` — registration captures `label: normalizeLabel(label, 'This device')`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:121-122` — stored records are re-normalized on read with the same unguarded cut, so the defect cannot be cleaned up by a later read.
- Distinct from #1993 (closed): that filing covers the client-auth device labels in `pairing.js` / `remote-clients.js`, which now carry a pair-safe `clipPairSafe`. The passkey store's normalizer is a separate function in a separate auth surface and was not covered.
- Pair-safe precedents in-repo: `client-auth/pairing.js:32-34`, `projects/project-setup.js:32-36`, `agent-memory/runtime.js` `clampLength`.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-surrogate-batch2-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real exported `createUiPasskeys` factory with a seeded store file on main 1a560de05, then calling the real `renamePasskey`:

- Label `'a' × 119 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'zzzz'`: persisted `customLabel` length 120, last code unit lone `U+D83D` (JSON tail `"aaa\ud83d"`), exactly 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode.
- ASCII control (`'b' × 200`): length 120, no lone surrogate, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

Passkey labels are how a user tells their devices apart on a security surface ("Office laptop", "Phone"). A label whose 120th code unit is half an emoji is stored corrupted forever and renders as U+FFFD in the device list; the user cannot fix it by renaming to the same text, because every write and read passes the same unguarded cut. It is the same defect class already fixed for the sibling client-auth labels (#1993), in a store that filing did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `normalizeLabel` in `ui-passkeys.js` never splits a surrogate pair: when the 120 cut lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary (back off the lone high surrogate), while ASCII values still cut at exactly 120.
- [ ] Tests pin the boundary cases with a named oracle: a rename and a registration label with an astral character straddling offset 120 persist labels with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding), and an over-cap ASCII label still stores exactly 120 code units.
- [ ] Existing `ui-passkeys.test.js` tests pass unchanged.

body:
## Summary

`packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js` clamps project notes, todos, and plans through one helper with no surrogate-pair guard:

```js
const clampLength = (value, maxLength) => {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return '';
  return value.length > maxLength ? value.slice(0, maxLength) : value;
};
```
(runtime.js:51-54)

Every call site cuts in UTF-16 code units at a fixed cap, so a character astride the cap is split and the lone surrogate is **persisted**:

- Note bodies — `PROJECT_NOTE_BODY_MAX_LENGTH = 3000` (:25): `createNote` (:691), `updateNote` (:733), and the sanitize paths (:75, :95, :691-area) all clamp, then `writeContext` writes the result to `<projectsDir>/<projectId>/context.json`.
- Todo text — `PROJECT_TODO_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH = 1000` (:28) via `sanitizeTodos` (:123) on the stored-context read/sanitize path (the direct mutation validator at :255 throws instead, so stored/legacy todos are the affected path).
- Plan titles — `PROJECT_PLAN_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH = 160` (:29) via `sanitizePlanTitle` (:136), used by `parsePlanMarkdown` and `createPlan`; the title is persisted both in context.json and as the plan file's `# ` heading.
- Plan bodies / raw markdown — `PROJECT_PLAN_BODY_MAX_LENGTH = 200_000` (:30): `createPlan` (:949) and `updatePlan` (:868) clamp, then `writeFile(..., 'utf8')` writes the plan `.md` file — UTF-8 encoding converts the lone surrogate to U+FFFD **in the file itself**, so the corruption is permanent even before any readback.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe vs the real module, ×2 identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-projectcontext-clamp-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` on the laptop, driving the real `createProjectContextRuntime` (main dc01ccf8d) with a temp `projectsDirPath`:

- Note: body = `'a'×2999 + U+1F600 + 'b'×10` → returned note body is 3,000 code units ending in lone **U+D83D**; on-disk `context.json` contains the `\ud83d` escape; readback via `readContext` still ends U+D83D; UTF-8 encoding of the body yields exactly **1 U+FFFD**.
- Plan: title = `'t'×159 + U+1F600 + …` → stored title is 160 code units ending lone U+D83D. Body = `'c'×199999 + U+1F600 + …` → the written plan `.md` file (200,168 bytes) contains **2 U+FFFD byte triples** (EF BF BD) — one from the clamped title in the heading, one at the body tail; the file's body literally ends with U+FFFD.
- Controls clean: an ASCII 3,010-char note clamps to 3,000 `a`s with 0 U+FFFD; an under-limit note containing U+1F600 round-trips intact.

## Why it matters

Project notes and plans are user/agent-authored long-lived content (the project knowledge store). A single emoji or CJK-ext character landing exactly on a cap silently corrupts the stored text: notes keep a lone surrogate in context.json that becomes U+FFFD at every later UTF-8 boundary, and plan markdown files get U+FFFD baked into the file on disk — the original character is unrecoverable. This is the same defect class as the sibling `clampLength` filings in project-config.js (#1976) and agent-memory/runtime.js (#1991); this module's helper is a separate copy and was not covered by either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No clamp in `project-context/runtime.js` (note body 3,000, todo text 1,000, plan title 160, plan body/raw 200,000) can end a string with a lone high surrogate or start one with a lone low surrogate: when the cut would split a surrogate pair, drop the dangling half (matching the guard used by the sibling fixes).
- [ ] Regression tests in `project-context/runtime.test.js` (or a sibling suite) pin: a straddling astral character at each cap is dropped whole, the persisted `context.json` and plan `.md` contents contain no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD introduced by clamping, and ASCII / under-limit content is unchanged.
- [ ] Existing project-context suites still pass.
