If an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the cut, the stored label ends with a lone high surrogate — which becomes U+FFFD when encoded or rendered. The remote-clients store file on disk holds the escaped lone surrogate (`\ud83d`), and the label is the operator-visible name of a paired device in the pending-devices and paired-clients lists, so a device named with an emoji at offset 79–80 shows a corrupted trailing character permanently, on every surface that reads the store.

## Evidence (main e6e11959d22c3508e6191f1dd10b83c85a9705de)

- `packages/web/server/lib/client-auth/pairing.js:32` — `return normalized.length > MAX_LABEL_LENGTH ? normalized.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_LENGTH) : normalized` in `normalizeStoredLabel` — a fixed code-unit cut with no pair guard; applied to every pairing session label on store normalize and on `createPairingSession`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/client-auth/remote-clients.js:17` — the same cut in `normalizeLabel`; applied on `createClient` and on every store normalize, so even a label written by another build is re-cut the same way on read.

- Guarded in-repo precedents for this exact defect class: `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js` truncates on a code-point boundary; `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/audit.js:58` and `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.js:74-76` back off a split high surrogate.

Paired-device labels are a security-adjacent surface: the operator uses them to tell their own devices apart when reviewing or revoking access. A corrupted trailing character is a papercut on exactly the name the operator typed to recognize a device, and it is persisted in both auth stores. The session-goal objective file store clamps content at the 1,000,000-char hard cap with a fixed UTF-16 slice and no surrogate-pair guard. `clampContent` is applied on every objective write, read, and version append; if an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the cap, the clamped text ends with a lone high surrogate — and `writeObjective` then persists that string to the objective `.md` file as UTF-8, where the lone surrogate is encoded as U+FFFD. The corruption is permanent: `readObjective` returns the objective with the boundary character already replaced by U+FFFD, and the same clamped text is what the goal auditor and progress check read. This is the store's own clamp, distinct from the create-path condensation in issue #1909 (`create.js` `fitObjective`): an objective that arrives through the objective routes, a fork inheritance copy, or a version append reaches this clamp without ever passing through `fitObjective`.

## Evidence (main 576aa7174c47897731125b4856e386a65bf2c9a4)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js:17` — `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_HARD_CAP = 1_000_000`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js:63` — `const clampContent = (content) => String(content ?? '').trim().slice(0, GOAL_OBJECTIVE_HARD_CAP);` — a fixed code-unit cut with no pair guard.
- All three call sites share the clamp: `writeObjective` at `:70` (persisted via `writeFile(..., 'utf8')` at `:75`), `readObjective` at `:106`, and `appendObjectiveVersion` at `:188` (objective version history, #1830).
- The read side of the same file is byte-careful — `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_MAX_READ_BYTES = GOAL_OBJECTIVE_HARD_CAP * 4 + 4` (`:21`) exists specifically "so a read that stops at the bound never splits the sequence of the cap's last char" — but the char-side clamp that follows the decode reintroduces a split at the code-unit level.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.test.js` pins the over-cap behaviour only with ASCII text; no surrogate-boundary case exists.
- Guarded in-repo precedent: `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so a value never ends in a lone surrogate; `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-401` skips a leading low surrogate on a tail slice.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-objectives-clamp-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real `writeObjective`/`readObjective` with `OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR` pointed at a scratch dir, input `'a' × 999,999 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'z' × 500`:

- `writeObjective` returns content of length 1,000,000 ending in lone `U+D83D` (high surrogate at index 999,999).
- The persisted `goals/<session>.md` file (1,000,002 bytes) contains the UTF-8 encoding of U+FFFD (`EF BF BD`) at the boundary.
- `readObjective` returns text with exactly 1 U+FFFD — the emoji is unrecoverable from the stored objective.
- ASCII control (`'a' × 1,000,500`): clamped to 1,000,000, 0 lone surrogates, no U+FFFD bytes in the file. Under-cap emoji control: pair intact.

## Why it matters

The objective file is the durable record of what the user asked the goal system to do — it is re-read on every session load, fed to the goal auditor, and copied on fork inheritance. A single emoji landing on the hard-cap boundary silently rewrites the stored objective's boundary character to U+FFFD forever; no later read can restore it, because the corruption happens before the bytes hit disk. The cap only fires on runaway objectives, but that is precisely the case the clamp exists for, and its sibling condensation path (#1909) was already judged worth fixing. The byte-side read bound in the same file shows the house intent: a bound must never split a character.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `clampContent` never splits a surrogate pair: when the cut at `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_HARD_CAP` lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary, so no value returned by `writeObjective`, `readObjective`, or `appendObjectiveVersion` ends in a lone surrogate.
- [ ] A test in `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.test.js` pins the boundary case with a named oracle: an astral character straddling the hard cap produces a persisted objective file with no U+FFFD bytes, and `readObjective` returns the objective with no U+FFFD; the existing ASCII over-cap tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Existing session-goal tests pass.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1909 (create-path `fitObjective` condensation), #1906 (session-goal auditor excerpts), #1907 (goal spec clip).

body:
## Problem

The notification template runtime's last-message extraction cuts text at a fixed UTF-16 offset with no surrogate-pair guard. `extractTextFromParts` slices the joined message text at `maxLength` (default `NOTIFICATION_BODY_MAX_CHARS` = 1,000), and the content-array branch of `extractLastMessageText` does the same; if an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the cut, the extracted `last_message` text ends with a lone high surrogate — which becomes U+FFFD when the value is encoded (push payload, JSON, or a summarizer prompt). This extraction is the canonical getter for the notification `{last_message}` variable: `runtime.js` calls it for both the ready and error notification paths, and `fetchLastAssistantMessageText` returns the same cut at caller-chosen lengths. The downstream 250-char shaping cut in `message.js` (issue #1922) masks the defect only at the default setting — a raised `maxLastMessageLength` makes this 1,000-char extraction cut the binding one, and every other consumer of the extracted value inherits the malformed string directly.

## Evidence (main 576aa7174c47897731125b4856e386a65bf2c9a4)

- `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:17` — `NOTIFICATION_BODY_MAX_CHARS = 1000`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:123-136` — `extractTextFromParts`; `:134` — `text = text.slice(0, maxLength);` — a fixed code-unit cut with no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:140-164` — `extractLastMessageText`; `:157` — `result = result.slice(0, maxLength);` — the same unguarded cut on the `info.content` branch.
- `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:166-198` — `fetchLastAssistantMessageText` returns `extractTextFromParts(target.content, maxLength)` at `:198`, so the fetched-message path shares the cut.
- `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/runtime.js:643` and `:715` — both notification paths take `extractLastMessageText(payload)` (falling back to `fetchLastAssistantMessageText`) into `prepareNotificationLastMessage` as the `last_message` template variable.
- No surrogate-boundary test exists for these functions: `grep -rn "surrogate" packages/web/server/lib/notifications/*.test.js` hits only the guarded APNs precedent's test (`apns-runtime.test.js:185` — "A cut inside a surrogate pair must not leave a lone surrogate behind").
- Guarded in-repo precedent, same folder: `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so a value never ends in a lone surrogate.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-template-extract-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real `createNotificationTemplateRuntime` with stub deps, input `'a' × 999 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 100`:

- `extractTextFromParts` (parts path): result length 1,000, lone surrogate `high@999:U+D83D`, exactly 1 U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- `extractLastMessageText` via the `info.content` array branch: length 1,000, lone `U+D83D` at 999, 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- `extractLastMessageText` via the `info.parts` branch: length 1,000, lone `U+D83D` at 999, 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- ASCII control (`'a' × 1,500`): length 1,000, 0 lone surrogates, 0 U+FFFD. Under-limit emoji control: pair intact.

## Why it matters

Every ready/error notification builds its `{last_message}` from this extraction. The extracted value is malformed at exactly the boundary the cap deliberately kept: any consumer that uses more than the default 250-char downstream cut — a raised `maxLastMessageLength` setting, the summarization input, or a caller of `fetchLastAssistantMessageText` with a larger `maxLength` — surfaces U+FFFD at the visible tail of the notification instead of the character the assistant actually sent. It is the same defect class already filed for other truncation sites (#1906, #1908, #1910, #1911, #1921, #1922, #1931, #1932), in a surface those filings did not cover: #1922 is the later shaping cut in `message.js`, not this extraction cut.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `extractTextFromParts` and the content-array branch of `extractLastMessageText` never split a surrogate pair: when the cut at `maxLength` lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary (the apns-runtime.js code-point-boundary precedent in the same folder).
- [ ] A test pins the boundary case with a named oracle: an astral character straddling the 1,000-char default cap produces extracted text with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding) through both `extractTextFromParts` and `extractLastMessageText` (parts and content branches); existing notification tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Existing notification runtime/template tests pass.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1922 (notification shaping truncation in message.js), #1932 (summarization fallback clippers), #1921 (session-knowledge truncate).

body:
## Finding

PR #1798 (fix for #1778) bounded and regular-file-judged the **read** of the UI-auth JWT secret file, and guarded the **generate-and-persist write in `getOrCreateJwtSecret`** with a by-path `fs.statSync(...).isFile()` check. The other write of the same file in the same module was left completely unguarded, and the guarded write is probe-then-write by path:

1. **`persistJwtSecret` has no non-regular check at all.** `packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-auth.js:494-503` (current main `b75911552a84`): it does `fs.mkdirSync(...)` then a bare `fs.writeFileSync(JWT_SECRET_FILE, secret, { mode: 0o600 })`. This is the secret-rotation path — `rotateJwtSecret` at ui-auth.js:743-745, called from the global sign-out handler at ui-auth.js:1098. Opening a FIFO for write blocks until a reader appears, so a FIFO (or other non-regular entry) at `<OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR>/jwt-secret` freezes the whole server on a global sign-out — exactly the failure #1778/#1798 set out to remove, on the write side.
2. **`getOrCreateJwtSecret`'s guard is probe-then-write by path.** ui-auth.js:473-483: `fs.statSync(JWT_SECRET_FILE).isFile()` decides `persistBlocked`, then `fs.writeFileSync(JWT_SECRET_FILE, ...)` re-opens by path. A FIFO swapped in between the probe and the write still blocks the write open (the #1823 host-lock shape, in the same file the PR just hardened).

## Evidence

- Source PR: #1798 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1798 (merge commit `d3a6b601cb`, verified ancestor of current main `b75911552a84`). Its diff touches only the read and the `getOrCreateJwtSecret` persist path; `persistJwtSecret` is not in the diff.
- Current main, verified twice (`git show origin/main:packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-auth.js`): `persistJwtSecret` at :494-503 writes with no stat/open flags; `getOrCreateJwtSecret` at :473-483 probes by path then writes by path.
- Laptop probe (x2, plus control), against the exact call shape `fs.writeFileSync(<fifo path>, 'x'.repeat(64), { mode: 0o600 })`: the write never settled within 3 s either time (`timeout` exit 124, no output); the same write to a regular file settled immediately and wrote 64 bytes. Probe dir: laptop `/tmp/probe-oc-jwt-fifo-20261108/`.
- Dedupe: #1778 (closed) covers only the read; no open or recently closed issue covers the secret-file write paths (searched `persistJwtSecret`, `rotateJwtSecret`, `jwt-secret`, `ui-auth FIFO`).

## Why it matters

The jwt-secret path sits in a user-writable data directory — the same threat model #1778, #1798 and the whole bounded-read family treat as untrusted. The read side now refuses a FIFO promptly; the rotation write still blocks the server event loop indefinitely, and it is reachable from an ordinary authenticated action (global sign-out), not just startup.

## Acceptance criteria

- `persistJwtSecret` never opens a non-regular `jwt-secret` path for write: if the path exists and is not a regular file, rotation keeps serving the new secret in-process, warns (no secret material in the log), and does not persist — mirroring the `getOrCreateJwtSecret` degradation.
- The write decision is made on the opened handle / descriptor (or an equivalent non-racy construction), not by a by-path stat followed by a by-path write, in both write sites.
- Tests in `ui-auth.test.js` (extending the #1778 suite): a FIFO at the secret path makes the rotation/global-sign-out path settle promptly and leaves the FIFO in place; a regular file still rotates and persists with mode `0o600`; the generated secret still serves the process when persistence is refused.

body:
## Problem

Both deterministic fallback clippers in the shared text summarization service cut at fixed UTF-16 offsets with no surrogate-pair guard. `distillNoteFallback` and `distillNotificationFallback` slice the candidate at `idealLimit - 1` / `limit - 1` and append `…`; if an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles either cut, the summary ends with a lone high surrogate followed by `…` — which becomes U+FFFD when the summary is encoded (spoken by TTS, carried in a notification, or stored as a project note), corrupting the visible/spoken boundary character. These fallbacks are the live path today: `summarizeText` reports the model provider unavailable and returns the fallback summary.

## Evidence (main 2314e0345a483efa92b795c600b21b2a619be493)

- `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.js:93-94` — `distillNoteFallback`: `best.slice(0, Math.max(0, idealLimit - 1))` (fallback `best.slice(0, idealLimit)` on :94) — fixed code-unit cuts, no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.js:109-110` — `distillNotificationFallback`: `candidate.slice(0, Math.max(0, limit - 1))` (fallback `candidate.slice(0, limit)` on :110) — same shape.
- `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.js:119-134` — `summarizeText` returns these fallbacks for every call (reason: 'Model summarization provider unavailable').
- Callers: `packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.js:151` (`/api/text/summarize`, modes tts/note/notification) and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:103-112` (notification mode, shared summarizer for notification text).
- `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.test.js` pins the notification fallback on ASCII only (`'The implementation now correctly loads notification templates before dispatchin…'`); no surrogate-boundary case exists for either mode.
- Distinct from #1922: that issue is `truncateNotificationText` in `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/message.js:32-42` (the last-message preview), a different function in a different file; this filing is the summarizer fallbacks in `text/summarization.js`.
- Guarded in-repo precedent: `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so a value never ends in a lone surrogate.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-summarization-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing the real `summarizeText` from `text/summarization.js`:

- Notification mode, `maxLength: 100`, input `'a' × 98 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 200` → summary length 100, code unit before `…` is `0xD83D` (lone high surrogate), lone-surrogate count 1, exactly 1 U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- Note mode, `maxLength: 150`, input `'a' × 148 + '😀' + 'b' × 250` → summary length 150, code unit before `…` is `0xD83D`, lone-surrogate count 1, exactly 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- ASCII control (notification mode, `'a' × 300`, `maxLength: 100`): length 100, 0 lone surrogates, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

These summaries are user-facing output: a note distilled for a project, a notification text, and text headed for speech. An emoji landing on the clip boundary renders (or is spoken from) a string containing U+FFFD at exactly the visible end of the summary. It is the same defect class already filed for other truncation sites (#1922, #1921, #1911), in a surface those filings did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Neither fallback ever splits a surrogate pair: when a cut lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary before the `…` is appended (both the primary `limit - 1` cut and the empty-clip `limit` fallback cut, in both functions).
- [ ] Tests in `packages/web/server/lib/text/summarization.test.js` pin both modes with a named oracle: an astral character straddling the clip produces a summary with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding) and the documented total length; existing ASCII expectations pass unchanged.
- [ ] Existing summarization, TTS-route and notification-template tests pass.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1922 (notification last-message truncation), #1921 (session-knowledge truncate), #1911 (session-assist excerpt).

body:
## Problem

The small-model prompt clamp cuts the prompt at a fixed UTF-16 offset with no surrogate-pair guard. `clampPromptToModelLimit` slices the prompt at `maxChars` and appends an ellipsis; if an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the cut, the prompt actually sent to the model ends with a lone high surrogate followed by `…` — which becomes U+FFFD when the prompt is encoded, corrupting the boundary character of the input the small model works from (session titles, summaries, commit messages and other `generateSmallModelText` callers). The truncated prompt is also one code unit over its own budget: `slice(0, maxChars) + '…'` has length `maxChars + 1`.

## Evidence (main 2314e0345a483efa92b795c600b21b2a619be493)

- `packages/web/server/lib/small-model/index.js:111` — `clampPromptToModelLimit` definition; `:122` — `` return { prompt: `${prompt.slice(0, maxChars)}…`, truncated: true }; `` — a fixed code-unit cut with no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/small-model/index.js:84-93` — `getModelInputCharBudget`: `maxChars = (contextTokens - reserve) * 4`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/small-model/index.js:323-331` — `generateSmallModelText` applies the clamp to every over-limit prompt (default `onOverflow: 'truncate'`) and sends the result as the generate prompt.
- `packages/web/server/lib/small-model/index.test.js:428` — the existing truncation test pins only ASCII (`'x' × 20,000`, 8k context → 16,000-char budget): it asserts the sent prompt ends with `…` and is under 20,000 chars; no surrogate-boundary case exists.
- Guarded in-repo precedent: `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so a value never ends in a lone surrogate; `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-401` skips a leading low surrogate on a tail slice.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-smallmodel-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), driving the real `generateSmallModelText` through a stub OpenCode HTTP server exactly as `index.test.js` does (model context 8,000, output limit 4,000 → `maxChars` 16,000):

- Input `'a' × 15,999 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 5,000` → result `inputTruncated: true`; the prompt captured at `/api/experimental/generate` has length 16,001, its last code unit before `…` is `0xD83D` (lone high surrogate), lone-surrogate count 1, and exactly 1 U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- ASCII control (`'a' × 21,000`): sent length 16,001, 0 lone surrogates, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

This clamp sits on the single funnel for small-model generation: every caller that opts into truncation sends this prompt. A character landing on the context-budget boundary is silently replaced by U+FFFD in the only copy of the input the model sees — at the exact tail the clamp deliberately kept. It is the same defect class already filed for other truncation sites (#1906, #1908, #1910, #1911, #1921, #1922), in a surface those filings did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `clampPromptToModelLimit` never splits a surrogate pair: when the cut at `maxChars` lands inside an astral character, the boundary moves to the pair boundary before the `…` is appended, and the resulting prompt length stays truthful to the stated budget (the ellipsis is accounted for).
- [ ] A test in `packages/web/server/lib/small-model/index.test.js` pins the boundary case with a named oracle: an astral character straddling the 16,000-char budget produces a sent prompt with no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding), `inputTruncated: true` still set; the existing ASCII truncation and `onOverflow: 'error'` tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Existing small-model tests pass.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1911 (session-assist excerpt), #1910 (routing history excerpts), #1921 (session-knowledge truncate), #1922 (notification truncation).

body:
## Summary

`truncateNotificationText` (`packages/web/server/lib/notifications/message.js:32-42`) cuts notification text at a fixed character offset with no surrogate-pair guard:

```js
const DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH = 250; // :1
export const truncateNotificationText = (text, maxLength = DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH) => {
  ...
  return `${text.slice(0, safeMaxLength)}...`; // :42
};
```

It is the final shaping step for the last-message text carried in notifications: `prepareNotificationLastMessage` (`message.js:45-53`) normalizes the assistant's last message and passes it through this truncation at the configured `maxLastMessageLength` (default 250). When the character at the cut is the high half of an astral character (emoji are routine in assistant replies), the notification text ends with a lone high surrogate followed by `...`; on the next UTF-8 encode (push payload, log line) that lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD, so the user sees a replacement character at exactly the visible end of the notification preview.

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main `d80108742`, two identical runs, also identical on the prior HEAD `c83639a92`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-notifmsg-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `message.js`:

- Input `'a' × 249 + U+1F600 + 'b' × 200`, limit 250 → output length 253, `charCodeAt(249) === 0xD83D` (lone high surrogate), suffix `...`, exactly 1 U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- The same defect reproduces through `prepareNotificationLastMessage` with `settings.maxLastMessageLength: 250` (same boundary character, same length).
- ASCII control (500 × `a`, limit 250): length 253, 0 U+FFFD. Under-limit control (`hi 😀`): emoji intact.

`message.test.js` pins only ASCII truncation (`truncateNotificationText('abcdef', 3) === 'abc...'`) — no surrogate-boundary case exists.

## Why it matters

This is the user-visible tail of every long notification: an assistant reply whose 250th character falls inside an emoji renders with U+FFFD in the notification preview — a visible corruption on the surface whose whole job is a faithful short preview. In-repo precedent for the correct shape exists in the same folder: the APNs collapse-id truncation (`packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-71`) explicitly stops on a code-point boundary so a value "never ends in a lone surrogate".

## Acceptance criteria

- `truncateNotificationText` never splits a surrogate pair: when the cut would land inside an astral character, back off (or advance) to a code-point boundary before appending `...`.
- Tests in `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/message.test.js` pin the boundary case with a named oracle: for an input with an astral character straddling the limit, the output contains no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode), and the same is asserted through `prepareNotificationLastMessage`; existing ASCII expectations (`'abcdef', 3 → 'abc...'`) still pass unchanged.
- Disposition recorded on this issue as an `agent-note:v1` comment.

body:
## Summary

`truncate` in the session-knowledge runtime (`packages/web/server/lib/session-knowledge/runtime.js:34-37`) cuts every knowledge entry at a fixed character offset with no surrogate-pair guard:

```js
const KNOWLEDGE_MAX_LENGTH = 8000; // :32
const truncate = (value) => (
  value.length <= KNOWLEDGE_MAX_LENGTH
    ? value
    : `${value.slice(0, KNOWLEDGE_MAX_LENGTH - 1)}…\n\n(truncated)`
);
```

`buildKnowledgeEntries` (`runtime.js:166-170`) applies it to the pinned-notes/plans entry and the memory entry — the project context written into OpenCode as the session's instruction entries, i.e. text that lands in the system prompt of every session (module header, `runtime.js:1-16`). When the character at the cut position is the high half of an astral character (emoji, some CJK/symbols), the entry ends with a lone high surrogate followed by the `…` marker; on the next UTF-8 encode that lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD, so the model is handed corrupted context at exactly the truncation boundary.

Second defect in the same expression: the marker is not counted against the budget. A truncated entry is 8,013 characters long (7,999 kept + `…\n\n(truncated)`), over the 8,000 budget the constant and its comment ("Budget for each entry; anything past it is cut", `runtime.js:31`) declare.

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main `d80108742`, identical on re-run and on the prior HEAD `c83639a92`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-knowledge-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `runtime.js` and calling the exported `buildKnowledgeEntries` with one pinned note whose body places U+1F600 straddling the cut (high surrogate at index 7,998 of the built block):

- Result entry (`openchamber.pinned`): length 8,013; `charCodeAt(7998) === 0xD83D` (lone high surrogate), followed by `…`; exactly 1 U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- ASCII control (9,000 × `a`): length 8,013, 0 U+FFFD — clean except for the same over-budget length.
- Under-limit control (`hi 😀`): emoji survives intact.

`runtime.test.js` covers truncation only by asserting the entry contains `(truncated)` (:437-444) — no surrogate-boundary or length-budget assertion exists.

## Why it matters

These entries are the pinned project context and stored-memory index injected into sessions. A pinned note or plan written in emoji/CJK-heavy prose that crosses 8,000 characters is silently corrupted at the boundary in every session that receives it, and the entry exceeds the size budget the module promises OpenCode. In-repo precedent for the correct shape exists: the APNs collapse-id truncation (`packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-71`) explicitly stops on a code-point boundary so a value "never ends in a lone surrogate".

## Acceptance criteria

- `truncate` never splits a surrogate pair: when the cut would land inside an astral character, back off (or advance) to a code-point boundary, the way `truncateToUtf8Bytes` in `apns-runtime.js` iterates code points.
- A truncated entry's total length, marker included, does not exceed `KNOWLEDGE_MAX_LENGTH` (8,000).
- Tests in `packages/web/server/lib/session-knowledge/runtime.test.js` pin both properties with a named oracle: for an input with an astral character straddling the cut, the entry contains no lone surrogate (no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode) and `entry.length <= 8000`; ASCII over-limit and under-limit emoji controls stay as they are today apart from the length accounting.
- Disposition recorded on this issue as an `agent-note:v1` comment.

body:
## Summary

`redactSensitiveText` (`packages/web/server/lib/source-control/url-redaction.js:42-56`) is the redactor used for free-form error text — relay errors (`packages/web/server/lib/relay/host-client.js:85`, `describeRelayError`, whose own comment at :82-84 says every relay error passes through it before reaching a log line or the relay status) and source-control route failures (`packages/web/server/lib/source-control/routes.js:51` and `:205`). Its only key/value patterns are:

```js
.replace(/([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*):\/\//... , ...)           // userinfo inside URLs
.replace(/\b(authorization|private-token|oauth-token)\s*[:=]\s*[^\s,;]+/gi, '$1=[redacted]')
```

So an `authorization: Bearer <token>` header value, an `x-api-key` header, and bare `key=value` credentials outside a URL all pass through **unchanged into logs**. The sibling git redactor `redactGitText` (`packages/web/server/lib/git/redaction.js`) handles exactly these shapes: Bearer scheme at :54, a `SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS` set (access_token|auth|authorization|credential|key|oauth_token|password|private_token|secret|token) at :5, and password/token assignment lines at :55. The two redactors have diverged: one was hardened, the other was not.

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main `cabb8f2bf`, two identical runs)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-redact-20261108/probe2.mjs` + `probe3.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `url-redaction.js`. `SECRET123` survives `redactSensitiveText` in:

- `authorization: Bearer SECRET123` → unchanged (leak)
- `authorization: Basic SECRET123` → unchanged (leak)
- `x-api-key: SECRET123` / `x-api-key=SECRET123` / `api-key=SECRET123` / `apikey=SECRET123` → unchanged (leaks)
- `private_token=SECRET123`, `token=SECRET123`, `access_token=SECRET123`, `client_secret=SECRET123`, `secret=SECRET123`, `password=SECRET123` (bare, outside any URL) → unchanged (leaks)
- relay-shaped: `relay error: authorization: Bearer SECRET123` and `relay error: x-api-key: SECRET123` → unchanged (leaks)

Controls (clean, as expected): credentials inside a URL are stripped (`https://x.com/r?api_key=...` → whole query dropped by `redactRemoteUrl`), and `Authorization: SECRET123` with a directly attached value is caught by the existing three-key pattern. `redactGitText` redacts the URL-query forms per-key; the point is the key/value and header forms, which only `redactGitText` covers and only inside the git surface.

## Why it matters

`describeRelayError` exists specifically because "Bun's WebSocket puts the full dial URL into its error messages" — the authors know provider/transport errors embed credentials. Provider and git error strings also routinely embed header echoes and `key=value` fragments (GitLab `private_token=`, OAuth `client_secret=`, API-key headers). Any such error reaching the relay status surface or the source-control logs today leaks the credential verbatim, while the git surface — using the other redactor — would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `redactSensitiveText` redacts, at minimum: `authorization: Bearer|Basic <value>` (scheme + value), `x-api-key` in `:`/`=` form, and bare assignments for the same sensitive key set the git redactor uses (access_token, api_key, client_secret, oauth_token, password, private_token, secret, token), without breaking the existing URL stripping or the existing `repository-identity.test.js` expectations (:313-320).
- New unit tests for `url-redaction.js` (there is no `url-redaction.test.js` today; the functions are only exercised indirectly) covering each leaked shape above plus the clean controls, with a named oracle: output must never contain the probe secret for any input shape.
- Prefer converging the two redactors' pattern sets (shared constants or a shared helper) so the next hardening lands in both surfaces at once; if convergence is out of scope, say so on the PR and cross-link this issue.

body:
## Problem

The session-assist `excerpt` function — the head/tail cut that builds the model context from conversation turns, attached quotes, and user comments — slices at fixed UTF-16 offsets with no surrogate-pair guard. If an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the head cut, the excerpt's head ends with a lone high surrogate; if it straddles the tail cut, the tail starts with a lone low surrogate. Both become U+FFFD when the assembled context is encoded for the model, corrupting the boundary character of the turn or quote the model reads.

## Evidence (main 2eb490a77c4cd985c7a71e1249963bcf797bacee)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/context.js:17-24` — `excerpt(text, limit)`: marker `'\n[Content omitted]\n'` (19 code units), `head = Math.ceil((limit - marker.length) / 2)`, `tail = limit - marker.length - head`, then `text.slice(0, head) + marker + text.slice(-tail)` — neither cut is pair-guarded; the small-limit branch (:20, `text.slice(0, Math.max(0, limit))`) has the same defect.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/context.js:125-126` — every turn's text passes through `excerpt` (`USER_CHAR_LIMIT = 8_000` for user turns, `ANSWER_CHAR_LIMIT = 16_000` for assistant turns, :4-5), as does the authored text.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/context.js:31-42` — attached content uses the same function: labels at 300, quoted sources at 4,000, link-kind message text and authored comments at 8,000.
- This module is the shared context builder: `loadAssistContext` is imported by the session-assist runtime, by `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.js:9` (routing history), and by `packages/web/server/lib/session-work/runtime.js:23` — so the corrupted excerpts reach every model call built on assist context.
- Existing tests (`packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/context.test.js:193-195`) exercise `excerpt` with ASCII only; there is no astral/surrogate case (grep for surrogate/U+1F600: no hits).
- Guarded siblings show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-401` skips a leading low surrogate on a tail slice, `packages/web/server/lib/dictation/local/worker-client.js:25-32` does the same, and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so it never ends in a lone surrogate.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-assist-excerpt-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing `excerpt` from the real `context.js` on main 2eb490a77:

- Small limit (100 → head 41, tail 40): text `'a' × 40 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 500` → head ends with a lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 40, 1 U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding. Text ending `… + '😀' + 'z' × 39` → tail starts with a lone low surrogate U+DE00 (index 60 of the excerpt), 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- Real assistant limit (16,000 → head 7,991, tail 7,990): the same straddles reproduce at scale — lone U+D83D at index 7,990 for the head cut, lone U+DE00 at index 8,010 for the tail cut, each 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- ASCII controls (20,000 × `'a'` at limit 16,000; 500 × `'a'` at limit 100): exact-limit excerpts, no lone surrogate.

## Why it matters

Session assist is the layer that decides what of a conversation the model sees next — recaps, suggestions, and (via its consumers) routing and session-work judgements all read these excerpts. The middle-omission cut exists for the longest, most substantive turns and attachments; an emoji/CJK character landing on either boundary is silently replaced by U+FFFD in the only copy of that text the model receives. It is the same defect class already filed for other truncation sites (#1906, #1907, #1908, #1909, #1866, #1803), in a surface those filings did not cover; the routing-history excerpts that cut these turns a second time at smaller limits are filed separately this run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `excerpt` never ends its head with a lone surrogate and never starts its tail with a lone low surrogate (including the small-limit branch): when a cut lands inside a surrogate pair, the boundary moves to the pair boundary, staying within the limit and keeping the `[Content omitted]` marker intact.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/session-assist/context.test.js` cover astral characters straddling the head and tail cuts at a small limit and at the real 16,000 assistant limit, asserting no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding.
- [ ] Existing session-assist tests pass; ASCII behaviour byte-identical.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1906 (session-goal auditor excerpts), #1908 (dispatch-result cut), #1909 (goal objective trim), #1866 (message-search snippets), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

body:
## Problem

The routing history excerpts cut conversation turns at fixed UTF-16 offsets with no surrogate-pair guard. `excerptHead` slices a user message at its limit and `excerptHeadTail` slices an assistant answer at its head and tail limits; if an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles any of those cuts, the excerpt ends with a lone high surrogate or starts with a lone low surrogate — which becomes U+FFFD when the history is encoded for the routing model, corrupting the boundary character of the conversation the model judges the new request against.

## Evidence (main 2eb490a77c4cd985c7a71e1249963bcf797bacee)

- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.js:12` — `excerptHead`: `` `${text.slice(0, limit).trimEnd()} […]` `` — a fixed code-unit cut; `trimEnd()` removes whitespace only, never a lone surrogate.
- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.js:14-15` — `excerptHeadTail`: `` `${text.slice(0, head).trimEnd()} […] ${text.slice(-tail).trimStart()}` `` — both cuts unguarded.
- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/defaults.js:128` — `HISTORY_LIMITS = { turns: 3, user: 600, answerHead: 300, answerTail: 300 }`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.js:17-22` — `turnsToHistory` applies these excerpts to every settled turn; `loadRoutingHistory` (:36-42) is the routing path's history source.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-work/runtime.js:252-254` — the session-work path reuses the same two helpers for its request (`REQUEST_CHARS = 1_500`, :45) and answer (`ANSWER_EDGE_CHARS = 500`, :47) excerpts, so the same defect reaches that model call too.
- There is no test file for this module at all: `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.test.js` does not exist.
- Guarded siblings show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-401` skips a leading low surrogate on a tail slice, `packages/web/server/lib/dictation/local/worker-client.js:25-32` does the same, and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so it never ends in a lone surrogate.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-routing-history-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing `excerptHead`, `excerptHeadTail`, and `turnsToHistory` from the real `history.js` on main 2eb490a77:

- Head cut at the real user limit (600): text `'a' × 599 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 500` → excerpt contains a lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 599; after UTF-8 encoding it contains exactly 1 U+FFFD.
- Head+tail head cut (300): `'a' × 299 + '😀' + …` → lone U+D83D at index 299, 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- Head+tail tail cut (300): text ending `… + '😀' + 'z' × 299` → the tail starts with a lone low surrogate U+DE00 (index 305 of the excerpt, after head + marker), 1 U+FFFD after encoding.
- `turnsToHistory` integration at the default `HISTORY_LIMITS` reproduces both: the user entry carries the lone U+D83D and the assistant entry the lone U+DE00.
- ASCII controls (2,000 × `'a'` through both helpers): no lone surrogate.

## Why it matters

This history is the conversation context the routing decision (and the session-work request/answer summary) is made from: the last settled turns, where the user's task and the previous answer's outcome sit — the head and tail are kept precisely because they carry the meaning. An emoji/CJK character landing on a cut is silently replaced by U+FFFD in the only copy of that turn the model sees. It is the same defect class already filed for other truncation sites (#1906, #1907, #1908, #1909, #1866, #1803), in a surface those filings did not cover; the session-assist `excerpt` that pre-cuts these turns at larger limits is filed separately this run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `excerptHead` never ends with a lone surrogate and `excerptHeadTail` never ends its head or starts its tail with a lone surrogate: when a cut lands inside a surrogate pair, the boundary moves to the pair boundary (the `[…]` marker and overall length contract stay truthful).
- [ ] New tests (create `packages/web/server/lib/routing/history.test.js`) cover astral characters straddling the head cut, the head+tail head cut, and the head+tail tail cut at the real `HISTORY_LIMITS` values, asserting no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding.
- [ ] Existing routing and session-work tests pass; ASCII behaviour byte-identical.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1906 (session-goal auditor excerpts), #1908 (dispatch-result cut), #1909 (goal objective trim), #1866 (message-search snippets), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

body:
## Problem

`createSessionGoal` condenses an over-limit objective in `fitObjective` (packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.js) by keeping the head and tail around a trim marker — but both cuts are plain `slice`s with no surrogate-pair guard. When an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles either cut, the condensed objective starts/ends a segment with a lone surrogate. That text is the goal's stored objective: written to the objective file (where the lone surrogate is baked in as U+FFFD at write time), kept inline in session metadata on the fallback path, and judged verbatim by the progress auditor.

## Evidence (main 51dab1a6c)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.js:62` — distilled path: `if (distilled) return distilled.slice(0, charLimit);` — a plain cut at the limit.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.js:63-65` — fallback head/tail path: `const half = Math.max(0, Math.floor((charLimit - TRIM_MARKER.length) / 2)); return `${objective.slice(0, half)}${TRIM_MARKER}${objective.slice(-half)}`;` — both cuts are fixed UTF-16 code-unit offsets with no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.js:133` — inline fallback: `objective: objectiveFile ? '' : objectiveText.slice(0, charLimit)` — the same unguarded cut applied to the (possibly uncondensed, ignore-limit) objective when the objective file cannot be written.
- Consumers: `createSessionGoal` passes the fitted text to `writeObjective` (objectives.js — the file the progress check reads back) or stores it inline in the goal record broadcast in session metadata. This is the durable objective, not a transient excerpt — #1906 covers the auditor's *excerpts* (audit.js) and its packet explicitly scopes out create.js fitObjective as a separate filing; #1907 covers the spec-writer's clip (spec-writer.js). Neither covers this function.
- Guarded siblings show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-402` and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73`.
- Existing tests (`packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.test.js`) contain no astral/surrogate case (grep for surrogate/emoji/U+1F600: no hits).

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-goal-create-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` + `probe-inline.mjs` (laptop), importing `createSessionGoal` from the real `create.js` on main 51dab1a6c, with an injected `persistSessionGoal` stub, `goalWriterSettings: { rewriteAll: false, charLimit }`, a nonexistent small-model provider (distillation fails cleanly — "OpenCode is not reachable" — so the head/tail fallback runs), and `OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR` pointed at a temp dir:

- Emoji-dense objective (`'😀' × 1,200` = 2,400 code units), charLimit 1002 (half = 453, odd): forcing the objective-file write to fail exposes the in-memory fitted objective — lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 452 (the head cut) **and** lone low surrogate U+DE00 at index 548 (the tail start); the string contains U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding.
- Same objective through the normal file path at charLimit 1002: the stored objective file `goals/<session>.md` contains exactly **2 U+FFFD** characters — one at the end of the head segment (byte 904) and one at the start of the tail segment (byte 1008) — the corruption is baked into the file at write time.
- Parity control (charLimit 1000, half = 452, even): stored file has 0 U+FFFD — the defect is exactly the boundary parity, as predicted.
- ASCII control (`'x' × 2,400`, charLimit 1000): trimmed objective with marker, 0 U+FFFD.

With the default limit (5,000) and the 95-char marker, `half` parity depends on the configured limit (Settings allows 1,000–1,000,000), so real emoji/CJK-heavy objectives hit this whenever the parity and a straddling character coincide.

## Why it matters

The fitted objective is the contract the whole goal loop runs on: it is persisted, broadcast, and handed to the progress auditor as the definition of done. Corrupting its first/last characters to U+FFFD — permanently, in the stored file — means the goal is judged against text the user never wrote, and the user inspecting the objective sees replacement characters at exactly the head/tail the trim kept. Same defect class as #1906/#1907, in the one session-goal condensation site those filings left out.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fitObjective` never returns a lone surrogate: the head cut, the tail cut, the distilled `slice(0, charLimit)`, and the inline `objectiveText.slice(0, charLimit)` in `createSessionGoal` all land on code-point boundaries (moving a boundary that lands inside a pair to the pair boundary, keeping the result within the char limit).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/create.test.js` cover an astral character straddling the head cut and the tail cut (both parities of the half), asserting the stored/inline objective has no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding, with the trim marker intact.
- [ ] Existing session-goal tests pass; ASCII behaviour byte-identical.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1906 (auditor excerpts, audit.js — its queue packet scopes this file out explicitly), #1907 (spec clip, spec-writer.js), #1866 (message-search snippets), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

## Problem

When a dispatched session's reply exceeds 50,000 characters, `outcomeBody` cuts it with a plain `slice(0, ANSWER_CHAR_LIMIT)` and no surrogate-pair guard. If an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the cut, the delivered text ends with a lone high surrogate — which becomes U+FFFD when the synthetic dispatch-result message is encoded for the parent session, corrupting the last character before the "[Cut at …]" marker.

## Evidence (main 51dab1a6c)

- `packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.js:51` — `ANSWER_CHAR_LIMIT = 50_000`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.js:182-184` — `outcomeBody`: `` `${text.slice(0, ANSWER_CHAR_LIMIT)}\n\n[Cut at ${ANSWER_CHAR_LIMIT} characters; read the rest with session.messages for ${sessionId}.]` `` — a fixed UTF-16 code-unit cut with no pair guard.
- `packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.js:195-206` — `buildDispatchResultMessage` wraps that body in the `<openchamber-session …>` synthetic message that carries the dispatched session's result to its parent; the runtime (`createDispatchResultsRuntime`, :209) delivers it onward, so the lone surrogate is encoded for the receiving session/API rather than staying a local display artifact.
- Guarded siblings show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-402` guards a tail slice against leaving a lone surrogate, and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so it "never ends in a lone surrogate".
- Existing tests (`packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.test.js`) contain no astral/surrogate case for the cut (grep for surrogate/emoji/U+1F600: no hits).

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-dispatch-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing `buildDispatchResultMessage` from the real `runtime.js` on main 51dab1a6c:

- Reply text = `'a' × 49,999 + '😀' (U+1F600) + 'b' × 100` (so the pair straddles offset 50,000): the built message contains a lone high surrogate U+D83D at the cut, and `Buffer.from(message, 'utf8')` contains U+FFFD (EF BF BD).
- ASCII control (50,100 × `'a'`): the cut message has no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD.
- Under-limit control (`'hello 😀 world'`): delivered whole, emoji intact.

## Why it matters

The dispatch-result message is how a parent session learns what its dispatched child actually answered; the cut exists precisely for the longest, most substantive replies. An emoji/CJK character landing on the boundary is silently replaced by U+FFFD in the one copy of the answer the parent is told to rely on ("read the rest with session.messages" only helps if the parent acts on it). It is the same defect class already filed/fixed for other truncation sites (#1906, #1907, #1866, #1803), in a surface those filings did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `outcomeBody`'s cut never ends with a lone surrogate: when offset 50,000 lands inside a surrogate pair, the cut moves to the pair boundary (the marker text and the stated 50,000-character figure stay accurate, or the text still truthfully describes the cut).
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.test.js` cover a reply with an astral character straddling the limit for the completed state (and the error/stopped wrappers that embed the same answer), asserting no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding.
- [ ] Existing dispatch-results tests pass; ASCII behaviour byte-identical.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1906 (session-goal auditor excerpts), #1907 (goal spec clip), #1866 (message-search snippets), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

## Problem

`normalizeGoalSpec` clips an over-limit goal spec with a plain `slice(0, charLimit)`. When an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddles the limit and the spec has no late line break, the returned spec ends with a lone high surrogate — which encodes to U+FFFD wherever the spec is stored, displayed, or fed to the progress auditor.

## Evidence (main 51dab1a6c)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/spec-writer.js:79-87` — `normalizeGoalSpec`: `const clipped = spec.slice(0, charLimit)` (:81); the line-break rescue (:84-85) only applies when `lastNewline >= charLimit * 0.8`, otherwise `clipped` is returned (after `.trim()`, which strips whitespace only and does not move a cut out of a surrogate pair).
- The clipped result is the goal spec: `writeGoalSpec` / `createSessionGoal` (`create.js`) use it as the spec that is persisted, shown in the goal UI, and judged against — so the corruption is durable, not a transient display artifact.
- Guarded siblings in the same codebase show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-402` guards a tail slice against leaving a lone surrogate, and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so it "never ends in a lone surrogate".

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-specwriter-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing `normalizeGoalSpec` from the real `spec-writer.js` on main 51dab1a6c, charLimit 500:

- Spec = 499 × `a` + 😀 + 2000 × `b` (no newlines): output length 500, ending with a lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 499; U+FFFD appears after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- Control with a line break at position 450 (≥ 0.8 × limit): output cuts at the newline, length 450, no lone surrogate — confirming the defect is specifically the no-late-newline branch.
- ASCII control: length 500, clean.

Existing tests (`spec-writer.test.js`) do not pin the pair-boundary behaviour for the clip.

## Why it matters

The spec is the contract the goal auditor judges progress against and the text the user sees as their goal. A spec whose final character is silently replaced by U+FFFD corrupts that contract at its closing line — the same defect class already fixed for guarded tails elsewhere, in a surface those fixes did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `normalizeGoalSpec` never returns a lone surrogate: when the `slice(0, charLimit)` cut lands inside a surrogate pair and the line-break rescue does not apply, the cut moves to the pair boundary.
- [ ] The line-break rescue behaviour and the `<= charLimit` length invariant are unchanged; ASCII behaviour is byte-identical.
- [ ] Regression tests in `spec-writer.test.js` cover the straddling-emoji no-newline case (asserting no lone surrogate) and the late-newline control case.
- [ ] Existing session-goal spec-writer tests pass.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1906 (session-goal auditor excerpts), #1866 (message-search buildSnippet), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

## Problem

The session-goal progress auditor excerpts the objective and the agent's latest answer before judging them, and both excerpt functions slice at fixed UTF-16 code-unit offsets with no surrogate-pair guard — so an astral character (emoji, some CJK/extended characters) straddling a cut leaves a lone surrogate at the excerpt edge. When that excerpt is encoded for the Jev request or the small-model prompt, the lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD: the auditor judges corrupted text at exactly the opening/closing boundaries it is told matter most.

## Evidence (main 51dab1a6c)

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/audit.js:50-52` — `excerptAnswer`: `` `${text.slice(0, ANSWER_HEAD_CHARS).trimEnd()}\n[…]\n${text.slice(-ANSWER_TAIL_CHARS).trimStart()}` `` with `ANSWER_HEAD_CHARS = 2_000`, `ANSWER_TAIL_CHARS = 8_000` (:48-49). `trimEnd`/`trimStart` strip whitespace only; they do not move a cut out of a surrogate pair.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/audit.js:61-67` — `excerptObjective`: head = `floor((limit - marker.length) * 0.4)`, tail = remainder; returns `` `${text.slice(0, head).trimEnd()}${marker}${text.slice(-tail).trimStart()}` `` — same unguarded cuts at both ends.
- Consumers: `buildJevAuditRequest` (:71, `state.answer = excerptAnswer(answer)`) and `buildSmallModelAuditPrompt` (:97) feed the excerpts to the judges; `runtime.js:528` passes `excerptObjective(goal.objective, getCheckObjectiveLimit())` into every progress check. The header comment (:54-60) says the check judges the objective's opening and its close ("Done when") — precisely the edges that get corrupted.
- Guarded siblings in the same codebase show the house pattern: `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.js:394-402` drops a leading low surrogate after a tail slice ("a plain slice at maxChars can land between the halves of a pair"), and `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/apns-runtime.js:60-73` truncates on a code-point boundary so it "never ends in a lone surrogate".

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-goal-audit-surrogate-20261108/probe.mjs` (laptop), importing `excerptObjective` / `buildJevAuditRequest` from the real `audit.js` on main 51dab1a6c:

- `excerptObjective`, limit 2000 (marker 55, head 778, tail 1167): emoji straddling the head cut → lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 777; emoji straddling the tail cut → lone low surrogate U+DE00 at the tail start. Both excerpts contain U+FFFD after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- `excerptAnswer` via `buildJevAuditRequest`: emoji straddling offset 2000 → lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 1999; emoji straddling the tail start → lone low surrogate U+DE00. Both become U+FFFD after UTF-8 encoding.
- ASCII control excerpt: no lone surrogates.

Existing tests (`audit.test.js:12-24`) cover only ASCII objectives/answers, so no test pins the pair-boundary behaviour.

## Why it matters

The auditor's three questions are judged on these excerpts, and its wording was validated on a labelled corpus (file header, audit.js:1-13) — feeding it U+FFFD-corrupted openings/closings is judging different text than was measured, on content (emoji/CJK-heavy goals and reports) that is common in real goals. It is the same defect class already fixed for the guarded tails in guests/service and APNs, in a surface those fixes did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `excerptObjective` never returns a lone surrogate: a head cut landing inside a surrogate pair and a tail cut landing inside a pair both move to the pair boundary; the result still satisfies `excerpt.length <= limit`.
- [ ] `excerptAnswer` (via `buildJevAuditRequest` / `buildSmallModelAuditPrompt`) never returns a lone surrogate at either cut, with the head/tail sizes otherwise unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `audit.test.js` cover all four cuts (objective head, objective tail, answer head, answer tail) with an astral character straddling each boundary, asserting no lone surrogate and that the opening/closing text is otherwise preserved.
- [ ] Existing session-goal audit tests pass; ASCII behaviour is byte-identical to today.

Related (different functions/files, same defect class): #1866 (message-search buildSnippet), #1803 (bounded-output accumulator).

body:
## Summary

`buildSnippet` (`packages/web/server/lib/message-search/store.js:99-146`) windows a message around its search match with UTF-16 code-unit offsets and slices at those offsets with no surrogate-pair guard, so three of its cuts can split an astral character (emoji and other non-BMP text) in half:

- **Window start** (`:122`, `start = anchor[0] - radius`): when the space snap at `:126-129` finds no space to move to, the snippet can begin with a lone **low** surrogate.
- **Window end** (`:123`, `end = anchor[1] + radius`): when the space snap at `:131-134` finds no space within 20 units, the snippet can end with a lone **high** surrogate (just before the appended `…`).
- **Fallback returns** (`:101` and `:109`, `text.slice(0, radius * 2)`): the no-match / lowercasing-changes-length paths cut at exactly 180 code units and can end mid-pair.

The sibling tail/window cuts elsewhere in this codebase all guard this exact case (see #1803: guests/service, the dictation worker client and the model downloader skip a leading low surrogate at a tail cut) — `buildSnippet` is the same shape of cut with no guard.

This is not an exotic input for this module: the store's own header (`store.js:1-9`) says the trigram index exists so text "in any script" matches and "CJK text needs no word segmentation" — spaceless text (CJK runs, emoji runs, long URLs/code) is precisely the text where the space snap cannot rescue the boundary, and precisely the text most likely to contain astral characters near a cut.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `9f499a294`)

Laptop probe against the real `buildSnippet` imported from the laptop primary (`~/git/fleet/probe-oc-snippet-surrogate-20261107/`, run twice, byte-identical results; full output in the creator evidence for this run):

- End cut: text `"needle " + "😀"×120` → snippet tail code points `[…, 1f600, 1f600, d83d, 2026]` — a lone high surrogate `U+D83D` immediately before the `…`.
- Start cut: text `"😀"×120 + "needle"` with radius 89 or 91 → snippet head `[2026, de00, …]` — a lone low surrogate `U+DE00` right after the leading `…` (radius 90 lands on a pair boundary and is clean, confirming the parity mechanism).
- Fallback: text `"q"×179 + "😀" + "w"×50` with a non-matching term → returned length 180 ending mid-pair (lone surrogate detected).
- Control: plain ASCII long text around a match → no lone surrogate, match intact.

A lone surrogate in the snippet is what the search UI receives: it renders as U+FFFD (or is dropped) in the result list, so the user sees a corrupted character at the snippet edge for exactly the messages — emoji-heavy or CJK — where the match window had to cut spaceless text.

## Why it matters

Message search is a living surface, and its snippets are the user's first read of a hit. A corrupted leading/trailing character is a visible papercut on common real content (emoji in chat messages are the norm, not the exception), and the fix pattern is already established in-repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `buildSnippet` never returns a string containing a lone surrogate: window start/end boundaries that land inside a surrogate pair are moved to the pair boundary (either direction is acceptable, but markers `MATCH_START`/`MATCH_END` placement and the existing word-snap behaviour stay intact).

body:
## Finding

PR #1756 made the Linear mapping UI show a "list is incomplete" note when `teamsMore` is true — but the note renders **in addition to**, not instead of, the "this workspace has no teams" note when the team list is empty. For the reachable server shape `{ teams: [], teamsMore: true }` the settings page simultaneously claims the list is incomplete **and** that the workspace has no teams — the second claim is false.

## Evidence

- PR #1756 (MERGED, merge commit `81922e718e04`, head `db037b13de62`) for issue #1732 (CLOSED).
- Current main (`cbed9e774f73`), `packages/ui/src/components/sections/integrations/LinearProjectMapping.tsx`: the truncated note renders whenever `linearMappingTeamsTruncated(mapping)` is true, and the very next block renders the `emptyTeams` note whenever `(mapping.teams ?? []).length === 0`. Neither condition excludes the other.
- The server can produce exactly that shape: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/teams.js` `listLinearTeams()` skips nodes that fail `readTeam` (missing id/key/name), and sets `teamsMore = true` when a page reports `hasNextPage` with no usable `endCursor` (and at the 20-page cap). Pages of unreadable nodes therefore return `{ connected: true, teams: [], teamsMore: true }`.
- PR #1756's coverage is helper-level only (`packages/ui/src/lib/linearProjectMapping.test.ts`): it asserts `linearMappingTeamsTruncated` on constructed literals — its headline case even asserts the literal's own `teamsMore` field — and nothing renders the component (or otherwise pins the two notes' interaction) for the empty-and-truncated state.

## Why it matters

The truncated note exists so users are not misled by an incomplete list (#1732). Rendering "this workspace has no teams" alongside it misleads in the opposite direction: a user with a large or partially unreadable workspace is told there are no teams to map at all, and may stop there instead of treating the list as incomplete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `teamsMore` is true and the team list is empty, the mapping section does **not** claim the workspace has no teams (the truncated/incomplete note is shown; the empty note is suppressed or reworded for that state).
- [ ] When `teamsMore` is false/absent and the list is empty, the existing "no teams" note still shows; when teams exist, neither note's behaviour changes.
- [ ] A test pins the empty-and-truncated combination (component render or an extracted render-decision helper), not just the `teamsMore` flag in isolation.

body:
## Finding

PR #1750 closed the ngrok stream-end flush test gap (#1694) for **stdout only**. The symmetric **stderr** flush in `startNgrokQuickTunnel` is still mutation-uncovered: deleting it keeps the whole ngrok suite green, so a regression there would ship silently — exactly the failure #1694 was filed to prevent.

## Evidence

- PR #1750 (MERGED, merge commit `260cc5e239d1`, head `7aaa29fc4ed7`) is test-only: it adds one test proving the stdout accumulator's `flush()` delivers an unterminated final URL line. Its recorded mutation check replaced only the **stdout** `flush()` call.
- Current main (`cbed9e774f73`): `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js` creates two accumulators (:379-380). Stdout `end` → `captureLines(stdoutAccumulator.flush())` (:386); stderr `end` → `captureLines(stderrAccumulator.flush())` (:395).
- `captureLines` is not diagnostics-only: it runs `extractNgrokPublicUrlFromText` over the lines (a stderr-carried URL can settle startup) and appends them to `recentOutput`, which is embedded in both startup failure errors (timeout and exit paths). An unterminated final stderr line — e.g. ngrok's fatal log line with no trailing newline — reaches both only through the :395 flush.
- Current main `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.test.js`: the only flush test is the #1750 stdout test; no test closes stderr with an unterminated final line (grep for `stderr`/`flush` in the test file returns only the stdout test's comments).

## Why it matters

ngrok writes its URL and its fatal errors as JSON log lines; the last line before a stream closes is precisely the one most likely to carry the decisive diagnostic. If the stderr flush regresses (or is dropped in a future accumulator refactor like #1705's), startup failures lose that line and a stderr-delivered URL never settles — with no test failing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test in `ngrok-tunnel.test.js`: the fake ngrok writes an unterminated final line to **stderr**, then closes stderr while staying alive; the line observably reaches capture (startup resolves from a stderr-carried URL, or the line appears in the startup error's output summary).
- [ ] Mutation check recorded on the PR/issue: removing the stderr `flush()` call in `startNgrokQuickTunnel` makes the new test fail.
- [ ] Existing ngrok tunnel suite passes unchanged otherwise.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #1750 (batch 2026-11-07 23:24 CST, watermark 1749 → 1797). Deduped against open/recently-closed issues and lane B's filings (#1821–#1825) and backlog REVIEW-FINDINGs. Related but distinct: #1693 / PR #1702 and #1767 concern flushing accumulators in the `exit` handler (exit-before-`end` race) — neither pins the stderr stream-`end` flush itself, which is this issue's scope. Lane B recorded this candidate as an unpromoted REVIEW-FINDING in `backlog-devtoday-openchamber.md`; this issue promotes it.

title: fix(web): plan-store readers report every I/O error as "is not valid JSON" — an unreadable valid plans.json / pool-plan-links.json gets the malformed-file 409 and the real error is discarded

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web

body:
## Summary

`readPlanStore` (`packages/web/server/lib/routing/plans.js:110-112`) and `readPoolPlanLinks` (`packages/web/server/lib/routing/pool-plan-links.js:44-46`) wrap their `readBoundedFileSync` call in a bare `catch {}` and rethrow **every** failure as:

> `<file> is not valid JSON. Fix or move it before saving …` — HTTP 409, `PLAN_STORE_MALFORMED` / `POOL_LINKS_MALFORMED`

But the shared bounded reader's contract (`packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, header comment) is explicit: expected outcomes (missing / too-large / not-regular) are **returned**, not thrown — and both callers already handle those three distinctly (plans.js:114-121, pool-plan-links.js:48-55). What actually reaches the `catch` is only an **unexpected I/O error** (EACCES, EIO, ELOOP, …) — none of which means the file is malformed JSON. The original error is discarded entirely: no `cause`, no error code in the message.

So a perfectly valid `plans.json` that the server process cannot read (wrong permissions/ownership after a restore, a mounted data dir, …) tells the user to "fix or move" a healthy file, and support/debugging gets a 409 that points at JSON corruption instead of the real `EACCES`.

The correct pattern already exists in the same codebase: `packages/web/server/lib/environment/store.js:120-123` catches the same reader's throw and reports `environment.json is unreadable: ${error?.code ?? 'error'}` — a distinct, truthful diagnostic that preserves the error code.

## Evidence (main `d0ca5b842a6e86893dd3b438a68a17764f431493`, 2026-11-07)

Laptop probe against the real `readPlanStore` / `readPoolPlanLinks` (node, run twice, identical both times; probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-plans-eacces-20261107/` on the laptop):

```
plans/control-valid:          OK -> {"version":1,"plans":[],"models":{},"pools":{}}
links/control-valid:          OK -> {"version":1,"links":{}}
plans/malformed:              THROW status=409 code=PLAN_STORE_MALFORMED msg=…/plans.json is not valid JSON. Fix or move it before saving plan information.
links/malformed:              THROW status=409 code=POOL_LINKS_MALFORMED msg=…/pool-plan-links.json is not valid JSON. Fix or move it before linking pool targets to plans.
plans/eacces-valid-content:   THROW status=409 code=PLAN_STORE_MALFORMED msg=…/plans.json is not valid JSON. Fix or move it before saving plan information.
links/eacces-valid-content:   THROW status=409 code=POOL_LINKS_MALFORMED msg=…/pool-plan-links.json is not valid JSON. Fix or move it before linking pool targets to plans.
```

The EACCES cases contain **valid JSON** (mode `000`, uid-owned); their errors are byte-for-byte identical to the genuinely-malformed cases, so the two situations are indistinguishable to the user and to any log reader.

Note the near-verbatim duplication: the two catch blocks are copies of each other (as are the two JSON-parse catches below them, plans.js:124-125 / pool-plan-links.js:58-59, which are correct — a parse failure *is* invalid JSON). Only the bounded-read catches mislabel the failure. (`readNotes` in the same plans.js:225 has no catch at all and lets the I/O error propagate raw — a third, inconsistent behaviour worth aligning while here, but not the defect filed.)

## Why it matters

Plans and pool-plan links drive the routing/pool-health surfaces. When the data dir's permissions break (a common restore/migration accident), the current message sends the user to edit or delete a valid file — at best wasted effort, at worst they "fix" it by moving it away and lose their plans. A truthful `unreadable: EACCES` message makes the actual fix (permissions) obvious.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unexpected I/O error from the bounded read (e.g. EACCES) in `readPlanStore` and `readPoolPlanLinks` produces a distinct diagnostic that names the file as **unreadable** and preserves the underlying error code (in the message and/or as `error.cause`) — following the `environment/store.js:121-122` pattern
- [ ] Genuinely malformed JSON still yields the existing `is not valid JSON` 409s (parse-catch behaviour unchanged); missing / too-large / not-regular outcomes unchanged
- [ ] Regression tests: a read that throws a non-JSON I/O error (e.g. an unreadable file, or a stubbed reader throw) asserts the new diagnostic for both stores, and the malformed-JSON case still asserts the old one
- [ ] Probe re-run: the `eacces-valid-content` cases report the unreadable diagnostic (with `EACCES` visible) while the `malformed` cases are unchanged

title: fix(web): shared bounded-output accumulator never validates maxChars — 0 makes slice(-0) keep the whole string and silently defeats the bound (PR #1752)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: status/needs-triage

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

The shared bounded output accumulator extracted by PR #1752 (`createBoundedOutputAccumulator`, the one implementation both tunnel modules now share per #1705) takes a `maxChars` option and never validates it. The bound is applied as `.slice(-maxChars)` in three places; with `maxChars: 0`, `slice(-0)` is `slice(0)` — the **whole string** — so the "bound" silently keeps everything: `recentText` and the held partial line grow without limit, the exact unbounded accumulation the primitive exists to prevent. A negative value slices from `length + maxChars`, keeping an arbitrary tail unrelated to any stated bound. No test constructs the accumulator with `maxChars: 0` or a negative value.

Today both production call sites (cloudflare-tunnel.js, ngrok-tunnel.js) call the factory with no argument and get the 64 KiB default, so this is latent, not live. But the option is the primitive's public contract — #1705's whole point was one shared implementation future callers rely on — and a caller passing a computed cap that can reach 0 (e.g. a remaining-budget calculation) would silently lose the bound instead of failing loudly. (Separately filed: #1803 covers this file's slices splitting surrogate pairs — a different defect at the same slice sites.)

## Evidence

- PR #1752 (MERGED, merge commit `c939e36f0347`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1752 — extracts the shared accumulator for #1705.
- Current main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc` (verified twice via the commits API; merge commit verified an ancestor of main in a fresh clone):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-output-accumulator.js:18` — `createBoundedOutputAccumulator({ maxChars = BOUNDED_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS } = {})` with no validation of the value.
  - Same file :25 (`recentText` in `push`), :30 (`pendingLine` in `push`), :36 (`recentText` in `flush`) — all three bounds are `(…).slice(-maxChars)`; `slice(-0) === slice(0)` returns the full string in JS.
  - The accumulator's tests exercise the default cap and line/flush behaviour; no case passes `maxChars: 0` or a negative number.

## Why it matters

A bounding primitive that silently un-bounds itself on an edge input is worse than one that throws: the failure mode is the memory growth the cap was supposed to make impossible, with no error anywhere. Shared primitives are exactly where a one-line validation pays for itself across every future caller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Constructing the accumulator with a non-positive or non-finite `maxChars` either throws a clear error or is clamped to a stated minimum — the chosen behaviour is documented in the module comment.
- [ ] Tests pin the `maxChars: 0` and negative cases, and pin that a small positive `maxChars` (e.g. 1) still bounds `recentText` and the held line.
- [ ] Default behaviour for the two existing no-arg call sites is unchanged; existing accumulator/tunnel tests still pass.
