body:
## Finding

PR #1786 routed the VS Code quota providers through the shared `keyOrTokenFrom` / `accessOrTokenFrom` selectors so a blank first credential field falls through to the valid second field identically in `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` and every fetch path (the #1759 defect: `||` on one side, `??` on the other, blank bearers sent). Its new regression suite pins the **positive** fallthrough — blank first field + valid second field → the second field is actually sent — for exactly **1 of the 11** provider ids: deepinfra, through its exported `fetchDeepinfraQuota` readAuth seam. For the other ten, the parametrized cases use single-field blank credentials and assert only "not configured, sends nothing" — the both-fields-present case, which is the selector's whole purpose, is unasserted on ten fetch paths. The test file's own comment concedes the shape: "The second field is the fallback the shared selector exists for: exercised through DeepInfra's readAuth seam…".

A regression in any one of the other ten fetch paths (e.g. a fetcher re-selecting with `||`/`??` directly, or reading the entry's fields in the wrong order) keeps the suite green while re-introducing #1759 for that provider. The sibling web suite from PR #1776 pins the positive fallthrough for all eight of its providers through the parametrized table; the VS Code suite is measurably weaker than the pattern it mirrors.

## Evidence

- PR #1786 (MERGED, merge commit `928d8ff0eb08`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1786 — fixes #1759. (Title says "ten" providers; body and test enumerate 11 ids.)
- Current main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc` (verified twice via the commits API; merge commit verified an ancestor of main in a fresh clone):
  - `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.test.ts:3523-3550` — the parametrized table: 11 provider ids, each case's credential is a single blank first field (`blankKey`/`blankOauth`), asserting `configured === false` and zero fetch calls.
  - `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.test.ts:3552-3571` — the only positive-fallthrough tests, deepinfra-only, via `fetchDeepinfraQuota({ readAuth })`, asserting `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for `{ key: '  ', token: 'real-token' }` and `{ key: '', token: 'real-token' }`.
  - `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:454-464` — the shared selectors themselves; nothing in the suite asserts that the other ten fetchers (claude, codex, github-copilot + addon, zai, zhipuai, openrouter, nano-gpt, neuralwatt, deepseek) select through them when both fields are present.

## Why it matters

#1759's bug was a configured/fetch disagreement caused by two selection spellings. The fix centralizes selection, but the regression net only proves centralization end-to-end for deepinfra; for the other ten providers it proves only the blank-credential half. The untested half is the half that sends a credential.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each of the 11 provider ids in the #1759 set, a test pins the positive fallthrough: blank/whitespace first field + valid second field → the provider is configured and the sent Authorization/token header carries the second field (through each fetcher's existing seam, exporting a fetcher for testability where deepinfra's pattern requires it).

title: fix(web): relay writeClaim's FIFO protection is probe-then-write by path — a FIFO swapped in after the probe still blocks the write open (PR #1769)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Finding

PR #1769 (for #1739) made the relay host claim read handle-judged and bounded, and set out to protect the write side too: `writeClaim` must never open a FIFO for write, because opening a FIFO for write blocks until a reader appears — freezing the relay claim path. The write-side protection is **probe-then-write by path**, not handle-judged: `writeClaim` first probes the claim path with `boundedReadSync` and returns early only if the probe reports `not-regular`; it then calls `fsImpl.writeFileSync(lockFilePath, …)` on the path. A FIFO swapped in between the probe and the write — the same swap-after-check threat model this codebase's other stores explicitly defend against (grows-after-stat / swapped-before-validation is a named, tested pattern in the sibling bounded-read work) — re-opens the exact event-loop freeze the PR eliminates: `writeFileSync` on a FIFO path blocks on open until a reader appears.

The module's own comment overstates the protection ("A non-regular file (e.g. a FIFO) at the claim path must never be opened for write either"), and the DOCUMENTATION bounded-read inventory row for this store reads as bound-complete on both halves.

## Evidence

- PR #1769 (MERGED, merge commit `5c63b77f668b`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1769 — fixes #1739.
- Current main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc` (verified twice via the commits API; merge commit verified an ancestor of main in a fresh clone):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/relay/host-lock.js:99-120` — `writeClaim`: :106 probes `boundedReadSync(lockFilePath, RELAY_HOST_CLAIM_MAX_BYTES)` and returns `true` only on `reason === 'not-regular'`; :113 then writes by path with `fsImpl.writeFileSync(lockFilePath, JSON.stringify({ pid: selfPid, … }))`. Probe and write are two separate path resolutions with no handle carried across.
  - Contrast `readClaim` in the same file (:83-97), which is genuinely handle-judged through the bounded reader — the write half is the asymmetric one.
  - The fake-fs test adapter for this module cannot return `not-regular` from the probe, so the early-exit branch is covered only by the one real-fs FIFO test, which exercises a FIFO present before the probe — not one swapped in after it.

## Why it matters

The claim watch runs on the relay's 30 s supervision path; a blocked write open stalls the server event loop, which is the failure #1739/#1769 exist to prevent. The window is narrow and the likelihood low, but the fix's stated guarantee ("must never be opened for write") does not hold as written, and the documentation row records the store as fully bound — the next reader of the inventory will trust a guarantee the code doesn't keep.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `writeClaim` writes through a handle judged non-regular at open time (e.g. open with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_NONBLOCK`, fstat-judge the handle, write through it), so a FIFO present at write-open time — whenever it appeared — cannot block; or the probe-then-write window is explicitly documented as accepted in the module and the DOCUMENTATION row corrected.
- [ ] A test pins the swapped-in-after-probe FIFO case (or the handle-judged write) the way sibling stores pin grows-after-stat.
- [ ] Existing host-lock tests (claim read/write, FIFO read refusal, fallback-to-start behaviour) still pass.

title: fix(web): over-cap and FIFO managed-process claim files can never be reaped — the bounded sweep read fails deterministically forever and the files are invisible in its counts (PR #1758)

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Finding

PR #1758 routed the managed-process registry's claim reads through the bounded reader under a 1 KiB cap (`MANAGED_PROCESS_CLAIM_MAX_BYTES` — a claim file is one pid integer). In `sweepDeadHolderClaims`, a claim whose bounded read fails is caught and "left for a later sweep, never guessed at". For a regular claim naming a live holder that is the right call — but an **over-cap or non-regular (FIFO) claim can never become readable**: its read fails deterministically on every sweep, forever. Such a claim file is never reaped, never counted (`reapOrphanedProcesses` reports it as neither inspected nor reaped), and never logged — a permanent, invisible leak in the registry directory, created by exactly the malformed-file states the bounded-reader migration was built to handle.

The PR's own test suite pins the leak as intended behaviour: "an over-cap claim is left for a later sweep, not swept as a dead holder" and "a FIFO claim settles the sweep and is left in place" — with no later mechanism that could ever settle either file.

## Evidence

- PR #1758 (MERGED, merge commit `a9cd93b5fb71`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1758 — fixes #1736 (the unbounded registry reads).
- Current main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc` (verified twice via the commits API; merge commit verified an ancestor of main in a fresh clone):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-process-registry.js:260-296` — `sweepDeadHolderClaims`: :263 reads the claim via `readBoundedText(claim.filePath, MANAGED_PROCESS_CLAIM_MAX_BYTES)`; any throw lands in the outer `catch` (:293-295) commented "Unreadable claim files are left for a later sweep, never guessed at."
  - The bounded read refuses over-cap and non-regular files by construction (`lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`), so those two classes fail identically on every future sweep; nothing else in the registry removes claim files except `removeClaimFilesForPid` (called for known pids on the normal paths) — an unreadable claim's pid-from-filename is never used as a fallback judgement.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-process-claim.test.js` — the over-cap test writes `999999` + 2,048 spaces (> 1 KiB cap) and pins the file left in place; the FIFO test pins the file left in place; neither has a companion "eventually reaped" case.

## Why it matters

Claim files exist to coordinate live/dead holder handover; #942/#1000 already had to give claim files an end of life once. A claim that is malformed in the two ways this migration explicitly anticipates (over-cap, FIFO) now has no end of life at all, and because the sweep counts it as nothing, the leak is invisible in the sweep's own reporting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A claim file that can never be read (over-cap or non-regular across repeated sweeps) reaches a terminal disposition — e.g. judged by its filename pid's liveness, quarantined/renamed aside with a log line, or removed after a stated grace — instead of being left forever.
- [ ] The disposition is visible: the sweep's inspected/reaped counts or a warning log account for permanently unreadable claims.
- [ ] Tests pin the terminal disposition for both the over-cap and FIFO claim shapes, replacing or extending the current "left in place" pins; readable live/dead holder behaviour is unchanged.

title: fix(web): route feedback compaction discards appends from another process — tail is read, fd closed, then temp+rename replaces the file unconditionally (PR #1749)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #1749 added append-side compaction to the route feedback log: when an append pushes the file past the 4 MiB cap, `recordFeedback` reads the newest 3 MiB tail from the open fd, closes the fd, and replaces the file via temp-write + rename (`writeFeedbackSnapshot`). The replacement is unconditional — nothing re-checks the file after the tail is read. Any feedback appended by another process sharing the OpenCode data directory between the tail read and the rename is silently discarded: the rename swaps in a snapshot taken before that append existed.

`recordFeedback` is fully synchronous, so a single process cannot interleave with itself; the exposure is cross-process. The store's own header states these files live in OpenCode's data directory and the sibling overrides file's format "must stay in step with `ModelRouteOverrides.parse`" — this directory is shared territory (the web server, the VS Code embedded server, and OpenCode itself all resolve the same data dir), so a second writer appending feedback in the compaction window is a realistic, if narrow, case. The compacted file is the interpreter's learned-choices input (`route-rules-routes.js` reads it per request), so lost entries are lost learning data with no signal anywhere.

## Evidence

- PR #1749 (MERGED, merge commit `bc399ffca4bf`, head `89830ea34`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1749 — bounds routing plan, pool-link, and feedback reads and adds the feedback compaction.
- Current main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc` (verified twice via the commits API; merge commit verified an ancestor of main in a fresh clone):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/routing/route-overrides-store.js:185-228` — `recordFeedback`: appends through the fd, computes `retained = feedbackTail(fd, stat.size)` (:205-207), closes the fd in `finally`, then calls `writeFeedbackSnapshot(feedbackFile, retained, mode)` with no re-stat, no lock, and no comparison against the file's current size/content.
  - `route-overrides-store.js:28-41` — `writeFeedbackSnapshot` writes `${file}.${pid}.<random>.tmp` and renames it over the live file unconditionally.
  - `route-overrides-store.js:43-60` — `feedbackTail(fd, size)` reads from the already-closed-after snapshot of the file: bytes appended after that read are not in `retained` and are not preserved by the rename.
- The existing compaction test (`route-overrides-store.test.js`, "keeps the newest complete feedback lines when the log reaches its cap") is single-process and single-writer; nothing pins the concurrent-append behaviour.

## Why it matters

Compaction is the one moment the feedback log is rewritten wholesale. A silent discard window at exactly that moment loses user feedback entries (the data the route interpreter learns from) with no warning — the compaction failure path logs, but the success path cannot detect that it overwrote a newer append.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An append that lands between the tail read and the rename survives compaction (e.g. re-stat/re-read under the rename decision, append the tail through the fd instead of replacing by path, or detect size/mtime change and retry the compaction), or the loss window is explicitly documented in the module documentation as accepted.
- [ ] A regression test simulates a second writer appending during compaction and pins that its entry is still present afterwards (or pins the documented accepted-loss behaviour).
- [ ] Existing feedback tests (cap, retention, FIFO, mode preservation) still pass.

body:
## Summary

A GitLab merge request's reference preview reports the wrong comment total: `fetchGitLabReferenceDetail` (packages/ui/src/components/references/gitlabReferences.ts) merges issue notes, review notes and verdicts into one thread, slices it to the newest 50, but sets `commentTotal` to `changeRequestContext.issueComments.length` — the raw issue-note count alone (line 238). That number is neither the merged thread's total nor the count of what was sliced, so the preview's "Latest {shown} of {total}" header (ReferencePreview.tsx `CommentsSection`, shown when `total > shown`) is wrong in both directions:

- **Silent truncation:** 30 issue notes + 40 review notes = 70 in the thread; the preview shows the newest 50 and reports total 30, so no truncation header appears and 20 comments are hidden as if the thread were complete.
- **False truncation:** 30 thread openers + 50 replies (replies nest under their openers) = 80 raw issue notes but only 30 top-level entries, all of them shown; the preview reports total 80 and claims "Latest 30 of 80".
- Even with no slicing, the total is wrong: 1 issue note + 1 review note + 1 verdict renders 3 comments with `commentTotal` 1.

The sibling issue branch in the same function (line 226) does it correctly: `commentTotal: comments.length`, the pre-slice merged count. The GitHub detail builder likewise reports a total for its whole thread.

## Evidence (main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc`, 2026-11-07)

Laptop probe against the real `fetchGitLabReferenceDetail` with stubbed reads (bun test, run twice, identical both times; probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-gitlab-commenttotal-20261107/`):

```
A merged=70 shown=50 commentTotal=30 headerShows=false
B toplevel=30 shown=30 commentTotal=80 headerShows=true
C merged=60 shown=50 commentTotal=60 headerShows=true
D merged=60 shown=50 commentTotal=60 headerShows=true
E merged=3 shown=3 commentTotal=1
```

C (60 flat issue notes on an MR) and D (GitLab issue, 60 comments) are controls: correct by accident / by construction. The existing test suite (gitlabReferences.test.ts, the detail test at ~line 104) builds a 1 issue + 1 review + 1 verdict thread but never asserts `commentTotal`.

Code: gitlabReferences.ts:232-238 builds `comments` from `threadedComments([...issueComments, ...reviewComments])` plus verdicts, returns `comments: comments.slice(-50)` with `commentTotal: changeRequestContext.issueComments.length`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a GitLab merge request, `commentTotal` equals the number of top-level thread entries before the 50-entry slice (issue notes after threading + review notes after threading + verdicts) — i.e. the same quantity the issue branch in the same function reports
- [ ] Probe cases A, B and E above report totals 70, 30 and 3 respectively; controls C and D stay 60
- [ ] A regression test in gitlabReferences.test.ts asserts `commentTotal` for a mixed issue+review+verdict thread, including one over the 50-entry slice and one with threaded replies
- [ ] No change to what is shown (the newest-50 slice and threading stay as they are); only the reported total changes

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

On merged PR #1554, CodeRabbit raised test-coverage findings for the new incremental-decoding / byte-cap tests in `packages/web/server/lib/environment/runtime.test.js` that were never replied to and are still missing on current main. (The Codex P2 on the same PR was fixed in ec42c24ae; these CodeRabbit items were not addressed.)

1. **Split two-byte character not covered** (Minor, inline): the chunk-split test splits only inside the four-byte emoji; the `é` in `café` stays whole in the first chunk, so a split inside a two-byte character (bytes `C3 A9`) is not exercised.
   - Comment: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1554#discussion_r4465863948 — coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-04T09:25:36Z, `runtime.test.js:138`
2. **Trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence not covered** (review-body nitpick): both new tests end on complete characters, so removing the `decoder.end()` call in `runCommand` leaves them passing — a regression that drops trailing bytes would not be caught. Suggested case: stdout `KEY=abc` followed by byte `0xC3`, asserting the applied value is `abc\uFFFD`.
3. **Cumulative multi-chunk cap not covered** (review-body nitpick): the byte-cap test sends one oversized chunk, so a per-chunk-only cap check would also pass it; the cumulative-across-chunks path in `runCommand` is untested. Suggested case: two 3 MiB chunks (6 MiB total) must trigger `output-too-large`.
   - Review: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1554#pullrequestreview-5766170868 — coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-04T09:25:37Z

## Evidence

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1554 (merged)
- No-response evidence: the inline thread (4465863948) has no replies and is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-08); no later commit added these cases.
- Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-08 via `gh api` read of `runtime.test.js`): the split test (line 129) splits at `emojiStart + 2` inside the emoji only; the cap test (line ~152) uses a single `fakeChild` output string; no test covers a trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence.
- Dedupe: searched open and closed issues for runtime.test / incomplete UTF-8 / decoder keywords on 2026-11-08 — no existing issue covers these gaps.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add the three test cases to `runtime.test.js` (oracle: StringDecoder semantics — a split two-byte character decodes intact; a trailing incomplete sequence surfaces as U+FFFD via `decoder.end()`; the byte cap is cumulative across chunks), each shown to fail against the corresponding broken implementation (per-chunk decoding, dropped `decoder.end()`, per-chunk cap check).
- Or resolve this issue by a documented decision that these cases are covered elsewhere (cite the covering tests).

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

On merged PR #1568, CodeRabbit raised a **Major** finding that was never replied to, never fixed, and is still live on current main:

> **Handle inaccessible parent and source repos before the fallback search.** GitHub Search returns `422` for the whole query when one `repo:` qualifier names a repo the token cannot access. `expandRepoNetwork` adds parent and source repos from metadata without an access check. `searchFallbackPr` rethrows the `422`, and `resolveGitHubPrStatus` does not catch it. The status request then fails, even when the accessible repo has the PR. Check each parent or source repo before adding its qualifier, or handle the `422` and keep the accessible targets.

## Evidence

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1568 (merged)
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1568#discussion_r4467377318 — coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-04T12:22:30Z, `packages/web/server/lib/github/pr-status.js:629`
- No-response evidence: the comment thread has no replies and is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-08); no fix commit followed it on the PR (the Codex P2 on the same PR was fixed in 439ec0bd3, this CodeRabbit thread was not addressed).
- Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-08, two independent `gh api` reads of `packages/web/server/lib/github/pr-status.js`):
  - `expandRepoNetwork` (lines 311–327) pushes `metadata.parent` / `metadata.source` repos with no access check.
  - `searchFallbackPr` (line 627; inner catch at line ~678) returns `null` for 403/404 but rethrows any other status — a 422 propagates.
  - `resolveGitHubPrStatus` calls `searchFallbackPr` in its fallback loop (line ~973) with no surrounding try/catch, so one inaccessible parent/source repo fails the entire PR-status request.
- Dedupe: searched open and closed issues for "422", "searchFallbackPr", "inaccessible parent" and pr-status keywords on 2026-11-08 — no existing issue covers this finding.

## Acceptance criteria

- Verify the finding against current main and record the verdict on this issue.
- Fix it so an inaccessible parent/source repo cannot fail the whole status request: e.g. check access before adding the `repo:` qualifier, or catch the 422 and retry the search with only the accessible targets.
- Add a regression test: fallback search where one network repo is inaccessible (422) still returns the PR found in an accessible repo.
- Or resolve this issue by a documented decision explaining why the scenario cannot occur.

title: fix(ui): i18n placeholder parity is untested and broken both ways — 122 locale strings drop the values callers pass, and 4 English integrate strings drop the {count} their callers and zh translations provide

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Summary

The UI's i18n dictionaries are kept in **key** parity by test (`packages/ui/src/lib/i18n/messages.test.ts`, "all locales stay in key parity with english"), but nothing checks **placeholder** parity — and it is broken in both directions. A probe comparing the `{placeholder}` set of every English string against each of the 14 other locales (9,089 keys) found **122 mismatches**, verified twice with identical results on main `4e6f75b43`:

### Direction 1 — locales drop placeholders English has (113 strings)

Almost all in the `gitView.*` family, in es (19), pl (22), pt-BR (19), fr (18), uk (18), ko (17), zh-CN/zh-TW (a few), plus `pl filesView.editor.saveNowManualTitle` dropping `{shortcut}`. The translations are generic rewordings that silently discard the value the caller passes:

- `gitView.changes.revertFileAria` — en: `'Revert changes in {path}'` (`packages/ui/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.ts:999`); fr: `'Rétablir le fichier'` (`fr.ts:814`). The caller passes the path — `ChangeRow.tsx:110`: `aria-label={t('gitView.changes.revertFileAria', { path: file.path })}` — so a French screen-reader user hears "revert the file" with no idea which file. Same shape for `collapseDirectoryAria` / `expandDirectoryAria` / `selectFileAria` / `toggleDirectorySelectionAria` (`{path}`), `gitView.conflict.*` and `gitView.stash.*` (`{operation}`), `gitView.header.removeRemote*` (`{name}`), `gitView.branch.branchToMergeInto` (`{branch}`).
- de, ja, nl, tr, ar, he keep the placeholders for the same keys (e.g. de `fr.ts` counterpart: `'Änderungen in {path} rückgängig machen'`), so parity is clearly the intended norm — these locales just lost the values.

### Direction 2 — English drops a placeholder its translations and callers have (8 strings)

`gitView.integrate.conflictsInFiles`, `moreFiles`, `showingFirstCommits`, `toMoveCount` in zh-CN and zh-TW carry `{count}` (e.g. zh-CN `'{count} 个文件存在冲突'`, `zh-CN.ts:1147`), but the English strings are bare labels — `'Conflicts in files'`, `'More files'`, `'Showing first commits'`, `'To move'` (`en.ts:1146/1150/1162/1165`). The callers pass the count in every locale — `IntegrateCommitsSection.tsx:347` (`toMoveCount, { count: ui.plan.commits.length }`), `:470`, `:480`, `:492` — so **English** users are the ones who never see how many commits/files are involved, while zh users do.

## Why it matters

- Aria labels and confirmation titles/descriptions are exactly where the identifying value (which file, which operation, which remote, how many commits) matters most; in 7 locales those surfaces are silently generic.
- In English, four integrate-view labels omit counts the UI already computed and passed.
- The existing test suite cannot catch any of this: it checks key parity and a handful of spot keys only, so every future translation refresh can regress placeholders invisibly. This is the same blind spot as #1813 (untranslated key), one level down.

## Evidence

- Probe (run twice, identical: `TOTAL_MISMATCHES 122 EN_KEYS 9089`): laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-i18n-placeholders-20261107/probe.ts` + full list in `all.txt` — imports the real dictionaries from `packages/ui/src/lib/i18n/messages/{en,de,fr,nl,es,ja,ko,pl,pt-BR,uk,zh-CN,zh-TW,tr,ar,he}.ts` and diffs the `{placeholder}` set per key.
- Spot-verified in source: `en.ts:999` vs `fr.ts:814`; `en.ts:1142` vs `fr.ts:956`; `en.ts:1146/1150/1162/1165` vs `zh-CN.ts:1147/1151/1163/1166`; callers `ChangeRow.tsx:110`, `IntegrateCommitsSection.tsx:347/470/480/492`, `FilesView.tsx:4540/4546`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every locale string carries the same placeholder set as its English source (or English gains the placeholder, for the integrate counts) — the probe above reports 0 mismatches.
- [ ] The four English `gitView.integrate.*` strings include `{count}`, matching what their callers pass and what zh-CN/zh-TW already render.
- [ ] The dropped-value translations (gitView family in es/pl/pt-BR/fr/uk/ko + the pl saveNowManualTitle) name the value again — rewording is fine, losing `{path}`/`{operation}`/`{name}`/`{branch}`/`{shortcut}` is not.
- [ ] `messages.test.ts` gains a placeholder-parity test over all locales (same shape as the existing key-parity test) so this cannot regress silently.
- [ ] Existing i18n tests pass (note: #1813 currently has the suite red for an unrelated untranslated key — do not conflate; this issue's test must pass on its own keys).

`basic: type-check` in pr-checks fails on main: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-fs-helpers-attachment.test.ts(1,46): error TS2307: Cannot find module 'bun:test'`. The file imports `bun:test`, but `packages/vscode/tsconfig.json` declares `"types": ["node"]` with no Bun types, and the package's other suites use `node:test`. This is one of the two current main-red components in the #813 tracker.

body:
# fix(web): guest clone stderr byte tail can split a multi-byte UTF-8 character — the 4096-byte cut in runGit lands mid-character and the failure diagnostic starts with U+FFFD

## Evidence (verified this run, main `4e6f75b43300d7667508804a9b939af713183ebc`)

`packages/web/server/lib/guests/clone.js`:

- `:186` — `const STDERR_TAIL_BYTES = 4096;`
- `:249-252` — the stderr tail is kept as raw bytes and cut at a raw byte offset, with no regard for UTF-8 character boundaries:

```js
let stderrTail = Buffer.alloc(0);
child.stderr?.on('data', (chunk) => {
  const joined = Buffer.concat([stderrTail, chunk]);
  stderrTail = joined.subarray(Math.max(0, joined.length - STDERR_TAIL_BYTES));
});
```

- `:243` and `:272` — both failure paths decode that byte tail in one shot: `stderrTail.toString('utf8')` (the `output-too-large` overflow result and the non-zero-exit result). If the cut landed inside a multi-byte character, its leading bytes are gone and the remaining continuation byte(s) decode to U+FFFD — the very first character of the diagnostic the user sees for a failed guest clone/fetch.

The chunk handling itself is sound (buffers are concatenated as bytes and decoded once, so a character split across pipe chunks survives — that part was dispositioned sound in the #1741 stream audit). The defect is only the tail-window cut: it is a second, independent place a character can be split, and the audit's buffer-then-decode reasoning does not cover it.

### Probe (laptop, against the real exported `runGit`, run twice — identical both times)

Fake `git` (via the `gitBinary` seam) writes 100 ASCII bytes + `€` (3 UTF-8 bytes) + 4095 ASCII bytes to stderr and exits 1, so the 4096-byte tail window starts on the last continuation byte of `€`:

- split case: `ok:false`, `stderr.length === 4096`, first character is U+FFFD (`fffdIndex: 0`)
- ASCII control (same layout, `EUR` in place of `€`): tail starts with `R`, no U+FFFD anywhere

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-clone-stderrtail-20261107/` on the laptop (`probe.mjs` + `fake-git.mjs`).

### The guarded precedent in the same codebase

`packages/web/server/lib/terminal/runtime.js:151` keeps a byte tail the same way and explicitly aligns the cut: `while (start < bytes.length && (bytes[start] & 0xc0) === 0x80) start += 1;` — it skips leading continuation bytes so its scrollback tail never starts mid-character. The string tails in `guests/service`, the dictation worker client and the model downloader likewise guard their cuts (#1803 covers the one unguarded string tail, in the shared bounded-output accumulator). `runGit`'s byte tail is the remaining unguarded one.

## Why it matters

This stderr tail is the diagnostic surfaced when a guest repo clone/fetch fails — exactly the moment a user (or an agent) is reading git's message to learn what went wrong, and git messages routinely contain non-ASCII repository paths, branch names and author text. A corrupted leading character is a small but real corruption of that only diagnostic, and it is the same class the codebase has repeatedly chosen to fix rather than accept (#1695/#1696/#1697 per-chunk decode, #1803 string tails, terminal runtime's byte tail).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After the tail cut, the retained bytes never begin with a UTF-8 continuation byte: leading continuation bytes at the cut are dropped (as `terminal/runtime.js:151` does), or an equivalent alignment is applied before decoding.
- [ ] Both decode sites (`:243` overflow, `:272` non-zero exit) return the aligned tail — fix at the accumulation/cut, not per call site, if that is cleaner.
- [ ] A regression test drives `runGit` (fake git binary) with stderr whose 4096-byte tail window lands inside a multi-byte character and asserts the returned `stderr` contains no U+FFFD at its start; an ASCII control and a tail shorter than the cap pass unchanged.
- [ ] Existing `guests/clone` tests still pass.

Filed by the fleet issue creator (`new-issue-creator-openchamber`) with a reproduced probe; not a duplicate of #1803 (shared accumulator's string tails) or #1741 (per-chunk decode audit — this byte-window cut is outside its disposition).

body:
Phase 1 of design #1808 (one provider, every surface — one registry contract for quota providers across the web backend, the VS Code backend and the UI catalog). Phases 2–3 are the adopted open issues #1738/#1744/#1757 (surface agreement) and #1747/#1755 (one selection per provider), each on its own lifecycle. This phase is **tests/docs only** — no fetcher, dispatch, catalog or configured-set behaviour changes; the current disagreements stay live under their own issues, now named in one place.

## Scope

1. **A checked-in provider manifest** — one file, in a location each package's tests can read (record which location/shape each package used; if a package's test runner cannot read outside its root, a checked per-package copy whose equality with the manifest is itself tested is acceptable), covering **every provider id that appears in any current list**, with per-surface presence for all five lists:
   - web registry registrations in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/index.js` (30 entries on main `4e6f75b433`),
   - VS Code dispatch cases in `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` (27 cases) **and** its `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` configured set (a separate list in the same file — both are rows),
   - UI catalog `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` in `packages/ui/src/lib/quota/providers/index.ts` (29 entries),
   - UI type union `QuotaProviderId` in `packages/ui/src/types/quota.ts` (30 ids),
   - the "Supported provider IDs (dispatcher)" table in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
   Each manifest row: id, display name, per-surface presence, and — for any id not present on every surface — either a **named exception** (reason + adopting issue) or an **alias** record (rule 3).
2. **The known disagreements at filing (main `4e6f75b433`, verified by the filer)** are recorded as exceptions, not silently normalised:
   - `mistral` — absent from VS Code dispatch + configured set → exception adopting #1757.
   - `command-code`, `opendesign` — absent from VS Code dispatch + configured set → exception adopting #1744.
   - `github-copilot-addon` — absent from the UI catalog → exception adopting #1738.
   - `openai` — present only in the UI type union; web treats it as a `credentialAliases` entry of `codex` → recorded as an **alias**, not a provider (its removal from the type union, if any, is a behaviour-adjacent change and is NOT part of this phase — record it as the alias row's open note).
3. **One conformance test per package** (web, vscode, ui): the test extracts that package's own provider list(s) and asserts equality with the manifest minus that surface's named exceptions. A provider appearing in a package list but absent from the manifest fails; a manifest provider silently absent from a package list fails. The web test also checks the DOCUMENTATION.md dispatcher table against the manifest (the docs row is a surface).

Method: re-derive every list from current main at implementation time — do not assume the filing-day counts above are still exact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The manifest exists, covers every id in every list above, and every non-uniform id carries a named exception (with adopting issue) or an alias record.
- [ ] Web, VS Code and UI packages each carry a conformance test as described, and the tests pass on the implementing change with exactly the filing-day exceptions (plus any new disagreement surfaced and exception-recorded with its own filed issue, if the re-derivation finds one).
- [ ] No production behaviour changes: no fetcher, dispatch case, configured-set, catalog or type-union membership changes in this issue.
- [ ] The contract's five rules are stated where the manifest lives (manifest header or the quota DOCUMENTATION.md), so a new-provider author meets them at the manifest, not in this issue.

title: fix(web): shared bounded-output accumulator's tail slices can split a surrogate pair — recentText and the held line can start with a lone low surrogate, unlike the guarded tails in guests/service, the dictation worker and the model downloader

body:
## Problem

`createBoundedOutputAccumulator` in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-output-accumulator.js` — the shared accumulator extracted by PR #1705 so the cloudflare and ngrok tunnel modules would stop diverging — bounds its rolling text and its held line with plain slices that can split a surrogate pair:

- :25 — `recentText = (recentText + decoded).slice(-maxChars);` (in `push`)
- :30 — `pendingLine = pendingLine.slice(-maxChars);` (in `push`, when a single line exceeds the cap)
- :36 — `recentText = (recentText + tail).slice(-maxChars);` (in `flush`)

None of the three skips a leading low surrogate. When the cut lands between the halves of an astral character (any character above U+FFFF — emoji, 𝄞, CJK ext.), the kept text starts with a lone low surrogate, and that character is corrupted to U+FFFD the moment the text is re-encoded — in the tunnel startup errors and diagnostics this accumulator exists to produce.

Every other tail-bounded reader in the server already guards exactly this cut:

- `guests/service.js:394-400` — `tail()`: "Keep the tail bound without leaving a lone surrogate at its head: a plain slice at maxChars can land between the halves of a pair" (added today by PR #1797, #1696).
- `dictation/local/model-downloader.js:189-197` — `appendStderrTail` skips the cut position forward when it lands on a low surrogate (added today by PR #1728, #1695).
- `dictation/local/worker-client.js:25-32` — the stderr tail slice does the same (#1697).

The shared accumulator is the one tail reader left unguarded — and it is the implementation design #1740's phase 3 proposes migrating the others onto.

## Why it matters

The accumulator's outputs are user-facing diagnostics and classification inputs:

- cloudflare managed tunnels (`cloudflare-tunnel.js` `waitForManagedTunnelReady`): lines from `push`/`flush` are classified ready/fatal, and a fatal line is interpolated into the error the user sees — `Cloudflared failed to start ${modeLabel}: ${line}`.
- ngrok (`ngrok-tunnel.js`): `captureLines` collects `push`/`flush` lines into `recentOutput`, which `appendNgrokOutputSummary` appends to the startup-timeout and exit errors.
- cloudflare quick tunnel (:443-446): `recentText` is matched against the tunnel-URL regex.

A single log line longer than the 64 KiB cap (`BOUNDED_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS`) containing an astral character at the cut position loses that character in the error text — the same corruption class #1695/#1696/#1697 were filed and fixed for, in the one module whose stated purpose (#1705) is to stop the tunnel copies diverging. Its test suite pins split-across-chunks decoding but has no case for the tail cut.

## Evidence (laptop probe vs the real module, ×2 identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-accumulator-surrogate-20261107/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `createBoundedOutputAccumulator` from main `26d859759ea4a7ddf54c9804815b1a7abb91ebee`, with `maxChars: 8` and the 16-code-unit text `abcdefg𝄞hijklmn` (𝄞 = U+1D11E = `\uD834\uDD1E` at indices 7-8, so the tail cut lands exactly on the low surrogate):

- Case 1 (`push` → `recentText`): `"\udd1ehijklmn"` — first code unit `0xdd1e`, a lone low surrogate; re-encoding it yields `"�hijklmn"` (the 𝄞 is gone).
- Case 2 (held line → `flush()`): `["\udd1ehijklmn"]` — the flushed final line carries the same lone surrogate.
- Control (same length, no astral character at the cut): `"ijklmnop"` — clean.

Both runs produced byte-identical output. Dedup: searches for "lone surrogate", "surrogate accumulator", "bounded-output-accumulator" and "surrogate pair tail slice" return only the closed sibling fixes #1695/#1696/#1697/#1722 — none covers the shared accumulator. The stream-output inventory (`lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md`, #1741) dispositions this accumulator "conforming-on-all-rules" on decode/cap/match/flush; the tail-cut surrogate guard is a fifth detail none of its rows checks, and the three sibling guards were added after (or outside) that audit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three tail slices in `bounded-output-accumulator.js` (`push` recentText, `push` pendingLine, `flush` recentText) skip a leading low surrogate after cutting, matching the guard shape already used in `guests/service.js` / `model-downloader.js` / `worker-client.js` — the kept text never starts with a lone low surrogate.
- [ ] Regression tests in `bounded-output-accumulator.test.js` pin the boundary: with a small `maxChars`, an astral character straddling the cut is dropped whole (never half-kept) in both `recentText` and the flushed held line. Oracle: the sibling tail readers' behaviour — the character survives whole or not at all.
- [ ] The existing accumulator tests (split multi-byte decode, line holding, flush idempotence, tail bounding) still pass unchanged, and the tunnel suites (`cloudflare-tunnel.test.js`, `ngrok-tunnel.test.js`) stay green.

title: fix(web): managed OpenCode log cursor readLogSince opens the log with plain 'r' and buffers the whole growth uncapped — a FIFO at opencode.log freezes the whole server on the 100 ms readiness poll, and a 42 MB log is read whole

body:
## Problem

`readLogSince` in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-opencode-state.js` (:127) is the managed OpenCode log cursor — and it is the one reader in that module the bounded-read work never gated:

- :130 opens the log with plain `openSync(logPath, 'r')` — no `O_NONBLOCK`, no regular-file check. The `fstatSync` at :131 runs only *after* the open settles, so it can never refuse a non-regular file.
- :132-135 allocates `Buffer.alloc(fileSize - offset)` and reads the **entire growth in one uncapped read** — no chunking, no per-drain cap.

Its sibling readers in the same file were routed through `readBoundedFileSync` by PR #1748 (#1622), and the shared inventory row for this module (`lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md`) covers only `state.json` / `draining.json`. The log cursor was left out.

## Why it matters

`readLogSince` is called **synchronously** from `lifecycle.js`'s readiness drain: `setInterval(drainOutput, MANAGED_LOG_POLL_MS)` with `MANAGED_LOG_POLL_MS = 100` (:116, :849), plus the exit (:831) and timeout (:845) handlers. So:

1. **A FIFO at `<dataDir>/managed-opencode/opencode.log` freezes the whole server.** The blocking sync open never returns, the event loop never resumes, and startup supervision (and everything else the server does) is dead — not just the readiness poll. This is the #1622 shape, one function over: that issue's own title records that a FIFO on the state paths "freezes the server event loop on the supervision path".
2. **A large growth is buffered whole, twice over.** Rotation caps the log at 5 MiB only at spawn (`rotateManagedLogIfOversized`); a running child keeps appending, and the drain's rotated-generation branch (`lifecycle.js`:806) re-reads `opencode.log.1` through the same uncapped cursor. Whatever accumulated since the last poll is allocated in one buffer and then concatenated again into the drain's `output` string.

## Evidence (laptop probe vs the real module, ×2 identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-logsince-20261107/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real `readLogSince` from main `145c8f8c711eaafa4665d6b8b3baef45bb58ca0f`:

- Control (48-byte log containing a listening line): `{ textLen: 48, offset: 48, hasUrl: true }` — settles immediately.
- Oversize (41,984,000-byte log, read from offset 0): `{ textLen: 41984000, offset: 41984000, ms: 37 }` — the whole file is buffered and returned in one read; no cap exists to trip.
- FIFO at the log path: never settled — killed by a 3 s timeout (exit 124) on both runs.

## Dedup

- #1622 (closed, PR #1748) bounded `readManagedOpenCodeState` / `readDrainingOpenCodeRecords` only — different functions, and its fix is the pattern to reuse.
- #1790 (open) is the UTF-8 tail-holdback defect *inside* this same function — a different mechanism (offset never advances past invalid lead bytes) with a different fix; this issue is the open/read gate and the read cap. The two fixes touch neighbouring lines and should be sequenced, not merged into one another's scope.
- #941 (closed) added spawn-time rotation; it does not gate or cap the read path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readLogSince` opens the log non-blocking (or otherwise refuses before blocking) and judges the opened handle with `fstat`: a non-regular file at the log path is treated as no output (empty text, offset unchanged) and the call always settles promptly.
- [ ] The read is chunked with a named per-call cap on bytes consumed (constant in the style of the module's other caps), so a single drain never allocates the whole growth; bytes past the cap are consumed by later polls via the returned offset, not dropped.
- [ ] The incomplete-UTF-8 tail holdback semantics are preserved (the returned offset still stops before a trailing incomplete sequence; see also #1790).
- [ ] `readLogTail` behaviour is unchanged for ordinary logs (it composes `readLogSince`).
- [ ] Regression tests: FIFO at the log path settles with empty text; a log larger than the per-call cap is consumed across successive calls with correct offsets and full content; a split multi-byte character at a chunk boundary still decodes whole on the next call.
- [ ] The shared read inventory in `lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` gains a row (or an updated row) for the log cursor stating its gate and cap.

title: fix(web): instance-dir owner read is whole and ungated — a FIFO at run/instances/<pid>/owner wedges server startup forever at the await in main(), and a 33 MiB owner file is buffered whole for a parseInt

body:
## Problem

`prepareInstanceDir`'s owner read is the one startup read in the managed-OpenCode lifecycle that is still ungated:

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/instance-dir.js:80` — `readOwner` does `fsPromises.readFile(ownerPath, 'utf8')` whole: no size cap, no regular-file check, no deadline. It only needs the leading integer (`Number.parseInt` at :81).
- `instance-dir.js:51` — it runs for **every** numeric folder under `<data-dir>/run/instances/` via `Promise.all`, on every server start.
- `packages/web/server/index.js:2156` — `main()` **awaits** `prepareInstanceDir(...)` before the agent-tool runtime, the managed-config runtime, and the listener are created. A read that never settles means the server never starts, with no error and no log line naming the cause.

Consequences, both verified below:

1. **A FIFO at `run/instances/<pid>/owner` wedges startup forever.** `readFile` on a FIFO with no writer never settles, so the `await` at index.js:2156 never returns. The folder name only has to be numeric (`/^\d+$/` at instance-dir.js:50) for the read to be attempted — a stray, planted, or sync/backup-restored FIFO in the shared data dir is enough.
2. **An oversized owner file is buffered whole.** The file this server writes is `${pid}\n` (instance-dir.js, `writeFile` in the claimed branch) — a handful of bytes — yet a 33 MiB owner file was read entire (34,603,012 bytes through the injected `fsPromises`) before its first line was parsed.

## Why this is not already tracked

- The shared inventory (`lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md`) has no row for the instance-dir owner file; its sibling lifecycle records in the same directory were bound one by one (#1736 managed-process registry, #1748 managed OpenCode state/draining at a named 64 KiB cap).
- #1706 covers the **CLI's** bin/lib pid/instance readers (`cli-process.js` `readPidFile` / `readInstanceOptions`) — a different tree, a different process, and different files. This is the server startup path.
- The bounded reader already exists: `lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js:80` (`readBoundedFile` — open once with `O_NONBLOCK`, judge from the handle, enforce the cap in flight). One nuance for the fix: `readOwner` receives an injected `fsPromises` surface (the module's test seam), so the fix either gives the bounded read an fs seam or performs the same handle-judged read through the injected surface — the seam must not be lost.

## Evidence (verified this run, on the laptop against the real module)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-instance-dir-owner-20261107/probe.mjs` — imports the real `prepareInstanceDir` from `origin/main` @ `928d8ff0eb08de4cf89079fe8f14a5448126b1a2`, injects real `node:fs/promises` wrapped only to count bytes returned by `readFile`, `pid: 505`, `isPidAlive: (p) => p === 404`. Run ×2 with identical results:

- **Control** — `instances/404/owner` containing `404\n`: settled in 1 ms, 4 bytes read, folder `404` kept (live owner), own folder `505` returned.
- **Oversize** — owner file `404\n` + 33 MiB of padding: settled in 47–48 ms after reading **34,603,012 bytes whole**; the owner was still parsed as 404 and the folder kept. No cap exists to refuse it.
- **FIFO** — `instances/404/owner` replaced by a FIFO with no writer: `prepareInstanceDir` **never settled** within the 3 s race in either run; the probe process itself could not exit afterwards and had to be killed by `timeout` (exit 124) — the blocked read holds the process exactly as it would hold `main()`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner read is bounded and regular-file-checked with a named cap sized to the file's real shape (a pid line; single-digit KiB is ample), enforced during the read on the opened handle, with a non-blocking open so a FIFO is refused promptly instead of awaited forever.
- [ ] Every refusal (missing, unreadable, over-cap, non-regular) takes `readOwner`'s existing fallback path — the folder-name pid — preserving today's missing/malformed semantics and the claim/abandon decisions built on them; no new throw reaches `main()`.
- [ ] The injected `fsPromises` test seam is preserved (existing `instance-dir.test.js` passes unchanged in behaviour), and new regression tests cover the FIFO and over-cap owner files, in the style of the sibling bounded-read suites.
- [ ] Semantics for real files are unchanged: a live owner's folder is kept, a gone owner's folder is removed, a claim/handoff is honoured exactly as today.

body:
## Finding

PR #1749 bounded the routing feedback log (`readFeedback` 4 MiB cap, append-side compaction to the newest 3 MiB). In the same change, `recordFeedback` gained a brand-new failure mode that the PR body and the module documentation never mention:

```js
const line = Buffer.from(`${JSON.stringify({ time: now(), ...entry })}\n`);
if (line.length > RETAIN_ROUTE_FEEDBACK_BYTES) {
  throw new RangeError(`Route feedback entries must fit within ${RETAIN_ROUTE_FEEDBACK_BYTES} bytes`);
}
```

Before PR #1749, `recordFeedback` was a plain `fs.appendFileSync` — it never threw for entry size. Now any single serialized feedback entry over 3 MiB (`RETAIN_ROUTE_FEEDBACK_BYTES`) throws a `RangeError` at the caller instead of being recorded, and no test pins that contract.

The throw may well be the right design (an entry larger than the retention window could never survive compaction), but today it is an undocumented, untested behaviour change riding inside a read-bounding fix whose body says "Semantics are preserved exactly where they matter" and "No schema or format changes".

## Evidence

- PR #1749 (MERGED, merge commit `bc399ffca4bf810963af94040dc3e3e58f534e10`, head commit `89830ea34`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1749 — fixes #1624.
- Verified on current main `928d8ff0eb08de4cf89079fe8f14a5448126b1a2` (fetched fresh via `gh api` this run):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/routing/route-overrides-store.js:185-190` — the `recordFeedback` throw above.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/routing/route-overrides-store.test.js` — grep for `RangeError` / "must fit" returns nothing; the PR's new tests cover the over-cap read warning, the FIFO read, and compaction of many small lines, but no single-oversized-entry case.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/routing/DOCUMENTATION.md` (as updated by PR #1749) documents the 4 MiB read cap and the 3 MiB compaction retention, but no per-entry size limit or throw.
- Deduped: issue searches for `recordFeedback RangeError` and "feedback entries must fit" return nothing; open feedback issues are #1655 (design parent) and #25 (handoff epic), neither covers this.

## Why it matters

A caller recording interpreter feedback with a large payload (long model output / correction note) previously succeeded; now it gets an exception from a store method whose contract never announced one. If any caller does not guard the call, the feedback action itself errors; if a caller does guard it, the entry silently vanishes. Either way the behaviour should be a named, tested contract — or removed in favour of the read/compaction caps alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage decides the contract: either (a) the per-entry limit is intentional — document it in `packages/web/server/lib/routing/DOCUMENTATION.md` next to the read/compaction caps and name what callers should expect, or (b) it is not — remove the throw and let the read cap + compaction bound the log.
- [ ] A regression test in `route-overrides-store.test.js` pins the decided behaviour for a single entry over 3 MiB (throw with the named error, or successful record followed by the documented read/compaction outcome). Oracle: the documented contract from the triage decision.
- [ ] Existing feedback tests (missing/over-cap/FIFO reads, compaction keeps newest complete lines) still pass.

title: fix(web): managed OpenCode log cursor holds back invalid UTF-8 lead bytes forever — PR #1718's incompleteUtf8TailLength treats overlong/never-valid leads (0xC0/0xC1/0xF5+) as incomplete sequences

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #1718 added `incompleteUtf8TailLength` so `readLogSince` holds back a trailing *incomplete* UTF-8 sequence instead of corrupting it to U+FFFD. The function's own comment promises:

> Invalid bytes (lone continuations, overlong leads) are not a prefix of any sequence and return 0 — they decode to U+FFFD exactly as before.

The implementation does not do that for lead bytes that can never start a valid sequence:

```js
const needed = byte >= 0xf0 ? 4 : byte >= 0xe0 ? 3 : byte >= 0xc0 ? 2 : 1;
const have = length - i;
return have < needed ? have : 0;
```

- `0xC0` / `0xC1` (overlong 2-byte leads, never valid in UTF-8) get `needed = 2`, so a log ending in one of them is held back (`have 1 < 2`).
- `0xF5`–`0xFF` (never valid: above U+10FFFF or not lead bytes at all) get `needed = 4`, so up to 3 trailing bytes are held back.

Because `readLogSince` returns `offset + consumed`, the held-back bytes are never delivered and the offset never advances past them while the log ends there: every later poll re-reads the same tail, and the byte(s) never reach the startup diagnostics this code exists to quote. That is exactly the "holding them back forever" outcome the PR's own test title says must not happen.

## Evidence

- PR #1718 (MERGED, merge commit `722831d8ef1054e399c299aa2c45f83782937379`, head commit `7a6e00b94`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1718 — fixes #1687.
- Verified on current main `928d8ff0eb08de4cf89079fe8f14a5448126b1a2` (fetched fresh via `gh api` this run):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-opencode-state.js:110-124` — comment vs the `needed` computation above.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-opencode-state.js:139-140` — `readLogSince` subtracts the held-back length from both the text and the returned offset.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/managed-opencode-state.test.js:278` — the test "still decodes invalid trailing bytes instead of holding them back forever" covers only a lone continuation byte (`0x80`); no case covers an invalid *lead* byte (`0xC0`, `0xC1`, `0xF5`–`0xFF`).
- This finding was first spotted by the pr-diff-review-b lane (2026-11-07 13:18 CST run) and left as a backlog REVIEW-FINDING; it is filed here by the primary pr-diff-review run. Deduped: issue searches for `incompleteUtf8TailLength`, "overlong", "invalid lead", and "readLogSince UTF-8" return only the closed parent #1687.

## Why it matters

The managed-OpenCode log tail is quoted in startup errors; a child that writes an invalid lead byte as its last output (corrupt/localized tool output, a truncated write from a dying process) loses those bytes permanently and stalls the log cursor at that offset, and the code does the opposite of what its comment and test title guarantee for this byte class.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `incompleteUtf8TailLength` returns 0 for trailing bytes that can never begin a valid UTF-8 sequence: `0xC0`, `0xC1`, and `0xF5`–`0xFF` (including when followed by continuation bytes).
- [ ] A regression test in `managed-opencode-state.test.js` extends the existing invalid-trailing-bytes case to invalid lead bytes: `readLogSince` delivers them (decoded as U+FFFD, as before PR #1718) and advances the offset past them. Oracle: the pre-#1718 decode behaviour for invalid bytes.
- [ ] The existing split-multi-byte hold-back tests (valid 2/3/4-byte sequences split at every byte position) still pass unchanged.

title: fix(web): project-icon discovery opens a project-controlled favicon with plain 'r' and no regular-file check — a FIFO favicon.ico blocks icon discovery forever, unlike the stored-icon reader in the same file

body:
## Summary

Project-icon **discovery** reads a favicon found inside the project's own directory — the less trusted of the module's two icon paths — with a plain `'r'` open and no regular-file check at all, while the **stored**-icon reader in the same file opens with `O_NONBLOCK` flags and refuses non-regular files, a discipline its header comment spells out as existing precisely so "open() itself" cannot block "on a FIFO with no writer before the handle stat can judge it non-regular (#1537)". A FIFO named `favicon.ico` (or `.png`/`.svg`/…) in any opened project — cloned repositories can contain FIFOs — makes `POST /api/projects/:projectId/icon/discover` never settle: `fsPromises.open(path, 'r')` on a FIFO blocks until a writer appears, so the size checks below it never run.

## Evidence (main `928d8ff0eb08de4cf89079fe8f14a5448126b1a2`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/project-icon-routes.js:46-47` — `readDiscoveredIcon` opens with plain `'r'`: `const handle = await fsPromises.open(filePath, 'r');`
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/project-icon-routes.js:49-56` — its handle stat judges only size (`=== 0` → empty, `> projectIconMaxBytes` → too-large); there is no `isFile()` check anywhere in the reader.
- Contrast, same file: `:1-8` defines `storedIconOpenFlags` (`O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX) with the #1537 rationale, and `:91-100` `readStoredIcon` opens with those flags and returns `not-regular` for non-files. The stored path serves files under the app's own data dir; the discovered path reads project-controlled files and got neither half.
- Call path: `POST /api/projects/:projectId/icon/discover` (`:468`) searches the project directory for `favicon.(ico|png|svg|jpg|jpeg|webp)` (`:492-510`) and awaits `readDiscoveredIcon(selected.path)` at `:514`.

### Probe (laptop, real `registerProjectIconRoutes` handler, real `fs/promises`, run twice, identical)

- **Control** — a regular 6-byte `favicon.ico` in the project dir: the discover handler settled, project updated with `iconImage` (`image/x-icon`).
- **FIFO** — `favicon.ico` created with `mkfifo` at the same path, search returning it as the selected candidate: the handler **never settled** within a 3 s race (both runs).

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-icon-discover-fifo-20261107/probe.mjs`.

## Why it matters

- Icon discovery runs against whatever project the user opens; a repository that contains a FIFO favicon (accidental artifact or deliberate plant) wedges the discover request forever and pins a libuv threadpool thread per attempt.
- The asymmetry is the tell: #1537 hardened the serve path for files the app itself wrote, and left the discovery path — the one that reads files a project controls — on the pre-#1537 pattern. #1053/#1305 (closed) fixed the discovered reader's whole-buffer and stat-race halves; the blocking-open half remains.
- The fix is mechanical and in-file: reuse `storedIconOpenFlags` for the discovered open and add the same `not-regular` refusal (mapped to a 4xx on the route, like `empty`/`too-large`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `readDiscoveredIcon` opens with `storedIconOpenFlags(platform)` (or the shared bounded reader's flags) and refuses non-regular files via its handle stat, so a FIFO favicon is rejected promptly and the discover route answers an error instead of never settling.
- A regression test in `project-icon-routes.test.js` covers a FIFO (or, via the injected `fsPromises` seam, a handle whose stat reports a non-file) discovered favicon: the route settles with an error response; the existing at-cap / empty / format-preference discover tests pass unchanged.
- The stored-icon GET/PUT/DELETE behaviour is untouched.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `discovered icon`, `project icon FIFO`, and `favicon FIFO`: #1537 (closed) covers the stored-icon **serve** path, #1686 (closed) its test gap, #1053/#1305 (closed) the discovered reader's buffering/stat-race halves. No issue covers the discovered reader's blocking open or its missing regular-file check.

body:
## Summary

In the web server's guest file access, the bounded text reader opens the target file with plain `'r'` and only judges the opened handle's regular-file stat **after** the open settles. A FIFO at a guest-readable path therefore blocks the read forever: the `isFile()` refusal in the reader is unreachable for exactly the file type it exists to refuse, and the pre-read stat in `readOperation` never checks the file type either (only `isDirectory()` and size — a FIFO's size is 0, so it passes both). The module's own header comment claims "the same discipline as `shared/bounded-file-read.js`", but the shared reader opens with `O_NONBLOCK` precisely so the open itself cannot block before the stat can judge the file; this reader kept the in-flight cap half of that discipline and dropped the open half.

## Evidence (main `928d8ff0eb08de4cf89079fe8f14a5448126b1a2`)

- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/files.js:194` — `const handle = await fsPromises.open(absolute, 'r');` (no `O_NONBLOCK`, no `O_NOFOLLOW`).
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/files.js:196-201` — the handle stat's `isFile()` check (throwing `EISDIR` "not a regular file") runs only after the open settles; for a FIFO it never runs.
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/files.js:225-233` — `readOperation`'s pre-read stat checks `isDirectory()` and `stat.size > GUEST_FILE_CONTENT_MAX` (2,000,000, `packages/sdk/src/contract.ts:407`) only; a FIFO passes both.
- `packages/web/server/lib/guests/files.js:183-192` — the reader's doc comment claims parity with `shared/bounded-file-read.js`; that module's `openFlags` include `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX for exactly this reason.
- Entry point: `runGuestFileOperation` (`files.js:302`, read dispatch `:338`) serves guest `read` operations for files inside the open project (grant `files`) or under granted `filesystem` patterns — paths whose contents the host does not fully control (any project can contain a FIFO: build artifacts, test fixtures, `mkfifo` leftovers).

### Probe (laptop, real `runGuestFileOperation`, run twice, identical)

- **Control** — a regular `control.txt` in the project dir: settled promptly, `{ok:true, result:{content:"hello guest"}}`.
- **FIFO** — `pipe.txt` created with `mkfifo` in the same dir, same grant: the operation **never settled** within a 3 s race (both runs).

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-guest-files-fifo-20261107/probe.mjs`.

## Why it matters

- A guest read of one FIFO hangs the request forever and pins a libuv threadpool thread on the blocked open; repeated reads of FIFO paths can exhaust the server's async-fs threadpool and stall unrelated file work in the whole process. There is no deadline on the operation to recover with.
- This is the same shape the fleet has been closing across the server (#1711, #1783, #1784, #1785): a regular-file guard that sits behind a blocking open is not a guard. This reader is the remaining instance in `lib/guests/` — the storage sibling was filed as #1784, the local-zip install as #1733; neither covers `files.js`.
- The fix pattern exists twice over: `shared/bounded-file-read.js`'s `openFlags` (cited by this module's own comment) and the stored-icon reader in `lib/opencode/project-icon-routes.js`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The guest text read opens with `O_NONBLOCK` (POSIX; plain `'r'` on win32, matching `storedIconOpenFlags`/`bounded-file-read` conventions), so a FIFO at a guest-readable path is refused promptly via the existing not-a-regular-file path instead of blocking the open; the in-flight byte cap behaviour is unchanged.
- A regression test in `guests/files.test.js` (real fs, temp dir + `mkfifo`, as the icon/markdown-grant FIFO tests do) shows a FIFO read settles with a refusal while a regular file at the cap and a grown-after-stat file behave exactly as before.
- Existing `files.test.js` suite passes; `write`/`list`/`stat` operations are unchanged.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `guest file FIFO`, `guests/files`, and `readBoundedText`: #1784 covers guest **storage** (`createReadStream` in the storage lock), #1733 covers guest local-zip install, #1620 (closed) covered the guest extension/auth stores' whole reads. No issue covers the `lib/guests/files.js` read path.

body:
## Problem

`inspectImage` in the markdown image grant route opens the referenced file **before** its regular-file guard, with no `O_NONBLOCK` — so a FIFO at the referenced path blocks the open forever, and the `isFile()` refusal that is supposed to reject it is unreachable.

- `packages/web/server/lib/markdown-image-grants/routes.js:276` — `fsPromises.open(canonicalPath, fsConstants.O_RDONLY | fsConstants.O_NOFOLLOW)` (no `O_NONBLOCK` anywhere in the file)
- `routes.js:282-283` — the guard runs only *after* the open settles: `handle.stat()`, then `if (!stats.isFile() || stats.size > (video ? MAX_VIDEO_BYTES : MAX_IMAGE_BYTES)) return { status: 'error' }`
- `routes.js:346` — the route handler (registered at `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/feature-routes-runtime.js:388`) awaits `inspectImage` per source in a sequential loop, with no deadline around it, so one FIFO source wedges the whole grant request — and every other source in it — indefinitely.

The path is message-referenced: by design (comment at `routes.js:261-265`) a referenced path "may sit anywhere on the machine", gated only by the assistant message referencing it, the signature check, and the size limits. An assistant message that references a named pipe — a crashed image generator's output pipe, a FIFO a tool left in the workspace, or a plain mistake — hangs the session's image-grant request forever instead of answering `error` like every other non-regular file does once the open returns.

This is the #1711 shape (an open placed before its regular-file guard, guard unreachable for FIFOs). The house pattern already exists: `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` opens with `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX precisely so a FIFO is refused promptly and the post-open `isFile` judgement can run.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3`)

Laptop probe against the **real** route module (express app registered with the module's own dependencies, OpenCode message fetch stubbed exactly as in `routes.test.js`; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-mdimage-fifo-20261107/`, runs `result2.txt` / `result3.txt`), x2 identical:

- **Control** (real 1x1 PNG at the referenced path): POST settled in 27-36 ms, HTTP 200, `results[0].status = "ready"`.
- **FIFO** (`mkfifo image.png` at the referenced path, referenced by the stubbed assistant message): POST **never settled within 3,000 ms** in either run; it unblocked only when the probe opened the FIFO for writing — i.e. the request was parked inside `open()` at `routes.js:276`, before the `:283` guard could execute.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `markdown-image-grants`, `inspectImage`, "image grant" and "FIFO image" — #1285 (closed) covers the same file's OpenCode *response-body* cap, not this open; #934 (closed) removed a different dead grant machinery. No issue covers `inspectImage`'s open.

## Why it matters

The grant route is on the chat rendering path: the UI asks it to prepare every local image/video a message references. One FIFO reference turns that into a permanently pending request (a thread in libuv's pool parked in `open(2)`, the HTTP request never answered, the per-source loop never reaching later sources) with no error, no log, and no timeout to trip. The size caps at `routes.js:8` / `:13` and the signature check show the file was designed to be judged defensively — the FIFO case is the one judgement that can never run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Opening a referenced non-regular file (FIFO at minimum) settles promptly with `status: 'error'` for that source; the request completes and later sources in the same request are still processed.
- The fix follows the house pattern (e.g. `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX at the open in `inspectImage`, platform-guarded as in `shared/bounded-file-read.js`), keeping the post-open `handle.stat()` `isFile` / size judgements as the deciding checks; behaviour for regular files (image + video signature, 10 MiB / 1 GiB caps, outside-workspace allowance) is unchanged.

body:
## Finding

PR #1720 gave guest extension storage an in-flight byte cap — but the read is a plain `createReadStream(file, { encoding: 'utf8' })`: no `O_NONBLOCK`, no regular-file refusal. A FIFO at `guest-storage/<id>.json` blocks the stream open/read forever, and because `runGuestStorage` runs inside the per-file serialized `withStorageLock` chain, one FIFO wedges every later storage operation for that guest extension (they queue behind a promise that never settles). The PR also shipped with **no tests at all** (one file changed, +15/−3): on current main, `guests/storage.test.js` (59 lines) contains no cap, grows-after-stat, or FIFO case, so neither the new in-flight cap nor the FIFO behavior is pinned. Finally, the shared inventory row that tracks this store (`shared/DOCUMENTATION.md`) still describes the pre-#1720 stat-gated shape and "follow-up-filed (#1680)", so the fleet's own bound-completeness record is stale for this store.

Scope note: #1680 (still OPEN) covers the stat-race #1720 fixed; the FIFO axis and the test gap are not in its scope, hence this separate filing (the same split as #1684 vs #1678 for the git stores).

## Evidence

- PR #1720 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1720), MERGED 2026-11-06, merge b29f6bc576d31f721da5f1e48f11702e49cd0cfd, head 8d1ee0f60379, for #1680 (OPEN). Diff stat: 1 file, 15 insertions, 3 deletions, no test file.
- Current main 3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3 (verified twice via the commits API; files read from main):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/guests/storage.js:39` — `const stream = createReadStream(file, { encoding: 'utf8' });` (default flags, follows anything, blocks on a FIFO).
  - `storage.js:13-22` — `withStorageLock` serializes operations per file on a promise chain; a never-settling read blocks all later operations for that file.
  - `storage.js:52-54` — the catch rethrows everything except ENOENT; a FIFO never reaches it because the read never settles.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/guests/storage.test.js` — 59 lines; `grep -n "exceeds|cap|FIFO|mkfifo|TOTAL"` returns nothing.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md:373` — the guest-storage row still reads "flawed: the cap is judged on a stat by path, then the file is read by path … follow-up-filed (#1680)".
- The house pattern on main: `shared/bounded-file-read.js` opens with `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX and refuses non-regular files from the handle; sibling stores fixed in this series pin FIFO + grows-after-stat tests (e.g. PR #1698, #1712, #1724).

## Why it matters

Guest storage documents are per-extension persistent state in the user's data directory, written under a lock that serializes access. An oversized-file cap that is untested can silently regress, and a FIFO at the storage path — from a stray mkfifo, a sync tool, or a malicious guest-adjacent process — freezes that extension's storage permanently instead of failing the one operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The storage read refuses a FIFO / non-regular file promptly with an error (not a hang), and operations queued behind it in `withStorageLock` settle; regression test with a real FIFO (`skipIf(win32)`), mirroring the sibling stores' tests.
- [ ] Tests pin the in-flight cap: an over-cap file is refused with "Storage exceeds its size limit", and a file grown past the cap after any pre-read check is refused without being buffered whole.
- [ ] Missing (ENOENT → empty entries), malformed, and schema-invalid behavior is unchanged; existing guest storage tests stay green.
- [ ] The `shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` guest-storage row is updated to the store's actual post-fix disposition.

body:
## Finding

PR #1723 replaced the theme runtime's stat-gated reads with a hand-rolled bounded reader, `readThemeFileBounded` — but it opens with plain `'r'`: no `O_NONBLOCK`. On POSIX, opening a FIFO for reading blocks until a writer appears, so the reader's own regular-file refusal (`handle.stat()` → `isFile()`) is unreachable for exactly the file type it exists to refuse. The exposure is real in `readCustomThemesFromDisk`: its directory filter deliberately admits symlinked theme files (`entry.isFile() || entry.isSymbolicLink()`), so a theme symlink pointing at a FIFO — or a regular theme file swapped for a FIFO between `readdir` and `open` — blocks theme loading forever. The shared bounded reader this change mirrors (`shared/bounded-file-read.js`) opens with `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK` for precisely this reason, and every sibling fix in this series (e.g. #1712, #1724) either uses it or copies its flags and pins a FIFO regression test. #1723's tests mock `fsPromises.open`, so no FIFO case can even be expressed in them.

Note: the fix must add `O_NONBLOCK` only, **not** `O_NOFOLLOW` — symlinked theme files are a supported feature (the runtime's own tests cover a linked theme); the shared reader's `noFollow` variant would break them.

## Evidence

- PR #1723 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1723), MERGED 2026-11-06, merge 1ba0011b6cd3f2b26947a69339a5181d68a8fde2, head e9478a430324, for #1682 (CLOSED).
- Current main 3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3 (verified twice via the commits API; file read from main):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/theme-runtime.js:119` — `const handle = await fsPromises.open(filePath, 'r');` (no flags).
  - `theme-runtime.js:122` — the `stat.isFile()` refusal sits after the blocking open.
  - `theme-runtime.js:145` — `readCustomThemesFromDisk` admits entries where `entry.isSymbolicLink()` is true, then calls `readThemeFileBounded` on the path.
  - The same helper is used by `saveImportedTheme`'s EEXIST conflict compare, so the fix covers both call sites.
- The pattern it should mirror, on main: `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js:36` builds `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | (noFollow ? O_NOFOLLOW : 0)`; its header comment (:12) states O_NONBLOCK "keeps open() itself from blocking on a FIFO".
- Test gap on main: `grep -rn "FIFO|mkfifo|O_NONBLOCK" packages/web/server/lib/opencode/theme-runtime.test.js packages/web/server/lib/opencode/theme-import.test.js` returns nothing; the PR's new tests inject a mocked `open`.

## Why it matters

Theme loading runs when the server lists/starts with custom themes; one planted or accidentally symlinked FIFO in the themes directory hangs it indefinitely instead of skipping the entry — the same hang class this whole bounded-read series exists to remove, reintroduced by a reader that copied the in-flight cap but not the open flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readThemeFileBounded` opens with `O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX (plain `'r'` on Windows), keeping symlink-following intact; a FIFO at a theme path — directly or via a symlink — is refused promptly as `notFile` and the remaining themes still load.
- [ ] A regression test exercises a real FIFO (mkfifo, `skipIf(win32)`, mirroring #1712/#1724's tests) instead of only a mocked `open`.
- [ ] Existing theme runtime/import tests stay green, including the symlinked-theme cases.

## Finding

Open PR #1721 bounds the Linear issue labels connection at 50 and reports `labelsMore` — but the flag stops at the type declaration. The PR adds `labelsMore` to the server summary, parses it in the web API layer, and declares it on the UI `LinearIssueSummary` type, yet **no UI component consumes it**: an issue with more than 50 labels still renders its first 50 label chips as if they were the complete list, with no truncation note. That is the exact failure mode filed before as #1732 (`teamsMore` reached no UI) and fixed by PR #1756 — every sibling truncation flag in this API *is* rendered: `commentsMore` drives a truncation note in `linearIssueContext.ts`, `subIssuesMore` renders a "First {count} shown" note in `ReferencePreview.tsx`, and `teamsMore` renders through `linearProjectMapping.ts`. Labels are rendered as chips in `ReferencePreview.tsx` (the same component that renders the `subIssuesMore` note), and PR #1721 does not touch it or any other component.

This is a follow-up to the open PR, not a block on it: #1721's bounding + API plumbing is correct and tested; the last mile — showing the signal — is missing.

## Evidence

- PR #1721 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1721), OPEN, head 63f697949748, for #1599 (OPEN). Its diff touches only: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/issues.js` (`labels(first: 50)` + `labelsMore: readPageInfo(node.labels).hasMore`), `packages/web/src/api/linear.ts` (`labelsMore: payload.labelsMore === true`), `packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts` (`labelsMore?: boolean` declaration), docs, and tests for the server and web-parse layers. No component or context file is in the diff.
- Current main 3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3 (verified twice via the commits API and a fresh clone): `grep -rn labelsMore packages/` returns nothing (the flag exists only on the PR branch).
- Sibling flags on main are consumed in the UI: `packages/ui/src/lib/linearIssueContext.ts:14` builds a truncation note from `commentsMore`; `packages/ui/src/components/references/ReferencePreview.tsx:522-538` renders the `subIssuesMore` note; `packages/ui/src/lib/linearProjectMapping.ts:30` consumes `teamsMore`.
