- The PR's own docs change states the intent: summaries "report `labelsMore` when Linear has another page, so the panel can show them … without presenting a partial list as complete" — the panel does not yet do that part.

## Why it matters

The purpose of #1599 / PR #1721 is that a partial label list must not look complete. Until a component renders the flag, users still see a silently truncated label list in the issue picker/preview — the bounding half landed, the signalling half reaches nobody.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `labelsMore` is true, the UI surfaces that more labels exist (e.g. a "+ more in Linear" note beside the label chips in `ReferencePreview.tsx`, mirroring the `subIssuesMore` note in the same component, with i18n strings for all locales).

body:
## Finding

The Linear issue reference preview renders the first 50 comments as if they were the whole thread. The truncation signal `commentsMore` exists end-to-end — server, web API parser, UI type — and one consumer (the agent's composer context) already honours it, but the human-facing preview component never reads it.

Chain on main `3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3`:

- Server: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/issues.js:112` fetches `comments(first: 50)` and `readIssue` at `:382` returns `commentsMore: readPageInfo(node.comments).hasMore` (the #1414 fix, closed).
- Web API: `packages/web/src/api/linear.ts:287` parses it through: `commentsMore: payload?.commentsMore === true`.
- UI type: `packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts:2267-2268` declares it, with the comment "In Linear's order; the first page only, `commentsMore` says there are others."
- The one consumer: `packages/ui/src/lib/linearIssueContext.ts:14-16` — `buildIssueContextText` prepends "only the first 50 comments are included; further comments exist on Linear" to the **agent's** context when the flag is set.

The missing consumer:

- `packages/ui/src/components/references/ReferencePreview.tsx` — `LinearPreview` maps the detail's comments at `:566-578` and renders `<CommentsSection state={comments} total={null} now={now} />` at `:643`. It never reads `full.commentsMore`.
- `CommentsSection` (`:137-156`) can only say a thread is partial via its `total` prop (`commentsLatest`: "Latest {shown} of {total}", rendered only when `total !== null && total > shown`). Linear has no comment count by design (`packages/web/server/lib/linear/DOCUMENTATION.md`: "Linear offers no comment count, so the comments connection's `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is the only truncation signal"), so `total={null}` is correct for Linear — and the boolean that is the only available signal is dropped instead.
- The same component already demonstrates the house pattern one section up: `SubIssuesSection` (`:510-543`) reads `issue.subIssuesMore` and renders a linked note, `references.picker.preview.subIssuesMore` ("First {count} shown, all of them in Linear", in all 15 locales), when the sub-issue list is first-page-only.

## Evidence

Laptop probe against the real component (transient test file in the laptop primary `~/git/openchamber-fork`, since removed and archived at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-linear-commentsmore-preview-20261107/`; harness mirrors `ReferencePreview.test.tsx`: `renderToStaticMarkup` + happy-dom, real `createWebAPIs`, real `I18nProvider`). Fixture: a `LinearIssue` with 2 comments and `commentsMore: true`, plus 1 sub-issue with `subIssuesMore: true` as the in-render control. Run twice, identical both times:

- Control: the sub-issues truncation note **does** render — "First 1 shown, all of them in Linear" present in the output.
- The "Comments" heading renders and both comment entries render (2 entries).
- No comment-truncation signal anywhere in the output: the `commentsLatest` "Latest …" header is absent, and no text matching /further comments|more comments exist|first 50 comments/ appears.

So for an issue whose thread exceeds one page, the rendered preview of a `commentsMore: true` issue is indistinguishable from a complete thread. Static chain verified separately by direct reads of every file:line above on the same main.

## Why it matters

This is the remaining human-facing half of #1414. That issue's fix landed the signal and the agent-context note, so an agent attaching the issue is warned its picture is partial — but the person reading the preview is not: they see the oldest 50 comments (Linear returns oldest first) presented as the complete discussion, with the newest comments — usually the ones that supersede the rest — silently absent. It is the same shape as #1768 (`statesMore` reaches the UI type but no consumer) and #1732/#1743: a completeness signal that stops one step short of the surface it was produced for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the Linear detail has `commentsMore: true`, the reference preview's comments section visibly says the thread continues on Linear (mirroring the `SubIssuesSection` pattern: a note, ideally linked to the issue on Linear, with the new i18n string in all 15 locales).
- [ ] When `commentsMore` is false/absent, the preview renders exactly as today (no note, no layout change).
- [ ] A regression test in `ReferencePreview.test.tsx` (or equivalent) renders a `commentsMore: true` Linear detail and pins the note's presence, and a `commentsMore: false` detail pins its absence — oracle: the rendered text, with the `subIssuesMore` note as the reference behaviour.
- [ ] The agent-context behaviour in `linearIssueContext.ts` is unchanged.

title: fix(vscode): session-state store reads sessions-archive.json and sessions-metadata.json whole with no size gate — a 34.6 MB file is accepted whole on every session list, and a FIFO at either path wedges session reads forever

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/vscode
labels.description: Package: vscode (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The VS Code session-state store reads its two state files whole with no size gate, no regular-file check, and no deadline:

- `packages/vscode/src/openchamberSessionState.ts:169` — `readJsonObjectFile` does `raw = await fsPromises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8')` and `JSON.parse`s whatever comes back. It is the only reader for both files (`sessions-archive.json` via `readArchived`, `sessions-metadata.json` via `readMetadata`).
- The injected seam makes the shape structural: `SessionStateFs.readFile` (`openchamberSessionState.ts:54`) returns a whole `Promise<string>` — there is no stat/open step at which a gate could be judged.

These are the **same two files** the web server keeps in the shared OpenChamber data directory (`getOpenChamberDataDir`, `openchamberSessionState.ts:139ff`; the module header notes a session archived from VS Code stays archived in the desktop app and vice versa). The web readers for them — `openchamber-sessions/archive-store.js` and `session-metadata-store.js` — go through the shared durable JSON store (`readDurableJsonFile`), which is handle-judged, regular-file-checked, and capped at `DEFAULT_DURABLE_JSON_MAX_BYTES` = 32 MiB enforced in flight (durable-json-store.js:62, :113-138). The VS Code mirror reader has none of that. It is also absent from the VS Code mirror rows in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` (which cover only bridge settings, quota local-file readers, and `opencode.ts` settings) — this mirror was never inventoried.

## Verified behavior (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-vscode-sessionstate-20261107/probe.ts` on the laptop, driving the exported `createSessionStateStore` with the real `fs.promises` against main `3a4a34eda126614862b99659ed34a45cbd6afda3`:

- **Control:** a small valid `sessions-metadata.json` settles in 0-1 ms and returns its entry.
- **Oversized:** a 34,603,044-byte valid metadata file (a 34,603,008-char pad value) is read, parsed, and returned whole — past the 32 MiB cap the web twin enforces on the same file.
- **FIFO:** with `sessions-archive.json` replaced by a FIFO, `readArchived()` never settles (3 s race, both runs). The read is async, so the extension host does not freeze synchronously — instead every caller that awaits it wedges forever, with no deadline anywhere in the chain.

## Why it matters

- **Every session list pays it, repeatedly.** The store caches nothing between calls by design (module header: "every read parses the file and every write re-reads it first"). `bridge-proxy-runtime.ts:225` awaits `readArchived()` + `readMetadata()` to overlay every proxied `GET /api/session` / `GET /api/session/:id`; the archive/unarchive and metadata get/set bridge calls (`bridge-system-runtime.ts`, `api:sessions/*`) await the same reads. A bloated or corrupt-growing file is buffered and parsed whole on each of those calls, for the life of the extension host.
- **A FIFO or non-regular file wedges session surfaces indefinitely.** Anything that lands a FIFO at either path in the shared config dir (another tool, a bad restore, a hostile checkout) makes session listing/archive/metadata calls never settle — no error, no timeout, nothing in the log.
- **The two runtimes disagree about the same file.** A file the web server refuses as over-cap is silently accepted by the extension host, so the fleet's gated-read contract (#1655 inventory) holds for these files only when the web server happens to be the reader.

## Fix shape

Gate `readJsonObjectFile` the way the package's own bounded readers do (`opencodeConfig.ts` `readCappedFileSync`, 4 MiB, and its chunked skill-file read): judge the opened file (regular file + size) and enforce the cap on the bytes actually read, extending the `SessionStateFs` seam as earlier seam fixes did (cf. #1766, #1753). The cap should be stated once and should not be smaller than what the web twin accepts for the same files (32 MiB durable default) unless triage picks a tighter, justified bound for these small files (the header notes they are "a few kilobytes").

Disposition for gated-out files must preserve this store's safety semantics: an over-cap or non-regular file is **unknown, not empty** — reads answer `null` (as a non-ENOENT I/O failure already does at :169-177), so write paths keep refusing to overwrite state they could not read. It must not fall into the malformed path (rename-aside to `.corrupt-*` and read as `{}`), which would move a merely-large valid file aside and let the next write drop its state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readJsonObjectFile` (or its replacement) refuses a file over the stated cap and a non-regular file (FIFO included) without buffering it whole; the refusal settles promptly and answers `null` (unknown), never `{}`.
- [ ] A file that grows between any pre-read judgement and the read is judged on the bytes actually read (no stat-only gate, #1605 pattern).
- [ ] Behavioural tests in `openchamberSessionState.test.ts` pin: control file still reads; over-cap file → `null` and no rename-aside; FIFO/non-regular seam double → `null` promptly; archive/metadata writes still refuse when the read answers `null`.
- [ ] The cap constant is named, byte-denominated, and its relation to the web twin's 32 MiB durable cap for the same files is stated in a comment.
- [ ] The reader is added to the VS Code mirror rows in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

body:
## Problem

The Cursor quota provider reads its token files synchronously, whole, with no size cap and no regular-file check:

- `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.js:71-79` — `readFileToken(path)` does `readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim()` (line 74) inside a try/catch that can only observe errors *after* the read returns.
- `cursor.js:81-87` — `loadAuthState()` reads both `CURSOR_TOKEN_FILE` and `CURSOR_REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE` through it. The file reads happen **before** the env-token branch is returned, so the read is paid (and can block) even when `CURSOR_TOKEN` is set in the environment.
- `cursor.js:175` / `cursor.js:374-379` — `loadAuthState()` runs on every `fetchQuota()` and every `isConfigured()` call, i.e. on quota-board polls.

Because the read is synchronous, a non-regular file does not just stall one request — it freezes the whole server event loop. And because there is no cap, an arbitrarily large file is buffered whole and used as the credential.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `4bffa9021984`)

Laptop probe against the real module (`~/git/fleet/probe-oc-cursor-tokenfile-20261107/probe.mjs`, fetch stubbed to capture the Authorization header; run twice, identical results):

- **Control:** small token file with a valid future-`exp` JWT → `fetchQuota()` settles, Authorization header length 48.
- **Oversized:** a 33,554,473-byte token file (valid JWT + `A` padding in the signature segment) → settled, and the Authorization header sent was 33,554,480 characters — the entire file was read and used as the token, past any plausible credential size.
- **FIFO:** `CURSOR_TOKEN_FILE` pointing at a FIFO → `fetchQuota()` never settled; the probe was killed by `timeout` (exit 124) in both runs. The synchronous read blocks the process, not just the call.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `CURSOR_TOKEN_FILE` / cursor token-file reads — no issue covers this reader. The shared inventory (`packages/web/server/lib/shared/DOCUMENTATION.md:378`) lists "Cursor token files — `quota/providers/cursor.js`" in the foreign-owned *excepted* row; the same row's mcpx daemon (`#1773`) and Muse login store (`#1774`) readers were filed individually because a synchronous unbounded read of a foreign file still freezes this server — the exception addresses ownership, not the freeze. Siblings with the same shape: `#1777` (APNs .p8 key file), `#1778` (UI-auth JWT secret file), `#1645` (quota auth-file readers in `lib/quota/utils/auth.js` — a different reader; it does not cover `providers/cursor.js`).

## Why it matters

The quota board polls providers in the background, so this is not a rare code path: anyone who points `CURSOR_TOKEN_FILE` / `CURSOR_REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE` at a path that is later replaced by a FIFO, a device, or a growing file (log rotation accidents, bind mounts, a token helper that writes via a pipe) freezes the entire OpenChamber server with no error and no log line. A merely large file is silently accepted as a credential and shipped as a multi-megabyte Authorization header on every poll.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readFileToken` reads through the shared bounded sync reader (`packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, `readBoundedFileSync`) or an equivalent gate: regular-file check / non-blocking open plus an explicit byte cap sized for a token (the credential pipeline elsewhere uses 64 KiB).
- [ ] Over-cap, non-regular, or unreadable token files degrade exactly like a missing file today: `readFileToken` returns `null`, `isConfigured()` reports not configured, and no exception escapes `loadAuthState()`.
- [ ] Regression tests in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/cursor.test.js` (or a sibling test file): small token file still loads; oversized file is refused without being sent as an Authorization header; FIFO at the token path settles promptly instead of hanging.
- [ ] The `DOCUMENTATION.md` inventory row is updated so the Cursor token-file reader's disposition matches the implemented gate.

## Finding

PR #1676 gave `packages/web/server/lib/shared/durable-json-store.js` a two-half size gate for every read in the module (both reader spellings and all three read points of both preserve spellings): a handle-stat half and a chunked in-flight half that reads at most cap+1 bytes. Its five added tests pin only the stat half — no test makes the stat and the read disagree, so the in-flight half is the only half of the gate no test exercises.

## Evidence

- PR #1676 (merged, merge commit `8cc23ba52d2a337064a450d464472cc48b9d702a`, verified ancestor of current main `5c63b77f668b7e4bd88dd9d50e1a836e3300b0ef` via compare API, behind_by 0): diff adds `readBoundedRaw` / `readBoundedRawSync` with the stat check and the chunked loop, plus five tests in the `bounded reads (#1649)` describe (stated default cap, valid-at-cap, static over-cap in both spellings, preserve over-cap, FIFO).
- Current main, verified this run via `gh api contents`: `durable-json-store.js:128` stat check (`stat.size > maxBytes`), `:131-138` chunked loop with the `total > maxBytes` throw; sync twin at `:162` / `:165-172`.
- Current main `durable-json-store.test.js:415` — the bounded-reads describe is unchanged; a grep for `grow` in the test file returns nothing.
- Mutation check (by inspection of the two halves): reverting the chunked loop to a whole-file `handle.readFile()` passes every existing test — the static over-cap tests still throw at the stat check and the FIFO tests still throw at the regularity check — while a file that grows after its stat is again buffered whole, reopening the growth half of #1649 for all fifteen caller stores at once (this module is the shared store behind the credential, config, tunnel, and session-metadata stores).

## Why it matters

The durable store is the highest-blast-radius reader in this family: one regression in its in-flight half silently un-bounds fifteen stores. The house pattern already treats this exact gap as worth pinning — issue #1686 / PR #1688 added grows-after-stat coverage for the stored-icon route, and issues #1753 / #1754 filed the same gap for the git identity store and settings-runtime. This is the same filing for the one store whose gate protects the most callers. No live defect is claimed: the gate code itself is verified correct on current main.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deterministic test makes the handle stat report a size at or under the cap while the handle's reads deliver more than the cap (through the module's existing fs-injection seam or a stat/read spy, as PR #1713's walkthrough tests do), and the reader throws `DURABLE_JSON_STORE_TOO_LARGE` — never a parsed value, never `malformed`.
- The test pins that at most cap+1 bytes are read before the refusal.
- The sync spelling is covered the same way, or the test file states why the async case suffices.
- The test names its oracle (the cap invariant: no read in this module buffers more than cap+1 bytes, whatever the stat said) in a comment.
- The existing durable-json-store suite passes unchanged.

## Dedup

Searches this run: `durable-json grows`, `durable json store in-flight`, and `grows-after-stat` (30 results) — the grows-after-stat items are #1766 (different stores), #1753 / #1754 (identity store / settings-runtime), #1686 CLOSED (stored-icon route), #1605 (fs routes / VS Code bridge). No issue covers the durable-json-store's in-flight half.

title: fix(web): provider read cache has a per-entry byte cap but no total — 300 entries × 2 MiB can retain ~600 MiB of response bodies in the server

body:
## Problem

The provider read cache (`packages/web/server/lib/provider-read-cache/index.js`) bounds each kept answer individually but never bounds the cache's total retained bytes:

- `index.js:20` — `MAX_CACHED_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024` is a **per-entry** cap: `remember` (`index.js:62-68`) refuses a single body over 2 MiB.
- `index.js:18` — `MAX_ENTRIES = 300` is the only aggregate bound, and it counts entries, not bytes: `while (entries.size > MAX_ENTRIES) entries.delete(...)`.
- There is no total-bytes accounting anywhere in the module (no running sum, no eviction on bytes).

So the cache can retain up to 300 × ~2 MiB ≈ **600 MiB of response bodies** in the long-lived server process. The cached routes include `/pulls/context` (`index.js:38`, 15 s TTL), whose answers carry diffs and are exactly the bodies that approach the 2 MiB per-entry cap. Entry expiry is lazy — an expired body stays in the `Map` until its own key is requested again or count-eviction reaches it — so the count cap, not the TTL, is what actually limits retention.

## Evidence (verified this run, on main `5c63b77f668b7e4bd88dd9d50e1a836e3300b0ef`)

Laptop probe against the real `createProviderReadCache` middleware (probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-readcache-total-20261107/probe.mjs` on the laptop; run twice, identical results):

- Filled 300 distinct query keys with bodies of 1,048,540 bytes each (under the per-entry cap): all 300 first requests reached the handler.
- Replayed all 300 keys: **300/300 answered from cache** — a retained-bytes lower bound of **314,562,000 bytes (300.0 MiB)**, with no eviction.
- Control: a body over the 2 MiB per-entry cap was served but **not** kept (replay reached the handler) — the per-entry half of the bound works; only the total is missing.

House precedent: the Octokit ETag cache carries both bounds after #848 ("300 entries, no per-entry or total byte bound") — `packages/web/server/lib/github/octokit.js:38` sets `ETAG_CACHE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024` and its eviction loop (`octokit.js:54`) runs while **either** the entry count **or** the total bytes is over its cap. This cache is the same shape with only the count half present.

The existing test file (`index.test.js`, 100 lines) has no size-, entry-count-, or eviction-behavior test at all.

## Why it matters

The managed server is a long-lived process serving every connected client; provider reads are shared across all of them, so distinct keys (different repos, issues, PRs, bindings) accumulate naturally during a busy session. An unbounded-in-bytes response cache is a slow memory-growth hazard with no operator-visible limit — the same defect class the fleet already fixed for the ETag cache in #848.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cache tracks retained bytes and evicts oldest entries while **either** `MAX_ENTRIES` or a new total-bytes cap is exceeded (shape follows `octokit.js`'s ETag cache); the total cap's value is stated in the module next to `MAX_CACHED_BYTES`, with a comment distinguishing per-entry from total.
- [ ] Re-`remember`ing an existing key does not double-count its bytes, and `clear(provider)` / full eviction leaves the byte accounting at the true retained total (no drift across clear/replace cycles).
- [ ] Tests pin the behavior: filling past the total evicts the oldest keys (they reach the handler again) while recent keys still answer from cache; the per-entry >2 MiB refusal still holds; a replaced key's bytes are counted once.
- [ ] Existing provider-read-cache tests still pass.

body:
## Finding

Open PR #1702 fixes #1693 by flushing the ngrok **stderr** accumulator in `onExit` before the startup error is built. The **stdout** accumulator has the identical race and is left unflushed: on current main, both accumulators release a held final unterminated line only on their stream's `end` event, and a child process's `exit` can fire before either stream ends. That matters more for stdout than for stderr here, because ngrok is spawned with `--log=stdout` — its structured log lines, including the error diagnostics that explain a startup failure, are written to **stdout**. If ngrok prints its final diagnostic without a trailing newline and exits while a background writer keeps the pipe open (the exact setup of PR #1702's own stderr test), `onExit` builds "Ngrok exited while starting" from `recentOutput` without that line — the same lost-diagnostic defect #1693 files for stderr, on the stream that actually carries ngrok's log.

## Evidence

- PR #1702 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1702), OPEN, head e3ec1a1089e8: its diff adds `captureLines(stderrAccumulator.flush())` to `onExit` in `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js` — stderr only; no stdout flush.
- Current main 2d834f82c7474b3f45b15058941f2fe068920ca7 (verified twice):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js:353` — ngrok is spawned with `--log=stdout --log-format=json`, so its log/diagnostics go to stdout.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js:379-380` — separate `stdoutAccumulator` and `stderrAccumulator`, both feeding the shared `captureLines` → `recentOutput`.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js:385-387` and `:394-396` — each accumulator is flushed only in its stream's `end` handler.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/ngrok-tunnel.js:432-434` — `onExit` on main flushes neither accumulator before building the error from `recentOutput`; PR #1702 changes this for stderr only.
- Dedupe: #1693 (OPEN) is explicitly scoped to the stderr line in its title and body; #1694 (CLOSED) covered the missing test for the stdout **stream-end** flush, since covered by PR #1750's test — neither covers flushing the stdout accumulator on **exit**. The cloudflare sibling (PR #1715, merged) flushes its accumulator on stream end and exit alike.

## Why it matters

The startup error is the only diagnostic a user gets when ngrok fails to start. Losing the final stdout line loses ngrok's own error record (that stream is where `--log=stdout` puts it), leaving a bare exit code — and once #1702 lands, the code will look deliberately handled while the primary stream's race remains.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `onExit` in `startNgrokQuickTunnel` flushes the stdout accumulator as well as the stderr one before the exit error is built (or #1702's scope is extended to both), with flush idempotent against the later `end` handlers (no line captured twice).
- [ ] A regression test mirroring PR #1702's stderr case for stdout: a final unterminated line on stdout, a background writer holding the pipe open so `exit` fires before stdout `end`, and the line present exactly once in the startup error.
- [ ] Existing ngrok tunnel tests, including PR #1750's stream-end flush test, stay green.

body:
## Finding

PR #1683 added the missing byte caps to the two git state stores #1678 named — contributor-provenance and managed SSH credentials — but each cap is judged **only on the pre-read handle stat**, and the read itself is still `handle.readFile('utf8')`, which buffers the whole file. Just as important, both stores still open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` and **no `O_NONBLOCK`**, so a FIFO at the state path blocks `open()` forever, before the handle stat that would refuse it as non-regular ever runs. Both stores serialize their operations (the SSH store's `read` is `enqueue(readState)`; the provenance store's `read`/`readMany` are enqueued), so one FIFO — or one file grown past its cap after the stat — defeats the cap and wedges every later operation on the chain. This is exactly the pair of residuals issue #1684 named and PR #1698 fixed for the sibling git network-operation and worktree-bootstrap stores in the same review batch; #1683's two stores were left in the pre-fix shape.

## Evidence

- PR #1683 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1683), MERGED 2026-11-06, merge 90739d745e1f, head 0d51632dd746, for #1678 (CLOSED).
- Current main 2d834f82c7474b3f45b15058941f2fe068920ca7 (verified twice via the commits API; file contents read twice):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/contributor-provenance-storage.js:102` — `fsImpl.open(filePath, O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)` (no O_NONBLOCK).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/contributor-provenance-storage.js:110` — the cap is a stat check only: `if (stats.size > maxRecords * MAX_STATE_BYTES_PER_RECORD) throw invalidStore();` (per-record cap at :17).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/contributor-provenance-storage.js:111` — `JSON.parse(await handle.readFile('utf8'))` buffers the file whole; a file grown after the stat is read entire, past the cap.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/contributor-provenance-storage.js:161,166` — `read` and `readMany` run inside the store's serialized `enqueue`, so a blocked open stalls the chain.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/ssh-credential-storage.js:60` — same open flags (no O_NONBLOCK); `:69` stat-only cap (`MAX_STORE_BYTES`, :19); `:70` `handle.readFile('utf8')` whole; `:78` `const read = () => enqueue(readState)`.
- The correct sibling pattern, already on main from PR #1698 for #1684: `network-operation-storage.js` / `worktree-bootstrap-storage.js` open with O_NONBLOCK on POSIX and enforce the cap in flight with a chunked handle read (at most maxBytes + 1 buffered), with grows-after-stat and FIFO regression tests.
- The design contract (#1655 rule 2, restated in `shared/DOCUMENTATION.md` by PR #1681): the bound half is "open once, judge from the handle, cap enforced in flight, non-regular refused". #1683's stores satisfy only the stat part of it.

## Why it matters

These are credential- and provenance-bearing state files in the user's data directory, which other tools and sync jobs also write to. The failure modes are the ones this whole fix series exists to remove: an oversized or racing write is buffered whole in memory despite the stated cap, and a FIFO at the path hangs the store's serialized operation chain indefinitely instead of being refused promptly — with the cap code giving a false impression that both are handled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both stores open with O_NONBLOCK on POSIX (keeping O_NOFOLLOW) so a FIFO at the state path is refused promptly with the store's existing invalid-store error, and the serialized chain behind it settles (regression tests mirroring PR #1698's FIFO tests).
- [ ] Both stores enforce their cap in flight (chunked handle read, at most cap + 1 bytes buffered), so a file grown after its handle stat is refused, never buffered whole (grows-after-stat regression tests with a lying-stat fs seam, mirroring PR #1698).
- [ ] Existing behavior is unchanged for missing, at-cap, over-cap-on-stat, malformed, and wrong-mode files; the #1683 tests stay green.

body:
# fix(ui): Settings search for "Custom provider" highlights nothing — the form only renders in add/edit mode, and the result never enters it

## Summary

The Settings search entry `providers.custom` ("Custom provider" — base URL / API key for an OpenAI-compatible provider) declares the Providers page, but its only anchor lives inside `CustomProviderForm`, which the Providers page renders **only** in custom-create mode (the user has already clicked through Connect → Custom) or custom-edit mode (an existing custom provider is selected for editing). Picking the search result just opens the Providers grid: no preparation enters either mode, the form never mounts, and the reveal loop silently gives up.

Same failure class as #1762 (anchor behind a sub-page gate the result never opens) and #1764 (anchor behind page-local mode state) — here the gate is the Providers page's add/edit flow state. Notably, its neighbours got preparation cases and this one didn't: `providers.connect` sets `settingsProvidersConnectRequested`, and `providers.classification` sets `settingsProvidersClassificationRequested`; `providers.custom` has neither a request flag nor any other handling.

## Evidence (verified on main `2d834f82c`, laptop probe x2 identical)

- Search entry: `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/search.ts:1512-1517` — `id: 'providers.custom'`, `page: 'providers'`, titleKey `settings.providers.page.custom.title`, keywords `other / custom / openai-compatible / base url / api key`. It has **no** `isAvailable` restriction at all (probe-verified), so it is offered to every user.
- Sole anchor: `packages/ui/src/components/sections/providers/CustomProviderForm.tsx:235` renders `settingsItem="providers.custom"`; grep over `packages/ui/src` finds the anchor nowhere else (full 261-entry anchor map, probe below).
- The form is flow-gated: `packages/ui/src/components/sections/providers/ProvidersPage.tsx` renders `<CustomProviderForm>` only in the candidate branch when `isCustomCreateMode` (`:224`: `isAddMode && candidateProviderId === CUSTOM_PROVIDER_ID`, form at :646) and in the edit branch when `isCustomEditMode && isEditableCustomProvider && editingCustomFormInitial` (form at :799). From the plain Providers grid — where a search result lands — neither holds.
- No preparation enters the gate: `prepareSettingsSearchTarget` in `packages/ui/src/components/views/SettingsView.tsx` handles `providers.connect` and `providers.classification` (probe-verified: those are the only two `providers.*` cases) — `providers.custom` is not handled, so the result id is returned unchanged, `openPage('providers')` shows the grid, and the reveal effect (`SettingsView.tsx:641-646`) queries `[data-settings-item="providers.custom"]` for `PENDING_ITEM_MAX_FRAMES = 30` frames (:86) and silently stops.
- Why the #325 guard misses it: the guard in `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/search.test.ts` asserts each entry id has a literal anchor somewhere in the component sources; the anchor exists literally in CustomProviderForm.tsx, so the test passes while the anchor is unreachable from where the result lands.

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-search-anchors-20261107/` (`probe2.py`, run twice with byte-identical output): entry page `providers`, no `isAvailable`, anchor in form at line 235, create-mode gate present, prepare handles `providers.custom` = false, prepare providers cases = [providers.classification, providers.connect]. Full 261-entry anchor map in the same directory (`map.txt`).

## Why it matters

"Custom provider" is the path for every OpenAI-compatible / self-hosted endpoint — a common thing to search for by name ("custom", "base url", "api key"). The search result promises the form and delivers the providers grid with no highlight and no hint; the user still has to know the Connect → Custom click path the search was supposed to replace. Its two sibling entries (`providers.connect`, `providers.classification`) both work because they got request flags — this one reads as an oversight when those were added, not a design choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Picking the `providers.custom` Settings search result opens the custom-provider create form (e.g. a preparation case that sets the same add-mode/candidate state the Connect → Custom path sets, in the style of the `providers.connect` / `providers.classification` request flags — or an equivalent shape the triager prefers) and highlights the form's anchored field.
- [ ] No regression: `providers.connect` still opens the connect picker, `providers.classification` still opens the Classification sub-page, and `providers.auth` / `providers.models` reveals are unchanged.
- [ ] Cancelling out of the search-opened form returns to the Providers grid cleanly (no stuck add-mode state), matching the manual Connect → Custom → Cancel path.
- [ ] A test pins `providers.custom`'s preparation behaviour, and the anchor guard or a companion test fails if an entry's anchor renders only inside a flow state its result does not enter — at minimum the providers.custom case is pinned.

## Notes

- Related: #1762 (same class, gated sub-page), #1764 (same class, page-local mode state), #1665 (wrong tab), #325 (closed; anchor-existence guard). Distinct mechanism from each: the anchor is on the right page but inside an add/edit flow state.
- Filed-only (task/triage): reusing the request-flag pattern is likely, but whether search should open create-mode directly (vs. the connect picker with Custom preselected) is a triage/UX call.

# fix(ui): Settings search for the TypeSafe API key opens the Routing page, but the field lives on Providers → Classification — the result highlights nothing

## Summary

The Settings search entry for the TypeSafe API key (`routing.token`) declares the wrong page. Picking it opens the **Routing** page (Auto tab) and waits to highlight an element that is never rendered there; the actual key field is rendered only on the **Providers → Classification** sub-page. The user lands on a page with no token field and no highlight, and the reveal loop silently gives up.

This is the wrong-*page* sibling of #1665 (a search result opened its page on the wrong *tab*). It also survives the guard test added for #325, because that test collects anchors globally, not per page (below).

## Evidence (verified on main `2ca4d6df965a`, laptop probe x2 identical)

- Search entry: `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/search.ts:1069-1076` — `id: 'routing.token'`, `page: 'routing'`, titleKey `settings.routing.token.label`.
- The **only** element carrying the anchor in the whole UI is on the other page: `packages/ui/src/components/sections/classification/ClassificationProvidersPage.tsx:262` renders `settingsItem="routing.token"` (the TypeSafe key field, :260-287). Grep over `packages/ui/src` for the anchor returns that one file; nothing in `packages/ui/src/components/sections/routing/` mentions `routing.token`.
- That sub-page is gated: `packages/ui/src/components/sections/providers/ProvidersPage.tsx:607` renders `ClassificationProvidersPage` only when `selectedProviderId === CLASSIFICATION_PAGE_ID`, which the search flow sets only via `settingsProvidersClassificationRequested` (ProvidersPage.tsx:111-127) — and `SettingsView` sets that flag **only** for result id `providers.classification` (`packages/ui/src/components/views/SettingsView.tsx:490-492`), never for `routing.token`.
- Picking the result instead: `prepareSettingsSearchTarget` calls `routingTabForSearchTarget('routing.token')`, which returns `'auto'` by the `routing.` prefix fallback (`packages/ui/src/components/sections/routing/routingTabs.ts:18-22`), opens page `routing`, and sets the pending item; the reveal effect (`SettingsView.tsx:624-660`) queries `[data-settings-item="routing.token"]` for 30 frames (`PENDING_ITEM_MAX_FRAMES`, :86) and then silently stops — no element, no highlight, no error.
- Scoping: the other eight `routing` search entries all anchor inside `sections/routing/` (RoutingPage.tsx, PoolAdvancedFields.tsx, RouteTuningFields.tsx, ModelPoolsSection.tsx) — `routing.token` is the sole wrong-page routing entry.
- Why the #325 guard misses it: `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/search.test.ts:346` ("every search entry id has a settings-item anchor in the component sources") collects anchors from **all** component sources into one global set, so an anchor that exists on a different page — behind a sub-page gate — passes.

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-routing-token-search-20261107/probe.mjs` (static trace of the real search flow against the real sources), run twice with identical output ending `BUG CONFIRMED`.

## Why it matters

The TypeSafe API key is the credential that switches Jev classification/routing to the user's own key; the search entry exists precisely so a user who searches "api key / token / routing" can find it. Today that path is a dead end that looks like nothing happened — the exact failure #1665/#325 were filed to eliminate, one level up (page instead of tab).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Picking the `routing.token` Settings search result opens the Providers page **on the Classification sub-page** and highlights the TypeSafe API key field (e.g. repoint the entry to `page: 'providers'` and route it through the same classification-request mechanism `providers.classification` uses, with the reveal targeting the token anchor — or an equivalent shape the triager prefers).
- [ ] No regression for `providers.classification`: its search result still opens the Classification sub-page.
- [ ] The #325 guard test in `search.test.ts` is strengthened so an entry whose anchor exists only on a **different page** (or only behind a sub-page gate its own result does not open) fails — at minimum for the tabbed/gated pages it can model (routing, providers/classification, projects, chat), or the routing.token case is pinned by a dedicated test.
- [ ] A test pins `routing.token`'s disposition (entry page + preparation behaviour), in the style of `routingTabs.test.ts`.

## Notes

- Related: #1665 (same class, wrong tab), #325 (closed; same-page anchor renames + the global guard test). This issue is distinct from both: the anchor id is correct and present — the entry's page and the sub-page opening are what's missing.

# fix(web): session-folders POST never measures the merged snapshot — a 3 MiB whole-copy POST into a 6 MiB store writes a 9 MiB file past the 8 MiB read cap and wedges GET/PATCH at 500

## Finding

The session-folders store's invariant (routes.js:8-18) is that a stored file must stay readable for everything the writer could legitimately write: the write cap is `MAX_BODY_BYTES` = 4 MiB (routes.js:6) and the bounded read cap is `MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` = 2 × that = 8 MiB (routes.js:18). The POST whole-copy path breaks that invariant by never measuring what it actually writes:

- The POST guard (routes.js:256-257) measures only the **incoming body**, pretty-printed: `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)) > MAX_BODY_BYTES`.
- The handler then merges that body with the **current stored snapshot** — `mergeSnapshots(current, body, now())` (routes.js:270) is a per-scope union: scopes/folders the writer never saw are kept, incoming folders win per id (routes.js:78-80 comment and merge body).
- The merged result is persisted with **no size check at all**: `await writeSnapshot(outgoing)` (routes.js:277), and `writeSnapshot` (routes.js:190-195) writes `JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2)` unconditionally.

So a store already holding ~6 MiB (legitimately, under the 8 MiB read cap) plus a whole-copy POST of ~3 MiB (legitimately, under the 4 MiB body guard) produces a ~9 MiB stored file that the bounded reader refuses. This is a different mechanism from #1745 (the PATCH guard measuring compact while writeSnapshot persists pretty): fixing #1745 does not close this hole, because the POST guard already measures pretty — it just measures the wrong object (the input, not the merged output).

## Evidence (probe vs the real module, laptop, main 2ca4d6df965ab7d38e1c7442033b1359f0fedd90)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-post-merge-cap-20261107/probe.mjs` on the laptop — registers the real `registerSessionFoldersRoutes` with real fs in a temp dir, seeds a valid store, POSTs a disjoint whole copy, then re-reads. Run twice, identical output:

- Seeded store: 6,020,235 bytes pretty (valid snapshot, one folder, 140,000 session ids) — GET before: **200**.
- POST body: 3,010,235 bytes pretty (disjoint scope, 70,000 session ids) — passes the 4 MiB guard; POST: **200**.
- Stored file after the POST: **9,030,416 bytes > 8,388,608** (`MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`).
- GET after: **500** `Stored session folders are malformed`.
- PATCH after (schema-valid `forget-scopes` change): **500** `Stored session folders are malformed`.

## Why it matters

Once wedged, every GET and PATCH on `/api/session-folders` returns 500: clients cannot read or incrementally change their folders. The only recovery is another whole-copy POST — and because `readCurrent()` returns `null` for the over-cap file, the POST handler's `readCurrent() ?? EMPTY_SNAPSHOT` (routes.js:269) merges against **empty**, silently discarding every stored folder the repairing body does not carry. A routine sync from a long-open tab or a second device (exactly the writers the merge exists for, per the routes.js:78-80 comment) can trigger it with both sides individually under their caps.

## Acceptance criteria

- The POST path measures the merged snapshot it is about to persist (in the persisted, pretty-printed form) and refuses with 413 — without writing — when it would exceed what the bounded reader can read back (`MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`), instead of writing a file the store then calls malformed.
- A regression test drives the real routes: seed a store near the read cap, POST a disjoint whole copy under the body cap whose merge exceeds the read cap, and assert the POST is refused and GET/PATCH still serve the pre-POST state.
- Existing behavior is preserved for in-cap merges (union semantics, tombstones, monotonic `updatedAt`), and the PATCH path's guard (#1745) is untouched or aligned so both write paths enforce the same invariant: nothing writable is unreadable.

Related: #1745 (PATCH compact-vs-pretty measurement), #1626 / #1623 (the bounded read this invariant rests on).

## Finding

The Mistral quota provider exists only on the web backend. The VS Code backend has no Mistral fetcher, no dispatch case, and no configured entry — so the moment #1735 adds `mistral` to the shared UI catalog (`QUOTA_PROVIDERS`), the VS Code host will request it through the bridge and every fetch will return `Unsupported provider`, and Mistral can never report configured there. This is the exact failure shape of #1744 (Command Code / Open Design), for the one remaining provider.

Evidence (verified on current main `81922e718e`, laptop primary `~/git/openchamber-fork`, this run):

- Web backend complete: `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/mistral.js:36` (`providerId = 'mistral'`, key-validity fetcher against `GET https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models`), registered in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/index.js:174-181` including `fetchQuotaForCredential`.
- VS Code backend absent: `grep -ri mistral packages/vscode/src` returns **0 hits** on main.
- Dispatch falls through: `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:4755` `fetchQuotaForProviderUncoalesced` switches on provider id; its 27 cases cover every other web provider except `command-code`/`opendesign` (#1744) and `mistral`; the default branch at `quotaProviders.ts:4839` returns `{ ok: false, configured: false, error: 'Unsupported provider' }`.
- Never configured: the configured-provider set built at `quotaProviders.ts:955` adds 27+ provider ids conditionally (e.g. `github-copilot-addon` at :1025) — `mistral` is never added, so the VS Code board cannot mark it configured even with a live enrolled credential.
- Request path: the shared UI calls the bridge method `api:quota:get` (`packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.ts:636`), which calls `fetchQuotaForProvider(providerId)` directly — no host-side filtering by backend support.

Why #1735 does not cover this: #1735 is scoped to the UI catalog/type registration and explicitly set the VS Code surface aside, reasoning that VS Code "already omits the web providers command-code and opendesign, so web-only is an existing precedent there". #1744 (filed after #1735) reclassified that omission as a bug: the board is shared, so a catalogued provider with no VS Code fetcher is broken in the VS Code host, not web-only by design. Under that ruling, Mistral is the third instance of the #1744 bug — latent today only because #1735 has not landed yet; it activates the moment the catalog entry appears.

## Why it matters

The fleet holds a live Mistral credential, and the provider's whole purpose is surfacing key validity (valid vs invalid/revoked) on the quota board (#1619). Landing #1735 alone would make the web board work while the VS Code board shows a permanent `Unsupported provider` error for a configured provider — a regression-looking state that triage would then have to rediscover. Fixing the VS Code port together with (or immediately after) #1735 closes the provider's cross-host gap in one pass, mirroring how the other 27 providers exist in both backends.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` gains a Mistral fetcher ported from the web provider (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/mistral.js`): enrolled `mistral` credential → `GET https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models`; 200 with a `data` array → `ok: true` with `usageAvailability: 'console-only'` and empty windows (no fabricated figures); 401/403 → the unauthorized error class; 200 without `data` → malformed class; no credential → `configured: false` / 'Not configured'.
- [ ] A `case 'mistral'` dispatch entry in `fetchQuotaForProviderUncoalesced` and a `mistral` entry in the configured-provider set (same key/token/access judgement as the web `isConfigured`), so the VS Code board can show it configured.
- [ ] Tests in `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.test.ts` pin the dispatch and the configured entry (the file already pins `Unsupported provider` behaviour for unknown ids at :1570 — Mistral must no longer land there).
- [ ] Sequencing noted on #1735: this issue and #1735 together complete Mistral's board presence; neither alone leaves a host broken.

Related: #1735 (UI catalog registration), #1744 (same bug shape for command-code/opendesign), #1619 (provider's origin), #1747 (the web fetcher's key-selection fix — the VS Code port should select the credential the same corrected way).

Found by: new-issue-creator-openchamber run 2026-11-07 00:50 CST — systematic three-way catalog diff (web registry vs UI catalog/types vs VS Code dispatch cases + configured set) run against laptop primary on main `81922e718e`; the diff was exactly {mistral, github-copilot-addon} vs the UI, and {command-code, opendesign, mistral} vs VS Code dispatch, with the first two pairs already filed as #1735/#1738/#1744.

body:
## Problem

Two quota providers share the defect filed for Mistral in #1747 and swept for eight more providers in #1751 — but both were missed by that sweep: `isConfigured` selects the credential with `||` while `fetchQuota` selects it with `??`. An empty-string first field therefore makes the two disagree, and a whitespace-only first field is sent to the API as a blank bearer <redacted> instead of falling through to the valid second field.

Verified on main `c939e36f034744b43900b5e87fd22ee651a72a08` (2026-11-07):

| Provider | `isConfigured` (`||`) | `fetchQuota` (`??`) |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/minimax-shared.js` (backs both `minimax-coding-plan` and `minimax-cn-coding-plan`) | :143 `entry?.key \|\| entry?.token` | :149 `entry?.key ?? entry?.token` |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/wafer.js` | :23 `entry?.key \|\| entry?.token` | :29 `entry?.key ?? entry?.token` |

The VS Code ports carry the same mismatch for exactly these providers: the configured-set builder in `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` judges minimax-coding-plan (:1003), minimax-cn-coding-plan (:1008) and wafer (:1030) with raw `key || token`, while its fetchers select with `??` (minimax :2387, wafer :3424).

The correct in-repo pattern already exists: `kimi.js`, `hyper.js`, `kilo.js`, `cline-pass.js` and `command-code.js` route both `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota` through one shared `getApiKey(auth)` built on `asNonEmptyString`, so empty/whitespace values fall through identically in both places. `ollama-cloud.js` and `opencode-go.js` likewise already select via `asNonEmptyString` in both paths — the sweep in #1751 was otherwise complete; these two files (three provider ids) are the remainder.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-minimax-wafer-20261106/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real provider modules with the `configureOpenCodeCredentials` seam (same harness as `minimax-shared.test.js` / `wafer.test.js`) and a stubbed global `fetch` capturing the Authorization header. Run twice, identical output both times:

```
wafer   empty-key: isConfigured=true fetch.configured=false ok=false error="Not configured" fetchCalls=0 auth=null
minimax empty-key: isConfigured=true fetch.configured=false ok=false error="Not configured" fetchCalls=0 auth=null
wafer   ws-key:    isConfigured=true fetch.configured=true ok=true fetchCalls=1 auth="Bearer  "
minimax ws-key:    isConfigured=true fetch.configured=true ok=true fetchCalls=1 auth="Bearer  "
wafer   control:   isConfigured=true fetch.configured=true ok=true fetchCalls=1 auth="Bearer <real-key>"
minimax control:   isConfigured=true fetch.configured=true ok=true fetchCalls=1 auth="Bearer <real-key>"
```

With `key: ""` and a valid `token`, `isConfigured` reports the provider configured, but `fetchQuota` returns `configured: false` / "Not configured" without ever calling fetch. With `key: " "`, the fetch goes out with a blank `Bearer ` header and the valid token is never tried.

Dedup: title/keyword search over open and closed issues for wafer / minimax / isConfigured / key-selection — #1747 (Mistral only) and #1751 (deepinfra, deepseek, neuralwatt, nanogpt, openrouter, zai, codex, copilot) are the only key-selection issues; neither names minimax or wafer in title, body, or comments (checked this run). The closed wafer/minimax issues (#484, #606, #608, #616) cover unrelated defects.

## Why it matters

Auth entries with an empty first field are realistic (a key cleared in one tool, a stored entry whose `key` was blanked while `token` remains). The quota board then shows MiniMax (both plans) and Wafer as configured while every fetch reports "Not configured" (or fails auth on a blank bearer), and the disagreement between the two selectors makes the failure invisible to anyone debugging from `isConfigured`. This is the last remainder of the #1747 pattern: fixing Mistral + the eight in #1751 and stopping here would leave the pattern alive in three provider ids across two surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `minimax-shared.js` and `wafer.js` each select the credential through a single shared helper (the `getApiKey`/`asNonEmptyString` pattern used by kimi/hyper/kilo/cline-pass/command-code), used by both `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota` — covering both MiniMax provider ids that share `createMiniMaxCodingPlanProvider`.
- [ ] The VS Code twins are fixed in the same pass: `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` configured-set checks (:1003, :1008, :1030) and fetchers (:2387, :3424) for minimax-coding-plan, minimax-cn-coding-plan and wafer use the same non-empty selection.
- [ ] Regression tests (extending `minimax-shared.test.js` / `wafer.test.js`, and the VS Code quota tests where a harness exists): `key: ""` + valid `token` → `isConfigured` true AND `fetchQuota` fetches with the token; `key: " "` + valid `token` → the token is used, never `Bearer `; both fields empty/whitespace → not configured in both.
- [ ] No behavior change when the first field holds a real value (probe control case above).

Related: #1747, #1751.

body:
## Finding

PR #1673 (merged, merge commit `9b5158a843189dd28e9b512dca7391dbb1e639c6`, verified ancestor of current main `c939e36f034744b43900b5e87fd22ee651a72a08` via compare API, behind_by 0) gated the four async readers in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-runtime.js` behind `readGatedFile` (current main `:131-145`):

- a stat half: `fsPromises.stat` judges regularity and `stat.size > SETTINGS_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (8 MiB) before the read; and
- a **growth half**: after `fsPromises.readFile`, `Buffer.byteLength(raw, 'utf8')` is rechecked against the cap, so — in the PR's own words — "a file grown past the cap between the two is still refused, never used".

Only the stat half has test coverage. The five tests PR #1673 added (`settings-runtime.test.js`, `describe('bounded settings reads (#1653)')`, `:908` on current main) use real files whose stat size already exceeds the cap (strict over-cap, lenient over-cap, preferences over-cap), a FIFO, and a within-cap control. No test makes the stat and the read disagree: a small stat with an over-cap read result. Verified on current main this run: the test file contains no grows-after-stat / stat-read disagreement case (grep for `grow`, `disagree`, `byteLength` in the test file returns nothing).

## Why it matters

The post-read recheck is the only part of this gate that stands between a growing settings/preferences file and the strict reader's callers. If it regresses (dropped, or compared against the wrong value), every existing test still passes — the stat gate catches every static over-cap file — while a file that grows past 8 MiB between stat and read is parsed and used whole, including by `readSettingsFromDiskStrict`, whose never-answer-`{}` contract exists because identity-regenerating callers would misread an empty answer as a first run. This is the same coverage shape the repo already treated as filing-worthy for the stored-icon route's post-read cap check (issue #1686, coverage added by PR #1688).

Note on scope: this issue is about the missing regression coverage for the growth half only. The gate's shape itself (stat + post-read recheck on the injected `fsPromises` seam, rather than the shared bounded reader) was the triage verdict for issue #1653 and was dispositioned "bound-complete" by the design #1655 phase-2 inventory (PR #1681) — this filing does not re-open that decision; it pins the behaviour that decision relies on.

**Oracle** (per the repo's testing doctrine): the invariant is "content whose byte length crosses the cap is refused, whatever its stat said". The factory's injected `fsPromises` seam is the deterministic oracle driver — the same seam the suite already wraps to simulate I/O failure in the migration abort test: a wrapped `fsPromises` whose `stat` reports a within-cap regular file while `readFile` returns over-cap content decides the case with no timing race.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deterministic regression test in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-runtime.test.js` models stat/read disagreement through the injected `fsPromises` seam (stat reports a small regular file; `readFile` returns more than 8 MiB): the strict reader rejects with `BOUNDED_FILE_TOO_LARGE`.
- [ ] The same disagreement case pins the lenient mapping: the lenient reader answers `{}` and the preferences reader reads as `{ status: 'failed' }` (merged document is the instance alone), matching the failure mappings the PR preserved.
- [ ] The test names its oracle (the cap invariant above) in a comment, matching the style of the bounded-reader tests in this repo.
- [ ] The existing settings-runtime suite passes unchanged (laptop / CI per repo convention).

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1673 (fixes issue #1653, CLOSED verified this run)
- PR diff: `readGatedFile` with the post-read `Buffer.byteLength` recheck and its comment; the five added tests listed above — none exercises growth after stat.
- Current main `c939e36f034744b43900b5e87fd22ee651a72a08`: `settings-runtime.js:131-145` identical to the PR diff (fetched via `gh api` contents this run); `settings-runtime.test.js:908` bounded-reads describe block unchanged, no growth case.
- Deduped this run: searches for "settings-runtime grows", "readGatedFile", "settings-runtime bounded", "in flight cap settings", and "1653" return only issue #1653 (CLOSED), design #1655 (OPEN) and its phase-2 audit issue #1656 (CLOSED) — none names this coverage gap; the full open-issue list (78 issues) contains no settings-runtime coverage item. Issue #1605 (OPEN) covers the same stat-then-read pattern in `lib/fs/routes.js` only, not this module.

body:
## Problem

Eight quota providers share the defect filed for Mistral in #1747: `isConfigured` selects the credential with `||` while `fetchQuota` selects it with `??`. An empty-string first field therefore makes the two disagree, and a whitespace-only first field is sent to the API as a blank bearer token instead of falling through to the valid second field.

Verified on main `260cc5e23` (2026-11-07):

| Provider | `isConfigured` (`||`) | `fetchQuota` (`??`) |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/deepinfra.js` | :19 `entry?.key \|\| entry?.token` | :25 `entry?.key ?? entry?.token` |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/deepseek.js` | :19 | :25 |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/neuralwatt.js` | :31 | :37 |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/nanogpt.js` | :48 | :54 |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/openrouter.js` | :61 | :67 |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/zai.js` | :107 | :116 and :150 (two fetch paths) |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/codex.js` | :24 `entry?.access \|\| entry?.token` | :28 `entry?.access ?? entry?.token` |
| `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/copilot.js` | :110 `entry?.access \|\| entry?.token` | :116 and :182 `entry?.access ?? entry?.token` |

The correct in-repo pattern already exists: `kimi.js`, `hyper.js`, `kilo.js`, `cline-pass.js` and `command-code.js` route both `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota` through one shared `getApiKey(auth)` built on `asNonEmptyString`, so empty/whitespace values fall through identically in both places.

## Reproduction (laptop probe, this run)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-quota-key-20261106/probe.mjs` on the laptop, importing the real provider modules with a stubbed `readAuth`/`fetchImpl`:

```
nanogpt isConfigured= true fetchQuota.configured= false ok= false error= Not configured fetchCalled= false
deepseek isConfigured= true fetchQuota.configured= false ok= false error= Not configured fetchCalled= false
codex    isConfigured= true fetchQuota.configured= false ok= false error= Not configured fetchCalled= false
nanogpt whitespace-key isConfigured= true Authorization sent= "Bearer  "
```

With `key: ""` and a valid `token`, `isConfigured` reports the provider configured, but `fetchQuota` returns `configured: false` / "Not configured" without ever calling fetch. With `key: " "`, the fetch goes out with a blank `Bearer ` header and the valid token is never tried.

Related: #1747 covers the same mismatch for Mistral only; its scope-correction comment already named nanogpt/openrouter/zai as sharing the pattern. This issue covers the eight remaining providers so the fix lands as one consistent sweep; if triage prefers, fold this into #1747 and close this as its sibling tracker — but do not fix Mistral alone and call the pattern done.

## Why it matters

Auth entries with an empty first field are realistic (a key cleared in one tool, an OAuth entry with `access` unset but a refresh `token` present). The quota board then shows a provider as configured while every fetch reports "Not configured" (or fails auth on a blank bearer), and the disagreement between the two selectors makes the failure invisible to anyone debugging from `isConfigured`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the eight providers above selects its credential through a single shared helper (the `getApiKey`/`asNonEmptyString` pattern used by kimi/hyper/kilo/cline-pass/command-code), used by both `isConfigured` and every `fetchQuota` path (including zai :150 and copilot :182).
- [ ] Regression tests per provider (or one parametrized suite): `key: ""` + valid `token` → `isConfigured` true AND `fetchQuota` fetches with the token; `key: " "` + valid `token` → the token is used, never `Bearer `; both fields empty/whitespace → not configured in both.
- [ ] No behavior change when the first field holds a real value.

title: fix(web): session-folders PATCH guard measures compact JSON but writeSnapshot persists pretty — a writer-producible snapshot exceeds the 8 MiB bounded read cap and wedges the store (#1626)

body:
## Finding

PR #1626 gave the session-folders store a bounded read at `MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES = 2 * MAX_BODY_BYTES` (8 MiB), on the stated invariant that a stored file must stay readable for everything the writer could legitimately have written. The 2x headroom does not hold for the PATCH write path: the PATCH size check measures the **compact** serialization, while `writeSnapshot` persists the **pretty-printed** serialization, and for this snapshot shape pretty can be ~3.75x compact — so the writer can produce a stored file the new reader refuses, after which the store is permanently stuck: GET answers 500 "malformed" and every later PATCH is refused on top of the unreadable file.

## Evidence

- PR #1626 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1626), MERGED, merge 8cd11be40df4, for #1623.
- Current main 8f61a0fd3f9849606a6d976b824431f2bd82ce36 (verified twice):
  - `packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/routes.js:18` — `MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES = 2 * MAX_BODY_BYTES`.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/routes.js:195` — `writeSnapshot` writes `JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2)` (pretty).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/routes.js:299` — the PATCH guard is `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(snapshot), 'utf8') > MAX_BODY_BYTES` (compact, no indent argument).
  - (The POST guard at :256 does measure the pretty form; the PR's comment says the check measures "the compact form the POST check measures", which is only true of the PATCH path — and that is exactly the path that defeats the cap.)
  - `folder-changes.js`: an `assign` change carries up to 10,000 session ids (ids min length 1); `hasValidFolderSnapshot` imposes no total count/length bound, so repeated PATCHes accumulate short ids in one folder's `sessionIds` until the compact check is the only gate.
- Probe (verbatim `JSON.stringify` shapes, run on the laptop, Node v24): a snapshot of one folder holding short session ids —
  - 1-char ids, n=1,000,000: compact 4,000,128 bytes (≤ 4 MiB, passes the PATCH guard), pretty 15,000,222 bytes (ratio 3.75) — over the 8 MiB read cap.
  - 2-char ids, n=800,000: compact 4,000,128 bytes, pretty 12,800,222 bytes (ratio 3.20) — also over.
  Per-element arithmetic matches: a session-id element at nesting depth 5 costs ~4 bytes compact (`"a",`) vs ~15 bytes pretty (newline + 10-space indent + `"a",`).
- Consequence on main: after such a write, `readCurrent` maps the bounded reader's `too-large` answer to `null` (malformed) — GET /api/session-folders returns 500 and PATCH refuses further changes ("Stored session folders are malformed"), with no in-band recovery short of the whole-copy POST repair or hand-editing the file.

## Why it matters

This is the exact failure #1626 set out to eliminate — a writer-producible file that the reader refuses — one serialization step later. Session folders are user data; a store that wedges at 500 with its own writes locked out is a data-availability bug, not a cosmetic cap mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A snapshot that passes every write-path size check is always readable back: add a regression test that builds a session-id-heavy snapshot just under the write cap (short ids, deep arrays), writes it through the real write path, and reads it back via GET/PATCH successfully — or the write is refused at write time with 413.
- [ ] The size invariant is stated in one place: either the PATCH guard measures the exact bytes `writeSnapshot` persists (pretty form), or the read cap is derived from a proven pretty/compact bound for this shape, with the arithmetic corrected in the `MAX_STORED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` comment (which currently misdescribes the POST check as compact).
- [ ] Existing bounded-read tests (over-cap refusal, FIFO refusal, at-cap read) stay green.

body:
## Problem

The server deliberately flags a check run whose annotations could not be read completely — but no UI type declares the flag, the API mapper drops it, and no surface renders it. A failed run whose annotations read failed (or hit the safety cap) is shown with no annotations and no indication that annotations are missing, exactly the silent-incompleteness #1420 set out to eliminate on the server side.

This is the #1732 pattern (a server completeness signal that cannot reach the UI) on the checks surface: #1732 covered `teamsMore` on `LinearMappingResult`; this is `annotationsTruncated` on the GitHub check-run path.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `8f61a0fd3f9849606a6d976b824431f2bd82ce36`, laptop primary, read twice)

- `packages/web/server/lib/github/routes.js:3299-3303` — the deliberate choice (#1420): an annotations read that fails or crosses the safety cap is caught per check run "so the checks summary still renders, but the partial list is never returned as complete — the run is flagged with `annotationsTruncated` instead."
- `packages/web/server/lib/github/routes.js:3381` — the flag is emitted: `...(truncatedAnnotations.has(Number(run.id)) ? { annotationsTruncated: true } : {})`. On that path no `annotations` are attached at all (the `parsedAnnotations.set` at :3312-3313 only runs on success), and `packages/web/server/lib/github/collections.js:97` `readCheckRunAnnotations` propagates page errors / cap overflows instead of returning partial pages.
- `packages/web/server/lib/github/routes.auth.test.js` — server tests pin the flag both ways (absent on success, `true` on failure/cap).
- `packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts:1525` — `GitHubCheckRun` declares `annotations?` (:1558) but no `annotationsTruncated`; a repo-wide grep for `annotationsTruncated` over `packages/ui/src`, `packages/web/src` and `packages/vscode/src` returns 0 hits.
- `packages/web/src/api/source-control.ts:748` `validateGitHubCheckRun` never checks the flag, and `:775` `mapCheckRun` maps `annotations` into the `CIRun` but has no flag to carry; `packages/ui/src/lib/source-control/types.ts:398` `CIRun` declares `annotations?: CIAnnotation[]` (:417) and likewise no truncation field.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/git/CheckRunList.tsx:20,48` — details render the annotations section only when `annotations.length > 0`, and `hasDetails` (:141-143) counts annotations by length only: a truncated run with no other output/steps renders as a failed row that cannot even be expanded, indistinguishable from a failed run that genuinely produced no annotations.
- `packages/ui/src/components/sourceBoard/pullAttachments.ts:15-32` — `failedRunText` (the text pinned to the composer when a user asks an agent to fix failed checks) includes an `annotations:` block only when annotations exist; the truncation state is never mentioned, so the agent is also told, by omission, that there were no annotations.

Dedup: title/keyword search over open and closed issues for `annotationsTruncated` returns only #1420 (CLOSED — the server-side fix that introduced the flag) and #1528 (OPEN design — the collection-completeness contract this flag belongs to). No issue covers the UI declaration/mapping/rendering remainder. Nearest sibling: #1732 (OPEN, Linear `teamsMore`, different field and surface).

## Why it matters

Annotations are where CI explains a failure (lint findings, test failure locations). When their read fails or exceeds the cap, the server knows and says so — and every consumer then throws that knowledge away. The user sees a bare failed check with no explanation and no hint that an explanation exists on GitHub; the "fix my failed checks" agent attachment inherits the same blind spot. The flag exists precisely so a partial view is never presented as complete; today it is presented as complete (empty) anyway.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `annotationsTruncated?: boolean` is declared on `GitHubCheckRun` (`packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts`) and on `CIRun` (`packages/ui/src/lib/source-control/types.ts`).
- [ ] `mapCheckRun` in `packages/web/src/api/source-control.ts` carries the flag through (and `validateGitHubCheckRun` rejects a non-boolean value when present), so both the PR panel and the board checks dialog receive it.
- [ ] `CheckRunList` surfaces the state: a truncated run shows an explicit "annotations could not be loaded completely" notice (new i18n string alongside `gitView.pr.checks.failedAnnotations*`), and the flag alone makes the run expandable (`hasDetails`).
- [ ] `failedRunText` in `pullAttachments.ts` notes the truncation when the flag is set, so pinned agent context does not imply a complete annotation list.
- [ ] Tests pin the chain: a mapper test that a flagged server run arrives as a flagged `CIRun`, and a `CheckRunList` render test for the notice; existing github routes / source-control / CheckRunList tests keep passing.

body:
# fix(ui): GitHub Copilot Add-on quota provider is never shown on the quota board — implemented by both backends and typed in the UI, but missing from QUOTA_PROVIDERS, and its fetcher duplicates the primary Copilot fetch exactly

## Finding

The server registry carries a distinct quota provider `github-copilot-addon` ("GitHub Copilot Add-on") with its own fetcher, and the VS Code twin implements it too — but the shared UI catalog `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` omits it, so no quota surface can ever select or display the add-on row. It is the one remaining server↔UI catalog disagreement besides Mistral (#1735). Worse, the add-on fetcher is an exact duplicate of the primary Copilot fetcher today: same endpoint, same credential, same window builder — pinned identical by the provider's own tests — so the current state is incoherent either way: a named provider that cannot be shown, whose data adds nothing over the primary row. Triage should pick one disposition (register it, or retire the duplicate) instead of leaving the dead row in both backends.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `8f61a0fd3`, laptop primary)

- Server: `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/copilot.js:176-179` — `providerIdAddon = 'github-copilot-addon'`, `providerNameAddon = 'GitHub Copilot Add-on'`, `fetchQuotaAddon` (its own result rows at :186-232). Registered as a distinct provider in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/index.js:212-221` (governed by `disabledBy: ['github-copilot']`), so `GET /api/quota/github-copilot-addon` and the configured-providers list both serve it.
- VS Code twin: `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:2121` `fetchCopilotAddonQuota`, dispatched at `:4764` (`case 'github-copilot-addon'`); its configured-set logic adds the id at `:1025`.
- UI type: `packages/ui/src/types/quota.ts:9` — `'github-copilot-addon'` IS in the `QuotaProviderId` union (unlike Mistral in #1735, the type side was registered).
- UI catalog: `packages/ui/src/lib/quota/providers/index.ts:8-39` — `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` lists 28 providers ending at `xai`; `github-copilot-addon` is absent. Every board surface iterates this catalog and nothing else: `UsageSidebar.tsx:96` maps it, `components/usage/usageGroups.ts:43` filters groups by it, `stores/useQuotaStore.ts:71` derives `allProviderIds` from it and `parseSettings` (`:74-76`) silently drops any saved dropdown selection not in it — so even a hand-saved `usageDropdownProviders: ['github-copilot-addon']` setting is discarded on load.
- Dedup: title/keyword search over open and recently closed issues for "copilot-addon" / "Copilot Add-on" finds no issue covering this; #1735 covers Mistral only (and its claim that every other server provider is in the UI catalog does not hold for the add-on).

### Probe (laptop, real modules, run twice with identical output)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-copilot-addon-20261106/probe.mjs` diffs the real server registry against the real UI catalog and type union, then calls the real `fetchQuota` / `fetchQuotaAddon` from `copilot.js` with an injected credential read and a stubbed upstream:

```
server-not-in-UI-catalog: mistral,github-copilot-addon
server-not-in-type-union: mistral
addon in type union: true | addon in UI catalog: false
primary: github-copilot {"premium_interactions":{"usedPercent":34.87,…,"valueLabel":"20,922 / 60,000 used"}}
addon:   github-copilot-addon {"premium_interactions":{"usedPercent":34.87,…,"valueLabel":"20,922 / 60,000 used"}}
upstream calls for the two rows: 2 | distinct urls: https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user
windows identical: true
```

The identical-output behavior is also pinned by `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/copilot.test.js`, which runs its whole matrix as `it.each([primary, add-on])` against the same payload.

## Why it matters

Two backends spend a real credentialed GitHub API call per add-on fetch for a result no UI can render, and the catalog disagreement is exactly the drift class #1735 asks to pin with a test — the add-on is the second live instance of it. If the add-on row is meant to exist (it has a distinct user-facing name and a distinct provider id in the type union), users on Copilot plans with add-on premium-interaction pools cannot see that pool; if it is not meant to exist, the duplicate fetcher, registry row and VS Code case are dead weight that will keep confusing every future catalog audit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One disposition is chosen and implemented: either (a) `github-copilot-addon` is added to `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` in `packages/ui/src/lib/quota/providers/index.ts` (name "GitHub Copilot Add-on", matching the server's `providerNameAddon`) and the board can fetch, select and render its result, or (b) the add-on provider is retired from the server registry, `copilot.js`, the VS Code twin and the `QuotaProviderId` union, with the removal noted as deliberate.
- [ ] If (a): the add-on row's relationship to the primary Copilot row is explicit in the UI (the two currently return identical windows from the same endpoint — showing two identical rows without distinction does not satisfy this).
- [ ] A catalog-agreement test pins the server provider list against the UI catalog/type (shared with #1735's third criterion — whichever issue lands second reuses the other's test rather than adding a second one), with any deliberate exclusions named in the test.
- [ ] Existing quota tests keep passing (`copilot.test.js`, `search`/quota UI tests, VS Code quota tests).

Found by: new-issue-creator-openchamber run 2026-11-06 17:50 CST. Cross-link: #1735 (Mistral, the other catalog omission).
