body:
## Summary

The routing store — the web server's store for the model-routing configuration — reads all five of its JSON files whole with no size gate and no non-regular-file protection, through two private helpers. It is the residual class fixed for the project config (#1490), the session-goal objective (#1582), the walkthrough pointer files (#1482), the project-icon serve path (#1537), and most recently agent-memory + project-context (#1607), in a store none of those fixes touched:

- `packages/web/server/lib/routing/store.js` — `readJsonFile` (:147) does `raw = await fs.readFile(file, 'utf8')` (:150) and `JSON.parse`s whatever comes back. It serves `routing.json` (`readConfig`, :323), `routing-auth.json` — the file holding the Jev API key alone, mode 0600 (`readToken`, :330), `classification.json` (`readClassifierSource`, :347) and `classifier-endpoint.json` — which can also hold a key (`readCustomEndpoint`, :357).
- Its synchronous twin `readJsonFileSync` (:171) does `raw = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')` (:174) for `auto-sessions.json` (`readAutoSessions`, :376). That read runs when the routing runtime is constructed (`lib/routing/runtime.js:176`, `store.readAutoSessions()` in the `createRoutingRuntime` initializer) — i.e. at server startup, before requests are served, and it is synchronous: a blocked or oversized read there does not hang one request, it freezes/startup-blocks the whole server on the event loop's only thread.

Neither helper uses the house standard that already exists for exactly this: `readBoundedFile` in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` — open once with `O_NONBLOCK`, judge from the opened handle, refuse non-regular files, buffer at most cap + 1 byte. The routing store was also not one of the fifteen stores migrated to the durable-store primitive in #978, and #892 fixed its write atomicity, not its reads.

## Why the caps are safe (write-side clamps)

Everything this store writes is tightly clamped by its own schemas, so a generous read cap per file loses nothing legitimate:

- `routing.json`: the effective config caps categories at 32 (`effectiveConfigSchema`, :107 `.max(32)`); each category carries name ≤ 60 chars, description ≤ 2,000 chars, model ids ≤ 200 + 200 chars, variant/agent ≤ 80 chars (`fileSchema` :75, record :83). A legitimate file is ≲ 90 KB.
- `routing-auth.json`: `{ token }` with token ≤ 4,000 chars (`authSchema`, :110) — ≲ 4.1 KB.
- `classification.json`: a version literal plus one enum source (`classifierSchema`, :112) — a few dozen bytes.
- `classifier-endpoint.json`: url ≤ 2,000 chars, model ≤ 200 chars, key ≤ 4,000 chars (`customEndpointSchema`, :123) — ≲ 6.3 KB.
- `auto-sessions.json`: sessions are capped at 1,000 by the runtime (`AUTO_SESSION_LIMIT = 1000`, `runtime.js:38`; read back with `.slice(-AUTO_SESSION_LIMIT)` at :176 and evicted to the limit at :478); each entry is sessionId ≤ 200 chars, directory ≤ 4,000 chars, one number (`autoSessionsFileSchema`, :132) — ≲ 4.3 MB at the pathological worst, ~0.3 MB for realistic directory paths.

## Verified this run (code-verified on origin/main 41c124c7c, read ×2 via `gh api` raw reads)

- Both helpers and all five call sites re-read independently twice on main `41c124c7ca7c82fbca59d866c43cb76961bfcba8`; the line numbers above are from the second read. There is no byte cap, no `stat`/`isFile` judgement, and no use of `readBoundedFile` or the durable-store primitive anywhere in `store.js` (full-file grep of the raw file: the only reads are :150 and :174).
- The store's own test suite (`routing/store.test.js`, 192 lines) contains no oversized-file, FIFO, or non-regular-file case (grep: no `MAX`/`oversize`/`fifo`/`bounded` case).
- `fs.readFile` / `readFileSync` on a FIFO with no writer blocks in `open()` before any judgement can run — the identical ungated pattern was probe-confirmed on the laptop for #1607 (FIFO never settled within 3,000 ms; 33 MB files buffered whole). A runtime probe of this store was **not** run this run: the laptop SSH tunnel was down for the entire run (repeated `laptop-agent: HTTP 502 … proxy closed during CONNECT` from `~/tools/laptop-ssh.sh`, plus the real-SSH fallback failing), and probes are never run on the sandbox. The defect is fully determined by the code above; a triage probe against `createRoutingStore` with an oversized file and a FIFO is a reasonable first confirmation step.

## Why it matters

These files sit in the user's data directory, which other tools, sync jobs and agents also write, and two of them hold API keys. One oversized or non-regular file at any of the five paths either buffers unboundedly on a routing read or — for `auto-sessions.json` — blocks server startup synchronously and indefinitely, with no error and no recovery path short of finding and removing the file by hand. The schema validators only run *after* the whole file is in memory, so they bound what is kept, not what is read. The malformed semantics are deliberately strict today (a broken `routing.json` throws rather than silently resetting the user's categories, per the module header) and must stay that way: an over-cap file must follow the malformed path, never read as empty/defaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `readJsonFile` and `readJsonFileSync` in `lib/routing/store.js` read through a bounded, handle-judged read (`readBoundedFile` / its sync spelling in `lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, or equivalent): at most cap + 1 byte is ever buffered, and a FIFO / directory / other non-regular file at any of the five paths is refused promptly instead of blocking the read — including the synchronous startup read.
- [ ] Each file's cap is documented in code with its headroom over the computed legitimate maximum from the write-side clamps above, the way the sibling fixes document theirs.
- [ ] Existing read semantics are preserved exactly per file: missing file still reads as today (defaults / null / no sessions); a malformed or over-cap `routing.json` still throws (never silently resets to defaults); the token / classifier / endpoint readers keep their current warn-and-null behaviour on unreadable files; `readAutoSessions` keeps its warn-and-[] behaviour — an over-cap file must never silently read as a valid empty state anywhere it does not already.
- [ ] Regression tests in `routing/store.test.js` (or the routing suites): oversized file refused without being parsed whole, FIFO/non-regular target refused without hanging (async and sync readers), at-cap and ordinary files read unchanged.
- [ ] No other store changes behaviour; the write paths, schemas and atomic writes (#892) are untouched.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `auto-sessions`, `readJsonFile`, `routing store`, `classifier-endpoint` and the open-issue list: #892 (closed) covers routing stores' non-atomic writes and corrupt-read discards — a different defect; #978 (closed) migrated fifteen *other* stores to the durable-store primitive; #1607 covers agent-memory + project-context, #1490 the project config, #1582 the session-goal objective, #1482 the walkthrough pointers. The routing store's reads are covered nowhere.

body:
Found by the #1530 phase-2 inventory (design #1528). Surface: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/issues.js`, issue-summary labels connection.

## The read

`ISSUE_SUMMARY_FIELDS` (:94) requests `labels { nodes { id name color } }` — no `first:` bound, no `pageInfo`, no count. Linear serves connections at its default page size, so an issue with more labels than the default page returns a prefix, and `readLabels` (:291) maps whatever nodes arrived into the summary's label list, which consumers present as the issue's labels. There is no truncation signal anywhere in the result.

Every other connection in this file carries its signal: list/search paginate by cursor with `hasMore`, children carry `pageInfo` into `subIssueProgress.more`, comments into `commentsMore`, states into `statesMore`. Labels are the exception.

## What done looks like

- The labels connection requests an explicit `first:` plus `pageInfo { hasNextPage }`, and the summary carries the truncation (a `labelsMore` flag in the established `*More` shape), or the read enumerates to exhaustion under a named cap.
- A test pins an over-page label set reading as incomplete, not whole.

## Acceptance criteria

- The labels connection in `ISSUE_SUMMARY_FIELDS` requests an explicit `first:` plus `pageInfo { hasNextPage }`, and the summary carries the truncation (a `labelsMore` flag in the established `*More` shape) — or the read enumerates to exhaustion under a named cap.
- A test pins an over-page label set reading as incomplete, not whole.

## The reads

`listProjectMRs` (:233) hard-codes `maxPages: 1`. Two call-site families consume the single page as the whole set without consulting `readPage`'s `hasMore`:

- `reconcileCreateMutation` (:796) — matches filtered from the page; exactly one → `succeeded`, otherwise `outcome-unknown`. A second match past page 1 is invisible, so a prefix can reach the affirmative verdict.

Dispositioned neighbours, for contrast: `listChangeRequests` (:960) and `listIssues` (:1063) wrap the same helper in `readPage` and return `hasMore` (signals), and `readCollection` (:49) exhausts under the cap and throws past it.

- Branch-status and create-reconciliation reads either go through `readCollection`-style exhaustion, or check `hasMore` and degrade explicitly (status: not authoritative; reconcile: `outcome-unknown`) when the page is a prefix.
- Tests pin the over-page case for at least the branch-status lookup.

## Acceptance criteria

body:
## Finding

No workflow in this repo ever evaluates this repo's own flake, so a flake that fails to evaluate at all can merge and sit on main until an external system trips over it. That already happened: PR #1386 broke every flake output on main, and the breakage was caught by a run in a different repo (dezren39/fleet), not by any check here.

## Evidence

- PR #1386 (commit `c9c959f193`, merged 2026-11-03) added the `fleet` input to `flake.nix` but left the outputs formals as `{ self, nixpkgs, opencode, }` with no `...`. Nix passes every input to `outputs`, so evaluating any output failed. `nix flake lock` never calls `outputs`, which is why the PR's lock regeneration passed.
- The breakage surfaced as #1387 via the fleet-build warm-export in dezren39/fleet (run 41555313761), with the misleading error `does not provide attribute 'devShells.x86_64-linux.fleet'` — the attribute existed; the outputs call itself was failing. Hotfix PR #1389 (commit `5d9b4e61c4`) added the `...`. Verified on current main `794e5f5c260ee4de1d8d9c4a29b330b009fde5aa`: `flake.nix` outputs formals now include `...`.
- The guards that look like they cover this do not run here:
  - `.github/workflows/nix-eval.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only and its `eval` job is gated `if: github.repository == 'openchamber/openchamber'`, so a dispatch in this repo validates nothing. Its eval targets are also upstream-shaped (`nix eval .#opencode-cli.drvPath`, `.#openchamber.bunDeps.drvPath`, `.#opencode-cli.node_modules.drvPath`); this flake's `packages` provide `openchamber`, `openchamber-desktop` and `default` only.
  - `.github/workflows/nix-hashes.yml` carries the same upstream gate on its job.
  - `.github/ci-policy.md` (lines 82–87) documents the skip: the eval job "is skipped outright … so a dispatch here validates nothing until the flakes are reconciled."
- Dedupe (2026-11-04): issue searches for `nix-eval` and for a flake-evaluation gate returned #971, #493, #87 and the closed #1387 — #1387 fixed only the formals line; no open or closed issue covers an evaluation check for this repo's own flake outputs.

## Why it matters

This flake is load-bearing for the fleet: it carries the shared nixpkgs pin (via `fleet`), the fleet binary-cache config, the lean `devShells.fleet` shell the build container uses, and the mcpx/opencode/openchamber module cascade. A total evaluation failure on main breaks every consumer at once, and the current detection path is "some other repo's scheduled job notices." A cheap evaluation check in this repo's own main tier would have caught #1386 in minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A check that runs automatically for this repo (main-tier `pr checks` on push to main, or a paths-gated workflow on `flake.nix`/`flake.lock` changes) evaluates this flake's own outputs without building them — e.g. `nix flake show` or `nix eval` of the `packages`/`devShells` derivation paths for one system.
- [ ] The check fails on the pre-#1389 flake (outputs formals without `...`) and passes on current main — red/green shown on the implementing PR.
- [ ] `.github/ci-policy.md`'s tier map is updated to describe the new check (and no longer claim evaluation validates nothing here, if the new check supersedes that note).

## Finding

PR #216 adds per-project visibility flags — `hiddenFromWork` ("Show in In work") and `hiddenFromAllSessions` ("Show in All sessions") in Settings > Projects > General — and wires them into the desktop sidebar: the In work zone, the List view's All sessions, and the List view sorted by time (load-status line included). The PR body states the remaining surfaces do not follow the checkboxes yet:

> "The Tree view and the phone sessions sheet do not follow the checkboxes yet."

No issue tracks that follow-up (searched open and closed issues for `hiddenFromWork`, "Tree view hidden project", and "sessions sheet" on 2026-10-21; the only phone-sheet issue, #18, is about sidebar layout generally and predates these flags).

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/216 (OPEN at filing; head `05955019c`)
- Flags defined on the project entry: `packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts:1368,1370` (PR branch); parsed in `packages/ui/src/lib/settings/parsers.ts:345-346`; checkboxes in `packages/ui/src/components/sections/projects/ProjectGeneralTab.tsx:116-123`.
- The only consumers are the desktop sidebar paths: `packages/ui/src/components/session/sidebar/list/SessionProjectCollection.tsx:212-223` (In work / All sessions sets) and `packages/ui/src/components/session/sidebar/sessionSidebarRowModel.ts` (List view; `hiddenFromAllProjectIds` skips the project and its load line). A `git grep hiddenFrom` on the PR branch finds no consumer in the Tree view or in any phone/mobile sessions sheet component.
- The PR's own sidebar documentation (`packages/ui/src/components/session/sidebar/DOCUMENTATION.md:324`) records the same gap: "The Tree view does not read `hiddenFromAllSessions`".

## Why it matters

The feature exists so a user can keep a side project out of their working lists. On the phone — a primary surface for this app — a "hidden" project's sessions still appear in the sessions sheet, so the setting silently does not do what its label says on that surface. In the Tree view the project itself staying visible is by design (it is how you get back to it), but its sessions ignoring the flags is an inconsistency a user cannot explain from the UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The phone sessions sheet honours `hiddenFromWork` and `hiddenFromAllSessions` the same way the desktop List view does (sessions of a hidden project leave the corresponding list; nothing is deleted or archived).
- [ ] Tree view behaviour is decided and implemented consistently: either its sessions follow `hiddenFromAllSessions`, or the Projects settings copy / sidebar documentation explicitly says the Tree view always shows everything.
- [ ] Tests cover the phone sheet filtering for both flags, matching the existing desktop sidebar tests.

body:
## Summary

The `packages/ui` test suites only pass when every file runs in its own process. A single combined `bun test` invocation over the same files produces dozens of phantom failures in files that are green individually. The repo works around this with `scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs` (one process per file), but the underlying cross-file state leakage is unfixed and untracked — anyone who runs the natural `bun test <dir>` command (or an IDE test runner, or a future CI change that batches files) gets a wall of false failures and no signal about which are real.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-18 on main `e409366de`)

Combined run:

```
cd packages/ui
bun test src/components/session/sidebar src/lib/i18n src/hooks
# 466 pass / 65 fail / 1 error — 531 tests across 105 files
```

The same files pass in isolation:

- `bun test src/components/session/sidebar/projects/useProjectRepoStatus.test.tsx` → 4 pass / 0 fail
- `bun test src/components/session/sidebar/projects/useSessionGrouping.test.tsx` → 6 pass / 0 fail
- `bun test src/components/session/sidebar/sessions/sessionSubtreeActions.test.ts` → 16 pass / 0 fail
- Even the first two combined together pass (10/10), so the failure needs a larger set / specific load order — consistent with shared-singleton leakage rather than individual test bugs.

Failure signatures in the combined run point at module-level state shared across files, e.g.:

- `useGitComparison.test.tsx:67` — expected 1 recorded request, received 2 (a request issued by another file's test is counted).
- `useRoutingSync.test.tsx:153` — routing store state observed mid-test does not match what that file set up (store contents from a neighbouring file).
- Sidebar suites (`useProjectRepoStatus`, `useSessionGrouping`, `runSessionSubtreeAction`/`collectSessionSubtreeIds`, session-row menu state, `SidebarHeader`) fail in the combined run while passing alone.

This matches the header comment in `scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs`, which documents the arrangement: the shared UI suites "keep module-level singletons (runtime endpoint, relay tunnel, stores, registries)" and "executed in one process they leak state into each other and fail by load order". A 2026-10-17 sweep run independently observed the same effect (~30 failures in one combined invocation over the sidebar/shortcuts/i18n/hooks files, all passing individually).

## Why it matters

- The per-file-process runner is slow and unusual; contributors who run `bun test` the standard way see 65 failures on a clean checkout of main and cannot tell real regressions from pollution.
- Load-order-dependent failures erode trust in the suite: a real regression inside a polluted area can hide among the phantom failures.
- The workaround is load-bearing but invisible: nothing in the contributor docs warns that combined runs are expected to fail.

## Suggested direction

Pick one (or both, in order):

1. **Root-cause the worst polluters.** Identify the shared singletons/stores that leak (runtime endpoint, routing store, session stores/registries are the prime suspects from the failure signatures) and reset them between files — e.g. a shared test setup that reinitializes the singleton stores, or moving the leaked state behind per-test factories. Shrink the combined-run failure count to zero for at least the `sidebar` + `hooks` + `i18n` subtree as a first milestone.
2. **Until (1) lands, make the failure mode honest.** Document in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (and the UI package README, if any) that UI tests must be run via `bun run test` / `run-isolated-tests.mjs`, and that a bare `bun test <dir>` is expected to fail from cross-file leakage — so a clean checkout doesn't look broken.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test src/components/session/sidebar src/lib/i18n src/hooks` in `packages/ui` on main finishes with 0 failures attributable to cross-file leakage (any remaining failure also fails in isolation), OR the interim documentation in (2) is in place and this issue is rescoped to the remaining polluters by name.
- [ ] The per-file isolated runner (`bun run test` in `packages/ui`) stays green either way.
- [ ] The polluting shared state is named in the issue/PR (which singleton/store, which files it leaked between), not just worked around with more process isolation.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/web/server/lib/git/routes.js:137-145` implements `resolveDirectoryQuery()` by selecting `value[0]` when Express supplies repeated query parameters as an array. Multiple routes use it for `req.query.directory`, including `/api/git/status` at `:801` (also occurrences around `:544`, `:1048`, `:1069`, `:1827`, and `:1938`). Therefore `?directory=A&directory=B` is silently treated as `directory=A`; the server neither rejects the ambiguous request nor makes the selection explicit.

## Why it matters

Clients that accidentally serialize duplicate parameters can inspect or operate on a different repository than the caller intended. Silently accepting only one value makes this input-shape error difficult to diagnose and can cause misleading Git UI/results.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Treat an array-valued `directory` query as invalid instead of taking its first element (return a consistent 400 response).
- Add route/helper tests for a single value, missing/empty value, and repeated values.
- Confirm all routes using `resolveDirectoryQuery()` reject duplicate `directory` parameters consistently.

body:
## Finding

The durable scheduled-task run history added by PR #2082 (`packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js`) has **no bound of any kind**:

- Every terminal run event appends a row to `scheduled-task-run-history.jsonl` forever — no rotation, cap, or retention window anywhere in the module or its DOCUMENTATION.md section.
- At store creation the whole file is read synchronously (`fs.readFileSync`) and every valid row is kept in the in-memory `rows` array for the life of the process; `listRuns` limits only what a query returns, not what is stored or loaded.

Verified this run against current main (`8d6bd5c68690df38bb5df8a42f189e95a96bc52d`) by reading the merged module end to end: the only limits present are `DEFAULT_LIMIT`/`MAX_LIMIT` on query results.

## Why it matters

This repo's other durable stores are explicitly bounded for exactly this failure mode (tracked-items: 8 MiB bounded reader; plan-notes whole-file read was filed and fixed as #1638). An append-only, ever-growing JSONL that is fully buffered at startup means startup cost and memory grow with total historical runs, unbounded — slowly, but monotonically, and the fix gets harder once the file is large in the field.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented bound exists for the run-history store (retention window, row cap, size cap with rotation, or an explicitly reasoned exception recorded in `scheduled-tasks/DOCUMENTATION.md`)
- [ ] Startup load does not buffer an arbitrarily large history file whole (bounded/streamed read, consistent with the house bounded-reader pattern), or the bound above makes the whole-file read provably small
- [ ] Existing `run-history.test.js` behaviour (exactly-one-row, dedupe, malformed-line tolerance) still passes, with a new test pinning the bound

Found by: pr-diff-review job, PR #2082 review (merge commit `e3d45067fae1`).

body:
## Evidence (origin/main 8d6bd5c68690df38bb5df8a42f189e95a96bc52d)

- `packages/ui/src/lib/pwa-clamps.ts:13-19` normalizes a recent-session title then uses `normalized.slice(0, 48)`. Its guard only backs off a trailing high surrogate.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/pwa-manifest-routes.js:9-13,55-57,179-182` uses the same pair-only guard for a 48-code-unit shortcut `name` and a 32-code-unit `short_name`.

These cuts can still land inside an extended grapheme cluster. For example, `"a".repeat(47) + "e\\u0301"` is truncated to 47 `a`s plus `e`, dropping the combining acute accent. `"a".repeat(45) + "👩‍👩‍👧‍👦"` is cut after `👩‍`, leaving an incomplete joined emoji. I reproduced both against the current UI/server clamp behavior in Node; the resulting code points end respectively at `U+0065` (without the combining mark) and `U+1F469 U+200D`.

## Why it matters

Recent-session shortcuts are user-visible manifest labels. The current pair-safe clamp prevents malformed UTF-16, but titles in languages using combining marks can lose their accent and joined emoji can render as a partial sequence at the length boundary.

## Related work and deduplication

Closed #2023 and merged #2035/#2036 fixed surrogate-pair splitting in PWA manifest clamps; merged #2112 tests those pair-safe boundaries. Those changes and tests do not preserve complete grapheme clusters. All-state issue/PR searches for `grapheme`, `grapheme cluster`, and `combining mark` found no tracked PWA grapheme-boundary fix. This request is for the distinct combining-mark/ZWJ boundary behavior, not another surrogate-pair guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- Truncate UI and server PWA shortcut labels only between extended grapheme clusters while keeping the existing UTF-16 length limits (48 for shortcut `name`, 32 for `short_name`).
- Add boundary tests at the UI and server paths for a combining-mark sequence and a joined emoji, asserting that no grapheme is split and the existing length limits remain satisfied.
- Keep the existing surrogate-pair regression coverage passing.

Two UI pair-safe clamps merged in the surrogate-pair batch have no test pinning them, unlike every sibling clamp in the same batch. Both helpers are file-local copies of a subtle guard, so a future refactor back to a plain `slice` would silently reintroduce lone-surrogate values with no failing test.

## Evidence

- PR #2027 (merged, merge commit e7f1ff4c602b6132761ab84946c684d05c87543d, commit 2433472290) — "fix(web,ui): keep PWA app-name clamps off surrogate pairs (#2021)": added `clipPwaInstallName` in `packages/ui/src/components/sections/openchamber/OpenChamberVisualSettings.tsx` (on current main 6e7afad1e5d97c3457b997defea0758a09b550f3 at :90, call sites :366 and :420) and the server twin in `settings-helpers.js`. The PR's only test change pins the server side (`settings-helpers.test.js`). Verified on main: `clipPwaInstallName` occurs only in that .tsx file, and `OpenChamberVisualSettings.test.tsx` contains only two render tests for unrelated sections — no PWA app-name or surrogate test.
- PR #2035 (merged, merge commit 7e4272931f0c352a7a43f58fc2683dfb7600cbcd, commit 26b87e4469) — "fix(web): make PWA manifest name clamps pair-safe" (#2023): added the pair-safe cap to `normalizeRecentTitle` in `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePwaManifestSync.ts` (main :18-33). The PR's only test change pins the server route (`pwa-manifest-routes.test.js`). Verified on main: `normalizeRecentTitle` occurs only in that hook file; no test file references it. Its output is persisted to localStorage as the recent-shortcuts signature and drives manifest rebuilds.
- Contrast, same batch: the other UI twins were pinned — #2030 (`tools.test.ts` for `pageTitleFromHtml`), #2036 (`pwa-manifest-bootstrap.test.js`, pins the client clamps at 64/48/32/30), #2038 (`gitlabReferences.test.ts`).
- Dedupe: issue/code searches 2026-11-11 for `clipPwaInstallName`, `normalizeRecentTitle`, and "untested UI twin" returned only the origin issues #2021/#2023/#2031 (all CLOSED — they requested the fixes, not test coverage). The fleet has treated a missing pair-safe regression test as file-worthy before (#2080, docker-tools fill-failure tail).

## Why it matters

These clamps protect values that are persisted or handed to the server (the applied PWA app name; recent-session titles stored in localStorage). The guard is a three-line idiom that is easy to lose in a cleanup refactor, and without a pin the regression is invisible until a title or app name renders as U+FFFD again.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test pins `clipPwaInstallName`: an astral character straddling offset 64 drops its high half (result encodes with no U+FFFD), and an over-cap ASCII name still cuts at exactly 64.
- A test pins `normalizeRecentTitle`: the same oracle at offset 48, with the ASCII control cutting at exactly 48.
- Exporting either helper for test, following the `tools.ts` / bootstrap test patterns, is acceptable; production behavior is unchanged.

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Evidence

`createBrowserControlBroker().request()` dispatches via `emitRequest()` before checking whether the caller's `AbortSignal` is already aborted (`packages/web/server/lib/browser-control/broker.js:73-81, 106-109`). The production emitter publishes the request to connected OpenChamber clients over SSE (`packages/web/server/index.js:235-260`), so a cancelled call can still cause a browser action after the caller has abandoned it.

Reproduction on current `origin/main` (`75e6bbe72b2767917e8e31493cba00a261ccae03`): create an `AbortController`, abort it before calling `broker.request('browser.click', ..., { signal })`, and use an `emitRequest` stub that increments a counter and returns `1`. The call rejects with status `499` but the counter is `1` (`pendingCount` is `0`). The existing test `rejects immediately when the caller is already cancelled` checks the rejection but not that no request was emitted. The focused broker suite currently passes 17/17.

## Impact

A browser client may execute a click, navigation, or other requested action even though the caller had already cancelled the operation. This violates cancellation semantics and can leave browser state changed without a live caller awaiting the result.

## Acceptance criteria

- Check a pre-aborted signal before dispatching through `emitRequest`; retain the existing cancelled (`499`) rejection.
- Extend the existing pre-cancelled test to assert that the emitter is not called and no pending request remains.
- Keep the no-client fast-failure and cancellation-after-dispatch behavior covered and passing.

title: fix(web): prevent session-folder IDs from colliding across scopes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

The session-folder contract says each folder ID is unique across the stored file (`packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/DOCUMENTATION.md:12-15`). The `PATCH` create branch checks only `foldersMap[change.scopeKey]` for the requested ID (`packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/folder-changes.js:158-168`), so it can create the same ID in a second scope. The client mirror has the same scope-local check (`packages/ui/src/lib/sessionFolders/folderChanges.ts:83-92`). Legacy import also processes scopes independently and matches incoming IDs only against folders in the current scope (`folder-changes.js:94-120`).

Deletion tombstones, however, are global by folder ID (`folder-changes.js:149-153`). If two scopes contain the same ID, deleting it from one scope records a tombstone for that ID; a later import filters folders against that global tombstone (`:90-99`, `:123-127`) and can remove the other scope's folder too. The `collapsedFolderIds` set is also keyed only by ID (`:212-214`).

I verified these paths and the documented invariant on current `main` (`412eb2c5ef6500e0ee20ae79ee5639bcbda30c68`). A runtime probe was not available because this worktree lacks the `zod` dependency required to import `folder-changes.js`.

## Why it matters

A colliding ID can make a delete or a later legacy-client import affect a different scope's folder, potentially dropping its folder and changing its collapse state. IDs are normally generated client-side, but the server accepts client-supplied IDs and the whole-copy import path also accepts IDs from older clients; neither path enforces the file-wide contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- Server create and import preserve file-wide ID uniqueness; reject or remap a collision without changing an unrelated scope.
- Keep client-side create semantics aligned with the server.
- Add regression coverage for a duplicate ID across two scopes, then delete/import one side and verify the other scope's folder and collapsed state remain intact (or the colliding write is rejected).

title: fix(model-choices): distinguish default effort from a literal default variant in suggestion decisions
body:
## Problem
`packages/web/server/lib/model-choices/notes.js:111` constructs `goal-writer:${model}:${variant ?? 'default'}`. The valid selections `{model: "p/m", variant: null}` and `{model: "p/m", variant: "default"}` therefore share an ID. `store.js:24` permits either variant, and `buildModelChoiceSuggestions` suppresses any ID present in decisions. Approving or declining one choice silently suppresses the distinct other suggestion.

Verified against main `76befc8a4c92ae4249f1acd8fbe4f893e4754bbb`. A prior local module probe recorded six goal-writer choices for `p/m` / `default`: a suggestion appears without a decision, but disappears after recording the decision ID for `p/m` / null.

- Encode model and nullable variant unambiguously, including delimiter-containing inputs accepted by the schema.
- Explicitly handle previously persisted ambiguous decision IDs without silently attributing a decision to the wrong selection; document the chosen migration policy.
- Add regression tests for both directions of null vs literal `default`, delimiter collisions, and legacy decisions; retain suppression for the exact decided choice.

The original feature landed in #505; this concerns decision identity, not bounded storage fixed by #2090.

The surrogate-pair-safe output tail added to `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/places/docker-tools.js` by PR #2052 has no regression test, even though the linked issue's acceptance criteria required regression tests for the tail sites. The fill-failure tail can silently regress (start with a lone low surrogate, re-encoding as U+FFFD) with no test failing.

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2052 (fix(web): spaces output tails never start inside a surrogate pair, for issue #2041):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2052
- Review: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2052#pullrequestreview-5821621018 (coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-09T04:20:47Z) — its "Prompt to fix all issues" carries the failed Linked Issues pre-merge check; the PR conversation summary records the same check as the PR's one failed pre-merge check (warning), with this resolution text:

> Add a regression test for the docker-tools.js fill-failure tail. Place an astral character (for example U+1F600) so the 2,000-character cut lands inside the pair. body:
## Finding (from PR review)

`normalizeContextTabLabel` in `packages/ui/src/stores/useUIStore.ts` retains a pre-existing lone high surrogate in a persisted context-panel tab label whenever the label is at or under the 120-code-unit limit.

CodeRabbit raised this on PR #2053 (fix(ui): useUIStore persisted clamps never split a surrogate pair, for issue #2042):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2053
- Review: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2053#pullrequestreview-5821649440 (coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-09T04:26:56Z, "Additional comments", Minor · Functional Correctness; CodeRabbit marked its own finding "Unverified" — it is verified below against current main)
- File:line at review time: `packages/ui/src/stores/useUIStore.ts:337`

Essence of the comment: an older clamp can leave `'a'.repeat(119) + '\uD83D'` as a 120-code-unit persisted label. The `trimmed.length > 120` condition skips `clipPairSafe`, so `sanitizeContextPanelTabs` retains that invalid label when it runs. Call `clipPairSafe` for every nonempty label, and add an exact-limit persisted-label case. Proposed change:

```diff
-  return trimmed.length > CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH
-    ? clipPairSafe(trimmed, CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH)
-    : trimmed;
+  return clipPairSafe(trimmed, CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH);
```

## No-response evidence

- PR #2053's only follow-up commit (7690267356, 2026-11-09T04:31:09Z) and the developing-today[bot] reply (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2053#discussion_r4509454858) address the separate inline comment about under-limit vim-mappings tests — nothing replies to, fixes, or defers this label-sanitization item.
- PR #2053 merged 2026-11-09T04:37:35Z with the item unaddressed. No open or closed issue covers this residual (searched clipPairSafe / sanitizeContextPanelTabs / normalizeContextTabLabel / "lone high surrogate" on 2026-11-11: none). Issue #2042 is closed as fixed by PR #2053, but this specific failure mode — a label already carrying a lone surrogate at or under the limit — is not fixed by it.

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`, cross-checked twice)

`packages/ui/src/stores/useUIStore.ts` lines 336–338 on main are unchanged:

```ts
  return trimmed.length > CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH
    ? clipPairSafe(trimmed, CONTEXT_PANEL_MAX_LABEL_LENGTH)
    : trimmed;
```

`clipPairSafe` (lines 238–242) only runs on the over-limit branch, and `sanitizeContextPanelTabs` normalizes persisted labels through this function (lines 507–508), so a persisted label of exactly 120 code units ending in a lone high surrogate survives sanitization unchanged and re-encodes as U+FFFD downstream — exactly the persisted-invalid-value class PR #2053 / issue #2042 set out to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- `normalizeContextTabLabel` (or its caller) applies the pair-safe clip to every nonempty trimmed label, so no persisted label retains a lone trailing high surrogate, regardless of length.
- A regression test covers the exact-limit case: a persisted label of 119 ASCII chars + a lone high surrogate (120 code units) is sanitized to a pair-safe value through `sanitizeContextPanelTabs` / the normalize path.
- Existing useUIStore clamp/context-panel tests still pass.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why retaining the value is acceptable.

title: fix(electron): updater E2E fixture crashes when a served file disappears

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The updater E2E fixture server snapshots directory entries at startup, then calls `fs.statSync(filePath)` inside its HTTP request callback without catching errors (`packages/electron/scripts/updater-e2e-fixture.mjs:82-98`). If a registered feed file is removed or becomes inaccessible after startup, a request for it throws an uncaught exception and terminates the fixture process, interrupting the update test instead of returning an HTTP error. The read stream also has no error handler for a failure after stat.

## Reproduction

At local `origin/main` 1fabc820a50f90c514592ceb3d05141606e54acd, using Node v24.21.0:

1. Create `test.yml` in a temporary feed directory and start the exported `createFixtureServer({ directory })`.
2. Delete `test.yml` after the server starts.
3. Fetch `<server-url>/test.yml`.

Actual: uncaught `ENOENT` at line 92; Node exits 1. Expected: a suitable error response, and the fixture remains available for subsequent requests.

## Acceptance

- Handle files disappearing or becoming unreadable without an uncaught exception or process exit; handle read-stream failures as well, including errors after headers are sent.
- Add a regression test that requests a removed file and checks both the response and continued server availability, plus a test for a read-stream error where practical.

Scope: local manual updater E2E fixture, not the production update server. Open PR searches for `updater-e2e-fixture`, `fixture ENOENT`, and updater/fixture/Electron titles found no matching fix. Existing #2057 concerns argument parsing, not request error handling.

body:
## Finding (residual credential leak in a merged security fix)

PR #1972 (merged `fff4161f505572af0ff02e21e5eeeef530c1c679`, closed #1920) widened `redactSensitiveText` in `packages/web/server/lib/source-control/url-redaction.js`, but two credential shapes still survive it verbatim on current main `e895968ba30b28f5345df0661d11278265505967`:

1. **Bearer/Basic-headed assignment values.** The scheme pattern (url-redaction.js:61) only matches `authorization:` + colon. The assignment pattern (:62) explicitly refuses values headed by `bearer`/`basic` (the `(?!(?:bearer|basic)\s)` guard, meant to protect the scheme word), so for any other shape the actual credential after the scheme word is never touched:
   - `authorization=Bearer <token>` — leaks
   - `token=Bearer <token>` — leaks
   - `api_key: Bearer <token>` — leaks
2. **Quoted JSON shapes.** A closing quote between key and colon defeats both patterns (the assignment pattern needs `[:=]` immediately after optional whitespace), so JSON-dumped headers/config pass through untouched:
   - `{"authorization": "Bearer <token>"}` — leaks
   - `{"x-api-key": "<token>"}` — leaks

## Evidence

- PR #1972 diff: `url-redaction.js` gained `sensitiveKeyPattern` (:47 on main), the scheme replace (:61) and the guarded assignment replace (:62); its new tests cover only the unquoted colon forms (`authorization: Bearer …`, `x-api-key: …`, `api_key=…`).
- Verified against CURRENT main, not just the PR diff: fetched `url-redaction.js` from main via the contents API (pattern confirmed at :47/:61/:62 in two independent reads) and imported the real module in node with a synthetic probe token, two identical rounds (2026-11-10): every shape listed above returned the probe token verbatim (`LEAK`), while the controls `authorization: Bearer <token>` and `access_token=<token>` were correctly redacted.
- Convergence twin: `packages/web/server/lib/git/redaction.js` (`redactGitText`) shares the equals-Bearer hole — its assignment pattern consumes only the word `Bearer` and leaves the token — so a fix should check both redactors, which is exactly the convergence #1920 asked for.
- Callers (per #1972): this redactor backs relay error text and source-control route failures, i.e. the leaked shapes land in logs / error surfaces.

## Why it matters

This is the exact class #1920 was filed and closed for — credentials surviving a redactor into logs — surviving in adjacent shapes the fix's own guard created or its patterns never covered. Error text that embeds a JSON header dump or an `authorization=Bearer …` config line is a realistic shape for relay/source-control failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- `redactSensitiveText` redacts the credential token (not just the scheme word) in: `authorization=Bearer <t>`, `authorization=Basic <t>`, any listed key with a Bearer/Basic-headed value (`token=Bearer <t>`, `api_key: Bearer <t>`), and quoted JSON forms (`{"authorization": "Bearer <t>"}`, `{"x-api-key": "<t>"}`).
- The scheme word and JSON structure survive as today (`authorization: Bearer [redacted]` behaviour unchanged); credential-free text is byte-identical.
- New tests in `url-redaction.test.js` pin every shape above with a probe-token oracle (token must not appear in output), mirroring the existing #1920 block.
- `redactGitText` is checked for the same shapes and fixed or explicitly scoped out with a reason recorded on this issue.

title: fix(ui): boundExtractedText 500,000-char cut can split a surrogate pair — document-attachments.ts slices extracted document text with no pair guard, and the lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD in the attachment text sent to the model

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Bug

`boundExtractedText` in `packages/ui/src/sync/document-attachments.ts:650-661` bounds extracted Office-document text at `MAX_EXTRACTED_TEXT_CHARS` (500,000, `:11`) with a raw slice and no surrogate-pair guard:

```ts
let end = MAX_EXTRACTED_TEXT_CHARS - TEXT_TRUNCATION_NOTICE.length
// ... bracket-citation adjustment may move `end` to lastOpenBracket ...
return `${text.slice(0, end)}${TEXT_TRUNCATION_NOTICE}`
```

If the cut at `end` falls inside an astral character (emoji, CJK extension, mathematical alphanumeric), the extracted text ends in a lone high surrogate. The result becomes the attachment's `textFile` (`:682`, consumed by `attachment-files.ts:416-417`), which is sent with the prompt — so the lone surrogate is UTF-8-encoded as U+FFFD in the document text the model actually reads, and the character itself is lost at exactly the truncation boundary. The bracket-citation adjustment can also move `end`, so the guard must apply to the final `end`, not just the initial computation.

## Evidence (verified this run, main d5955751c)

Laptop probe through the real path (`~/git/fleet/probe-oc-docattach-surrogate-20261108/`, laptop): built a real `.docx` whose extracted text (the extractor prepends `# Document\n\n`) places U+1F600 straddling the 499,957-char cut, then called the real `extractDocumentAttachments`. Run twice, identical:

- Output length 500,000 (bound + notice, as designed), but the character at the cut position (index 499,956) is U+FFFD — `has_emoji: false`, `fffd_count: 1`, tail reads `…aaaa�\n\n[Document text t…`.
- A misaligned-by-12 control run (emoji not at the cut) produced no U+FFFD, confirming the corruption is the boundary cut, not the extraction.

Dedup: search for `document-attachments` / `boundExtractedText` / extracted-text truncation filings returns none (only unrelated extraction filings #1948, #1546).

## Why it matters

Document attachments are how users hand the model reports, decks and spreadsheets. A document long enough to hit the 500k bound with an astral character at the boundary silently loses that character and injects a replacement character into the model's context — the same pair-split corruption the repo has been eliminating across its model-facing clamps (#2043, #1911), in a surface those sweeps did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- `boundExtractedText` never returns a lone surrogate: when the final `end` (after the bracket-citation adjustment) falls inside a surrogate pair, the cut backs off to the pair boundary (drop the partial character), matching the pair-safe pattern used elsewhere in the UI.
- Regression test in `document-attachments.test.ts`: an over-limit document whose text straddles the cut with an astral character yields no lone surrogate and no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode, the truncation notice is intact, and total length stays within the 500,000 bound; under-limit and ASCII over-limit controls unchanged.
- Existing `document-attachments.test.ts` tests pass.

title: fix(web): CLI log follow (followFile) decodes each poll's bytes on its own — a multi-byte character split across polls is corrupted in 'openchamber logs --follow' output

body:
## Bug

`followFile` in `packages/web/bin/lib/cli-log-files.js` — the follower behind `openchamber logs --follow` (`packages/web/bin/lib/commands-logs.js:87`) — decodes each 400 ms poll's newly appended bytes on its own:

- `cli-log-files.js:119`: `const chunk = remainder + buffer.toString('utf8');`
- The `remainder` it carries between polls (`:108`, `:121-122`) is a *string* remainder (the unterminated last line), not a byte remainder. A multi-byte UTF-8 character whose bytes are split across two polls — a writer flushing a line in pieces, a slow pipe, any append that lands mid-character at a poll boundary — is decoded in pieces: each partial sequence becomes U+FFFD immediately, and the original character is unrecoverable by the time the rest of its bytes arrive.

This is the per-chunk decode class the repo has fixed repeatedly for pipe output (#1695, #1697, #1734, design #1740's stream-output contract), but this consumer is a *polling file reader*, not a pipe: it was not named in the #1741 audit disposition (checked this run), and `followFile` itself has no test — `cli-bounded-reads.test.js` covers only its sibling `readTailLines`.

## Evidence (verified this run, main d5955751c)

Laptop probe against the real `followFile` (`~/git/fleet/probe-oc-followfile-utf8-20261108/`, laptop), run twice with identical results:

- Split append: write `mood: ` + first 2 bytes of U+1F600, wait 900 ms (past the 400 ms poll), append remaining 2 bytes + ` done\n` → delivered line is `"mood: ��� done"` — 3 U+FFFD, the emoji is gone.
- Control: the same line appended whole in one poll → delivered exactly as `"mood: 😀 done"`.

## Why it matters

`logs --follow` is the live diagnostic surface for a managed OpenChamber server. Log lines routinely contain non-ASCII text (paths, prompts, error messages in other languages, emoji). Any line whose bytes straddle a poll boundary is silently corrupted in exactly the output a person is reading to diagnose a problem, with no signal that the text they see is not what the server wrote.

## Acceptance criteria

- `followFile` never delivers U+FFFD for a character split across polls: carry the undecoded byte tail between polls (e.g. a `StringDecoder` held across polls, or a byte-level line remainder), and flush it correctly when the follower is stopped / the file is truncated (`stats.size < position` reset at `:111-113` must also reset the decoder state).
- A regression test drives `followFile` with an append split mid-character across two polls and asserts the delivered line is byte-identical to the appended line; ASCII and whole-append controls unchanged.
- Existing CLI tests pass (`cli-bounded-reads.test.js` and the bin suite).

body:
# fix(ui): browser history title clamp can split a surrogate pair — recordVisit in browser/history.ts slices page titles at 200 with no pair guard, and the result is persisted in the browser-history store

## Evidence (main 876a25236)

`packages/ui/src/lib/browser/history.ts`:

- `MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 200` (:24).
- `recordVisit` (:60): `const title = String(visit.title ?? '').trim().slice(0, MAX_TITLE_LENGTH) || previous?.title || '';` — a raw slice with no surrogate-pair guard. A cut landing between the halves of an astral character leaves the stored title ending in a lone high surrogate (U+D800–U+DBFF).

The result is persisted, not transient: `useBrowserHistoryStore` (`packages/ui/src/stores/useBrowserHistoryStore.ts`) wraps the history state in zustand `persist` (:49) under the storage name `openchamber-browser-history` (:86, partialize :89), so the cut title is written to local storage and re-read on every later visit to the browser panel, where it is also the suggestion/search text (`suggestVisits` matches on entry titles). At the first UTF-8/JSON encoding the lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD and the page's real character is lost from the stored history entry.

Page titles are uncontrolled text — sites routinely put emoji and other astral characters in `<title>` — so a long title with an astral character at position 200 is a realistic input, not an edge case the user types by hand. `packages/ui/src/lib/browser/history.test.ts` covers `recordVisit` (8 references) but has no astral-straddle case.

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the real module, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-browserhistory-surrogate-20261108/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun), importing the real `recordVisit` from a verbatim copy of `packages/ui/src/lib/browser/history.ts` (+ its `./url` dependency) at main 876a25236.

- Straddle title `'a'×199 + U+1F600 + 'tail'`: stored entry title length 200, ends in a lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 199, exactly **1 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip.
- ASCII control (250 chars): length 200, no lone surrogate, 0 U+FFFD.
- Under-limit control (`'Hi 😀 there'`): returned unchanged, no lone surrogate, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

The browser panel's history is the return-to-address surface for dev servers and staging pages; its stored titles are the labels and search text for those entries. A straddling character is silently corrupted in the persisted entry and stays corrupted across restarts — the same persisted-clamp defect class fixed for session titles, PWA names and settings clamps, on a surface those fixes did not cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- `recordVisit`'s title clamp in `packages/ui/src/lib/browser/history.ts` never produces a lone surrogate: a cut landing inside a surrogate pair moves to the pair boundary (drop the partial character), matching the pair-safe behaviour landed for the other persisted UI clamps.
- Regression tests in `packages/ui/src/lib/browser/history.test.ts` cover an astral character straddling the 200-char cut: no lone surrogate, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode, result within the limit; ASCII over-limit and under-limit emoji controls unchanged.
- Existing UI tests still pass.

# fix(ui): multi-run title clamps can split a surrogate pair — renameRun, askOtherModels and createMultiRun slice titles at 200 with no pair guard, and the cut titles are persisted in session metadata

## Evidence (main 876a25236)

Three multi-run title cuts, all `trim().slice(0, 200)` with no surrogate-pair guard:

- `packages/ui/src/lib/multirun/runActions.ts:25` — `renameRun`: `const nextTitle = title.trim().slice(0, 200);` The result is persisted on every run member via `requestSessionMetadataUpdate(sessionId, { openchamber: { multirun: { title: nextTitle } } }, …)` (:35).
- `packages/ui/src/lib/multirun/runActions.ts:89` — `askOtherModels`: `const title = (session.title || prompt.text.split('\n')[0] || 'Run').trim().slice(0, 200);` The title is stored in the membership record (`title` in the `MultiRunMembership` at :90-99) and persisted via `requestSessionMetadataUpdate(session.id, multiRunMembershipPatch(membership), …)`.
- `packages/ui/src/stores/useMultiRunStore.ts:162` — `createMultiRun`: `const runTitle = (params.title ?? params.name).trim().slice(0, 200);` The run title is embedded in every created lane's session title (:254-258) and in the persisted membership identity (`title: runTitle` at :261).

A cut landing between the halves of an astral character (emoji, some CJK/symbol planes) leaves the persisted title ending in a lone high surrogate (U+D800–U+DBFF). At the first UTF-8/JSON encoding of the session metadata it becomes U+FFFD, so the user's character is lost from the stored run title on every member session. The UI already has pair-safe precedent elsewhere (e.g. the pair-safe clamps landed for #2028/#2035), but none of these three sites uses one, and there is no straddle test for any of them (`packages/ui/src/lib/multirun/title.test.ts` covers title derivation, not these clamps).

## Reproduction (laptop probe vs the verbatim real code, run twice, identical both times)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-multirun-surrogate-20261108/probe.ts` on the laptop (bun), running `renameRun` copied verbatim from runActions.ts at main 876a25236 with only `requestSessionMetadataUpdate`/`registerMultiRunSession` stubbed (the stub captures the metadata patch that would be persisted), plus the verbatim title expressions from runActions.ts:89 and useMultiRunStore.ts:162.

- Input `'a'×199 + U+1F600 + 'tail'` at all three sites: result length 200, ends in a lone high surrogate U+D83D at index 199, exactly **1 U+FFFD** after a UTF-8 encode round-trip. For `renameRun`, the captured session-metadata patch carries the corrupted title — this is the persisted form, not a display string.
- ASCII control (250 chars) at the same expression: length 200, no lone surrogate, 0 U+FFFD.

## Why it matters

Run titles come from user rename input, existing session titles, and first-prompt text — all free text where emoji are routine. The rename path writes the cut title to every member session's metadata at once, so one straddling character corrupts the run's name across the whole run, permanently (the lost half of the pair cannot be recovered from the stored U+FFFD).

## Acceptance criteria

- All three cuts — runActions.ts:25 (`renameRun`), runActions.ts:89 (`askOtherModels`), and useMultiRunStore.ts:162 (`createMultiRun`) — never produce a lone surrogate: a cut landing inside a surrogate pair moves to the pair boundary (drop the partial character), matching the pair-safe behaviour landed for the settings/PWA clamps.
- Regression tests cover each site (or the shared helper they route through) with an astral character straddling the 200-char cut: no lone surrogate in the persisted title, no U+FFFD after UTF-8 encode, result within the 200 limit; ASCII and under-limit controls unchanged.
- Existing UI tests still pass.

title: fix(web): OpenCode service-env reader reads service.json whole with no size gate — readOpenCodeServiceEnv buffers the OpenCode CLI's file entire (and blocks the managed-OpenCode launch path on a FIFO), unlike the shared bounded reader

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`readOpenCodeServiceEnv` reads the OpenCode CLI's `service.json` whole, synchronously, with no size gate and no regular-file check — a plain by-path `readFileSync`. This file is **not OpenChamber's own state**: it belongs to the OpenCode CLI ("The file belongs to the OpenCode CLI and is not a published contract", module header), which puts it squarely in the shared bounded reader's design class (#1254: files whose size the server does not control). The sibling environment store in the same lib was already filed for the same defect (#1609); this reader was missed.

`packages/web/server/lib/environment/opencode-service-env.js` (main `6b3b879219`):

- `:20-28` — `readOpenCodeServiceEnv(configDir)` does `fs.readFileSync(path.join(configDir, 'service.json'), 'utf8')` inside a bare `catch { return {} }`. No stat, no cap, no non-regular rejection: an oversized file is buffered and `JSON.parse`d entire, and a FIFO at that path blocks the synchronous read indefinitely.
- The zod schema (`:16-18`) validates only **after** the full read + parse.

Call path: `packages/web/server/index.js:1429` wires it into the environment runtime; `lib/environment/runtime.js:290-294` `forOpenCode()` calls it, and `forOpenCodeResolved()` feeds the managed OpenCode launch fingerprint and the launch itself. So the unbounded/blocking read sits on the managed-OpenCode launch path: a bad `service.json` doesn't just cost memory, it can stall a launch.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probes against `origin/main` `6b3b879219`)

Probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-05-creator-oc/` (laptop):

- `probe-svcenv.mjs`: a `service.json` with one env value of 2 MiB is returned whole — `readOpenCodeServiceEnv(dir).BIG.length === 2097152`. No cap fires.
- `probe-fifo.mjs`: with `service.json` as a FIFO with no writer, the read **blocked past a 3 s timeout** (exit 124) — the launch path hangs rather than answering `{}`.

Dedup: `gh issue list --state all --search "service.json"` returns no issue for this reader; #1609 covers `lib/environment/store.js` (`environment.json`), a different file and function.

## Why it matters

Environment variables for a managed OpenCode are a handful of short strings; nothing legitimate is anywhere near even 1 MiB. The reader's own contract is "anything unexpected reads as no variables" — an over-cap or non-regular file should land in that same `{}` outcome instead of an unbounded buffer or a hung launch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The read is size-gated and non-regular-safe — shared bounded reader (`lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`) or an equivalent handle-based gate — with over-cap, non-regular, and unreadable inputs all producing the current `{}` outcome (never a throw, never a block).
- [ ] The cap is documented in the module (1 MiB is generous for an env map; the routing/linear precedents are 4–8 MiB if a larger house value is preferred — pick one and say why).
- [ ] Normal behaviour unchanged: valid `service.json` values still reach `forOpenCode()`; invalid names still filtered by `isVariableName`; enterprise-mode bypass untouched.
- [ ] Regression tests cover an over-cap file and a non-regular file (FIFO or directory) returning `{}` promptly, and keep the existing environment suites green.

title: fix(web): event-stream replay store load reads its file whole with no size gate — createReplayStore load() synchronously buffers global-replay.jsonl entire (and blocks hub construction on a FIFO), unlike the shared bounded reader

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`createReplayStore`'s `load()` in `packages/web/server/lib/event-stream/replay-store.js:155` reads the durable global-stream replay file whole, synchronously, with no size cap and no regular-file check:

```js
text = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
```

The text is then split into a lines array and every record parsed and materialised (`replay-store.js:161-185`), so peak memory is several times the file size. `load()` is called synchronously when the global message-stream hub is constructed (`lib/event-stream/global-hub.js:76`, `const persisted = durable.load();`), with `filePath` = `~/.config/openchamber/event-stream/global-replay.jsonl` (or `$OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR/event-stream/global-replay.jsonl`, `replay-store.js:26-32`).

The store's own writer compacts after 4,096 records / 8 MiB appended since the last snapshot (`replay-store.js:23-24`, `maybeCompact`), but `load()` — the one reader — trusts the on-disk size completely:

1. A file that is larger than the writer's bound (external growth, corruption, a snapshot whose entries carry unsanitised large `serializedFrame` payloads — `sanitizeEntry` caps nothing about frame length, `replay-store.js:43-57`) is buffered and parsed whole at hub construction.
2. If the path is a FIFO (or another non-regular file that never yields EOF), `readFileSync` never returns and hub construction — and with it the global event stream — blocks forever.

Unlike the shared bounded reader (`lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` — handle-judged, `O_NONBLOCK`, cap enforced during the read), this reader has no gate at all. The append-only JSONL shape makes a bounded/streaming load natural: records are applied line by line, and a torn tail is already treated as end-of-trust (`replay-store.js:169-173`).

## Evidence (verified this run, on laptop against the real module from `origin/main` @ `8cd11be40d`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-replay-store-ungated-20261104/` (real `replay-store.js` extracted from `origin/main`), run ×2 with identical results:

- Control: empty store file → `load()` returns head `{position: 0, upstream: ''}`.
- Oversize: a 37,180,574-byte `global-replay.jsonl` (32,768 valid `local` records, 1 KiB frames) → loaded whole, all 32,768 entries materialised in the returned state. No rejection, no cap — 4.6× the writer's own 8 MiB compaction bound.
- FIFO: the replay path replaced by a FIFO with no writer → `load()` never returned within 3 s (probe killed by timeout, exit 124), both runs.

## Why it matters

- Availability: the global stream hub is constructed on the server's serving path; a blocked or multi-hundred-MB replay file turns a restart into a hang or an OOM instead of a degraded stream.
- Defence in depth: compaction bounds what the writer leaves behind in the happy path, but the reader is the trust boundary for whatever is actually on disk at boot — edited, corrupted, restored-from-backup, or raced files all arrive through `load()`.
- The fix must preserve the load semantics: a torn final line ends trust at that point, records after a malformed mid-file record are ignored with a warning, and `recordsSinceSnapshot` / `appendedBytes` are initialised from what was read (`replay-store.js:182-185`) — a bounded or streaming load has to keep those counters honest, or refuse-and-start-fresh explicitly rather than silently mis-counting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `load()` no longer buffers the whole replay file unbounded: it either streams/bounds the read under a named cap (sized from the writer's compaction bounds, with the rationale recorded) or refuses an over-cap / non-regular file explicitly (warn + start from empty state), and a FIFO at the replay path returns promptly instead of blocking hub construction.
- [ ] Torn-tail and malformed-record behaviour is preserved (trust ends at the first bad record; the warning still fires for a mid-file malformation).
- [ ] `recordsSinceSnapshot` / `appendedBytes` after load reflect what was actually accepted, so post-load compaction still triggers correctly.
- [ ] Regression tests pin the oversize and FIFO cases; existing `replay-store.test.js` and `global-resume.test.js` still pass.

title: fix(web): model-choices store reads its file whole with no size gate — read buffers model-choices.json entire (a FIFO wedges the store's whole serialized queue), and its decisions array is never pruned, unlike the shared bounded reader

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The model-choices store — the web server's store for the user's manual model/effort choices and their answers to suggestions built from them (`model-choices.json`) — reads its file whole with no size gate and no non-regular-file protection. It is the residual class fixed for the project config (#1490), the session-goal objective (#1582), agent-memory + project-context (#1607), the routing store (#1608) and the environment store (#1609), in a store none of those touched:

- `packages/web/server/lib/model-choices/store.js` — `read` (:69) does `text = await fs.readFile(filePath, 'utf8')` (:72) and `JSON.parse`s whatever comes back. There is no byte cap, no `stat`/`isFile` judgement, and no use of `readBoundedFile` anywhere in the file (full-file read: :72 is the only read).
- Every operation goes through that read: `record` (:103), `snapshot` (:112) and `decide` (:118) are all read-modify-write cycles serialized on one promise queue (`serialized`, :61–67). A FIFO at the path never settles the first read — and because every later operation chains behind it, one non-regular file wedges the *entire* model-choices surface (recording, Settings snapshots, decisions) for the life of the process, not just one request. An oversized regular file is buffered and parsed whole before the zod schema runs — the schema bounds what is *kept*, not what is *read*.

The house standard for exactly this already exists: `readBoundedFile` in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` — open once with `O_NONBLOCK`, judge from the opened handle, refuse non-regular files, buffer at most cap + 1 byte. This store was not one of the fifteen migrated to the durable-store primitive in #976.

## The write side does not fully bound the file either

Events are retained properly — newest 5,000 within 90 days (`MAX_MODEL_CHOICE_EVENTS`, :17; `MODEL_CHOICE_RETENTION_MS`, :18; `retained()`, :94–97) — but **decisions are never pruned**: `fileSchema` (:46) puts no maximum on the `decisions` array, and `decide` (:118–121) appends one entry per decision id (deduped only by id; ids up to 400 chars, `decisionSchema` :40) with no count or age bound. So even the store's own writer lets the file grow without limit over time, and there is no computed legitimate maximum a read cap could simply mirror. Triage should pair the read gate with a decisions bound (count and/or retention window, mirroring the events policy) so the cap it documents is real.

## Verified this run (code-verified on origin/main 41c124c7c, read ×2 via `gh api`)

- `read` and the :72 `readFile` re-read independently twice on main `41c124c7ca7c82fbca59d866c43cb76961bfcba8` (contents API, blob `1cdeb9f18d689e6914a6f89e757d9c61448534b3`); the line numbers above are from the second read. Full-file grep: :72 is the only read in `store.js`; no cap, no handle judgement, no bounded reader; `decisions` unbounded in schema (:46) and in `decide` (:119–120).
- The store's test suite (`model-choices/model-choices.test.js`, 302 lines) pins the *events* retention cap but contains no oversized-file, FIFO, or non-regular-file read case (grep: the only `MAX_` hits are the events-retention test).
- `fs.readFile` on a FIFO with no writer blocks in `open()` before any judgement can run — the identical ungated pattern was probe-confirmed on the laptop for #1607 (FIFO never settled within 3,000 ms; 33 MB files buffered whole). A runtime probe of this store was **not** run this run: the laptop SSH tunnel was down for the entire run (repeated `laptop-agent: HTTP 502 … proxy closed during CONNECT` from `~/tools/laptop-ssh.sh`, plus the real-SSH fallback failing), and probes are never run on the sandbox. The defect is fully determined by the code above; a triage probe against `createModelChoiceStore` with an oversized file and a FIFO is a reasonable first confirmation step.

## Why it matters

The file sits in the user's data directory, which other tools, sync jobs and agents also write. One oversized or non-regular file at that path either buffers unboundedly on every model-choice operation or silently wedges the whole surface behind the serialized queue — no error, no recovery short of finding and removing the file by hand. The malformed semantics are deliberately strict (store.js :66–67: a malformed file is an error, never an empty history — "writing over it would erase what it held") and must stay that way: an over-cap file must follow the existing `ModelChoiceStoreError` (500) path, never read as empty history. And until decisions are bounded, the file outgrows any cap chosen from the events policy alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `read` in `lib/model-choices/store.js` reads through a bounded, handle-judged read (`readBoundedFile` in `lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, or equivalent): at most cap + 1 byte is ever buffered, and a FIFO / directory / other non-regular file at the store path is refused promptly instead of wedging the serialized operation queue.
- [ ] Decisions are bounded on write (count and/or retention, mirroring the events policy), and the read cap is documented in code with its headroom over the resulting legitimate maximum (events ≲ 5,000 retained entries plus the bounded decisions), the way the sibling fixes document theirs.
- [ ] Existing read semantics are preserved exactly: missing file still reads as `{ version: 1, events: [], decisions: [] }`; a malformed or over-cap file still throws `ModelChoiceStoreError` with status 500 (never silently reads as empty history); the serialized read-modify-write behaviour of `record`/`snapshot`/`decide`/`clear` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `model-choices/model-choices.test.js`: oversized file refused via the error path without being parsed whole, FIFO/non-regular target refused without hanging (and the queue still serves the next operation), decisions bound enforced, at-cap and ordinary files read unchanged.
- [ ] No other store changes behaviour; the write path's atomic rename (#117 class) and the input schemas are untouched.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `model-choices`, `environment.json`, `environment store`, `quota credential`, `relay-identity` and the full open-issue list: #147 (closed) is the feature that built this store; #688 (closed) covers model-choices *limit params* being judged by `z.coerce` — a different defect; #1607 covers agent-memory + project-context, #1608 the routing store, #1609 the environment store, #1490 the project config, #1582 the session-goal objective. This store's read — and its unbounded decisions array — are covered nowhere. (A previous creator run noted this store as "same class, weaker" and prioritised #1608; this filing adds the verified decisions-growth defect, which that note did not cover.)

title: fix(web): zhipuai-coding-plan quota provider still selects its key with ?? — an empty key field hides a valid token (the #1747/#1751 sweep missed it)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

The web Zhipu AI Coding Plan quota provider still selects its credential with a raw nullish chain — the defect class fixed for Mistral by PR #2270 (for #1747) and for eight sibling providers by #1751. Both sweeps missed this provider, plausibly because its shape hides the usual symptom: `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota` share one `getApiKey`, so the two never *disagree* — but the shared selection itself is wrong, so a valid `token` sitting behind an empty or whitespace-only `key` field is never used.

## Evidence

- Found in the Ring-2 sibling scan while reviewing PR #2270 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2270, MERGED, commit d5c6c8acfec69d5921f4f7b6a5fe9bc370c94010, merge ed69275942f7702feca0084295fefc0c58b3b9c4 = current main HEAD). #2270 routed Mistral's selection through `asNonEmptyString` at `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/mistral.js:45,49` (verified on main, two independent reads).
- Current main ed69275942f7702feca0084295fefc0c58b3b9c4 (file fetched twice, byte-identical), `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/zhipuai-coding-plan.js`:
  - `:82-87` `getApiKey(auth)`: `const apiKeyFromAuth = entry?.key ?? entry?.token;` then `if (apiKeyFromAuth) return apiKeyFromAuth;` — `??` does not fall through on `''`, and the truthiness guard then drops to the config-file fallback, so the auth entry's `token` is never tried when `key` is empty.
  - `:106` `isConfigured` is `Boolean(getApiKey(auth))` and `:110` `fetchQuota` uses the same `getApiKey` — both inherit the defect identically.
  - `:129` the fetch sends the selected value as the `Authorization: Bearer …` header, so a whitespace-only `key` (`'   '`, truthy, returned verbatim) is sent as a blank bearer instead of the valid `token`.
  - The file already imports `asNonEmptyString` (`:29`, used at `:78` and `:199` for other fields) — the correct helper is in scope; only the key selection does not use it. `asNonEmptyString` (`packages/web/server/lib/shared/guards.js:55-59`) returns the trimmed string or null for non-string/empty/whitespace input.
- Probe (verbatim selection expression from `getApiKey`, Node): `{key: '', token: 'real-token'}` → `null` (token ignored; provider reports "Not configured" unless an unrelated config key happens to exist, which then silently wins instead); `{key: '   ', token: 'real-token'}` → `'   '` (sent as the bearer); `{key: 'real-key', token: 'real-token'}` → `'real-key'` (normal path unaffected).
- `zhipuai-coding-plan.test.js` (177 lines on main) contains no empty/whitespace-key or token-fallthrough case — its only auth fixture is `{key: 'test-token'}` (`:3`).
- Dedupe: issue searches (2026-11-13) for `zhipuai`, `asNonEmptyString`, `zhipuai getApiKey`, and `zhipuai-coding-plan empty key token fallthrough` return #1751 (CLOSED; its table names eight web providers — zhipuai-coding-plan is not among them), #1759 (CLOSED; the VS Code port only), and no issue covering the web provider's `getApiKey`. Every other web provider checked in the same scan (cline-pass, command-code, codex, copilot, deepinfra, deepseek, hyper, kilo, kimi, meta, minimax-shared, nanogpt, neuralwatt, ollama-cloud, opencode-go, openrouter, wafer, zai) already selects through `asNonEmptyString`.

## Why it matters

The quota board's job is honest credential state (the #1619/#1747 design premise). A Zhipu entry with an empty first field — a half-written enrollment, a key cleared in one tool while the token remains — reports "Not configured" despite holding a valid credential, and a whitespace-only key misreports the credential as rejected by the API. Because `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota` agree here, the failure has no visible inconsistency to debug from, which is how two dedicated sweeps of this exact pattern passed it by.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getApiKey` in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/zhipuai-coding-plan.js` selects through `asNonEmptyString` (`asNonEmptyString(entry?.key) ?? asNonEmptyString(entry?.token)`), so empty/whitespace fields are treated as absent and the trimmed value is used; the config-file fallback is reached only when neither auth field yields a usable value.
- [ ] New `zhipuai-coding-plan.test.js` cases mirroring PR #2270's Mistral pins: `{key: '', token: <valid>}` fetches with the token; `{key: '   ', token: <valid>}` fetches with the token (never a blank bearer); an all-empty entry reports not configured from `fetchQuota` and `isConfigured`.
- [ ] No behavior change when `key` holds a real value, and existing zhipuai tests stay green.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

For source PR #2270: accept-with-followups. Ring 1: the diff implements #1747's three acceptance criteria verbatim — both selectors route through `asNonEmptyString` and the 3 new tests pin the empty-key, whitespace-key, and all-empty shapes across both entry points. Ring 2: followup gap (this issue, filed under the reviewer's normal charter) — the sibling scan of every web quota provider found zhipuai-coding-plan.js:84 still selecting with a raw `??` chain, a provider both the #1751 web sweep and the #1759 VS Code sweep left uncovered. Ring 3: #2270 completes the #1619/#1747 honest-credential-state goal for Mistral; the programme-level pattern is not fully closed until this last web provider is swept.

title: fix(ui,web): PWA app-name and fallback-manifest clamps still split grapheme clusters — #2114 residual in index.html, pwa-clamps, settings-helpers
