body:
## Finding

PR #2118 (merged `7518c4fe43ee`, closing issue #2114) made the PWA shortcut clamps grapheme-safe in the UI hook helper and the server manifest route — but the same extended-grapheme-cluster splitting remains live at every other PWA name clamp on current main. These are the #2114 defect (a combining mark dropped off its base character, or a ZWJ emoji sequence cut mid-sequence) on surfaces #2114 did not enumerate.

## Evidence (current main `6c34b89a6fb9324f8b1c89a44ebebde5a7c7867c`)

- `packages/web/index.html:32-40` — the fallback manifest builder's `clipPairSafe` is pair-safe only. It backs `normalizePwaName` (app name cap 64, :42-50) and `truncate` (:52-57), which clamps the shortcut title at 48 (:189), the session `short_name` at 32 (:217), and the app `short_name` at 30 (:231) — the same manifest labels, at the same caps, that PR #2118 fixed in the server route.
- `packages/ui/src/lib/pwa-clamps.ts:3-7` — `clipPwaInstallName` (cap 64) is still the pair-safe slice; PR #2118's body states it was left unchanged, and it sits in the same file as the new `clipGraphemeSafe` helper used by `normalizeRecentTitle`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-helpers.js:193-197` — `clipPairSafe` (pair-only) backs `normalizePwaAppName` (:199-208) at `PWA_APP_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` 64 (:93); the persisted app name feeds the manifest `name`.

Probe (node, verbatim `clipPwaInstallName` from main; the index.html and settings-helpers guards are the identical three-line slice):

- `"a".repeat(63) + "e\u0301" + "tail"` → 63 `a`s + a bare `e` (U+0065): the combining acute U+0301 is dropped. Grapheme-safe result drops the cluster whole: 63 `a`s.
- `"a".repeat(62)` + the family ZWJ sequence 👩‍👩‍👧‍👦 + `"tail"` → ends with a lone 👩 (U+1F469), a partial joined sequence. Grapheme-safe result: 62 `a`s.

Dedupe: `gh search issues` for "grapheme" returns only closed issue #2114 (shortcut scope); no open or closed issue covers the app-name / fallback-builder clamps.

## Why it matters

The install name and the fallback-builder manifest are user-visible labels (install prompt, home-screen shortcuts). Titles and app names in languages using combining marks lose accents at the cap, and joined emoji render as partial sequences — precisely the harm #2114 fixed for the route/hook surfaces, still reachable through the fallback builder whenever it serves the manifest.

## Acceptance criteria

- Truncation at the three sites above cuts only between extended grapheme clusters, keeping the existing UTF-16 caps (64 app/install name; 48/32/30 in the fallback builder), mirroring PR #2118's approach (`Intl.Segmenter` with the pair-safe slice as fallback where Segmenter is unavailable).
- Boundary tests pin a combining-cluster straddle and a ZWJ-sequence straddle at each surface: `pwa-manifest-bootstrap.test.js` (index.html), the UI pair-safe-clamps tests (`clipPwaInstallName`), and `settings-helpers.test.js` (`normalizePwaAppName`).
- Existing pair-safe regression tests keep passing.
- Out of scope: the other `settings-helpers.js` sanitizer clamps (fonts, labels, etc.) — this issue covers only `normalizePwaAppName` there.

title: fix(ui): scope coalesced reads by Authorization header

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/ui
labels.description: Package: ui (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` `6c34b89a6fb9324f8b1c89a44ebebde5a7c7867c`, `packages/ui/src/lib/runtime-fetch.ts:311-317` builds `coalesceReadKey` from method, URL, and `x-opencode-directory`; it does not include `Authorization` or otherwise bypass coalescing for caller-supplied credentials. At `:375-387`, a matching in-flight key causes the later caller to reuse the first request's promise and response clone.

Different caller credentials are supported: `packages/ui/src/lib/runtime-fetch.test.ts:233-251` pins that `runtimeFetch` preserves an existing caller `Authorization` header. Reproduced the key calculation for two overlapping GETs to `/api/config/providers` with `Bearer token-A` and `Bearer token-B`: both produce the same key (`GET <URL>\0`), so the second call can receive the first response without sending its own Authorization header. The actual route path is directly wired to the shared key in `runtime-fetch.ts:375-387`.

All-state issue searches for `runtimeFetch coalesceReadKey Authorization`, `read coalescing auth headers`, `config providers concurrent bearer token`, `Authorization coalesce`, `credential read coalescing`, and `runtime fetch auth header collision` found no matching issue. All-state PR searches for the coalescing/Authorization implementation found no match. Test execution was attempted with `bun test packages/ui/src/lib/runtime-fetch.test.ts` but is blocked because the worktree lacks the `zod` dependency.

## Why it matters

If callers use different credentials for an allowlisted GET to the same URL and directory, in-flight coalescing can cross the authorization boundary: a caller can receive data fetched under another caller's credentials. The issue affects the response returned by the shared promise, not only whether the second network call is saved.

## Acceptance criteria

- Do not coalesce requests with different `Authorization` values (or safely include authorization identity in the key without exposing secrets in logs/state).
- Add a regression test with overlapping same-URL requests and different bearer tokens; each caller must receive only the response for its own credential, and the distinct requests must not share one fetch.
- Keep coalescing for truly identical safe reads, including requests with the same authorization context and directory.

body:
## Evidence

Verified on current `origin/main` `b9c8327dce20266aa77cd9e41d070b555680e4f8`. In `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/template-runtime.js:175-203`, `fetchLastAssistantMessageText(sessionId, messageId, ...)` fetches only the newest five messages, looks for the requested assistant ID (`:197-200`), then falls back to any newest stopped assistant message when that lookup misses (`:201-203`). The completion handler passes the finishing message ID at `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/runtime.js:642-645`.

A direct reproduction against the real function: the messages endpoint returns one stopped assistant message `{ id: "newer-message", content: "newer unrelated answer" }`; requesting `fetchLastAssistantMessageText("session-1", "requested-message")` returns `newer unrelated answer`. Thus, if the requested message is absent from the bounded page (for example, because newer messages arrived before a delayed completion notification is rendered), the `{last_message}` variable can contain a different turn’s answer.

## Why it matters

Completion notifications can attribute unrelated or stale assistant output to the turn that just finished. The notification may be misleading, and potentially expose content from another turn in the user-visible notification.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- When a non-empty `messageId` was supplied but is absent from the fetched page, do not substitute a different message; return empty or use a bounded retry/read strategy that confirms the requested ID.
- Preserve the existing newest-stopped-assistant fallback only when no message ID was supplied.
- Add tests for requested ID found, requested ID absent while a different stopped assistant is present, no requested ID fallback, and empty/error page behavior.

All-state issue searches for `fetchLastAssistantMessageText`, notification message-ID fallback, stale assistant notification, and completion `last_message` found no direct issue. Closed #1948 concerns surrogate-safe truncation inside the same module, not message selection. All-state PR search found no matching implementation.

labels.name: kind/performance

labels.name: source/creator

body:
## Evidence

Verified against current `origin/main` `b48160561d0bf8c77c42496e83f39460c025e111`. `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-sessions/session-linked-issues.js:23-33` accepts an arbitrary array of entries whose `id`, `title`, and `url` have no size limits; `linkOperationSchema` has no entry-count limit. The endpoint at `routes.js:1524-1526` accepts JSON up to 1 MiB and passes the full parsed operation to `setSessionLinks`.

`buildLinkedIssuesPatch` (`session-linked-issues.js:90-98`) loops once per incoming entry and filters the current list on every iteration; when linking (`linked: true`) it also appends each item before the next full filter. Thus one valid batch can make the work grow quadratically with the batch/current-list sizes. Each call can also append more unique entries to the persisted `openchamber.linked_issues` array, which has no total-entry or serialized-size cap, so repeated requests can grow the metadata and future update cost without bound. The HTTP byte cap limits one request body but does not cap cumulative stored state or provide an explicit work budget.

The focused test command could not run in this checkout because dependencies are absent (`zod` is not installed); source-level verification was performed on the current-main blob.

## Why it matters

A large but valid linked-issue operation can occupy the serialized session metadata update with repeated full-array scans and write a large metadata value. Repeated smaller operations can grow the list indefinitely, making ordinary future link/unlink operations progressively more expensive.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Define explicit limits for incoming batch count and `id`/`title`/`url` sizes, and reject over-limit operations with a clear 400 before changing metadata.
- Bound the stored linked-issue list or total serialized size so repeated unique links cannot grow session metadata without limit; define behavior for already-oversized legacy lists.
- Avoid a full list filter per entry (for example, perform identity matching/deduplication in one bounded pass) so accepted work has a clear linear budget.
- Add tests at each limit and just beyond it, verify rejected requests do not partially modify the list, and pin that accepted batch work preserves the existing identity/re-link semantics.

All-state searches for session-link batch limits, `linked_issues` bounds, linked metadata size, and `setSessionLinks` found no direct duplicate. Closed #1975 fixed the surrogate boundary for titles in the older `session-link.js` builder; it does not bound the incoming batch schema or persisted list in `session-linked-issues.js`. Open/all-state PR searches found no implementation for these bounds.

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` `398f9469bd0f1a140d2ab4a20da67aac7569e250`, `packages/ui/src/contexts/ThemeSystemContext.tsx:220-255` loads `/api/config/themes`. A 401 intentionally returns for the UI auth gate, but other non-OK responses return silently (`:239-241`); JSON/schema/network failures are also swallowed by the empty catch (`:244-251`). `finally` only clears `customThemesLoading` (`:252-255`), leaving `customThemes` at its empty/default value. The theme picker in `packages/ui/src/components/sections/openchamber/OpenChamberVisualSettings.tsx:489-507` then continues displaying the available fallback themes, and its reload control at `:510-535` provides no failure feedback. A user can therefore see fallback themes while imported themes failed to load, with no indication to retry or diagnose the problem.

Reproduce by making `GET /api/config/themes` return HTTP 500, invalid JSON, or a payload that fails `themeListSchema`; open Visual Settings and observe that loading ends without an error or status message. The 401 auth-gate behavior should remain quiet. Existing context tests cover stale reload ordering but do not assert visible handling of load failures.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Preserve the existing fallback behavior, but retain a recoverable load-error state for non-401 HTTP errors, invalid payloads, and network failures.
- Surface a concise failure/status in Visual Settings (and keep the reload action available) so users can distinguish a successful empty theme list from a failed request.
- Clear the error on a later successful reload; keep stale-request/runtime-key guards intact.
- Add focused tests for HTTP failure, malformed payload or rejected fetch, successful recovery, and the intentionally quiet 401 path.

All-state issue searches for custom-theme load errors, theme fetch failures, `/api/config/themes`, and `ThemeSystemContext` found no matching issue; open-PR search for theme-load/custom-theme errors found no implementation. Related theme-loader PRs #1942 and #1723 address filesystem safety and read-size limits, not user-visible load failures.

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` `398f9469bd0f1a140d2ab4a20da67aac7569e250`, `packages/web/server/lib/markdown-image-grants/routes.js:155-175` scans each assistant text part and initializes `let fence = null` inside the per-part loop. The parser therefore forgets an open Markdown code fence at a content-part boundary. `markdownImageSources` then extracts image syntax from the next part (`:178-215`), and the grant endpoint accepts a source when it appears in that set (`:351-365`).

Repro input: an assistant message whose first text part is ```` ```md ```` and whose next text part contains `![hidden](/path/to/valid.png)` followed by the closing fence. The image is inside fenced code, but the second part is scanned as outside code and can authorize a grant. Existing test `packages/web/server/lib/markdown-image-grants/routes.test.js:262-270` verifies a single-part fence and does not cover a fence spanning parts.

All-state issue searches for `"markdown image grant"`, `"fenced code" image`, and `markdownImageSources` found no matching issue. Related closed #1785, #934, and #1285 concern FIFO inspection, dead grant machinery, and response size bounds respectively. All-state PR search for `markdown image grant fenced` found no matching implementation.

## Why it matters

This parser is the authority check that prevents a remote client from minting image grants for paths not actually referenced by the assistant message. Misreading code examples as live Markdown weakens that boundary and may grant access to a local image path merely mentioned in a code sample.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve fenced-code state across adjacent text parts while continuing to ignore non-text parts.
- Add a regression test with the opening fence in one text part, an image reference in another, and the closing fence in a later part; the image source must not be authorized.
- Preserve existing authorization for image references outside fences and existing single-part fenced/inline-code behavior.

The focused test could not be run in this checkout: `bun run --cwd packages/web test -- server/lib/markdown-image-grants/routes.test.js` exits 127 because `vitest` is not installed.

title: fix(vscode): bound selected text before attaching it to context
body:
## Evidence

The VS Code `openchamber.addToContext` command reads the entire active-editor selection with `editor.document.getText(selection)` (`packages/vscode/src/extension.ts:401-402`) and forwards that string unchanged to the active panel or chat view (`:417-428`). In the WebView, the `addContextSelection` handler wraps the full string in a `Blob` and `File` (`packages/vscode/webview/main.tsx:1545-1562`), then `addVSCodeSelectionAttachment` calls `readFileAsDataUrl(file, file.type)` and stores both the `File` and resulting data URL in application state (`packages/ui/src/sync/input-store.ts:426-455`). There is no selection-size check at any of these boundaries.

A large editor selection therefore incurs multiple full-size representations (string, Blob/File, base64 data URL) and is retained in UI state, with no bounded failure path. This can cause excessive memory use or make the WebView unresponsive/crash. The issue is source-verified; it has not been reproduced in a live VS Code instance.

## Suggested fix

Define an explicit maximum selection/attachment size. Reject or clearly warn in the extension before forwarding oversized selections, and validate again in the WebView/store boundary before constructing a Blob or reading it as a data URL so other message producers cannot bypass the limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Oversized selections are not forwarded or retained, and the user receives a clear actionable message.
- The WebView/store path independently enforces the same bound before allocating/encoding the attachment.
- Tests cover a selection just below the limit and one above it at both boundaries.
- Existing normal-sized Add to Context behavior remains unchanged.

## Finding

Both credential redactors still leak credentials in single-quoted shapes. PR #2083 (fixing #2074) taught `redactSensitiveText` and `redactGitText` to redact double-quoted JSON values and scheme-headed assignments, but every new pattern anchors on a double quote (`"?\s*[:=]\s*"`) or on a bare `:`/`=` immediately after the key. A single quote between key and colon, or around the value, defeats all of them — and in the scheme-headed colon form the plain pattern redacts the quoted scheme word `'Bearer` instead and leaves the token itself.

Single-quoted credential shapes are realistic log/error text: Python-style dict reprs (`{'Authorization': 'Bearer …'}`) from helper tooling, single-quoted JS object dumps, and hand-logged header objects.

## Evidence

- PR #2083 — https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2083 (MERGED, merge commit 02cbf091378f40d9ed2c6d7b686bbda6b6ca290a, closes #2074). Its added patterns on current main 158baff0c4af4f3b630e3f6dbcafe5fae8997fd3:
  - `packages/web/server/lib/source-control/url-redaction.js:66` quoted pattern and `:71` scheme-headed pattern; `:61`/`:72` neighbours share the same double-quote/bare-separator assumption.
  - `packages/web/server/lib/git/redaction.js:64` quoted pattern and `:65` scheme-headed pattern (converged twin, #1920).
- Probe against the real modules fetched from current main (158baff, two contents reads), fake token, run twice with identical results (`probe4-result.txt`, `probe-git-result.txt` in the lane evidence dir):
  - `{'x-api-key': '<token>'}` → unchanged, token leaks (both redactors)
  - `{'password': '<token>'}` → unchanged, token leaks (both)
  - `{'authorization': 'Bearer <token>'}` → unchanged, token leaks (both)
  - `authorization: 'Bearer <token>'` → `authorization=[redacted] <token>'` — the scheme word is redacted, the token leaks (both)
  - Control: `{"authorization": "Bearer <token>"}` (the #2083 shape) → correctly redacted (both)
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-11 for redact/single-quote returned only #1920 and #2074 (both CLOSED — they covered bare, scheme-headed, and double-quoted shapes). No open issue covers single-quoted shapes. The primary pr-diff-review lane reviewed the same batch (PRs #2046–#2085) on 2026-11-11 15:24 CST and filed nothing on #2083.

## Why it matters

These redactors are the last line before git/source-control error text and diagnostics are shown to users and agents. The family has now leaked three times in successive residuals (#1920 → #2074 → this one) because each fix enumerates quote styles instead of treating a quoted value generically. A credential in an error message is exposed exactly when something already went wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both `redactSensitiveText` (url-redaction.js) and `redactGitText` (redaction.js) redact the credential — preserving key, separator, scheme word, and quote style — for at least: `{'x-api-key': '<t>'}`, `{'password': '<t>'}`, `{'authorization': 'Bearer <t>'}`, and `authorization: 'Bearer <t>'`.
- Regression tests pin the single-quoted shapes in both redactors' suites, alongside the existing double-quoted cases; credential-free text stays byte-identical and all existing redaction outputs are unchanged.
- A short audit note in the PR for any remaining quote/separator shape the patterns still cannot see (or none, if the fix generalizes the quoted-value pattern).

body:
`downloadAsMarkdown()` in `packages/ui/src/lib/exportSession.ts:143-152` creates a Blob URL, clicks a temporary download anchor, removes it, and revokes the URL immediately in the same call stack. The click initiates the browser download, but the browser may consume the Blob URL asynchronously; revoking it immediately can race that read and make a Markdown export fail or produce an incomplete file.

Both the current-session export (`packages/ui/src/components/layout/Header.tsx:497-499`) and session-tree export (`packages/ui/src/components/session/sidebar/sessions/SessionNodeItem.tsx:827-829`) use this fallback. The analogous file download helper in `packages/web/src/api/files.ts:406-413` defers revocation with a 100 ms timer, while the Markdown export helper has no delay. This is a source-backed browser-timing risk; I did not reproduce it in a browser.

## Acceptance criteria

- Do not revoke the Blob URL in the same synchronous call stack as `anchor.click()`; use a cleanup mechanism that gives the browser time to consume the download URL.
- Add a focused test for the required ordering/lifecycle behavior, and verify the Markdown export downloads the complete content in the supported browser test/manual check.
- Preserve the current filename, MIME type, and both export call paths.

body:
## Finding

The Mistral quota provider added in PR #1633 selects its API key with a nullish chain but judges configured-ness with a truthiness chain, so the two disagree for an entry whose earlier field is an empty (or whitespace) string: `isConfigured` says the provider is configured, while the fetch either reports "Not configured" or sends the empty/whitespace value as the bearer token and reports the real credential as invalid. Sibling providers avoid exactly this by selecting through `asNonEmptyString` (e.g. `kimi.js`: `asNonEmptyString(entry?.key) ?? asNonEmptyString(entry?.token)`).

## Evidence

- PR #1633 (https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/1633), MERGED, merge 36e12d7b8a9b, for #1619.
- Current main 8f61a0fd3f9849606a6d976b824431f2bd82ce36 (verified twice), `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/mistral.js`:
  - `isConfigured`: `Boolean(entry?.key || entry?.token || entry?.access)` — an empty `key` falls through to a real `token`/`access`.
  - `fetchQuotaForEntry`: `const apiKey = entry?.key ?? entry?.token ?? entry?.access;` — `??` does **not** fall through on `''`, so the empty string wins; the following `if (!apiKey)` then returns `configured: false, error: 'Not configured'`.
  - A whitespace-only `key` (`'   '`) is truthy, so it is selected and sent as `Authorization: Bearer    `, producing a 401 that the provider classifies as "Invalid or revoked API key" even when a valid `token`/`access` sits in the same entry.
  - `normalizeAuthEntry` (`quota/utils/auth.js`) returns object entries unmodified — it does not trim or drop empty fields, so nothing upstream cleans this shape.
- Probe (the verbatim selection expressions, laptop Node): entry `{key: '', token: 'real-token-value'}` → `isConfigured` = `true`, selected apiKey = `""`, fetch verdict = "Not configured" (`configured: false`). Entry `{key: '   ', access: 'real-access'}` → selected apiKey = `"   "`.

## Why it matters

The quota board's job is honest credential state. A stored entry with an empty first field (a half-written enrollment, an OAuth-shaped entry carrying `access` beside an empty `key`) currently flips between "configured" and "not configured" depending on which function you ask, or misreports a live credential as revoked — the two failure shapes this provider's classification design (#1619) was built to keep distinct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Key selection in `mistral.js` treats empty/whitespace fields as absent (the `asNonEmptyString` pattern the sibling providers use), so `isConfigured` and `fetchQuota`/`fetchQuotaForCredential` can never disagree.
- [ ] New `mistral.test.js` cases: `{key: '', token: <valid>}` fetches with the token; `{key: '   ', access: <valid>}` fetches with the access value; an all-empty entry reports not configured from both entry points.
- [ ] Existing mistral tests (valid key, 401/403, malformed 200, transport failure) stay green.

body:
## Summary

`bun run test` fails on clean `main` (5df5db566) in exactly one file: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.test.js` cannot load because its `./quotaCredentials` mock does not provide the `MANAGED_PROVIDERS` export that `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.ts` now imports.

## Evidence

- Verification run for the opencode-update acceptance gate, run 43652377452 (2026-11-14T23:16Z, head 5df5db566, workflow_dispatch): `nix build .#openchamber` passed; full test suite 105/106 files passed in the vscode leg, 1 failed — `src/bridge-system-runtime.test.js`: "Unhandled error between tests — SyntaxError: Export named 'MANAGED_PROVIDERS' not found in module '.../packages/vscode/src/quotaCredentials.ts'". Run concluded failure; FAILED_STEP recorded as `bun run test`.
- Reproduced locally on a clean checkout of main @5df5db566 (2026-11-14T23:55Z): `bun test src/bridge-system-runtime.test.js` in `packages/vscode` fails with the identical SyntaxError.

## Root cause

- b0173cf9a (#2283, for #2281) added `export const MANAGED_PROVIDERS` to `packages/vscode/src/quotaCredentials.ts` (line 13) and made `bridge-system-runtime.ts` import it (line 12, used at line 609 for the credentials allowlist).
- `bridge-system-runtime.test.js` mocks `./quotaCredentials` via `mock.module` (around line 60) with only the function exports (credentialStatus, deleteCredential, importCursorCredential, normalizeCredential, readCredential, validateCredential, writeCredential). The mock predates #2283 and lacks `MANAGED_PROVIDERS`, so Bun's ESM linker rejects the import of the module under test.

## Fix

Add `MANAGED_PROVIDERS` to the `mock.module('./quotaCredentials', ...)` factory in `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.test.js`, mirroring the real export: `['exe-dev', 'cursor', 'zenmux', 'opendesign']`. Oracle: the real export in `quotaCredentials.ts:13`; the manifest conformance test `quotaProviderManifest.test.ts` derives the same list from source.

## Acceptance

- `bun test src/bridge-system-runtime.test.js` passes in `packages/vscode`.
- The vscode leg of `bun run test` passes (no other file regresses).
- A main-branch `opencode-update` run gets past the test gate (this is the acceptance gate for #1587 / task 9587, which is dep-blocked on this issue).

Filed by repo queue lane any-a (task 9587) — second distinct pre-existing main failure found by the #1587 verification runs, routed to its own track like #2284.

title: fix(vscode): Open Design credential management is unwired in the VS Code surface — bridge allowlist and webview route interceptor still exclude 'opendesign'

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.description: Epic: opencode-platform - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Problem

PR #2279 ported the Open Design quota fetcher into the VS Code backend and
flipped the manifest to `vscode_dispatch: true` / `vscode_configured: true`
for `opendesign` (see `packages/web/server/lib/quota/provider-manifest.json`).
The conformance test (`packages/vscode/src/quotaProviderManifest.test.ts`) only
checks the dispatch switch and the configured set in `quotaProviders.ts`, so it
passes. But the **credential-management** path — the one a user actually
touches to store, validate, or delete an Open Design session cookie — was not
updated, so the feature is unreachable from the VS Code UI:

1. `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.ts:609` — the
   `api:quota:credentials` handler rejects any provider not in the hardcoded
   list `['exe-dev', 'cursor', 'zenmux']` with `"Unsupported credential
   provider"`. `'opendesign'` is missing, so GET/PUT/DELETE/VALIDATE all
   fail before the handler body runs.
2. `packages/vscode/webview/main.tsx:1297` — the fetch interceptor regex
   `^/api/quota/credentials/(exe-dev|cursor|zenmux)(?:/(validate|import))?$`
   does not match `/api/quota/credentials/opendesign`, so even if the bridge
   were fixed the shared quota Settings UI would never route the request to
   the bridge (it would attempt a real fetch and fail in the extension
   host).
3. `packages/vscode/src/quotaCredentials.ts:99` — `validateCredential` has no
   `opendesign` branch (only `zenmux`, `exe-dev`, `cursor`). So a PUT that
   reached the handler would call `validateCredential` as a no-op and store
   the credential without ever checking the session — accepting an expired or
   malformed cookie. The web surface validates via
   `validateOpenDesignCredential` (`packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/opendesign.js:181`).

Net effect: the VS Code surface advertises Open Design quota support (manifest
+ fetcher + `listConfiguredQuotaProviders`), can display quota when the
credential file was written by the web surface, but cannot create, edit,
validate, or delete an Open Design credential itself. This is the same class
of defect #1744/#1757/#1735 closed for the *fetch* path, now present on the
*credential* path.

## Evidence

- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.ts:609` (hardcoded allowlist).
- `packages/vscode/webview/main.tsx:1297` (interceptor regex).
- `packages/vscode/src/quotaCredentials.ts:99` (validateCredential, no opendesign branch).
- Web counterparts that DO support opendesign:
  - `packages/web/server/lib/quota/credentials/store.js:7` (`MANAGED_QUOTA_PROVIDERS` includes `'opendesign'`).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/quota/credentials/providers.js:19` (normalizer).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/quota/routes.js:18,56,70` (validator wiring).
  - `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/opendesign.js:181` (`validateOpenDesignCredential`).
- `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviderManifest.test.ts` only asserts the dispatch
  switch and configured set, so it does not catch the bridge/webview drift.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix shape

1. Add `'opendesign'` to the bridge allowlist in `bridge-system-runtime.ts:609`
   (ideally derive the list from `ManagedProvider`/a shared constant instead of
   a literal, so the next provider port can't drift the same way).
2. Extend the webview interceptor regex in `main.tsx:1297` to include
   `opendesign` (e.g. `(exe-dev|cursor|zenmux|opendesign)`).
3. Add an `opendesign` branch to `validateCredential` in `quotaCredentials.ts`
   that mirrors `validateOpenDesignCredential` — fetch
   `${OPEN_DESIGN_API_BASE_URL}/auth/get-session` with the stored cookie and
   `x-vela-workspace-id` header and throw `OPEN_DESIGN_SESSION_EXPIRED_ERROR`
   (imported from `quotaProviders.ts`) when the session is not an object.
4. Extend the manifest conformance test to assert the bridge allowlist and the
   webview interceptor regex match the managed-credential provider set, so a
   future port cannot silently leave the credential path unwired.

## Notes

- `command-code` is intentionally not in this path: it reads its key from
  OpenCode's auth store, not the managed credential store, so no credential
  management is needed there.

## Finding

PR #2117 — the fix for issue #2115 (replace the six literal NUL bytes in `packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js` with `\0` escapes) — is OPEN but can no longer merge: GitHub reports it conflicted, and the fix is still needed on current main.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-12, main `6c34b89a6fb9324f8b1c89a44ebebde5a7c7867c`)

- `gh api repos/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pulls/2117`: `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: "dirty"`; head `cab38808514e31ce463ba8a23ab8770cf08d1e87`, base `8d6bd5c68690`. Compare head…main: diverged, 1 ahead / 17 behind.
- Cause: PR #2119 (merged `ef7e6352bc4f`, closing issue #2116) rewrote the same file after PR #2117 branched from the same base. Because the file contains literal NUL bytes, git treats it as binary, so the two changes cannot be merged textually — both-modified binary is a hard conflict.
- The fix is still needed: issue #2115 is OPEN, and a byte scan of `run-history.js` on current main (contents API) finds **10 literal NUL bytes** at offsets 1656, 1666, 3759, 3777, 4463, 4481, 5530, 5539, 6656, 6677. PR #2119's retention code added four more NUL-joined key-template sites beyond the six PR #2117 escaped. PR #2117's head file has 0 NULs but is 4,913 bytes against main's 7,715 — it predates the retention bound and cannot simply be force-landed.
- Dedupe: `gh search issues` for "2117" returns only issue #2115 itself; no shepherd/tracking issue exists for this PR.

## Shepherd outcome wanted

Land the #2115 fix on current main and dispose of PR #2117: either rebase/recreate its change on top of current `run-history.js` (escaping **all 10** current NUL sites while preserving PR #2119's retention code and tests), or close PR #2117 with a comment naming the replacement PR. Issue #2115 should close when the landed fix merges.

## Acceptance criteria

- `run-history.js` on main contains 0 literal NUL bytes (byte scan via contents API) and its diff renders as text on GitHub.
- The `\0` escapes preserve the exact runtime key separators (existing run-history tests pass, including PR #2119's retention tests).
- PR #2117 is closed (not silently left conflicted) with a comment naming the landed replacement / merge commit.
- Issue #2115 is closed by the landed fix.

title: fix(web): scheduled-tasks run-history.js contains literal NUL bytes — git/GitHub treat the source file as binary, hiding its diffs

body:
## Finding

`packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js` — the new durable scheduled-task run-history store added by PR #2082 — contains **6 literal NUL bytes (0x00) embedded in source** on current main, used as key separators inside template literals instead of the `\0` escape sequence:

- `run-history.js` — `runKey` template: `` `${projectID}<NUL>${taskID}<NUL>${sessionID ?? ''}` `` (byte offsets 1053, 1063 in the file as served by the contents API)
- `run-history.js` — the load-time `appendedTerminalKeys.add(...)` template (byte offsets 2050, 2068)
- `run-history.js` — the `dedupeKey` template (byte offsets 3381, 3390)

Verified this run against current main (`8d6bd5c68690df38bb5df8a42f189e95a96bc52d`): fetched the file via the GitHub contents API, counted 6 NUL bytes, all inside those three template literals.

## Why it matters

Git and GitHub classify any file containing a NUL byte as **binary**. Consequences, already visible:

- PR #2082's own diff renders this file as "Binary files /dev/null and b/packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js differ" — the new store's implementation was never reviewable in the PR diff.
- Every future PR touching this file will likewise show no text diff on GitHub, and `git grep` / `git diff` / blame tooling treats it as binary, hiding changes to the run-history evidence store from normal review.

The runtime behaviour is correct (a NUL separator works), which is exactly why this slipped through: only the review/tooling surface is broken.

## Fix shape

Replace each literal NUL byte in the three template literals with the escape sequence `\0` (identical runtime string, plain-text source). No other change needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run-history.js` contains zero NUL bytes (byte scan) and `git check-attr diff` / a test PR diff renders it as text
- [ ] The existing `run-history.test.js` suite still passes unchanged (dedupe keys are byte-identical at runtime)
- [ ] A repo-wide byte scan finds no other committed source file with literal NUL bytes, or any found are filed/fixed the same way

Found by: pr-diff-review job, PR #2082 review (merge commit `e3d45067fae1`).

body:
## Problem

The Linear workflow-states truncation signal `statesMore` is produced by the server, passed through the web API, and declared on the UI type — but no UI consumer ever reads it. The one place workflow states are shown, the Source Board state picker, silently presents a first-page-only list as if it were complete.

## Evidence (verified on main `2d834f82c7474b3f45b15058941f2fe068920ca7`, laptop tree + probe x2 identical)

- Server builds the signal deliberately: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/issues.js:157-159` — comment "A team holds a handful of workflow states; one page of 50 covers every real team, and statesMore says when it did not", `STATES_PAGE = 50`, `STATES_QUERY` requests `states(first: 50)` with `pageInfo { hasNextPage }`.
- Server returns it: `packages/web/server/lib/linear/issues.js:584` — `return { connected: true, states, statesMore: readPageInfo(connection).hasMore }` from `listLinearIssueStates`. Server tests pin both values (`issues.test.js:655` false, `:677` true past one page).
- Web API passes it through: `packages/web/src/api/linear.ts:334` — `return { connected: true, states, statesMore: payload?.statesMore === true }` in `toIssueStates`; `issueStates()` at `:543`.
- UI type declares it: `packages/ui/src/lib/api/types.ts:2316` — `statesMore?: boolean` on `LinearIssueStatesResult`, documented "True when the team holds more workflow states than the one page fetched."
- Sole UI consumer drops it: `packages/ui/src/components/sourceBoard/SourceBoardLinearStatus.tsx:34-47` — `useTeamStates` stores only `{ teamId, states }` (`setLoaded({ teamId, states: ... })` at `:42`) and returns `LinearWorkflowState[]`; the string `statesMore` appears nowhere in the component. The dropdown at `:106` maps only the fetched states, with no truncation note, no disabled/overflow item, and no other indication.
- Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-statesmore-20261107/probe.py`, run twice, identical): `ui_consumers_outside_types = []` — no file under `packages/ui/src` other than the type declaration references `statesMore` at all.
- Siblings are all consumed, which makes this the odd one out in the same family: `commentsMore` is read in `packages/ui/src/lib/linearIssueContext.ts:14`, `subIssuesMore` in `packages/ui/src/components/references/ReferencePreview.tsx:522,531`, and `teamsMore` is now read via `linearProjectMapping.ts` after #1732.

## Why it matters

For a team with more than 50 workflow states, the Source Board picker is silently incomplete: states past the first page cannot be selected, so an issue cannot be moved to them from OpenChamber, and nothing tells the user the list is partial (the design #1528 contract: complete, or say so). If the issue's current state is itself past the first page, it also does not appear in its own picker. The server and API layers did the work to signal this; the last hop drops it.

Dedup: `gh` search over open and closed issues for `statesMore`, `SourceBoardLinearStatus`, and workflow-states truncation returned only #1599 (labels connection, a different field), #1598/#1732 (teams), and #1414 (comments) — none covers `statesMore` or the Source Board picker. Related: #1528 (completeness contract), #1732 (teamsMore sibling, fixed).

## Acceptance criteria

- When `issueStates` returns `statesMore: true`, the Source Board state picker visibly says the list is incomplete (e.g. a non-selectable note item in the dropdown, in the existing i18n style/locales pattern used for the teamsMore note), or the picker fetches the remaining pages so the list is actually complete.
- When `statesMore` is false/absent, picker behaviour is unchanged.
- A test pins the disposition: a `statesMore: true` result produces the truncation indication (or the completed list), and a false/absent result does not.
- No change to the server query, `STATES_PAGE`, or the `LinearIssueStatesResult` shape — the signal already exists end to end to the UI type.

body:
## Problem

The shared quota board offers Command Code and Open Design — both are in `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` and in the `QuotaProviderId` union — but the VS Code quota backend has no implementation for either: not a fetcher, not a dispatch case, not a configured-provider entry, not one mention in `packages/vscode/src`. In the VS Code runtime every board fetch for these two providers returns `Unsupported provider`, and a user who holds the credentials can never see either pool in the extension, while the same board on the web runtime (whose server registry implements both) works.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `8f61a0fd3f9849606a6d976b824431f2bd82ce36`, laptop primary, read twice)

- `packages/ui/src/lib/quota/providers/index.ts:12,37` — `QUOTA_PROVIDERS` lists `{ id: 'command-code', name: 'Command Code' }` and `{ id: 'opendesign', name: 'Open Design' }`; `packages/ui/src/types/quota.ts` includes both ids in `QuotaProviderId`. `packages/ui/src/stores/useQuotaStore.ts` derives the board's fetch list from this catalog, so the VS Code surface requests both ids exactly like the web surface.
- `packages/vscode/src/bridge-system-runtime.ts:642` — the extension's `api:quota:get` handler answers board fetches with `fetchQuotaForProvider(providerId)` from `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts`.
- `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts:4755-4844` — `fetchQuotaForProviderUncoalesced` has 27 cases (`claude` … `xai`); there is no `command-code`, `opendesign` (or `mistral`) case, so both fall to the `default:` at :4833-4840 and return `{ ok: false, configured: false, error: 'Unsupported provider' }`.
- A case-insensitive grep for `command-code|commandcode|opendesign|open-design|mistral` over all of `packages/vscode/src` (excluding tests) returns zero hits: no fetcher, no `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` entry (:953ff adds 25+ providers, neither of these), no credential handling.
- The web backends exist and are tested: `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/command-code.js` (`providerId = 'command-code'`, reads the OpenCode auth entry / `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY`, 15 s deadline, plan-window derivation) and `opendesign.js` (`providerId = 'opendesign'`, managed session-cookie credential), both registered in `packages/web/server/lib/quota/providers/index.js`. The VS Code package already reads the same credential sources for sibling providers (OpenCode auth entries throughout `quotaProviders.ts`; managed credentials in `quotaCredentials.ts`).

Dedup: title/keyword search over open and closed issues for the VS Code quota dispatch / `command-code` / `opendesign` returns #1735 (OPEN — Mistral missing from the UI catalog; it notes this VS Code omission in one sentence as an "existing precedent" but files nothing for it and scopes its fix to the UI catalog), #1738 (OPEN — Copilot Add-on, implemented in VS Code, UI-catalog side only), #480 (CLOSED — the same unreachable-provider defect for Open Design on the *web* UI, fixed by adding the catalog entry the VS Code backend never matched). No issue covers porting these two fetchers to the VS Code backend. Mistral's VS Code case is deliberately left to #1735's disposition: it is not in the UI catalog yet, so the board does not request it in any runtime today; whoever lands #1735 should add the VS Code case in the same pass or file it then.

## Why it matters

The quota board is the fleet's measurement surface, and it is one shared UI over two backends. A provider that works on web and answers "Unsupported provider" in the extension is silent drift of exactly the kind the VS Code port exists to prevent (the port's history is a chain of per-provider parity fixes: #507–#517 clamps, #919/#912 planLabel, #911 credential source). Command Code is a live fleet pool (its web fetcher encodes Drew's 2026-11-01 plan-window read rule), so extension users lose a real reading, not a placeholder.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/vscode/src/quotaProviders.ts` implements `command-code` and `opendesign` fetchers mirroring the web providers' semantics (same endpoints, credential sources, deadlines, window derivation — including Command Code's plan-window-only rule and Open Design's import-required / session-expired errors), dispatched from `fetchQuotaForProviderUncoalesced`.
- [ ] `listConfiguredQuotaProviders` reports both providers when their credentials are present (and respects `disabled_providers` like sibling rows).
- [ ] VS Code quota tests cover both new fetchers (configured/unconfigured, success windows, auth failure), mirroring the web providers' test matrices; existing VS Code quota tests keep passing.
- [ ] A parity guard (test or shared list) names the deliberate VS Code exclusions, if any remain after this change, so the next web-only provider add is a visible decision rather than silent drift (shared with #1735/#1738's catalog-agreement criterion — reuse, don't duplicate).

body:
## Problem

`readMergedSettingsSync` in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-files.js` reads both settings files whole, synchronously, with no size cap and no regular-file check:

- `settings-files.js:201` — `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(settingsFilePath, 'utf8'))` buffers `settings.json` entire.
- `settings-files.js:208` — `parsePreferencesDocument(fs.readFileSync(preferencesFilePathFor(settingsFilePath, path), 'utf8'))` buffers `preferences.json` entire.

This is the documented hot-path reader ("Modules that read one profile key off the disk on a hot path use `readMergedSettingsSync`", `lib/opencode/DOCUMENTATION.md:608`). Its callers run it per operation, not once at startup:

- `lib/session-assist/runtime.js:21`
- `lib/session-goal/runtime.js:44`, `lib/session-goal/spec-writer.js:110`
- `lib/session-work/runtime.js:37`
- `lib/small-model/index.js:56`
- `lib/walkthrough/model-settings.js:29`

Unlike the shared bounded reader (`lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`, `readBoundedFileSync` — handle-judged, `O_NONBLOCK`, cap enforced during the read, missing / too-large / not-regular as distinct answers), this reader:

1. Buffers a file of any size into memory and parses it whole, on the server event loop, synchronously.
2. Blocks forever if either path is a FIFO (or another non-regular file that never yields EOF): `readFileSync` on a FIFO with no writer never returns, freezing the whole server, not just the calling feature.

## Evidence (verified this run, on laptop against the real module from `origin/main` @ `8cd11be40d`)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-settings-merged-ungated-20261104/` (real `settings-files.js` + `settings-registry.json` extracted from `origin/main`, real `node:fs` injected exactly as the production callers inject it), run ×2 with identical results:

- Control: small valid `settings.json` + `preferences.json` → merged document returned correctly.
- Oversize: `settings.json` of 33,554,448 bytes (valid JSON, one padded string value) → parsed whole and returned, `customKey` length 33,554,432. No rejection, no cap.
- FIFO: `settings.json` replaced by a FIFO with no writer → `readMergedSettingsSync` never returned within 3 s (probe killed by timeout, exit 124), both runs.

The settings files are legitimately small (instance facts + profile fields bounded by the settings registry), so a named cap has a schema-bounded worst case to be sized from at triage — the same disposition pattern as the other ungated-store filings in this series (e.g. #1615, #1627, #1628).

## Why it matters

- Availability: one bad file at either path (corrupt growth, a misplaced FIFO/symlink, a runaway writer) wedges every feature that consults a profile key — small-model resolution, goal/assist toggles, session work — and with them the server's event loop.
- Consistency: the repo has a house standard for exactly this read (`readBoundedFileSync`); this hot-path reader is an unconverted holdout, and it takes its `fs` by injection, so the bounded reader can be adopted without changing caller signatures.
- Semantics to preserve: a missing or unreadable file contributes `{}` per file and the caller's default applies ("missing is not default"); any conversion must keep missing distinct from too-large / not-regular rather than silently treating an oversize file as absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both reads in `readMergedSettingsSync` go through a bounded, handle-judged read (the shared `readBoundedFileSync` or an equivalent with the same answers), under a named byte-cap constant sized from the registry-bounded worst case, with the sizing rationale recorded.
- [ ] Missing-file behaviour is unchanged (contributes `{}` per file); too-large and not-regular files also contribute `{}` for that file but are distinguishable in a log/warning, never silently conflated with missing.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: an oversize `settings.json` and an oversize `preferences.json` are refused without being parsed whole, and a FIFO at either path returns promptly instead of blocking.
- [ ] Existing settings-files / settings runtime tests still pass.

body:
Found by the #1530 phase-2 inventory (design #1528). Surface: `packages/web/server/lib/github/routes.js`, canonical mutation reconciliation.

## The reads

Three single-page REST reads feed the canonical mutation reconcile / perform paths with no completeness disposition — no pagination, no `total_count`/Link check, no completeness flag:

- `routes.js:584` — `octokit.rest.pulls.list({ state: 'all', head, base, per_page: 100 })` in `reconcileCreateMutation`. The result decides uniqueness: exactly one candidate → `succeeded`, otherwise `outcome-unknown`. A second matching PR past page 1 is invisible, so a prefix can reach the affirmative verdict.
- `routes.js:613` — `octokit.rest.issues.listLabelsOnIssue({ per_page: 100 })` in `reconcileExistingMutation` (labels kinds). Set equality against the page-1 prefix decides `succeeded` vs `outcome-unknown`; labels past 100 can make a differing set read as equal.
- `routes.js:753` — `octokit.rest.pulls.listRequestedReviewers({ ... })` in `requestedReviewers` — no `per_page` at all (GitHub default 30), and only the `users` array is read. It feeds both the reviewers reconcile and `setReviewers` (:763), which diffs desired vs current and issues add/remove writes from the prefix.

## Why it matters

#1528's contract: a collection feeding a verdict either exhausts under a named cap (with the probe/error discipline of `lib/github/collections.js`) or degrades to an explicit unknown — it never resolves a prefix to the affirmative verdict. These three reads can.

## What done looks like

- Each read goes through a `collections.js` reader (or an equivalent named-cap loop with the probe-past-cap error), or carries an explicit completeness check that forces `outcome-unknown` when the set is provably larger than the page read.
- `requestedReviewers` also states what happens to team requests (currently dropped silently) or records why users-only is the product.
- Tests pin the over-page case for at least the reviewers diff and the create reconciliation.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three reads (routes.js pulls.list in reconcileCreateMutation, listLabelsOnIssue in reconcileExistingMutation, listRequestedReviewers in requestedReviewers) either exhausts under a named cap via a collections.js-style reader, or forces outcome-unknown when the set is provably larger than the page read.
- [ ] No prefix of a collection can reach an affirmative `succeeded` verdict.
- [ ] requestedReviewers reads with an explicit per_page and consumes the complete set before setReviewers diffs desired vs current.
- [ ] Tests demonstrate the more-than-one-page case for at least the uniqueness verdict in reconcileCreateMutation.

body:
## Problem

The per-user ("personal") project config — `<projectsDir>/<stem>.json`, holding a project's scheduled tasks, project setup, and loop approvals — is read with a plain whole-file `readFile` and **no size gate, no regular-file check, and no read bound**, on both surfaces:

- Web: `readJsonDocumentIfPresent` (`packages/web/server/lib/projects/project-config.js:546-560`, the `readFile` at :549) is the only reader behind `readRawProjectConfigFromDisk` (:562-568, current + legacy path). Every hot path funnels through it: `listScheduledTasks` (:682), task upserts/state updates, `readProjectSetup` (:1085), `updateProjectSetup` (:1090), loop approvals (:887), and shared-setup updates (:1111).
- VS Code twin: `packages/vscode/src/bridge-project-setup-runtime.ts:77-86` (the `readFile` at :80), used at :116 for the same personal file.

The sibling reader **in the same two files** shows the contract this path misses. The shared project config (`.openchamber/project.json`, #1247) is read by `readSharedConfigRaw` (web `project-config.js:1039-1070`; vscode twin at :141+) through an open handle with `O_NONBLOCK`, an `isFile()` rejection, a stat gate, and a capped read at `SHARED_PROJECT_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES` = 1 MiB (`project-setup.js:214`). Its comment (:1033-1038) spells out why: a path-based read "would follow a symlink to a device or FIFO (stat size 0) and buffer without bound, and a file swapped or grown between the two calls escapes the gate". The personal-config reader has none of those guards, and its writer is not capped either: `writeRawProjectConfigToDisk` (:621-640) serializes the whole document with no byte check (the shared writer checks at :1141), and untouched scheduled tasks are re-persisted from their raw on-disk records verbatim, so unknown/oversized fields a newer build or a hand edit put in the file are read whole and rewritten whole forever.

## Evidence (verified this run, main c0143eaa1ca27cb32216415eeb002ff339cb4b05)

- Code read in the laptop primary and re-verified via `gh api` raw contents (two channels agree) for all line references above, both twins.
- Laptop probe against the real `createProjectConfigRuntime` (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-personal-config-20261103/probe.mjs`, temp projects dir):
  - Control: a small valid config lists 0 tasks.
  - Oversized: a valid 33,554,465-byte config (32 MiB of padding in an unknown key) was **read whole and parsed in 41 ms with no size refusal** — 32× the 1 MiB cap the shared reader in the same file enforces.
  - FIFO: with a FIFO planted at the config path and no writer, `listScheduledTasks` never settled — the probe produced no further output and had to be killed at its 30 s timeout (exit 143). The shared reader rejects a non-regular file immediately instead of opening it.

## Why it matters

This is the #1254 "read it bounded" contract's remaining hole in the project-config module, and the asymmetry is the tell: the checkout-resident shared file got the full bounded treatment because a checkout is untrusted, but the personal file is also not exclusively this build's output — it is shared across processes (Electron, CLI serve, and the VS Code host all use the same projects dir; the file lock at :464+ exists precisely because multiple writers share it), preserved verbatim across builds with different field sets, and reachable by anything that can write the user's config dir (sync tools, other OpenChamber builds, a stray symlink). Today a bloated, planted, or non-regular file at that path either buffers unboundedly into a long-lived server on every task/setup read, or wedges the read outright. A bounded reader with the shared path's semantics (refuse non-regular, refuse over-cap, with the refusal surfaced rather than treated as "no config") closes it without changing any legitimate behavior: real personal configs are orders of magnitude under 1 MiB.

## Acceptance criteria

- The personal project-config read on both surfaces (web `project-config.js`, vscode `bridge-project-setup-runtime.ts`) goes through a bounded reader with the shared reader's semantics: open-handle read, non-regular files rejected, a named byte cap (the shared 1 MiB cap or a justified sibling constant), and growth past the cap during the read refused.
- An over-cap or non-regular personal config is surfaced as an error/invalid state — never silently treated as an empty/missing config, and never repaired by overwriting it from an empty read (the shared writer's too-large guard at :1137-1148 is the precedent).
- Regression tests on both surfaces: an over-cap file is refused (not buffered whole), a FIFO/non-regular path is refused promptly (no hang), and a normal config round-trips unchanged.
- Existing project-config / project-setup tests still pass (`project-config.test.js`, `project-setup.test.ts`).

Related: design #1254 (bounded-read contract), #1247 (the shared-config fix this is the residual of), #1410 (stat-then-read residual class). Filed by the new-issue-creator-openchamber run 2026-11-03 13:50 CST. Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-oc-personal-config-20261103/`.

title: fix(web): session-goal objective and version-history writes are not atomic — writeObjective and writeVersionList truncate the stored file in place, so a failed or interrupted save loses the objective or the whole version history

labels.name: area/web
labels.description: Web app

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The session-goal objective and its version history are written in place, with no temp-and-rename, so a failed or interrupted write can destroy the stored data.

- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js:82` — `writeObjective` calls `fs.promises.writeFile(objectiveFilePath(sessionId), text, 'utf8')` directly. `writeFile` opens the target with truncation first, so any failure after the open (ENOSPC, EIO, a process kill mid-write) leaves the previous objective truncated or empty.
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js:181` — `writeVersionList` rewrites the whole `*.versions.json` with the same pattern on every save and every prune. A failure there loses the entire retained version history, not just the newest entry.

Nothing else in `session-goal/` writes through a temp file: `grep -n writeFile packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/` returns only these two lines.

## Existing primitive

`writeDurableJsonFile(filePath, contents, { mode })` in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/durable-json-store.js:437` already does the safe thing: it writes a unique temp file in the same directory, renames it over the destination with retry, and removes the temp file on failure. It was introduced by closed design #976 for this kind of write. `mode` is required, so the call sites must state the file mode (the goal files are user data; use the mode they are created with today).

## Why this is distinct from closed issues

- #1372 (closed) fixed save ordering between the objective file and metadata. It did not address how each file is written.
- #1582 and #1949 (closed) cover reads and the clamp cut, not the write path.
- No open issue or PR touches `session-goal/objectives.js` writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- `writeObjective` and `writeVersionList` write through `writeDurableJsonFile` with an explicit `mode`, and the file mode is unchanged for existing goal files.
- A regression test in `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.test.js` injects a failure during the write (for example through the `fs` option the durable helper already accepts) and asserts that the previous objective and the previous versions file are still readable and unchanged afterwards.
- No temp file (`*.tmp-*`) remains in the goals directory after a failed write.
- The existing `objectives.test.js` cases still pass.

## Oracle

The test's expected result is the pre-failure content: after an injected failure, `readObjective` and the versions reader return exactly the values from before the write, and the goals directory lists no temp files.

body:
## Finding

`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/DOCUMENTATION.md` (line 480 on current main) still lists as a known gap that the v2 versioned store "is implemented and tested, but `lifecycle.js` still reads/writes the v1 `state.json` + `draining.json` pair until it is wired to the store". That wiring is exactly what merged PR #2322 did: `lifecycle.js` now loads/migrates/reaps the v2 store at factory creation and dual-writes it on every state transition for one release. The known-gaps line — the document's authoritative list of what is not done — now states the opposite of the shipped behaviour. The header comment in `managed-opencode-state.js` ("Replaces the v1 state.json + draining.json pair for reads/writes once lifecycle.js is wired to it") is also stale in the other direction: after #2322 the store does not replace the v1 pair yet; both are written, and the store is the ownership record for action paths.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2322 "Versioned v2 managed-OpenCode state store, write-ahead handoff, v1 migration, store-only reaper (#82)" — MERGED 2026-11-16T15:42:45Z, head `b4f37dfe2577a062de9089b294f602a3cf293366`, merge commit `7f561c20275b8172c6b1ed23e7db90d03f31bedf` (ancestor-verified against main: compare behind=0).
- PR #2322's own diff updated the DOCUMENTATION.md known-gaps line only to the intermediate store-layer wording ("implemented and tested, but lifecycle.js still reads/writes the v1 pair until it is wired"); the wiring commit in the same PR then made that sentence false.
- Wiring visible in the #2322 diff (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/lifecycle.js`): `syncStore(() => loadManagedStore())` at factory creation; `writeOwnState` -> `recordGenerationStart`; `clearOwnState`/`clearManagedStateIfOwned` -> `closeGenerationForPid`; `persistDrainingOpenCode` advances store generations to `draining`; `isOwnedOpenCodePid` consults non-closed store generations first.
- Verified on current main (`8dfacfb962e7d6e665b6348b0a59845322ffc35c`, PR #2327's merge): `DOCUMENTATION.md:480` still reads "...but `lifecycle.js` still reads/writes the v1 `state.json` + `draining.json` pair until it is wired to the store; upgrade handoff (a newer install taking over) is not done (see `TODO.md`)."

## Why it matters

The managed-OpenCode lifecycle is safety-sensitive (ownership, signalling, handoff). A maintainer or agent trusting the known-gaps list would believe the v2 store is dead code and the v1 pair is the only record — the reverse of the action-path truth — and could "clean up" the store wiring or debug ownership against the wrong source. The remaining real gap in that sentence (upgrade handoff not done) should stay; only the store-wiring claim is stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DOCUMENTATION.md` known-gaps line updated: the v2 store is wired into `lifecycle.js` as a dual-write with the v1 pair for one release, the store is the ownership record for action paths, and the v1 pair's retirement is the remaining step; the upgrade-handoff gap stays listed.
- [ ] The `managed-opencode-state.js` v2 header comment is aligned with the same dual-write reality (no "replaces ... once wired" future tense).
- [ ] No code or behaviour change; `lifecycle.js` and the store suites are untouched and still pass.

body:
## Evidence

`POST /api/session-knowledge/pin` (`packages/web/server/lib/session-knowledge/routes.js:54-67`) validates `sessionId`, `directory`, `kind`, and `pinned`, but the `id` only passes `asNonEmptyString` — no length cap, no existence check, no set-size cap. `setPin` (`packages/web/server/lib/session-knowledge/runtime.js:368-385`) unions any such id into the persisted pin set via `persistSessionMetadata` with no bound.

Probe against the real runtime with stub deps (read/store only):

```
await rt.setPin('s1', '/tmp', 'note', 'x'.repeat(5000), true);
await rt.setPin('s1', '/tmp', 'note', 'y'.repeat(5000), true);
await rt.setPin('s1', '/tmp', 'note', 'constructor', true);
// -> notes count: 3, first len: 5000, stored bytes: 10083
```

Every call with a fresh junk id permanently grows that session's metadata store (each id up to the 1 MB route body cap); unknown ids match nothing in `collect`/`collectSummary`, so the growth buys nothing. `readPins` dedupes but never trims.

## Why it matters

Same shape as #2113 (project-context todo-ID bounds before writing `context.json`): client-supplied IDs persisted into a JSON store need a bound, or a buggy or hostile local client can bloat session metadata without limit, and every later `sync`/`collectSummaryForSession` re-reads the bloated store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pin `id` rejected (400) when it exceeds a documented max length (project-context precedent: 1000 chars) or when the pin set for the kind is already at a documented max count.
- [ ] Optionally: pinning an id that matches no known note/plan is rejected or warned, so junk never persists.
- [ ] Regression test through `setPin`/`readPins` (or the route): oversized id rejected, over-count pin rejected, valid pin still round-trips.

body:
## Summary
`saveChats` in `space-archive.js` caps each chat at 256 MiB (`CHAT_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES`) and the chat count at 1000 (`ARCHIVE_MAX_CHATS`), but enforces **no total budget**. A space delete stages every exported chat to `.incoming-<spaceId>` on the host's dataDir disk *before* the first import, so one hostile or merely large space can stage up to ~256 GiB (1000 x 256 MiB) plus JSON stringify/parse copies in memory. The all-or-nothing refusal (`chats_not_saved`) happens only *after* the take-out loop, so the disk is already consumed even when the save ultimately throws.

## Where
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-archive.js:27` — `ARCHIVE_MAX_CHATS = 1000`
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-archive.js:231-250` — take-out loop: every chosen chat `exportChat` -> `writeFileSync(.incoming/<id>.json)` before any import ("Each chat is taken out and written to disk before any goes in")
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-archive.js:251,300-310` — `!allowUnsaved` refusal/rollback happens after staging and after partial imports
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-archive.js:276-285` — import loop re-`readFileSync`s each staged file and `importChat`s it
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-opencode.js:217` — `CHAT_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024` (per-chat only)
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/space-opencode.js:260-282,336-355` — `readCapped`/`exportChat` enforce the per-chat cap, nothing total
- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/host.js:329-336` — real source wiring (`listChats`/`exportChat` straight from the space container)

## Why this is a defect
- The space side is explicitly untrusted for this path ("A chat taken out is untrusted data" — `space-opencode.js:11-12`). A compromised space container can answer `exportChat` with 1000 chats just under 256 MiB each. `readSpaceSessions` caps the *list* (10 pages x 100, 8 MiB/page) but every listed chat is then exported at up to 256 MiB.
- Worst case staged on host disk: 1000 x 256 MiB = **~256 GiB** in `<dataDir>/spaces/archive/.incoming-<spaceId>`, plus one full in-memory `JSON.stringify` copy at write time and one `JSON.parse` copy at import time per chat, plus whatever `hostOpenCode.importChat` buffers. `SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS` (30 min) bounds time, not bytes.
- Failure mode is disk exhaustion / OOM during an ordinary space delete, and with `allowUnsaved=false` the `chats_not_saved` throw at :251/:300 comes *after* the staging already filled the disk — the `finally` cleanup at :313 only helps if the disk survived that long.
- The entry-side hardening (`ARCHIVE_ENTRY_MAX_BYTES`, bounded reader at :99) shows the intended pattern; the much larger chat-staging side just lacks the total side of it.

## Expected
- Enforce a running total budget on `saveChats` staging (e.g. an `ARCHIVE_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES`), counting each exported chat's staged bytes and aborting the take-out early with the existing `tooLarge`/`failed` accounting before the disk fills.
- Better: stream per chat (export -> import -> drop staging file) instead of stage-all-then-import, so at most one chat is staged at a time; keep the all-or-nothing rollback semantics for what was imported.
- At minimum, check the running total before `writeFileSync` and fail fast rather than after all 1000 writes.

## Evidence / repro
- Code-verified on `origin/main` (`5091c6507` at hunt time): per-chat cap x max-chat count arithmetic above; no total-bytes symbol exists anywhere in `spaces/` (grep `TOTAL|TOTAL_MAX|staged.*bytes|incoming.*cap` finds only the per-chat and per-entry caps).
- Dedupe: open-issue grep plus `gh issue list` search for `archiv|staging|disk|quota|budget|large` hits only #2310 (tools-filler tar path), #2299/#2304 (prototype/path issues), #1628/#1641/#1643 (other bounded-reader gaps) — none covers archive chat-staging totals. No closed-issue match either.
- No live 256 GiB repro attempted (would fill the dev disk); the defect follows directly from the cited loops and caps.

## Acceptance
- A space offering chats whose *sum* exceeds the new total budget fails fast (or streams) without staging the full sum to `.incoming-*`.
- Single small chats / normal archives behave exactly as today; existing `space-archive.test.js` take-out/rollback cases still pass.
- Regression test: stub `source.exportChat` with N chats of known byte size and assert the save aborts once the running total crosses the budget (host untouched, staging cleaned).

title: fix(web): message-stream WebSocket silently first-picks repeated directory/lastEventId params — ambiguous stream scope

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: area/web
labels.description: Web app

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The message-stream WebSocket connection handler parses its scope from the upgrade URL with silent first-pick reads (`packages/web/server/lib/event-stream/runtime.js:130-131` on `origin/main` `a5959da2f`):

```js
const requestedLastEventId = requestUrl.searchParams.get('lastEventId')?.trim() || '';
const requestedDirectory = requestUrl.searchParams.get('directory')?.trim() || '';
```

A client (or a misbehaving proxy in the middle) that sends `?directory=/a&directory=/b` gets silently scoped to `/a`: the value flows into `acceptDirectoryMessageStreamWsConnection` (`directory-ws-bridge.js:19`), labels every forwarded event (`:75`) and is `.set()` onto the upstream OpenCode URL (`:115-116`). Same for a repeated `lastEventId`: resume starts from the first cursor while the caller may have meant the second, silently replaying or skipping events.

Probe on this checkout (exact expressions from runtime.js):

```
get(directory) = "/a"        getAll(directory) = ["/a","/b"]
get(lastEventId) = "1"        getAll(lastEventId) = ["1","2"]
```

## Why it matters

Every other directory-scoped surface in this server rejects a repeated `directory` as ambiguous input instead of silently selecting one: git routes via `resolveDirectoryQuery` (`lib/git/routes.js:138-155`, issue #2121), source-control routes (#2292), project-directory routes (#2123), walkthrough pr-diff/pr-file (#2312). The WS message-stream path is the outlier, and its scope decision is stickier than an HTTP 400-able route: once scoped, the socket streams one directory's events indefinitely under a label derived from an ambiguous request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A directory-stream upgrade whose URL carries more than one `directory` (or more than one `lastEventId`) value is refused (error frame + non-1000 close, mirroring the HTTP surfaces' 400) instead of streaming under the first value.
- Single-value and absent params behave exactly as today.
- Regression test through the existing `wsServer.emit('connection', socket, { url })` seam (cf. `rebind.test.js:177`).

## Suggested fix shape

In the `connection` handler, before the `isGlobalStream` branch, check `requestUrl.searchParams.getAll('directory').length > 1 || requestUrl.searchParams.getAll('lastEventId').length > 1` and close with an error frame; keep `.get()` for the single-value path.

## Dedupe

Open-issue grep + `gh search` for event-stream/message-stream repeated directory, lastEventId ambiguity, directory-ws-bridge: only hits are #2292/#2291/#2123 (HTTP git/source-control/project-directory surfaces) and #2312 (walkthrough HTTP) — none covers the WS message-stream path. No open PR touches `lib/event-stream/runtime.js` directory handling.

title: fix(web): active session goal stalls with no wakeup after a failed continuation — turn charged, timer never re-armed

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` `a5959da2f`, `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/runtime.js`:

1. **Failed continuation is charged but never retried.** `tick` persists `turnsUsed + 1` first (`:828-841`), then `await sendContinuation(...)` (`:853`), which throws on any prompt-POST failure (`:546-552` via `openCodeFetch` + `assertPromptResponse`, `:393-396`). The throw propagates to `armTimer`'s fire handler, whose `.catch` only warns (`:862-865`). The comment at `:825-827$ ("if the write lands and the prompt fails, the goal just waits for the next idle tick") is wrong in exactly this case: the session was idle when the tick ran and a failed POST starts no turn, so **no new `session.idle` transition arrives** — and the status-event path at `:943-950$ is the only re-arm source. The goal sits `active` with a consumed turn and no timer. Any transient `POST /prompt` failure (OpenCode restart, 500, HTML proxy page — the throw path already has a dedicated test at `runtime.test.js:606-626`, which asserts only the warning) strands it until the user manually messages/pauses/resumes. Note the failure can even disarm actively: a non-idle status (e.g. error) takes the `else clearTimer` branch at `:947-948`.
2. **Idle event landing during a slow tick is dropped.** The fire handler does `if (stopped || inflight.has(sessionId)) return;` (`:860$) — the only wakeup vanishes. The sibling runtime handles the identical hazard the opposite way: `dispatch-results/runtime.js:460-462$ does `if (ticking.has(sessionId)) return arm(sessionId)` with an explicit "must not be lost" comment. A tick that outlives `idleQuietMs` (15s at `:58$; the tick does session fetch + objective read + status probe + child probe + message page + audit model call) can still be in `inflight` when a re-armed timer fires. The double-arm guards at `:903/:912/:958$ prevent overlap but do not recover the dropped wakeup.

## Why it matters

Visible symptom: goal badge stays `active`, turns stop advancing, and only manual intervention revives it. Mechanism 1 is reachable on any transient prompt failure; mechanism 2 is narrow (slow tick + fresh idle) but the same stuck symptom.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed `sendContinuation` re-arms the idle-quiet timer (no extra turn charge — the turn was already persisted) instead of leaving the goal timerless; or documents why a retry must wait for an operator-visible signal.
- An idle status arriving while a tick is `inflight` re-arms (dispatch-results `return arm(...)` pattern) instead of being dropped; overlap guards stay intact.
- Regression tests: continuation-failure re-arms (and does not double-charge); slow-tick overlap preserves exactly one pending wakeup. The existing HTML-failure test (`:606-626$) keeps passing.
- No change to the charge-before-prompt ordering or the turn-cap accounting.

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed issues for `goal stall`, `goal stuck`, `continuation fail`, `session-goal retry`, `goal active stuck`: no tracker (hits were unrelated byte-cap/CI/design issues). Adjacent but distinct: #2295 (objectives version-list read), #2159/#2154 (notification surfaces).

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` `a5959da2f`, `packages/web/server/lib/notifications/runtime.js:772-860` arms a 500ms debounced question push on `form.created` / `openchamber:page-waiting` (`pushQuestionDebounceTimers`, keyed by session). Nothing ever cancels that timer: there is no `form.settled` / `form.replied` / `page-settled` branch anywhere in the file (grep for `settled|replied|cancelled` hits only the `permission.replied` branch at `:862`). The permission path right below it does the right thing — `permission.replied` with a matching request key clears `pushPermissionDebounceTimers` (`:862-880`) — so the two blocking-request kinds behave asymmetrically.

Plumbing reaches the dead end today: every SSE payload flows through `onPayload` in `packages/web/server/index.js:1254` (`void maybeSendPushForTrigger(payload, { spaceId })`), so `form.settled` (which `session-runtime.js:137` already handles for the pending-request list) arrives at the trigger runtime and falls through every branch. `openchamber:page-settled` is worse: `index.js:1984-2000` broadcasts it as a UI event but never forwards it to `maybeSendPushForTrigger` at all.

## Reproduction (probe, bun, against `createNotificationTriggerRuntime` at this commit)

- `form.created` then `form.settled` 100ms later, wait 900ms → push still fires: `["desktop","ui","push","apns"]`.
- Control, same timing: `permission.asked` then `permission.replied` → `[]` (timer correctly cancelled).
- Control: unanswered `form.created` → pushes (debounce itself works).
- `openchamber:page-waiting` then `page-settled` 100ms later → still pushes.

## Why it matters

Answering a form or waiting page from a second client (or quickly in the same one) still buzzes every registered phone/PWA with "Input needed" for a prompt that is already resolved. Stale pushes for resolved prompts train users to ignore the real ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `form.settled` for a session with a pending question timer clears the timer (session-keyed, mirroring the existing per-session timer granularity; the `permission.replied` unknown-ID precedent at `:870-876` applies).
- `openchamber:page-settled` is forwarded to `maybeSendPushForTrigger` (same call site shape as the waiting branch) and clears the pending question timer the same way.
- Regression tests mirroring the existing `permission.replied` cancellation coverage: settle-inside-debounce pushes nothing; unanswered asks still push after the debounce; unknown-ID settle does not throw.
- No change to the 500ms debounce timing or the permission flow.

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed issues for `question debounce`, `form.settled`, `stale question`, `answered form notification`: no tracker. #2159 (native registration race) and #2154 (notification content pages) are adjacent but distinct surfaces.

labels.name: kind/bug
