labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
The live-session status maps decoded from `/api/session/active` are plain JSON objects, but every reader uses an unguarded bracket read, so any id matching an `Object.prototype` member (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`, `__proto__` — all pass the `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,128}$` session-id shape) is reported as live even when that session was never running.

Evidence (origin/main `a5959da2f`):

- `packages/web/server/lib/dispatch-results/runtime.js:381` — `if (statuses[sessionId]) return { kind: 'running' };` (`sessionId` validated by `sessionIdSchema` at :59, which prototype names pass)
- `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/runtime.js:600` — `if (isWorkingStatus(statuses[sessionId])) return;` where `isWorkingStatus = (status) => Boolean(status)` (:419)
- `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/service.js:608-612,1327` — `activeSessions()` returns the raw decoded map (:600-606, no null-prototype/hasOwn guard) and `asPublicStatus(statuses[sessionID])` maps any truthy read to `{ type: 'busy' }`
- `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/session-actions.js:143` — `Boolean(isRecord(statuses) && statuses[sessionID])` (outer guard does not cover the inner inherited read)
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/session-activity.js:79` — `children.some((id) => Boolean(statuses[id]))`
- Same shape in `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/environment-actions.js:49` and `packages/web/server/lib/environment/routes.js:39` (`statuses[name]` over reference names)

Repro (node, plain JSON-decoded map — no server needed):

```
const statuses = JSON.parse('{"ses_abc123": {"state":"busy"}}');
for (const id of ['constructor','toString','hasOwnProperty','valueOf','__proto__','ses_nope'])
  console.log(id, '->', Boolean(statuses[id]));
// constructor/toString/hasOwnProperty/valueOf/__proto__ -> true; ses_nope -> false
```

So `readWatchedSession('constructor')` answers `running`, the goal tick at `session-goal/runtime.js:600` treats it as working and returns early, and `sessionStatus` answers `busy` — for ids that were never active.

Why it matters: a phantom-running verdict suppresses exactly the fallthroughs that matter — dispatch-result settlement (timer rearms forever, entry never settles), goal audits, idle notifications, and UI presence. The guarded sibling in the same tree shows the intended pattern: `message-queue/runtime.js:532` reads through `asRecord(statuses[sessionId])`, which rejects inherited functions. This is the same defect class as #2299 (config-v2 section helpers) on a different surface with different consequences — not a duplicate (dedupe: open-issue grep for status/active-session/phantom/constructor plus `gh search` for statuses/session-activity/isActive/busy-idle/phantom all empty; closed prototype-lookup issues #939/#944/#965/#988 are config lookups).

Acceptance:
- Every active-status read above uses an own-key check (e.g. `Object.hasOwn`), a null-prototype map after decode, or the existing `asRecord`-style guard — no inherited member can read as live.
- Regression tests: for each prototype-name id, `readWatchedSession`/goal-tick/`sessionStatus`/`isActive` answer not-running/idle/unknown on a fixture map containing only one real session; a real active id still answers running/busy.
- Existing session-activity/dispatch-results/session-goal/control test suites stay green.

body:
## What

`packages/web/server/lib/spaces/tools-filler.js` hardcodes `/usr/bin/tar` and `/bin/sync` in `FILLER_PROGRAM` — the script that runs on the host to fill a space's tools volume. On NixOS (and any system without those FHS paths) the fill fails, and the filler tests are red:

```
fill failed: /usr/bin/tar --no-same-owner ended with Error: spawnSync /usr/bin/tar ENOENT
```

```
$ ls -la /usr/bin/tar
ls: cannot access '/usr/bin/tar': No such file or directory
$ which tar
/run/current-system/sw/bin/tar
```

The program's own test asserts it "is one line, so it is safe as one argument on every host" (`tools-filler.test.js:47-50`) — the absolute paths defeat exactly that portability intent.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/server/lib/spaces/tools-filler.js:71`: `run('/usr/bin/tar', ['--no-same-owner', ...])`.
- Same file (`:77`-ish, `run('/bin/sync', [], ...)`) — `/bin/sync` is equally absent off-FHS and would fail next once tar is fixed.
- `server/lib/spaces/tools-filler.test.js`: `writes package.json ... writes the marker last` → expected `{code: 0}`, got `{code: 1}`; `writes no marker when a needed package is missing after the install` → stderr shows the tar `ENOENT` above instead of the expected `node_modules/@opencode/plugin/package.json is missing`.
- Clean `main` @ `31469e209`, `packages/web`, `bunx vitest run`: these are 2 of the 9 failing tests (the other 7 are config-isolation, filed separately).

Note the test's fake-`npm`-on-`PATH` pattern already proves the filler can rely on `PATH` lookup: the program calls `run('npm', ...)` and `run(process.execPath, ...)` for everything else — `tar`/`sync` are the only two absolute host paths.

## Why it matters

- The filler runs on the deployment host during space setup, so this is a production portability defect, not just a test issue: spaces cannot fill on NixOS hosts.
- The failure message (`spawnSync ... ENOENT`) points at the environment rather than the hardcode, and the second test's real assertion (missing-package marker behavior) is unreachable behind it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `FILLER_PROGRAM` resolves `tar`/`sync` via `PATH` (or probes a small candidate list) instead of hardcoded `/usr/bin/tar` + `/bin/sync`.
- [ ] Both `FILLER_PROGRAM, run` tests pass on a machine without `/usr/bin/tar` (this laptop) and on FHS machines.
- [ ] The one-line-program safety test still passes; no change to the install/marker semantics.

## References

- Failing tests: `server/lib/spaces/tools-filler.test.js:108-155`.
- Sibling red-suite (different cause, filed separately): web config-discovery isolation across `messaging-config`, `providers-disabled`, `model-pools-folder-config`.

body:
## What

Three `packages/web` suites (7 tests) are red on a clean `main` on any machine whose real global OpenCode state contains the sections under test. Each test pins the config env it knows about, but a different homedir-derived source leaks through in each file:

| Suite | Failing tests | Leaking global |
|---|---|---|
| `server/lib/opencode/messaging-config.test.js` | 4 | `~/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` (has `messaging`) re-enters via the project walk |
| `server/lib/opencode/providers-disabled.test.js` | 2 | `~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc` (names `claude-code`, `_antigravity`, `openai`) via the default `OPENCODE_CONFIG` path |
| `server/lib/routing/model-pools-folder-config.test.js` | 1 | `~/.opencode/` unconditionally added to config sources |

Same recurrence class as #2308 (vscode npm-registry isolation, filed this run) and closed #1289 — tests that pass on a bare machine and fail on a developer machine.

## Evidence

Full `packages/web` run on clean `main` @ `31469e209`: `Test Files 4 failed | 526 passed`, `Tests 9 failed` (the other 2 are the `/usr/bin/tar` hardcode, filed separately).

### 1. `messaging-config.test.js` — project walk to `/` re-admits the global file

`server/lib/opencode/websearch-config.js:68-90` — `readProjectConfigFiles` walks **all** ancestors to the filesystem root, and `PROJECT_CONFIG_NAMES` (`:58-61`) includes `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`. For a temp dir under `$HOME`, the `/home/user` ancestor + `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` resolves to the real global file, which on this laptop contains a `messaging` section.

`server/lib/opencode/config-v2.js:810-` — `findProjectConfigOverride` only excludes `layers.paths.userPath`/`userOverridePath` (both `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`-based, i.e. `~/.config/opencode/`), so `~/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` is not excluded — even though the comment on the function claims "Global JSON and JSONC files cannot re-enter through the project walk". Observed: expected project path under `/tmp/...`, received `/home/user/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` (4 tests).

### 2. `providers-disabled.test.js` — default `OPENCODE_CONFIG` runtime file leaks

The test pins `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` to a tmpdir in a child process, but the default custom path is `$HOME/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc`, which exists on this laptop and names extra providers. Direct probe:

```
$ OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/probe-dis node --input-type=module -e "...readConfigLayers(null)..."
paths: {..., "customPath": "/home/user/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc"}
user   -> ["openai","anthropic"]
custom -> ["claude-code","_antigravity","openai"]
```

`configuredProviderIds` (`providers.js:403-414`) unions those into the off-state universe, so `readProviderOffState(null, ['groq'])` reports `{_antigravity, anthropic, claude-code, groq: allowlist}` instead of `{anthropic, groq}` (and the policy test gains the same phantom ids).

### 3. `model-pools-folder-config.test.js` — `~/.opencode` pushed unconditionally

The test pins `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (tmp) and deletes `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, yet dozens of extra pools (`argon-plan`, `deepseek-*`, … — all defined in the real `~/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` and `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`) merge in. Cause:

`server/lib/opencode/shared.js:1106` — `pushDir(path.join(os.homedir(), '.opencode'))` inside `readConfigSources`, unconditional on any pin. With a real `$HOME`, the machine's `~/.opencode` always merges.

## Why it matters

- `bunx vitest run` in `packages/web` is red on a clean checkout for any developer with a lived-in `~/.opencode`, `~/.config/opencode`, or opencode runtime state — i.e. nearly every real contributor machine — with failures that point at config-resolution logic rather than test isolation.
- GitHub Actions is disabled in this fork (open #2274), so local suites are the only gate; 7 permanently red tests mask real regressions across messaging, provider policy, and model routing.
- The `findProjectConfigOverride` comment actively asserts the re-entry it fails to prevent, which will mislead the next reader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three suites pass with the real machine state present (use this laptop's files as the fixture: `~/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` with `messaging` + pools, `~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc` with extra providers) and on a bare machine.
- [ ] Each test isolates every homedir-derived source its implementation reads: `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` pins where the impl honors them, plus `HOME`/homedir isolation (or a seam) for `readProjectConfigFiles`'s walk-to-root, the default custom path, and the unconditional `~/.opencode` push.
- [ ] Correct the `findProjectConfigOverride` comment if the exclusion stays narrow, or widen the exclusion so the comment becomes true (either is fine; say which).
- [ ] No production resolution-order changes beyond what isolation requires; test-only diff preferred.

## References

- Same class: #2308 (vscode npm-registry isolation, this run), closed #1289 (web `routes-upgrade.test.js`).
- Disabled CI that would otherwise mask/flag this: #2274.

body:
## What

`packages/vscode/src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts` is red on a clean `main` for any developer whose `~/.npmrc` points at a non-default npm registry. The third test ("reports installed and latest versions from the v2 info route") is the only test in the file that does not pin `npm_config_userconfig`, so it resolves `@opencode/cli` through the machine's registry mirror, while its own `fetch` stub only knows `registry.npmjs.org`.

This is the un-pinned VS Code twin of **#1289** (closed), which fixed the same class in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/routes-upgrade.test.js`. Commit 5f9deb2ce (`fix(npm): honor configured registry for package metadata lookups (#2348)`) added `npm_config_userconfig=missing-test.npmrc` pins to tests 1 and 2 of this file but missed test 3.

## Evidence

`packages/vscode/src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts:61-77`:

```ts
test('reports installed and latest versions from the v2 info route', async () => {
  const manager = createManager();
  globalThis.fetch = (async (input) => {
    const url = String(input);
    if (url.endsWith('/api/info')) return new Response(JSON.stringify({ version: '2.0.1', ... }));
    if (url.includes('registry.npmjs.org')) return new Response(JSON.stringify({ version: '2.0.2' }));
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ tag_name: 'v2.0.2' }));   // <- github shape, not a packument
  }) as typeof fetch;

  assert.deepEqual(await getOpenCodeUpgradeStatus(manager), {
    available: true,
    currentVersion: '2.0.1',
    latestVersion: '2.0.2',
    ...
  });
});
```

The file's `afterEach` (`:13-20`) restores the *original* `npm_config_*` env values, and the test process starts with none set, so the resolver falls through to `~/.npmrc`:

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/npm-registry-config.js:8-13` — `configPath()` = `npm_config_userconfig`/`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, else `path.join(os.homedir(), '.npmrc')`.
- `:79-80` — `configuredValue(values, 'registry') || DEFAULT_NPM_REGISTRY`.
- `packages/vscode/src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.ts:73-92` — `fetchLatestVersion` throws `Failed to resolve latest OpenCode version` when the packument has no usable `version` (the stub's `{tag_name:'v2.0.2'}` fallback).

## Reproduction (this laptop, `~/.npmrc` = `registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`)

Clean `main` @ `31469e209`:

```
$ cd packages/vscode
$ bun test src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts
13 pass
1 fail   ... opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts:70:12
actual:   { available: null, error: "Failed to resolve latest OpenCode version", ... }
expected: { available: true, currentVersion: "2.0.1", latestVersion: "2.0.2", ... }
```

Controls (same checkout, same command):

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| as-is (`~/.npmrc` → npmmirror) | 13 pass / **1 fail** |
| `HOME=/tmp/vs-home-probe` (no `.npmrc`) | 14 pass / 0 fail |
| `npm_config_userconfig=/nonexistent.npmrc` | 14 pass / 0 fail |
| `npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org npm_config_userconfig=/nonexistent.npmrc` | 14 pass / 0 fail |

Full package run: `105/106` test files pass; `src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts` is the only red file. The web siblings are green on the same machine (`server/lib/opencode/routes-upgrade.test.js`, `npm-registry-config.test.js`, `npm-registry.test.js`, `v2-install.test.js`: 70/70), so this is specifically the un-pinned VS Code file, not the resolver.

## Why it matters

- `bun run --cwd packages/vscode test` is red on a clean checkout for every mirror user (China/Nix/corporate registry setups), with a failure message ("Failed to resolve latest OpenCode version") that points at version logic rather than test isolation.
- GitHub Actions is disabled in this fork (open **#2274**, recurrence of #54), so local suites are the only gate; a permanent, machine-dependent red masks real regressions in a 106-file package.
- It is the same recurrence class #1289 documented and fixed for the web twin; the vscode twin was only half-pinned by #2348.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every test in `packages/vscode/src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts` pins `npm_config_userconfig` to a non-existent file (and sets/clears `npm_config_registry` / `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` as needed) before calling `getOpenCodeUpgradeStatus`, mirroring tests 1-2 in the same file and `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/routes-upgrade.test.js`.
- [ ] Alternatively/additionally the stub matches the registry URL structurally instead of `url.includes('registry.npmjs.org')`, so the test states its intent (a packument-shaped response) rather than one host.
- [ ] `bun test src/opencode-upgrade-runtime.test.ts` passes both with `~/.npmrc` = `registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com` and with no `~/.npmrc` (verify both).
- [ ] No production route/resolver behaviour changes; test-only diff.

## References

- Closed precedent: #1289 — same class, web `routes-upgrade.test.js` (fix commit added the `npm_config_userconfig` pin there).
- Partial fix that missed this test: 5f9deb2ce / #2348.
- Disabled CI that would otherwise mask/flag this: #2274.
- Resolver: `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/npm-registry-config.js`.

title: test(electron): web-server-imports guard misses the .then() destructure shape — createDevTunnelClient in main.mjs is unchecked (PR #2303)

labels.name: kind/test
labels.description: Test coverage, test infrastructure, or test-only fixes

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/electron
labels.description: Package: electron (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #2303 added `packages/electron/web-server-imports.test.mjs` to guard the Electron main process against a repeat of #2300 (a knip dead-code cleanup de-exporting a name Electron imports from `@openchamber/web/server` at module-link time). The guard parses two import shapes:

1. static named imports — `import { a, b } from '@openchamber/web/server/...'`
2. await-import destructures — `const { a } = await import('@openchamber/web/server/...')`

A third shape, present in the very file that broke in #2300, is parsed by neither pattern and is therefore completely unchecked — not even as unresolvable:

```js
// packages/electron/main.mjs:4395-4396 (current main 31469e209a06)
devTunnelClientPromise = import('@openchamber/web/server/lib/dev-tunnel/client.js')
  .then(({ createDevTunnelClient }) => createDevTunnelClient({ logger: log }))
```

If a future dead-code cleanup de-exports `createDevTunnelClient`, this guard stays green and the break surfaces only lazily at runtime, the first time a dev tunnel is requested: the `.then` destructure yields `undefined` and calling it throws a TypeError (the `.catch` on the chain resets `devTunnelClientPromise` and rethrows to the caller).

## Evidence

- Source PR: #2303 (merged, head `896ba24f9bf08ff52b5b26ea7d7aa3833c0f7663`, merge commit = current main HEAD `31469e209a06c86bc5c22cbbe85b1db60bd7f5e8`) — its new test file's `staticImports` regex requires `import ... { } from`, and its `dynamicDestructures` regex requires `(const|let|var) { } = await import(...)`; the `.then(({ ... }) => ...)` shape matches neither.
- Verified against current main (`31469e209a06c86bc5c22cbbe85b1db60bd7f5e8`):
  - Full scan of all 52 non-test + 18 script `.mjs` files under `packages/electron/` (via the contents API): the only `@openchamber/web/server` imports are 9 static named names in `main.mjs`, 1 in `early-startup.mjs` (`clearAppImageArgv0FromProcessEnv`), the covered await-destructure `startWebUiServer` (`main.mjs:1674`), and the uncovered `.then` destructure above (`main.mjs:4395`). No namespace or default-only web/server imports exist today.
  - Simulating the guard's own two regexes (after its comment-stripping) over `main.mjs` from main: the checked set is exactly those 10 names; `createDevTunnelClient` is not in it.
  - `createDevTunnelClient` is exported today at `packages/web/server/lib/dev-tunnel/client.js:59` — there is no live break; this is a guard-coverage gap only.
- The guard itself is wired in: `scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs` discovers every `*.test.mjs` under `packages/electron`, and the root `test` script runs the electron package through it — so extending the parser is sufficient; no CI wiring change is needed.
- Dedupe: searched open and closed issues for the guard / `web-server-imports` / `createDevTunnelClient` (2026-11-16) — only #2300 (closed, the regression this guard was built for) is related; nothing tracks this coverage gap.

## Why it matters

The guard's stated purpose is to catch exactly the #2300 failure class before merge, independently of knip. A shape it silently skips — in the same file, for a lazily-loaded module — recreates the blind spot for the dev-tunnel surface, and the failure mode is worse than #2300's: not a startup link error, but a runtime TypeError on first use of a feature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The guard also extracts names destructured in `.then(({ ... }) => ...)` continuations of a dynamic `import('@openchamber/web/server...')` (including the `import(...).then(...)` chain in `main.mjs`), and asserts each against the target module's exports.
- [ ] A negative-control test (or a documented manual verification in the PR) shows the guard fails when `createDevTunnelClient`'s export is removed from `packages/web/server/lib/dev-tunnel/client.js`, and passes on the unmodified tree.
- [ ] All previously checked names (10 across `main.mjs` / `early-startup.mjs`) remain checked — the checked-count does not silently drop.
- [ ] `node --test packages/electron/web-server-imports.test.mjs` passes, and the file is still discovered by `scripts/run-isolated-tests.mjs`.

Found by: pr-diff-review job, PR diff review of PR #2303 (and the #2296/#2297/#2302 batch) against main `31469e209a06c86bc5c22cbbe85b1db60bd7f5e8`.

title: fix(ui): voice-capture submit has no client deadline and no cancel — a stalled transcription request leaves the composer stuck in "submitting" with no way out

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/ui
labels.description: Package: ui (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

The façade voice-capture submit path has **no client-side deadline and no in-flight cancellation**. While `state === 'submitting'`, the capture UI renders only a spinner and "Transcribing…" — the record/attach, cancel and discard controls are all gated to other states — and the §6.1 reducer has **no transition out of `submitting`** except `submit_succeeded` / `submit_failed` (`cancel` and `discard` are ignored). So if the `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` request never settles, the composer's voice-capture control is stuck on a spinner for the life of the page, with audio still held locally and no way to retry, discard or re-record. The only recovery is reloading the app, which throws away the composer draft.

A stalled request is not exotic here: `runtimeFetch` installs no default timeout, `transcribeViaFacade` passes no `AbortSignal`, and even after response headers arrive the body is read with a bare `await response.json()` — a stalled body hangs forever too. The façade's own provider deadline is 120 s (opencode `packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts:573`), so the request can legitimately take minutes before the client would ever hear anything; a proxy/relay/server stall simply extends that without bound.

## Evidence

`packages/ui/src/lib/dictation/use-facade-voice-capture.ts`
- `submit` (lines 274-305): `dispatch({ type: 'submit' })` then `await transcribeViaFacade(...)` — no `AbortController`, no `signal`, no timeout; success calls `onInsertRef.current(transcription.text)` (line 296) regardless of whether the capture was torn down or superseded meanwhile.
- No generation/ownership guard for the submit attempt (contrast `acquisitionRef`, which guards the microphone acquisition at lines 94-99 / 178-182).

`packages/ui/src/lib/dictation/facade-transcription.ts`
- `transcribeViaFacade` (lines 423-454): `await input.fetchFn(...)` (line 435) with no signal; `const data = await response.json().catch(() => undefined)` (line 449) — a body that never completes never rejects.
- `voiceCaptureReducer` (lines 498-528): `cancel` only leaves `recording`/`reviewing` (line 512); `discard` only leaves `reviewing`/`error`/`inserted` (line 524). From `submitting` nothing but `submit_succeeded`/`submit_failed` moves the state.
- `canCancelCapture` (line 530): `'submitting'` is explicitly not cancellable.

`packages/ui/src/lib/runtime-fetch.ts`
- `runtimeFetch` (line 335) forwards `init` verbatim and adds no default timeout (`coalesceReadKey`'s `hasSignal` logic at lines 387-389 only skips read coalescing). Elsewhere in the UI a deadline is supplied by the caller — e.g. `packages/ui/src/sync/bootstrap.ts:61` uses `runtimeFetch("/health", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(4000) })` — so the transport supports it; this caller just never sets one.

`packages/ui/src/components/dictation/FacadeVoiceCapture.tsx`
- `showReview` covers `reviewing | submitting | error` (line 69), but the actionable buttons are gated: submit/discard only in `reviewing` (lines 133-142), retry/discard only in `error` (lines 144-153). `submitting` renders the spinner (line 143) and the "Transcribing…" line (lines 159-161) and nothing else; the record/attach buttons only render in `idle`/`inserted` (lines 86-109).

`packages/ui/src/lib/dictation/facade-transcription.test.ts`
- Lines 316-319 pin the current behaviour: `canCancelCapture('submitting') === false` and `run('submitting', ['cancel']) === 'submitting'`. Any fix that adds a cancel path must update this test deliberately, which is why the deadline is the recommended minimum.

## Repro (no code change needed)

1. Put a stall between the UI and the opencode server's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (e.g. point the UI at a local proxy that accepts the connection and never responds, or stop the opencode server's event loop after accepting the upload).
2. Open the composer voice capture, attach a small audio file (or record a short clip and stop), and press submit.
3. The control shows the spinner and "Transcribing…" indefinitely. There is no cancel, discard, retry or record/attach control in this state; the audio stays in memory (and as an object URL) and the state never changes. Reloading the app is the only way back.

The same happens for a response whose headers arrive but whose body never ends, because the body read has no deadline.

## Why it matters

- A single stalled transcription leaves the feature in a permanent, non-recoverable state in the composer — the same "wedged forever with no deadline" defect class this repo has fixed repeatedly (#824, #943, #1032, #788, #931), but here on the new client-side façade path introduced with #2271.
- The audio is retained (blob + object URL) for the lifetime of the page and the user cannot discard it.
- Recovery costs the user their in-progress draft, which is the exact thing §6.3 exists to protect.
- Because `submit` also has no attempt-ownership guard, a resolution that arrives after the surface is torn down still calls `onInsert`; the draft-origin guard in `ChatInput` catches the session-switch case, but the request itself is never aborted and the hook has no way to know its result is stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- `transcribeViaFacade` / the hook thread an `AbortSignal` through `runtimeFetch` and set a client deadline that comfortably exceeds the façade's 120 s provider deadline (one exported constant, not a magic number at the call site).
- A request that never settles reaches a terminal state within that deadline: `submitting` → `error` with a retryable `FacadeTranscriptionError` (`network_error` today, or a dedicated timeout code) so the existing retry/discard buttons return.
- A response body that never completes is covered by the same deadline (abort cancels the body read).
- The hook discards a late result: after the attempt is abandoned (deadline, teardown, or any future cancel), a resolved transcription must not call `onInsert`.
- The UI never leaves the user without an exit while `submitting`: either the deadline always settles the state, or a cancel/discard control is offered in `submitting` (if the latter, update `facade-transcription.test.ts:313-320` and the §6.1 comment in `facade-transcription.ts:476-482` so the pinned state machine matches).
- Regression tests: a fetch that never resolves settles to `error` within the deadline (fake timers); a late resolution after abandonment does not call `onInsert`; reducer coverage for every path out of `submitting`.

## Suggested fix shape

Add an aborted attempt in `submit` (own `AbortController`, `setTimeout` cleared in `finally`), pass `signal` into `transcribeViaFacade` → `fetchFn(url, { method: 'POST', body, signal })`, and map `AbortError` to a retryable `network_error` (or a new `timeout` code added to `RETRYABLE_CODES`). Keep the §6.1 "cancel in recording/reviewing" contract if the deadline is considered sufficient, and simply guarantee that `submitting` always settles. Mirror the `acquisitionRef` generation pattern for submit attempts so a stale resolution cannot insert.

body:
## Summary

The VS Code `api:config/skills/files` bridge handlers (GET/PUT/DELETE) pass the client-supplied `filePath` straight into `path.join(skillDir, relativePath)` with no traversal guard. `GET ../../secret` reads, `PUT ../../pwned` writes (`mkdir -p` + write), and `DELETE ../../x` unlinks outside the skill directory. The web twin for the same operations is hardened twice (route-level reject + resolve-and-contain); the VS Code twin has neither layer.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main 4c71146c4)

Vulnerable sinks — `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts`:

- `readSkillSupportingFile` (:3553-3554): `const fullPath = path.join(skillDir, relativePath)` — no `..`/absolute check, no containment assert. FIFO/size-hardened only.
- `writeSkillSupportingFile` (:3605-3610): same raw join, then `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(fullPath), { recursive: true })` + `fs.writeFileSync` — a traversal write creates directories outside the skill root.
- `deleteSkillSupportingFile` (:3612-3631): same raw join + `fs.unlinkSync`, then parent cleanup `while (parentDir !== skillDir)` — when `fullPath` escapes, the loop condition never matches the skill root, so it walks and `rmdir`s empty ancestors outside the skill dir until a non-empty/error stop.

Unvalidated entry — `packages/vscode/src/bridge-config-runtime.ts:885-956`:

- `:899-902` only trims and rejects empty `filePath`; no `..`/absolute/backslash rejection.
- `:917`, `:936`, `:951` forward the raw `relativePath` to the three sinks above.
- `skillName` is constrained (must match a discovered/existing skill to yield `sources.md.dir`, `:904-911`), but any legitimate skill name + `../../…` `filePath` escapes — the traversal is in `filePath`, not `skillName`.

Web twin is hardened (parity reference):

- Route-level reject: `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/skill-routes.js:702,810,848` via `isUnsafeSkillRelativePath` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-normalization-runtime.js:442-453`: rejects empty, posix-absolute, and any `..` segment after backslash normalization).
- Sink-level containment: `assertPathWithinSkillDir` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js:1166-1179`: `realpathSync(skillDir)` + `path.resolve` + `path.relative` must stay within root, else `EACCES`), enforced by web `readSkillSupportingFile` (:1181-1182), `writeSkillSupportingFile` (:1254-1255), `deleteSkillSupportingFile` (:1262-1264, cleanup loop anchored on the realpath `root`).

Local probe (node, fixture tree `…/skills/demo` + sibling `…/secret.txt`):

- `path.join(skillDir, "../../secret.txt")` resolves outside the skill root (`inside=false`) and `readFileSync` returns the sibling content (`read-escape=YES`).
- Same-shaped join + `mkdir -p` + write drops `…/pwned.txt` outside the skill dir (`write-escape=YES`).

## Why this matters

- Any caller that can reach the VS Code bridge `api:config/skills/files` methods (GET/PUT/DELETE) with a legitimate skill name can read arbitrary files the extension host can read (GET returns content), write/overwrite arbitrary files it can write (PUT creates parents), and delete arbitrary files (DELETE unlinks + prunes empty parents upward). The read side keeps its FIFO/size gates; the traversal bypasses the directory boundary, not the size gate.
- Fix precedent already exists in-repo (web): either mirror `isUnsafeSkillRelativePath` at the bridge case, mirror `assertPathWithinSkillDir` in the three vscode sinks (or both, as web does).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET/PUT/DELETE api:config/skills/files` with `filePath` containing a `..` segment, an absolute path, or a backslash-`..` equivalent is rejected (400/`EACCES`-style) before any fs access, matching the web `isUnsafeSkillRelativePath` judgement.
- [ ] `readSkillSupportingFile` / `writeSkillSupportingFile` / `deleteSkillSupportingFile` in `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.ts` resolve against the real skill root and refuse targets outside it (web `assertPathWithinSkillDir` parity), so a direct unit call with `../../…` cannot read/write/unlink.
- [ ] `deleteSkillSupportingFile` parent-dir pruning is anchored on the contained root and cannot `rmdir` directories outside the skill dir.
- [ ] Regression tests: traversal GET returns an error (not sibling content), traversal PUT creates nothing outside the skill dir, traversal DELETE removes nothing outside it.

body:
## Finding

Merged PR #2297 changed the install-copy size judgement in both copies of `copyDirectoryNoSymlinks` — SKILL.md is now judged against the 4 MiB `SKILL_MD_MAX_BYTES` limit instead of the 1 MiB supporting-file cap — but only the web copy got regression tests. The VS Code copy (`packages/vscode/src/skillsCatalog.ts`) has no test coverage for the copy caps at all: `packages/vscode/src/skillsCatalog.test.ts` is 42 lines with no install/copy/size-cap tests, and the VS Code `copyDirectoryNoSymlinks` is a private function (line 453), unlike the web copy which is exported for its test file. The two copies are duplicated logic kept in sync by hand, so the untested copy is exactly where a future cap change can silently diverge — the failure mode #2297 itself fixed on the web surface (a loadable 1–4 MiB SKILL.md failing to install).

## Evidence

- PR #2297 (MERGED, head `4e3948cec9b2c36f8ce0dd4223cc5168c8479305`, merge commit = current main HEAD `4c71146c4407c9f8e09c25974ada94dcf81311d7`), closes #1647: https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2297
- Web copy: `packages/web/server/lib/skills-catalog/install.js` — new `perFileLimit` logic plus two new tests in `install.test.js` (2 MiB SKILL.md installs; 4 MiB+1 aborts with `exceeds the 4194304 byte limit`), on top of the pre-existing supporting-file abort test.
- VS Code copy: `packages/vscode/src/skillsCatalog.ts:467` — identical `perFileLimit = name === 'SKILL.md' ? SKILL_MD_MAX_BYTES : SKILL_SUPPORTING_FILE_MAX_BYTES` logic (its `SKILL_MD_MAX_BYTES` at :20 is 4 MiB), with zero tests referencing `copyDirectoryNoSymlinks`, the caps, or install copying in `skillsCatalog.test.ts` (verified by grep on current main `4c71146c`).
- The scan-side contract is shared in spirit only: web `scan.js:15` defines `SKILL_MD_MAX_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024`; the VS Code file defines its own copy — another hand-synced duplicate.

## Why it matters

Install-copy caps are a safety boundary for clone-controlled content (see #1366, which added these caps after a probe copied 20,000 dirs + a 256 MiB file). A behaviour change to that boundary on the VS Code surface with no test means a regression there — in either direction, rejecting loadable skills or admitting oversized files — ships silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests on the VS Code surface pin the same three cases the web surface pins: a 2 MiB SKILL.md installs, a 4 MiB+1 SKILL.md aborts with the 4194304-byte-limit error, and a >1 MiB supporting file aborts with the 1048576-byte-limit error (export `copyDirectoryNoSymlinks` for tests like the web copy, or drive the cases through the public install path).
- The tests fail if the VS Code `perFileLimit` judgement is reverted to the single 1 MiB cap.
- Existing `skillsCatalog.test.ts` cases keep passing.

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Stage A window already closed (summary on developing-today/code#2313) — no shadow verdict recorded.

title: fix(electron): PR #2296 de-exported provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot — desktop main process import now fails to link (login-shell-env.js)

body:
## Finding

Merged PR #2296 (remove unused exports so the dead-code gate passes, closing #2092) de-exported `provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot` in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/login-shell-env.js` — but the Electron desktop main process imports and calls it. On current main the module defines it as a plain `const` with no export, while `packages/electron/main.mjs` still does a named ESM import of it. A named import of a non-existent export is a link-time `SyntaxError`, so the desktop main process cannot load its module graph at all — the app fails to start, on every platform (the import statement itself fails to link, not just the non-Windows call site).

Knip flagged the export as unused because the only consumer is `packages/electron/main.mjs`, evidently outside the dead-code gate's scanned project set — the same false "unused" claim was already made once in closed issue #682 (closed not-planned 2026-10-28, while this import existed).

## Evidence

- PR #2296 (MERGED, head `05d2d348686c993b26b12da081cc37b31dc909de`, merge commit `77f00e0202eac8ce1f38fee46ef86a1766094efc`, verified ancestor of main `4c71146c4407c9f8e09c25974ada94dcf81311d7`): https://github.com/developing-today-forks/openchamber/pull/2296 — diff hunk in `login-shell-env.js`: `-export const provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot` → `+const provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot`.
- Current main `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/login-shell-env.js:22`: `const provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot = (snapshot) => { ... }` — no export; the sibling getter `providedLoginShellEnvSnapshot` remains exported.
- Current main `packages/electron/main.mjs:1520`: `import { provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot } from '@openchamber/web/server/lib/opencode/login-shell-env.js';` and `:1531`: `if (process.platform !== 'win32') provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot(shellEnv);` (in `inheritUserShellEnv`, before the in-process server starts).
- The module's own header and `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/DOCUMENTATION.md:555` document this handoff as the mechanism by which an embedding host that already probed the login shell prevents the server from re-probing synchronously on the main thread.
- Cross-check of the PR's other 38 de-exported symbols against current main (full-tree grep): every other symbol's remaining uses are inside its defining module (the web `command-code.js` copy of `parseCommandCodeCredits` kept its export precisely because its test imports it). This is the only cross-module break.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk) — REPRODUCED

- Commit tested: current main `4c71146c4407c9f8e09c25974ada94dcf81311d7` (byte-identical `login-shell-env.js` extracted from the main tarball).
- Environment: laptop, Node v24.21.0. Command: a consumer module containing Electron's exact import line (`import { provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot } from './login-shell-env.js';`) run with `node consumer.mjs`.
- Result: exit 1 — `SyntaxError: The requested module './login-shell-env.js' does not provide an export named 'provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot'`. Control (same file with `export` restored, i.e. the pre-#2296 shape): prints `function`, exit 0.
- No existing test or CI covers this: the merge commits' check runs on main all completed as `skipped`, and the dead-code gate that motivated the change does not see the Electron consumer.

## Why it matters

This is a regression on main that breaks the desktop (Electron) surface outright: the main process throws during module linking before any window or server starts. It also removes the documented login-shell-env handoff, whose whole purpose is to keep a synchronous shell probe off the Electron main thread.

## Acceptance criteria

- `provideLoginShellEnvSnapshot` is importable again from `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/login-shell-env.js` (restore the export), OR the Electron handoff is replaced with a mechanism that does not need it and `packages/electron/main.mjs` no longer imports it.
- A guard exists so the dead-code gate cannot repeat this: the Electron package's imports of `@openchamber/web` modules are covered by the gate's project set, or a test/check performs the named imports `packages/electron/main.mjs` makes from web server modules.
- `bun run dead-code` (check:changed) still passes on clean main after the fix — by the consumer being scanned, not by the export being removed again.
- Electron main module graph loads (the consumer-import probe above passes against the real file).

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Stage A window already closed (summary on developing-today/code#2313) — no shadow verdict recorded.

body:
## Problem

`readSectionEntry` / `writeSectionEntry` / `deleteSectionEntry` in `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/config-v2.js:40-78` test entry presence with inherited property lookup (`config[section][name] !== undefined`) instead of an own-property check. Any name inherited from `Object.prototype` therefore reads as a configured entry in a config that defines nothing:

```
readSectionEntry({ providers: {} }, 'providers', 'constructor')  // => { value: [Function: Object], ... } — found
readSectionEntry({ providers: {} }, 'providers', '__proto__')     // => { value: Object.prototype, ... } — found
readSectionEntry({ providers: {} }, 'providers', 'toString')     // => found
deleteSectionEntry({ providers: {} }, 'providers', 'constructor') // => true (removes nothing)
```

Verified on origin/main `4c71146c4` with a direct node probe against the module (all of `constructor`/`__proto__`/`toString`/`hasOwnProperty`/`valueOf` report found:true; `legit-id` correctly reports false; both deletes spuriously return true).

## Impact

- `GET /api/provider/:providerId/source` (`opencode/routes.js:383`) with a prototype name: `providerExistsIn` (`providers.js:34`) returns true, so the response fabricates `sources.{user,project,custom}.exists: true` plus a phantom `config` projected off `Object`/`Object.prototype` — the same "fabricate configured:true" shape as closed #939 (quota registries) and #944 (getProviderAuth), which both hardened their own lookups but not these shared helpers.
- `DELETE /api/provider/:providerId/auth` with a prototype name: `removeProviderConfig` (`providers.js:308`) gets `true` from `deleteSectionEntry` without removing anything, reports a removal, and rewrites the config file for no change.
- Same three helpers serve the agents and commands sections (`opencode/agents.js`, `opencode/commands.js`, `opencode/shared.js:815`), `openchamber-control/provider-actions.js:190-551`, and `spaces/host-providers.js:110`, so every surface inherits the phantom-read / spurious-delete behavior.
- The write path (`PUT /api/provider`) is not prototype-pollutable: `validateCustomProviderConfig` rejects `__proto__` via `PROVIDER_ID_PATTERN` (note `constructor` passes the pattern and lands as a real own-property entry, which then reads back fine — only never-defined prototype names misbehave).

## Fix suggestion

Own-property checks in all three helpers (`Object.hasOwn(config[section], name)`), mirroring `hasConfigKey` in the same file (:799), which already uses `Object.hasOwn`. Add a prototype-name regression test mirroring `auth.test.js:165` ("does not resolve prototype-name provider ids").

## Acceptance

- `readSectionEntry` returns `value: undefined` for `constructor`/`__proto__`/`toString` on a config that does not define them; `deleteSectionEntry` returns `false` for them.
- `GET /api/provider/constructor/source` reports all `exists: false` with a null config on a clean config; `DELETE` reports no removal and does not rewrite the file.
- New regression test covering prototype names for the section helpers; existing `config-v2.test.js` suite stays green.

title: fix(web): /api/fs/raw stat-then-open lets a regular-file-to-FIFO swap hang the handler

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Web app

body:
## Problem

`GET /api/fs/raw` in `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js` validates the target with a path-based `stat` and then re-resolves the same path with a blocking `open`:

- `:1370` `const canonicalPath = await fsPromises.realpath(resolved.resolved)`
- `:1372-1375` `const stats = await fsPromises.stat(canonicalPath); if (!stats.isFile()) return 400` — rejects a FIFO present at stat time
- `:1411` `const handle = await fsPromises.open(canonicalPath, 'r')` — blocking read-only open, no `O_NONBLOCK`

If another local process replaces the regular file with a FIFO in the stat/open gap, the `isFile()` check has already passed and the blocking `open('r')` on a FIFO with no writer never settles. The request handler hangs holding its slot; unlike the fs/write identical-content check (`:22-29`, `O_NONBLOCK` open before the handle stat, #1533) this path gets no non-blocking protection.

## Evidence (origin/main `4c71146c4`, real-handler probe, no repo changes)

Probe against the real `registerFsRoutes` handler with native `fs/promises` in an isolated tmpdir, wrapping `stat` to swap the path to a FIFO (unlink + mkfifo) after the handler's own stat of the same path returns, then racing the handler against a timeout:

- Control (regular 10-byte file, no swap): handler settled in ~17 ms.
- Swapped (stat sees the regular file, path is a FIFO before open): handler did not settle within 2500 ms — `VULN-CONFIRMED`.

The hang is in the native blocking `open` at `:1411`; the pre-open stat gate cannot prevent it once the path is re-resolved.

## Impact

Any local writer able to replace a workspace file being served via `/api/fs/raw` (media player range request, download, large-file view) can wedge that request indefinitely. Repeated swaps wedge one handler slot per request.

## Suggested fix and acceptance criteria

- Open once with `O_NONBLOCK` (POSIX; keep `:26-29` platform pattern) and judge regularity on the open handle (`fstat`/`isFile()`) instead of the path stat, clearing non-blocking before streaming if needed — same shape as the identical-content check and `shared/bounded-file-reader` openFlags.
- Preserve existing behavior: 400 outside-workspace / not-a-file, 416 unsatisfiable range, empty-file fast path without open, range headers, download disposition, and handle cleanup on complete/disconnect/open-error.
- Add a deterministic regression test through the injected `fsPromises` seam that swaps the path to a FIFO after stat and proves the raw handler settles promptly with a non-regular-file refusal instead of entering blocking open.
- Run the fs routes test suite.

Related but distinct: #1605 covers read/preview-serve cap growth on whole-file reads (explicitly states raw streaming is not affected); #2268 covers the same swap class in settings-runtime; #1730 covers it in git-status line counting; #2294/#2295 cover symlinked favicons and versions.json whole reads.

title: fix(web): session-goal version history reads its .versions.json whole (FIFO freezes server; unbounded buffer) — readVersionList lacks the bounded read that readObjective has

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Summary

`packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js` protects the objective file itself with a bounded, FIFO-safe read (`readObjective`, lines 87-121: `O_NONBLOCK` open, handle stat, chunked read capped at `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_MAX_READ_BYTES`), but the companion **version-history** file (`<data-dir>/goals/<sessionId>.versions.json`) is read with a plain `fs.promises.readFile(..., 'utf8')` in `readVersionList` (lines 157-177) with no size gate and no non-blocking open.

A swapped-in FIFO (no writer) or an oversized file at that path therefore hangs `readFile` indefinitely, freezing every caller:
- `GET /api/goals/objective/:sessionId/versions` (line 188, `listObjectiveVersions`)
- `PUT /api/goals/objective/:sessionId` (line 73, `writeObjective` → `appendObjectiveVersion` → `readVersionList`)
- `GET /api/goals/objective/:sessionId/versions/:versionId` (`readObjectiveVersion`)
- `DELETE .../versions/:versionId` (`deleteObjectiveVersion`)

This is the same defect family as #2268 (settings reads FIFO) and #1628 (space records) — an unbounded whole-file read on a user-reachable path — and is inconsistent with the protection already applied to the sibling objective file (readObjective) in the same module.

## Evidence

File: `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/objectives.js`
- `readObjective` (lines 87-121): bounded, FIFO-safe (uses `O_NONBLOCK`, handle `stat()`, chunked read ≤ `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_MAX_READ_BYTES`).
- `readVersionList` (lines 157-177): `raw = await fs.promises.readFile(versionsFilePath(sessionId), 'utf8')` — whole file, no open flags, no stat, no cap. Only a `try/catch` that returns `[]` on thrown errors; a FIFO never throws, it hangs.
- `versionsFilePath` (line 135): `path.join(goalsDir(), \`${sessionId}.versions.json\`)` — same data dir as the objective file.
- Callers validate `sessionId` via `isValidObjectiveKey` before reaching `readVersionList`, so the gap is purely the read shape, not key handling.

The test suite already has a FIFO regression for the objective file (`objectives.test.js`, "rejects a FIFO at the objective path promptly instead of blocking", line ~63) but none for the versions file.

## Why it matters

- DoS: a single FIFO (or multi-hundred-MB file) at `<data-dir>/goals/<id>.versions.json` makes the goal-history endpoints and goal saves hang forever, with no timeout.
- The versions file is bounded on disk by `GOAL_OBJECTIVE_VERSION_CAP` (20) × up to 1M chars, so an oversized read is plausible in normal (non-adversarial) use too, not just a planted file.
- Inconsistent with the module's own `readObjective` contract and with the shared bounded-read helper (`lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `readVersionList` opens the versions file with `O_NONBLOCK` (POSIX), stats the handle, returns `[]` when the path is not a regular file, and reads at most a defined byte cap (enforced during the read, chunked, not a single max+1 allocation).
- A FIFO at the versions path resolves to `[]` within the test timeout (mirroring the existing objective-file FIFO test).
- A directory at the versions path resolves to `[]`.
- An oversized versions file resolves to `[]` (or is otherwise not buffered whole).
- Existing version-history tests still pass (append/list/read/delete/prune/cap).
- Regression test added in `objectives.test.js` covering the FIFO case for the versions file.

## Suggested fix shape

Mirror `readObjective`: open with non-blocking flags, `handle.stat()`, reject non-regular, chunked read up to a `GOAL_VERSIONS_MAX_READ_BYTES` cap, then `JSON.parse` the clamped buffer. Or adopt `lib/shared/bounded-file-read.js` if a sync/async result shape suits the caller; either way the read must not buffer the whole file before judging size.

body:
## Summary

`POST /api/projects/:projectId/icon/discover` reads a project-controlled favicon path and stores its bytes as the project icon without rejecting symlinks or ensuring the opened file resolves inside the project directory.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/project-icon-routes.js:474-559` — the discover handler selects `favicon.(ico|png|svg|jpg|jpeg|webp)` candidates from `fsSearchRuntime.searchFilesystemFiles(project.path, ...)`, takes `selected.path`, and passes it to `readDiscoveredIcon(selected.path)` before writing the bytes into `projectIconsDirPath` and serving them later via `/api/projects/:projectId/icon`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/project-icon-routes.js:50-89` — `readDiscoveredIcon` opens the path with `fsPromises.open(filePath, storedIconOpenFlags(process.platform))` where `storedIconOpenFlags` is `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX (`:3-24`, no `O_NOFOLLOW`), then checks `handle.stat().isFile()` and size bounds and reads chunks. `open` follows symlinks and `fstat` reports the target, so a symlink whose target is a regular file passes the regular-file/size checks.
- The handler does not `lstat` the discovered path, reject symbolic links, or verify `realpath(selected.path)` stays within `project.path` before reading.

## Why it matters

A project containing a symlink named like `public/favicon.png -> /path/outside/project` causes discover to read the symlink target (up to the 5 MiB cap) and persist/serve its contents as the project icon. This allows reading arbitrary regular files reachable by the OpenChamber server process through the icon discovery flow, which is problematic for tunneled/remote UI access or multi-user scenarios where project contents should not grant reads outside the project tree.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Reject discovered icon candidates that are symbolic links (e.g. `lstat` and require non-symlink, and/or open with `O_NOFOLLOW` on POSIX) and/or require `realpath(selected.path)` to be contained within the project root before reading.
- Add regression coverage: a favicon symlink inside the project pointing to a regular file outside the project is not discovered/read/stored (returns an appropriate 4xx/not-found/error response), while a normal in-project favicon still works.
- Keep existing protections (non-regular rejection for FIFOs, empty/oversize handling, bounded read, supported format checks).

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`ce3173a4923e4bd365bea77f0b16c55636fbc8c2`, 2026-11-15), `packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.js` builds and executes a shell command for the macOS `say` TTS endpoint using untrusted request fields:

- `packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.js:196-197` reads `rate` and `voice` from `req.body`:
  - `const { text, rate = 200, language, languageSample } = req.body || {};`
  - `let voice = typeof req.body?.voice === 'string' && req.body.voice.trim() ? req.body.voice.trim() : 'Samantha';`
- `routes.js:225-230` imports `child_process.exec` and wraps it with `promisify(exec)` as `execAsync`.
- `routes.js:237` escapes `text` for shell embedding (`replace(/'/g, "'\\''").replace(/"/g, '\\"')`) but does **not** validate/sanitize `voice` or `rate`.
- `routes.js:242` interpolates `voice`, `rate`, and `tempFile`/`escapedText` into a shell command string:
  - `const cmd = \`say -v "${voice}" -r ${rate} -o "${tempFile}" --data-format=aac '${escapedText}'\`;`
- `routes.js:245` executes it via `await execAsync(cmd);`.

`voice` is placed inside double quotes with no escaping for `"`, `$`, `` ` ``, `\`, newlines, or shell metacharacters. `rate` is inserted unquoted/unvalidated and can contain non-numeric shell syntax. Because `exec` runs through a shell, crafted values can break argument boundaries.

## Why it matters

On macOS (`process.platform === 'darwin'`, checked at `routes.js:203-205`), `/api/tts/say/speak` can become a local command-execution primitive in the server process context if an attacker can reach the endpoint and supply a crafted body. Even in local-desktop usage this is a high-risk trust-boundary bug (browser content/extensions or other local callers hitting the web server API can inject shell syntax). It is also brittle input handling: malformed `rate`/`voice` produce confusing shell failures instead of a clear 4xx validation error.

## Reproduction shape (code-level)

1. On macOS, send `POST /api/tts/say/speak` with JSON such as:
   - `{"text":"hi","voice":"Samantha\" -o /tmp/x #","rate":200}` or
   - `{"text":"hi","voice":"Samantha","rate":"200; echo injected"}`
2. `routes.js:242` interpolates these values directly into `cmd`, and `routes.js:245` executes the string with `exec`.
3. The shell interprets the injected syntax instead of treating `voice`/`rate` as data (observable by command side effects or altered `say` invocation).

I did not execute a live exploit; this is verified from the current source path.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Replace shell-string execution with an argv-based API (`execFile`/`spawn`) so `voice`, `rate`, `tempFile`, and `text` are passed as arguments without shell interpretation.
- Validate and coerce `rate` to a safe numeric range/type (e.g. finite integer within accepted words-per-minute bounds) and return 400 for invalid values.
- Constrain `voice` before use (allowlist installed/known voices from `say -v '?'` capability data, or a strict safe-name pattern) and reject/normalize invalid values.
- Add route-level tests covering:
  - valid `voice`/`rate`/`text` still generate and return audio on darwin-capable paths (or mocked command invocation asserting argv, not shell string);
  - malicious/metacharacter `voice` and non-numeric/injected `rate` are rejected with 4xx and never passed to a shell command;
  - existing behavior for `language: "auto"` voice selection remains intact for valid inputs.
- Preserve temp-file cleanup and current response headers/status behavior for successful requests.

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` (ce3173a49, 2026-11-15), `packages/web/server/lib/source-control/routes.js` defines a local `resolveDirectoryQuery` that silently selects the first value when Express supplies a repeated `directory` query parameter:

```js
// packages/web/server/lib/source-control/routes.js:22-25
const resolveDirectoryQuery = (value) => {
  const directory = Array.isArray(value) ? value[0] : value;
  return Object.prototype.toString.call(directory) === '[object String]' ? directory : '';
};
```

This resolver is used by both source-control read routes:

- `GET /api/source-control/repository-context` (`:186-192`): `bindingService.resolveContext(resolveDirectoryQuery(req.query?.directory))`
- `GET /api/source-control/binding` (`:236-243`): `bindingOperations.read(resolveDirectoryQuery(req.query?.directory))`

A request like `?directory=/repo/a&directory=/repo/b` is parsed by Express as `['/repo/a', '/repo/b']`; the resolver returns `/repo/a` and the route proceeds with that directory instead of rejecting the ambiguous scope.

By contrast, the git resolver in `packages/web/server/lib/git/routes.js:137-146` explicitly rejects array-valued query parameters as ambiguous and returns `null` so callers can return an invalid-parameter response (#2121).

## Why it matters

A client that accidentally serializes `directory` twice (or an intermediary that duplicates the parameter) can silently read source-control context/binding state for the first project instead of receiving a clear client error. Rejecting ambiguous scope is safer and easier to diagnose than silently selecting one value, and keeps source-control routes consistent with the git/project-directory query handling contracts.

## Related

- #2121 (closed, git resolver rejects repeated directory)
- #2123 (open, `project-directory-runtime.js` still selects first element)
- #2291 (open, git routes bypassing `resolveDirectoryQuery`)

This issue is distinct: it covers the source-control module's own resolver and its `/api/source-control/repository-context` and `/api/source-control/binding` callers.

## Acceptance criteria

- `resolveDirectoryQuery` in `packages/web/server/lib/source-control/routes.js` rejects an array-valued `directory` query parameter as ambiguous instead of selecting element zero (return the same invalid/empty sentinel the existing callers treat as a bad request, or update callers to return HTTP 400 consistently).
- `GET /api/source-control/repository-context` and `GET /api/source-control/binding` return a consistent client error (400) for repeated `directory` values without resolving context/binding for an arbitrary selected directory.
- Add route/resolver tests covering: single valid `directory`, missing/empty `directory`, and repeated `directory` values for both endpoints (and confirm no binding/context resolution occurs for the rejected repeated case).
- Preserve existing single-value behavior for valid string `directory` parameters.

## Evidence

On `origin/main` (ce3173a49, 2026-11-15), `packages/web/server/lib/git/routes.js` has `resolveDirectoryQuery` (line ~137-145) that rejects array-valued query parameters as ambiguous and returns `null`. Some git routes use it, but many read query params raw and only reject falsy values, so a repeated parameter (Express parses `?directory=A&directory=B` as an array) passes the truthy check and is forwarded to git/service functions as a non-string.

Examples (current lines):
- `GET /api/git/remote-url` (715-721): `const directory = req.query.directory; if (!directory) return 400` and `const remote = req.query.remote || 'origin';` then `getRemoteUrl(directory, remote)`. A repeated `directory` or `remote` becomes an array and is passed through.
- `GET /api/git/current-identity` (733-738): raw `directory` passed to `getCurrentIdentity(directory)`.
- `GET /api/git/has-local-identity` (749-754): raw `directory` passed to `hasLocalIdentity(directory)`.
- `POST /api/git/set-identity` (765-767): raw `directory` required/passed.
- `GET /api/git/primary-root` (849-853) and `GET /api/git/toplevel` (864-868): raw `directory` while other git routes (e.g. `/api/git/status` at 816, `/api/git/worktrees` at 555, `/api/git/diff-range` at 1063/1084, `/api/git/log` at 1842) use `resolveDirectoryQuery`.
- `POST /api/git/commit-summaries` (879-883), `GET /api/git/diff` (937-941), and many subsequent git endpoints (grep shows 30+ `req.query.directory` reads without `resolveDirectoryQuery`) take raw directory values.

Downstream, `packages/web/server/lib/git/service.js` passes `directory` into `createGit(directory, ...)` / simple-git and `remoteName` into `git.remote(['get-url', '--', remoteName])` (e.g. `getRemoteUrl` at ~2843), so array values cause type confusion instead of a clear 400.

## Why it matters

Ambiguous or malformed query input can target the wrong repository context or produce confusing failures deep in git operations. This is the same class fixed for routes using `resolveDirectoryQuery` in #2121, but remaining endpoints (and the `remote` parameter) were not brought to the same contract.

Related: #2121 (closed), #2123 (open, different module: project-directory-runtime filesystem/config scope).

## Acceptance criteria

- All git routes that accept `directory`, `remote`, `path`, `branch`, `base`, `head`, or `hash` via query/body reject repeated (array) and non-string values consistently (reuse `resolveDirectoryQuery` or equivalent validation) and return a client error (400) without passing ambiguous values to git/service functions.
- `/api/git/remote-url` validates `remote` as a non-empty string (defaulting to `origin` only when absent), not a truthy array.
- Add route/helper tests covering single value, missing/empty value, and repeated values for representative endpoints (`remote-url`, identity routes, primary-root/toplevel, and at least one diff/log-style route still using raw reads).
- Preserve existing single-value behavior and the intentional `resolveDirectoryQuery(..., preserveWhitespace)` cases.

title: fix(web): prevent settings reads hanging when a regular file is swapped for a FIFO

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Problem

`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/settings-runtime.js:131-145` implements `readGatedFile` as `stat(path)` followed by `readFile(path)`. The stat rejects a FIFO and checks the 8 MiB limit, and the post-read byte check catches growth. But the path is resolved again by `readFile`: if another local process replaces the regular settings/preferences file with a FIFO after `stat` returns, `readFile` opens the FIFO and waits indefinitely for a writer. The check that is supposed to reject non-regular files is therefore bypassable in the stat/read gap. `readSettingsFromDiskStrict` (`:718-732`) hangs directly; lenient and preferences reads use the same helper and can stall their callers too.

## Reproduction (verified on current `origin/main` `072ba8c8e1c2db95897878554d4c544dd5294c7c`)

Using the real `createSettingsRuntime` and native `fs/promises` in an isolated temporary directory, wrapped `stat` to first stat the regular settings file and then replace its path with a FIFO before returning the successful result. `readSettingsFromDiskStrict()` then entered the native `readFile` on that FIFO and did not settle within 2 seconds (probe timed out). No repository files were changed.

## Impact

A path replacement in the user's settings directory can wedge settings reads in the server. The new bounded-read guard explicitly aims to reject FIFOs promptly, but the path-based check/read sequence does not preserve that guarantee under concurrent replacement. The post-read byte-length check covered by #1754 protects growth, not a non-regular replacement that never reaches the post-read check.

## Suggested fix and acceptance criteria

- Read from one opened handle rather than re-resolving the path after `stat`; use nonblocking/open-handle regular-file validation so replacing the path after validation cannot redirect the read to a FIFO.
- Preserve the existing missing-file, strict, lenient, and preferences error mappings and the 8 MiB cap, including the during-read/growth bound.
- Add a deterministic regression test through the injected `fsPromises` seam that swaps the path to a FIFO after stat and proves the strict reader settles promptly with a non-regular-file refusal; cover the shared helper's lenient/preferences callers as appropriate.
- Run the settings-runtime test suite.

Related, distinct trackers: #1653/#1754 cover adding and testing the settings read size gate; #1605 covers stat/read cap races in the filesystem read and preview routes, not this settings-runtime path.

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`072ba8c8e`), `packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js` computes `readStart = size - loadCap`, then, whenever `readStart > 0`, unconditionally slices through the first newline (`raw = raw.slice(firstNewline + 1)`).

Reproduced with two valid JSONL rows and `maxLoadBytes` set to exactly the byte length of the newest row plus its newline. In this setup, `readStart` is exactly the start of the newest row, so the read window contains one complete row. `createScheduledTaskRunHistory()` nevertheless returned `[]`: it discarded that row as if the window had begun mid-line. The current test in `run-history.test.js` covers a window beginning halfway through a row, but not one beginning at a line boundary.

## Why it matters

When an oversized history file is loaded with a byte cap, a complete newest row can disappear from the in-memory history if the cap happens to align with the beginning of a JSONL row. This loses valid recent run evidence; it is not limited to the incomplete oldest row the bounded-tail logic intends to omit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve the first row when `readStart` is at the beginning of a JSONL line; discard the first fragment only when the byte before `readStart` is not a newline.
- Add regression coverage for both an exact line-boundary window (newest complete row retained) and a mid-row window (partial first row discarded).
- Keep the startup read within `maxLoadBytes` and retain the existing malformed/torn-line behavior.

## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`072ba8c8e1c2db95897878554d4c544dd5294c7c`), `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js` handles explicit overwrite in `POST /api/fs/upload` by opening a fresh same-directory temporary file with `fsPromises.open(tmp, 'wx')` (around lines 1722-1724), then renaming it over the existing file (around line 1741). The temp file is created with the process default mode filtered by umask; the existing target's mode is not copied. A disposable filesystem reproduction of this exact create-then-rename pattern changed an executable `0755` file to `0644` under the normal `022` umask.

The route does this only when `overwrite=true`; its existing upload tests verify atomic replacement but do not assert mode preservation. Overwriting an executable script or other permission-sensitive file can silently remove its executable bit (and may replace other mode bits), leaving the uploaded content unusable or changing its access semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit overwrite preserves the existing target's permission mode unless the API intentionally documents a different mode policy.
- New-file uploads retain their current safe default permissions.
- Add a regression test that overwrites a file with non-default mode bits (including an executable file) and verifies the committed file's mode.
- Keep the atomic temp-file-and-rename behavior and existing overwrite/no-overwrite race protections.

body:
## Evidence

On current `main` (`072ba8c8e1c2db95897878554d4c544dd5294c7c`), `packages/ui/src/apps/mobileRelayFetch.ts:16-35` races `tunnel.fetch()` against a timer and returns `{ failure: 'timeout' }` without aborting the request. The relay client already supports `RequestInit.signal`: `packages/ui/src/lib/relay/tunnel-client.ts:796-821,823-839` removes the stream and sends `StreamAbort` when that signal aborts. Without cancellation, a timed-out request remains in `channel.streams` until a response or channel failure; the timeout wrapper has stopped observing it.

This wrapper is used for connection health/session checks and for the non-idempotent pairing redemption POST (`packages/ui/src/apps/mobileConnections.ts:1650-1659`). A timeout can therefore leave relay work and stream state active after the UI has already reported failure. Existing `mobileRelayFetch.test.ts` checks timeout results but does not assert that the underlying request is cancelled.

## Suggested fix

Give each relay attempt an abort controller and abort it when its budget expires, while preserving the distinction between a timeout and other transport failures. Ensure retry attempts receive fresh signals and do not reuse an aborted signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- A relay request that exceeds its budget is aborted, causing the tunnel stream to be cleaned up and the abort frame to be sent when the channel is still available.
- A response arriving before the deadline is unchanged; a timeout still reports `failure: 'timeout'`.
- Each retry gets a usable, fresh signal, and non-idempotent pairing redemption is never retried.
- Add deterministic tests that observe the abort signal on timeout, verify no abort on success, and preserve the existing retry/timeout behavior.

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`072ba8c8`), `packages/ui/src/stores/useSmallModelStore.ts:48-67` writes a successful `/api/small-model` response to `byKey` without checking whether the request is still current. `invalidate()` at `:78-80` clears both `byKey` and `inFlight`, but does not cancel or mark pending requests stale. A request started before invalidation can therefore complete later and repopulate the cache; if a fresh request has completed first, the older answer can overwrite it.

Invalidation is wired to provider/settings changes and runtime endpoint changes (`:89-92`). The availability hook fetches as controls become active (`packages/ui/src/hooks/useSmallModelAvailability.ts:9-18`); the result gates goal checks and AI rename (`packages/ui/src/hooks/useSessionGoal.ts:34-46`, `packages/ui/src/components/session/useSessionAiRenameAction.ts:16-40`). A late stale `available: false` can disable these controls after configuration made the model available; a late `true` can leave them enabled after it became unavailable, until the cache refreshes.

The existing store tests cover settled invalidation and request coalescing (`useSmallModelStore.test.ts:63-73`), but not a pending response that arrives after invalidation. I verified the behavior from source; I did not run a timing repro.

## Suggested fix and acceptance criteria

- Ensure invalidation makes all earlier requests unable to update the cache (for example, with an invalidation generation or per-key request identity).
- Ensure an older request's cleanup cannot remove a newer request from the in-flight map.
- Add a deterministic regression test: defer request A, invalidate, start and resolve request B, then resolve A; assert B's availability remains cached. Include a control showing normal same-key request coalescing still works.
- Preserve the current behavior where failed or malformed responses do not erase a known answer.

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`072ba8c8`), the legacy whole-snapshot POST at `packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/routes.js:250-290` merges the incoming snapshot (`:271-272`) and persists the merged result (`:285-289`), but computes `changed` using only `merged.foldersMap` versus `current.foldersMap` (`:273`). `mergeSnapshots()` also merges `collapsedFolderIds` and `deletedFolderIds` (`:44-53, 108-125`). Therefore a collapse-only or tombstone-only state change can be written while `changed` stays false, leaving `updatedAt` unadvanced by the route and `announce()` uncalled.

The event is the refresh path for other clients: `packages/ui/src/sync/session-folders-sync.ts:5-14` reloads on `session-folders-changed`, and `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/feature-routes-runtime.js:769-784` broadcasts the server event. A read-only route repro with fake file I/O posted the same `foldersMap` plus `collapsedFolderIds: ['f1']`; the merged collapse state was persisted but the announcement count remained zero.

Dedupe: all-state searches for `session folder collapsedFolderIds notification`, `session folders announce collapse legacy POST`, `session-folders tombstone notification`, and `session folders` found no matching tracker. OPEN #2103 is unrelated login throttling; closed #1761 concerns oversized merged snapshots, not change notification. Open-PR searches for the collapse/announcement terms found no implementation. `bun test packages/web/server/lib/session-folders/routes.test.js` could not start because `zod` is not installed in this checkout.

## Why it matters

Clients connected to the same server can retain stale folder-collapse or tombstone state after a legacy client writes it. The state is durable on disk, but other clients may not refresh until a later unrelated event or stream reconnect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Detect changes to all persisted merge state, including `foldersMap`, `collapsedFolderIds`, and `deletedFolderIds`, not only the folder map.
- When a legacy POST changes that state, advance `updatedAt` monotonically and announce the revision so connected clients reload it.
- Add regression coverage for a collapse-only POST and a tombstone-only POST, asserting the persisted snapshot, advanced revision, and one announcement; preserve no-op POST behavior.

body:
## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`072ba8c8`), `packages/web/server/lib/fs/workspace-file-names.js:80-94` enforces `MAX_WORKSPACES = 8` when starting a load (`:89-93`), but the asynchronous completion handler unconditionally calls `workspaces.set(directory, ...)` (`:84-87`). If a pending workspace entry was evicted to make room for later requests, its completion can reinsert it without rerunning the size check.

Verified with the real `createWorkspaceFileNameIndex` module and an injected fake `spawn`: start nine distinct workspace lookups concurrently, complete the eight newer listings first and the evicted oldest listing last, then look up the oldest workspace again. The call counts were `callsAfterNine: 9`, `callsAfterRevisitOldest: 9`; the second lookup reused the evicted entry instead of starting a fresh listing. This demonstrates that concurrent completions can restore an entry after eviction and violate the cache's eight-workspace bound. The route is reachable through `/api/fs/find-by-name` in `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js:1116-1129`.

All-state issue searches for `workspaceFileNames concurrent cache evict MAX_WORKSPACES pending stale`, `workspace cache eviction file index`, `find-by-name bounded cache`, and `MAX_WORKSPACES workspace`, plus open-PR searches for `workspace-file-names cache`, found no matching tracker or implementation.

## Why it matters

The cache is explicitly bounded because each listing can produce a sizeable in-memory filename index. Under concurrent lookups across distinct workspaces, evicted entries can be resurrected and the intended bound no longer limits retained indexes, increasing server memory beyond the designed cap.

## Acceptance criteria

- Ensure completion of an evicted pending lookup cannot reinsert its result into the bounded cache (or otherwise keep retained workspace indexes within `MAX_WORKSPACES`).
- Add a deterministic regression test with more than eight distinct pending workspace loads, completing an evicted load after the others, and verify it is not retained beyond the cap.
- Preserve same-workspace in-flight request coalescing and normal cache freshness behavior.

## Evidence

On current `origin/main` (`072ba8c8`), `packages/ui/src/lib/sessionKnowledgeApi.ts:51-76` caches each summary for five seconds. `summaryCacheKey()` includes only the directory and session ID (`:53-55`); `fetchSessionKnowledgeSummary()` returns the cached promise without making a request while it is fresh (`:69-76`). The module does not include or observe runtime identity. Meanwhile, `packages/ui/src/lib/runtime-switch.ts:163-203` changes the active runtime endpoint and emits runtime-change events, but does not invalidate this cache.

Reproduction: on runtime A, fetch a session summary; switch to runtime B; within five seconds fetch the same directory/session summary again. The second call returns the promise cached from A rather than requesting B, so the UI can display notes/plans/memory counts from the previous runtime. This is distinct from OPEN #2145, which covers pending loads in `useAgentMemoryStore`, not this summary cache.

The existing focused test could not run in this checkout: `bun test packages/ui/src/lib/sessionKnowledgeApi.test.ts` stops because `zod` is not installed. The source path above demonstrates the cache-key and endpoint-switch behavior directly.

## Why it matters

Runtime switches can expose stale project/session knowledge in the newly selected runtime's UI and misrepresent which context that session carries.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scope cached summaries to the active runtime or invalidate them when the runtime changes, so a post-switch fetch cannot reuse a prior runtime's promise/result.
- Add a regression test that fetches the same directory/session on runtime A, switches to B within the cache window, and verifies the second fetch uses B's response.
- Preserve same-runtime request deduplication and the short freshness window.
