## Evidence

`packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/screenshots.js:40-74` builds the filename from a label and a timestamp with millisecond precision, then writes with `fs.writeFile` (which truncates an existing destination). Two `browser.capture` calls for the same label in the same millisecond therefore receive the same path.

Reproduced against the real filesystem by running two concurrent `writeScreenshot` calls with the same `now` and label: both returned `.openchamber/screenshots/same-2026-11-21T05-00-00-123.jpg`, and the final file contained only the second capture (`second`). The current test suite covers path shape and content but not collisions (`screenshots.test.js`).

## Impact

Concurrent captures can silently replace one another. Both tool calls report success and return the same Markdown path, so the earlier screenshot is lost and answers or review evidence can show the wrong image.

## Acceptance criteria

- Concurrent captures with the same label and timestamp produce distinct paths, without replacing an existing capture.
- Add a regression test that runs concurrent writes with a fixed clock and verifies both files retain their respective contents.
- Keep the returned paths project-relative and preserve the existing label sanitization and MIME extension behavior.

title: fix(web): project plan saves write the plan body in place — a save can leave it truncated or read half-written

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

Saves of project plan markdown files write the live file in place. `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js` calls `fsPromises.writeFile(filePath, raw, 'utf8')` on the existing plan file for shared-plan saves (`:925`) and linked-plan saves (`:955`), and `fsPromises.writeFile(path.join(plansDir, file), ...)` for new plans (`:1000`). `writeFile` opens with `w`, which truncates the destination before any bytes are written. The context store in the same file (`:343-352`) already writes a temp sibling and renames it with `renameWithRetry`, so the plan bodies are the odd ones out.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js:955`: linked plan save, `await fsPromises.writeFile(filePath, raw, 'utf8');` after the expected-content check at `:901-909`. The file is the user's plan body.
- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js:925`: the same in-place write for shared plans.
- `packages/web/server/lib/project-context/runtime.js:343-352`: the context store uses `${filePath}.tmp-…` plus `renameWithRetry`, which is the pattern the plan saves do not follow.
- Fresh searches: #2378 covers prompt, skill, plugin and snippet writers, and does not name `project-context`. #99 (closed) covers the context store's rename, not plan bodies. #2330 and #899 are different stores. No open or closed issue or PR names project-context plan saves.

## Why it matters

A plan is user-authored content. If a save is interrupted or the disk fails partway, the plan body can be left truncated with no error, and the previous text is gone. A reader that runs during the truncate window (the plans list or plan view) sees an empty or partial plan. The new-plan create at `:1000` has the same exposure, though its file is new, so the loss is limited to the body being written.

## Suggested fix shape

Route the three plan writes through the same temp-plus-rename helper that the context store uses (`renameWithRetry`, or `writeFileAtomic` from `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/atomic-write.js`). Keep the expected-content check and the `access` ENOENT guard before the write, and keep the symlink behaviour in mind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Shared-plan save, linked-plan save and new-plan create write through temp-plus-rename; no in-place `writeFile` remains for plan bodies in `project-context/runtime.js`.
- [x] A failed replacement leaves the previous plan file intact and removes the temp file.
- [x] A concurrent reader during save never observes an empty or partial plan (for example a read loop during a save never sees a length below the old or new length).
- [x] The existing 409 expected-content conflict and ENOENT refusal still fire before any write.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/electron/main.mjs:1885-1904` makes `navigateWindow` reject when `BrowserWindow.loadURL()` fails, except for explicitly allowed benign aborts. But `createBrowserWindow` starts initial navigation without observing that promise at `:2896-2899` (`void navigateWindow(...)`). This path is used for both the main window (`activateMainWindow`, `:2988-2993`) and additional host windows (`createAdditionalWindow`, `:3140-3149`). Unlike the guarded host-switch and `window.open` call sites, these initial loads have no rejection handler. A failed renderer load therefore becomes an unhandled rejection instead of a handled startup/window failure; on Node's default unhandled-rejection policy this can terminate the Electron main process.

## Why it matters

A transient or invalid initial UI URL / local renderer load failure can take down the desktop app rather than leaving the failed window in a controlled state or reporting the error through the existing logger. The main-window path is especially important during startup; the additional-window path can affect opening a configured host.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every initial `navigateWindow` call started by `createBrowserWindow` observes non-benign rejections.
- Main-window startup and additional-window creation handle/report a failed load without an unhandled rejection; define whether the failed window is closed or an error is surfaced.
- Add regression coverage for a rejected `loadURL()` on both initial-window paths, while preserving the benign-abort behavior for the splash path.

body:
## Verified behavior

`packages/electron/main.mjs:5239` starts `mutateSettingsRoot(...)` with `void` when a valid `desktop_set_window_theme` payload changes `desktopSplashColors`. The mutation promise rejects if the settings directory/write/rename fails (`writeJsonFile` at `:649-668`); the mutation chain intentionally recovers internally for later writes, but the returned `next` promise still rejects (`:674-685`). This call site neither awaits nor catches that returned rejection. Node's default unhandled-rejection behavior can therefore terminate the Electron main process on a settings persistence failure during a theme update, instead of reporting a recoverable save error. Other settings mutation call sites await the operation.

This is separate from geometry debounce persistence (#2432): the affected entry point is the theme IPC handler and it writes `desktopSplashColors` through the shared settings mutation chain.

## Why it matters

A transient filesystem/permission/disk error while saving splash colors can crash the desktop app. The same `mutateSettingsRoot` implementation is deliberately resilient enough to keep subsequent writes flowing, but this fire-and-forget caller bypasses that recovery at the caller boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Handle rejection from the fire-and-forget theme settings mutation (for example, log a useful warning and keep the app alive, or await and return a controlled IPC failure).
- Add a regression test for a rejected settings write from the `desktop_set_window_theme` path that proves the failure is observed/handled and does not become an unhandled rejection.
- Preserve the existing serialization and recovery behavior of `settingsMutationChain`.

## Evidence

In `packages/electron/main.mjs:5114-5134`, `desktop_get_installed_apps` starts `void refresh()` and immediately returns cached data. `refresh()` awaits `buildPlatformInstalledApps`, creates the cache directory, writes `discovered-apps.json`, then emits an update. The handler's intentional stale-cache response makes an app crash disproportionate to a recoverable cache refresh failure.

## Suggested fix

Keep refresh asynchronous, but handle/report its rejection so the cache remains stale and the app continues running; optionally surface a bounded diagnostic event/log. Add a regression test that makes the refresh reject and verifies the IPC call returns its cache response without an unhandled rejection or process crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rejected installed-app enumeration or cache persistence does not become an unhandled rejection in the Electron main process.
- The existing cached response remains available when refresh fails.
- A focused regression test covers the failure path, and successful refresh still emits `openchamber:installed-apps-updated`.

body:
## Evidence

At `packages/electron/window-geometry-state.mjs:35-44`, `run()` awaits `persist(browserWindow)`, but both the immediate path (`void run()`) and the timer callback (`void run(timer)`) discard the returned promise without a rejection handler. The `finally` only releases revision state; it does not consume the rejection.

Reproduction on `origin/main` `467fe4ff902346179398264136e974df19c7bb2a`:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { createWindowGeometryState } from "./packages/electron/window-geometry-state.mjs"; const s=createWindowGeometryState({persist:async()=>{throw new Error("simulated settings write failure")}}); s.schedule({id:1,isDestroyed:()=>false},true); setTimeout(()=>console.log("survived"),50);'
```

Node v24.21.0 exits 1 with `Error: simulated settings write failure` and never prints `survived`. The production persistence function `writeWindowState` calls `mutateSettingsRoot` → `writeJsonFile`, which can reject on filesystem/permission/disk errors. Production callers schedule immediately on close/quit/restart (`packages/electron/main.mjs:499, 2694, 2712, 2719, 5394, 6270, 6281`) and debounce move/resize/maximize events (`:2679-2690`).

## Impact

A transient settings-file write failure during window geometry persistence becomes an unhandled rejection and can terminate the Electron main process instead of leaving the app running with the prior saved geometry. The immediate paths are especially exposed during shutdown/restart, and the debounced paths can crash the app during normal use.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rejected `persist()` calls from both immediate and timer-driven scheduling are handled, without an unhandled rejection or process termination.
- State cleanup remains correct after rejection, and a later geometry update can persist successfully.
- Add regression tests for both scheduling modes; retain the existing stale-timer/revision behavior.
- Log or otherwise surface persistence failure through the existing Electron logging path without turning a non-critical geometry write into an app crash.

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/electron/main.mjs`, `spacePreviews` is a process-lifetime `Map` (around line 1199). `spacePreviewOf(spaceId)` inserts a `{ ports, chain }` entry whenever a preview port is opened (around lines 1221–1228). `closeSpacePreviewPort()` removes the closed port but leaves the entry in the map (around lines 1249–1253), and `closeAllSpacePreviewPorts()` clears ports without deleting entries (around lines 1255–1263). There is no `spacePreviews.delete(...)` in the file. Thus, previewing and later removing spaces leaves one retained map entry per space for the lifetime of the Electron process, even when its port set is empty.

Each preview also passes its `session` to `hardenPanelSession()`, which adds it to the process-wide `panelSessions` set (around lines 1131–1137). That set likewise has no removal path. A fresh all-state issue search for `spacePreviews` and browser-panel space-session cleanup, plus an open/closed PR search, found no existing tracker.

## Impact

A user who creates, previews, and removes many isolated spaces accumulates stale per-space records and session references in the long-lived desktop process. The amount grows with lifetime usage rather than the number of currently existing spaces.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Add an explicit space-preview teardown path that runs when a space is removed (and safely handles any in-flight proxy update before dropping its state).
- Remove the stale `spacePreviews` entry and release any per-space session tracking that is no longer needed, without affecting the persistent user browser-panel session or another live space.
- Add a deterministic regression test covering preview-open, preview-close/space-removal, and state cleanup; verify a later space can still initialize and apply its proxy normally.

title: fix(ui): prevent saving stale drafts after a dirty guest editor disappears
body:
## Problem

A dirty SDK guest file editor can disappear when its extension is paused or removed. The host then loses access to the editor snapshot but can still keep `canvasDirty` set. If the user chooses Save (including as part of a dirty-file navigation prompt), `saveDraft` sees no canvas handle, clears the dirty flag, substitutes `EMPTY_CANVAS_READ`, and writes `draftContent` instead. For a guest editor whose edits were never handed to the text draft, that is the old content; the save can succeed and navigation can continue while the guest edits are lost.

Relevant source on `main` (`467fe4ff902346179398264136e974df19c7bb2a`):
- `packages/ui/src/lib/guests/capabilities.ts:10-12`: a paused/disabled guest is no longer active.
- `packages/ui/src/lib/guests/file-editors.ts:27-31`: inactive guests no longer match as file editors.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx:4074-4077` and `4931-4951`: the matching guest editor is conditionally mounted.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx:1950-1957`: when dirty but the editor handle is absent, the host clears the dirty flag and proceeds without a snapshot.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx:1975-1990`: the no-snapshot branch writes the text draft and reports the write as saved.

This is distinct from an in-flight snapshot failure: those are rejected and correctly abort save/handoff. Here the handle is already gone, so no snapshot request is made.

## Expected behavior

A Save action must not report success or proceed with navigation after a dirty guest editor has disappeared unless the guest's latest document contents were preserved and written. Preserve a host-readable last dirty snapshot before teardown, or fail closed and keep the unsaved state/action blocked until the user can recover it; do not silently write the stale text draft.

Add a regression test that edits a guest file, pauses/removes its editor before saving, and verifies that the save cannot silently replace the guest edits with the old draft. Cover the dirty-navigation Save path as appropriate. Pausing/removing an editor that has no unsaved edits should continue to work normally.

title: fix(electron): window geometry revision entries accumulate after windows close

labels.name: status/triaged
labels.description: Triage verified and routed; see agent note

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` at `d2a2277f5f3ba7c5c36726f2a28ad699e3b24f62`, `packages/electron/main.mjs:318` initializes `state.windowGeometryRevisions` as a `Map`. `debounceWindowStatePersist` at lines 923–949 increments and stores an entry for every browser-window ID at lines 926–927. When the debounce fires, lines 936–938 remove the timer but leave the revision entry. The `closed` handler at lines 2746–2762 also does not delete the revision or cancel/delete the associated timer. A source-wide search found no other cleanup or reader of this map.

## Why it matters

The Electron main process is long-lived, and every window ID that reaches the geometry persistence handler leaves a permanent map entry after the window closes. Repeated window creation/closure therefore grows retained state for the lifetime of the process. The map is small per entry, but has no bound or cleanup.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove a window’s revision entry when its final geometry persistence has completed, and/or clean it up on window close while safely invalidating any pending callback.
- Ensure an older in-flight debounce cannot persist after a newer revision or after the window has closed.
- Add focused tests for repeated updates, timer completion, and close with a pending timer; verify both timer and revision maps do not retain closed-window entries.
- Existing geometry persistence behavior for the main window remains intact.

title: fix(web): retire the v1 managed OpenCode state fallback after the v2 transition
body:
## Problem

The managed OpenCode v2 store landed in #82 / PR #2322, but the v1 `state.json` + `draining.json` compatibility path remains live in `lifecycle.js`. `isOwnedOpenCodePid` still treats a v1-only record as a reason to run `ps` and infer ownership from the process command; startup adoption and drain recovery also continue reading the v1 files. The documentation says the dual-write was kept for one release and identifies retiring these readers as the remaining step.

Once the compatibility release has passed, leaving the fallback active keeps two ownership sources and retains the legacy PID-reuse/`ps` inference path, despite the v2 store being the ownership record.

## Scope

Complete the post-transition cleanup from #82: make `store.json` the sole managed-OpenCode ownership and drain record, then remove v1 writes and fallback reads from lifecycle action/adoption/recovery paths. Preserve the #82 v1-to-v2 migration for existing installations; do not remove migration support or change the separate listener/supervisor work tracked by #81.

## Evidence

On `main` `37b1667f6`:
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/DOCUMENTATION.md` says the v2 store is dual-written with v1 files "kept for one release" and lists v1 ownership checks, startup adoption, and drain recovery as the remaining retirement work.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/lifecycle.js` `isOwnedOpenCodePid` accepts v1-only records and invokes `ps`; lifecycle startup/drain paths still read or write the v1 pair.
- #82 is closed as complete via merged PR #2322, which explicitly retained v1 compatibility for one release. No open PR currently handles the follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- `store.json` is the only live ownership/drain source after the compatibility transition; no v1 fallback can establish ownership or invoke the legacy `ps` check.
- Existing v1 installations still migrate to v2 with every active/draining generation preserved; migration tests retain a no-lost-generations oracle.
- Lifecycle tests cover startup adoption, handoff, drain recovery, and stale/recycled PID behavior without relying on v1 files.
- Remove obsolete v1 dual-writes/readers and update `DOCUMENTATION.md` to describe the final state and migration behavior.
- Keep scope separate from #81's listener/supervisor changes.

Related: #82 (completed v2 store and one-release compatibility path), #81 (listener/supervisor).

body:
## Evidence

`packages/web/server/lib/message-search/routes.js:29-33` parses `session` with `z.string().trim().catch('')`. Express represents repeated query keys as arrays, so `GET /api/openchamber/message-search?q=secret&session=target-session&session=other-session` makes parsing fall back to `session: ''`. At lines 81-84 the route sends `sessionId: query.session || null` to the search runtime, silently removing the requested session constraint.

Verified with a live Express route probe: the request returned HTTP 200 and called `messageSearchRuntime.search` with `sessionId: null`. `packages/web/server/lib/message-search/store.js:275-280` adds the session predicate only when `sessionId` is truthy, so the resulting search spans every indexed conversation. Message-search documentation describes this as full-text search over conversations, while the `session` parameter is documented as restricting results to one conversation. The existing `routes.test.js` covers limit parsing only and has no repeated-session regression case; its current tests pass.

## Why it matters

A malformed or accidentally duplicated session filter can return matching message snippets from conversations other than the one the caller intended to inspect. The failure is fail-open: instead of rejecting an ambiguous filter, it broadens scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated `session` query parameters are rejected or otherwise cannot broaden the search to an unscoped query.
- Add a route regression test showing repeated `session` values do not call the runtime with `sessionId: null`.
- Keep scalar session searches and deliberately unscoped searches working as intended.

body:
## Evidence

In `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/openchamber-routes.js:122-145`, `parseString` accepts only scalar strings. Express represents repeated query keys as arrays, so `reportUsage=false&reportUsage=true` makes `parseString(req.query.reportUsage)` return `undefined`. `parseReportUsage(undefined)` defaults to `true`, so the route passes an opt-in to `checkForUpdates` instead of honoring the explicit opt-out.

The downstream update payload in `packages/web/server/lib/package-manager.js:204-215` uses that boolean to include an install ID and send the `reportUsage` value to the configured update API. A focused reproduction is:

`GET /api/openchamber/update-check?appType=web&reportUsage=false&reportUsage=true`

The route's existing test covers a single `reportUsage=false` value, but not repeated values.

## Impact

When an update API is configured, a malformed or ambiguously constructed request that contains the user's explicit opt-out can report usage and include an install identifier. This violates the expected privacy behavior of the opt-out.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated `reportUsage` values do not become an opt-in when any supplied value is an explicit opt-out. Prefer rejecting an ambiguous value or failing closed to `false`.
- Add a regression test showing repeated opt-out parameters never call `checkForUpdates` with `reportUsage: true` (and preserve the intended single-value/default behavior).
- Confirm the downstream payload omits the install ID when reporting is disabled.

body:
## Finding

`GET /api/projects/:projectId/scheduled-tasks/run-history` silently drops a repeated `taskId` filter and returns unfiltered project history. The handler passes `req.query.taskId` through `asNonEmptyString(...) ?? undefined` (`packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/routes.js:89`). Express supplies repeated query parameters as an array; `asNonEmptyString` rejects non-strings (`packages/web/server/lib/shared/guards.js:55-58`), so the route calls `listRuns` without `taskID`. The reader only narrows when `taskID` is truthy (`packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/run-history.js:199-210`).

## Reproduction

On current `origin/main` (`a52ae96a69ca24b9117e0eed2fd1ea01fc92da8c`), request:

`GET /api/projects/code/scheduled-tasks/run-history?taskId=A&taskId=B`

A live Express probe returned HTTP 200 with runs for both task A and task B; the reader received `{ projectID: "code" }`, with no `taskID`.

## Why it matters

A caller that intended to view one scheduled task receives the project-wide history with a success response. This is the same silent-filter-widening class already fixed for repeated `limit` and being fixed for repeated `since`/`until`, but those checks do not cover `taskId`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reject a present non-string/repeated `taskId` with HTTP 400; do not call `listRuns`.
- [ ] Preserve absent and empty `taskId` behavior, and preserve a valid single task ID.
- [ ] Add route-level regression coverage for repeated `taskId` (and valid/absent controls).

Related, narrower work: #2371 and PR #2416 cover repeated `since`/`until`, not `taskId`.

body:
## Summary

The electron SSH manager reads the shared `settings.json` through `readJsonRoot`, which returns `{}` on any parse failure. Its write paths then read-modify-write the whole file from that empty base. One malformed byte in `settings.json` therefore makes the next SSH host update silently replace the whole file with only the SSH keys it touched, erasing every other setting and the SSH instance config itself, with no error and no preserved copy.

This is the same failure class as #940 (GitHub gh-CLI toggles), #907 (Linear), and #1274, which were fixed on the web side. #940 covers only `packages/web/server/lib/github/auth.js`. The electron `ssh-manager.mjs` reader was not covered by any of them.

## Evidence (origin/main `097ac0b3146bb8fa7571c9847a5547d2999c58af`)

- `packages/electron/ssh-manager.mjs:108-115` `readJsonRoot`: `try { JSON.parse(...) } catch { return {}; }`, so a parse failure is indistinguishable from an empty file.
- Read-modify-write sites that persist the `{}`-based root: `setInstances` (`:884-921`, write at `:920`), `updateHostRuntime` (`:1009-1023`, write at `:1023`), and `persistLocalPort` (`:1084-1093`, write at `:1093`). `persistLocalPort` runs on every successful SSH connect (`:1708-1714`).
- The shared path is real: `early-startup.mjs:101-105` `settingsFilePath()` returns `<OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR>/settings.json`, which `main.mjs:645` passes to the manager. The same file holds the theme, default host and desktop hosts.
- The comment at `:119-121` says the atomic write prevents readers from seeing partial JSON that then gets coerced to `{}`. The atomic write does not protect against a file that is already malformed. A malformed file, from a hand edit or a crash in an older non-atomic writer, still hits the lenient reader.

## Reproduction (executed against the real module at `097ac0b31`)

```js
// settings.json = { "theme": "dark", "desktopSshInstances": [{ "id": "a", "destination": "u@h" }], }   <- one trailing comma
const mgr = new ElectronSshManager({ settingsFilePath: file, appVersion: 'x', emit() {} });
await mgr.persistLocalPort('a', 2222);
// file afterwards: { "desktopSshInstances": [] }
```

With a valid file, the same call keeps `theme`, `desktopDefaultHostId`, and the instance, and adds `localForward.preferredLocalPort`. With the malformed file, `theme` and the SSH instance are gone.

## Why it matters

Losing `settings.json` loses the user's SSH host configuration and preferences. A connect to any SSH host is enough to trigger it. The web side already has a strict reader for this, and the electron copy was missed.

## Suggested fix shape

- Replace `readJsonRoot` in write paths with a strict read that throws on a malformed file, or reuse the strict three-state reader from `packages/web/server/lib/shared/durable-json-store.js` (#977), which preserves the bad file aside. Read-only callers can keep the lenient behavior if needed.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - a regression test that a malformed `settings.json` is not rewritten by `persistLocalPort`, `updateHostRuntime`, or `setInstances`, and the original bytes survive (or the call fails loudly);
  - a valid-file test that unrelated keys (`theme`, `desktopDefaultHostId`, `desktopHosts`) are preserved across each write path.

## Dedupe

Searched all states for `readJsonRoot`, settings wipe, malformed/corrupt settings, and `ssh-manager`. Nearest hits are #940 (web github, closed), #907 (web linear, closed), #1274 (closed), #887/#891 (magic-prompts), #892/#898/#899/#905 (closed web stores), and #1644 (vscode read-size). None covers electron `ssh-manager.mjs`. No open PR touches `packages/electron/ssh-manager.mjs`.

body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`b003844b3936e58acebf5605e35032160835a1a5`), `packages/ui/src/components/auth/SessionAuthGate.tsx:489-511` parses non-OK response text and immediately reads `data.tunnelLocked` for HTTP 401 or `data.retryAfter` for HTTP 429. The `JSON.parse` try/catch only handles syntax errors; valid JSON `null` parses successfully, then property access throws. The outer catch at lines 521-531 treats that as a network-level failure and schedules a transient retry (or shows a generic error) instead of handling the actual 401/429 response.

This is reproducible by returning `Response` status 401 or 429 with body `null`; it does not require malformed JSON. Existing test file: `packages/ui/src/components/auth/SessionAuthGate.behavior.test.tsx`.

## Why it matters

A valid-but-unexpected JSON body from a proxy/server on an authentication response can make the gate misreport a definite server response as a connectivity problem. For 401, this can delay or obscure the locked/authentication state; for 429, it can bypass the rate-limited state.

## Acceptance criteria

- Treat parsed JSON as untrusted and require a non-null object before reading `tunnelLocked` or `retryAfter` (fall back to `{}` for other shapes).
- Add behavior tests for 401 and 429 responses whose body is the literal JSON `null`; they should take the respective locked and rate-limited branches without scheduling a transient network retry or throwing.
- Preserve existing behavior for malformed JSON and valid object responses.

title: fix(tts): say speak writes to a predictable shared temp file and leaks it on failure — concurrent requests can collide and the file is never cleaned up
body:
## Summary

`POST /api/tts/say/speak` writes its audio to a predictable path in the shared OS temp directory, `os.tmpdir()/say-${Date.now()}.m4a` (`packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.js:281-282`). Nothing makes the name unique or exclusive, and the failure path does not clean up. The rest of this server uses `fs.mkdtemp` for temp output (`cloudflare-tunnel.js:456`, `git/service.js:6674`, `skills-catalog/install.js:315`), so this route is the outlier.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.js:281-282`: `const tempDir = os.tmpdir(); const tempFile = path.join(tempDir, \`say-${Date.now()}.m4a\`);`
- `:291`: `execFileAsync('say', ['-o', tempFile, ...])` writes the file. `:294` reads it back with `readFile`. `:297` unlinks it, fire-and-forget.
- If `say` throws at `:291`, the catch at the end of the handler returns 500 and the temp file, whatever `say` already wrote, is never removed.
- No test in `packages/web/server/lib/tts/routes.test.js` covers the temp path. The existing tests stub `buildSayArgs` and the non-darwin branch.

## Why it matters

1. **Concurrent requests can share a file.** Two `speak` requests that reach `Date.now()` in the same millisecond get the same `tempFile`. Each `say` overwrites the other's output, and the first request to finish unlinks the file the second is still about to read. The second request then fails with ENOENT and returns 500 to the client. Any client that fires two speech requests together can hit this.
2. **Predictable name.** The name is guessable from the clock, and a same-user process or a symlink planted in the temp directory before the request runs would redirect `say -o` to another file. On macOS `os.tmpdir()` is the per-user `$TMPDIR`, so the exposure is limited to the same user; the fix is still the same.
3. **Leaked files on failure.** Every failed `say` leaves whatever partial output it wrote in the temp directory.

Scope: this is limited to the macOS `say` path, which is the only path that reaches `say` (the route returns 503 on other platforms before it gets here). I have not reproduced the same-millisecond collision on macOS. The finding comes from reading the code. The naming and the missing cleanup are visible without running it.

## Suggested fix shape

- Create a per-request directory with `fs.promises.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'openchamber-say-'))` and write the audio file inside it. The directory name is unpredictable and created exclusively, so a symlink cannot be planted in advance.
- Remove the whole directory in a `finally` after the response has been built, so failures leave nothing behind. Use `fs.promises.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
- Use the same pattern as `cloudflare-tunnel.js:456`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two `speak` calls with the same `Date.now()` (fake timers) each get their own directory and both return the audio bytes.
- [ ] If the stubbed `execFile` rejects, the temp directory is removed and the response is 500.
- [ ] The success path removes the directory once the audio has been read.
- [ ] A unit test asserts the output path is inside a directory created by `mkdtemp` and not a bare `os.tmpdir()` child.
- [ ] No change to the `buildSayArgs` argv contract (`routes.test.js:168-173` keeps passing).

title: fix(ci): release workflows swallow codesign failure via || true

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Problem

The release workflows swallow `codesign` failures with `|| true`, so the entitlement checks run on invalid input.

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:286`: `ENTITLEMENTS=$(codesign -d --entitlements :- "$APP_PATH" 2>&1 || true)`
- `.github/workflows/release-desktop-smoke.yml:174`: same line.

The following `grep -q "com.apple.security.app-sandbox"` and the `for key in ...` entitlement checks then run on whatever `codesign` printed. If `codesign` fails (file not found, command not found, permission denied), `ENTITLEMENTS` holds the error text or is empty, and the sandbox and required-key checks give a result that does not reflect the signed app.

## Why it matters

These steps are the release gate that rejects a sandboxed build or one missing JIT/entitlement keys. A silent failure here can ship an artifact that was never verified.

## Fix shape

- Drop `|| true`. Capture the output and exit code explicitly, for example `if ! ENTITLEMENTS=$(codesign -d --entitlements :- "$APP_PATH" 2>&1); then echo "codesign failed: $ENTITLEMENTS"; exit 1; fi`.
- Apply the same change in both workflows.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `codesign` failure in either workflow fails the step with a non-zero exit before any entitlement check runs.
- A correctly signed app still passes both workflows unchanged.

Found by the improvement-issue-creator lane-b pass (read-only audit at `origin/main` 8726d55da).

title: fix(ui): concurrent first dictation starts can create competing WebSockets

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: app/ui
labels.description: Package: ui (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Verified behavior

`DictationClient.ensureConnected()` checks `connectPromise` at `packages/ui/src/lib/dictation/dictation-client.ts:109-115`, but waits for `refreshRuntimeUrlAuthToken()` at `:123-127` before assigning `connectPromise` at `:129`. If two first-time calls enter while token refresh is pending, both pass the check and wait. Once refresh resolves, each creates its own WebSocket. Each `ready` frame then assigns `this.socket` (`:165-171`), so one caller can complete against a socket that is no longer the client's tracked socket. `onclose` only rejects pending operations when its socket is the tracked one (`:200-204`), leaving operations on the losing connection without the expected connection-loss cleanup.

This can occur when multiple starts arrive together before the first connection is established; it creates duplicate connections and can strand in-flight dictation operations if the untracked connection closes.

## Why it matters

Concurrent initial dictation starts can race during token refresh, resulting in multiple server WebSockets for one shared client and connection state that no longer matches the streams using it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reserve/share the in-flight connection promise before awaiting token refresh so concurrent callers join one connection attempt (or otherwise serialize the entire refresh-and-connect sequence).
- Add a deterministic test with a deferred token refresh and two concurrent `ensureConnected()` calls; assert only one WebSocket is opened and both callers resolve from the tracked socket.
- Cover close/error cleanup for the shared attempt so no caller or pending operation is left unresolved.

## Dedupe

All-state issue searches for `DictationClient ensureConnected concurrent`, `dictation duplicate websocket`, `websocket race`, and `dictation` found no issue for this connection-establishment race. Related closed #1017 concerns the server-side chunk reorder buffer; closed #2305 concerns the voice-capture submit deadline; open #2331 concerns cleanup of a dictation archive. None covers concurrent client connection setup. The current open PR inventory has no dictation client change.

title: fix(web): two live-session status readers still resolve Object.prototype members — warming skips prototype-named sessions and the idle reaper never reaps them
body:
## Summary

#2311 fixed the `Object.prototype` lookup class in six places (merge `1c4a19301`), but two live-session status readers still index the record returned by `/api/session/active` directly, so a session whose id is `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf` or `__proto__` is silently misread. #2311's evidence list did not include either file.

Both sites read the same payload — `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`session-warming/runtime.js:58`) keeps `Object.prototype` on the parsed result, so a missing key still yields a truthy function.

### Site 1 — prompt-cache warming silently skips such sessions

`packages/web/server/lib/session-warming/runtime.js:231`

```js
const active = activeSessionsSchema.safeParse(unwrapOpenCodeResponse(await readBoundedResponseJson(...)));
return active.success ? Boolean(active.data[sessionId]) : null;
```

Reproduced with a probe against the real warm loop: session `ses_plain` got 1 ping and `warmUntil: 1003600000`; session `constructor` got 0 pings and `warmUntil: null` — it is treated as running when it is idle, so the warming window is never armed and the cache stays cold for that id.

### Site 2 — the idle-session reaper never reaps them

`packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-sessions/routes.js:602`

```js
sessions.map((session) => [session?.id, activeStatuses[session?.id] ? { type: 'busy' } : { type: 'idle' }])
```

Probe result: id `constructor` reports `busy` while `Object.hasOwn(activeStatuses, 'constructor') === false`. `idle-session-reaper.js` consumes this map, so a prototype-named idle session is never reaped; the residue stays in the live set and counts against the dispatch cap (#791).

Session ids of that shape are accepted: the id regex is `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,128}$` (noted in #2311).

## Suggested fix

Guard both lookups with `Object.hasOwn`, or build the map with a null prototype — the shape #2311 landed at `dispatch-results/runtime.js:381`:

```js
if (Object.hasOwn(statuses, sessionId) && statuses[sessionId]) return { kind: 'running' };
```

For site 2 the whole `getSessionStatuses` map can be built with `Object.hasOwn(activeStatuses, session?.id)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both sites no longer resolve `Object.prototype` members; a session named `constructor` reads as not-running in the warm loop and as `idle` in `getSessionStatuses`.
- [ ] Regression tests for both paths, following the existing tests in `session-warming/runtime.test.js`.
- [ ] `grep` for bare `[sessionId]`/`[session?.id]` indexes on status records in the three files returns nothing unguarded.

Related: #2311 (same class, other sites), #791 (dispatch cap affected by live-set residue).

title: fix(web): prompt, skill-supporting, plugin and snippet file saves write in place — a save can leave OpenCode-watched files truncated or read half-written

body:
## Problem

Several user-save writers still replace live files in place with `fs.writeFileSync`, although `writeMdFile` and the other config writers use `writeFileAtomic` (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/atomic-write.js`). `atomic-write.js` documents why this matters: OpenCode watches these files and reloads on every change, so an in-place write can be read half-finished, and a crash mid-write leaves the file truncated.

`fs.writeFileSync(path, data)` opens the file with `w`, which truncates it before any bytes are written. A reader, or OpenCode's watcher, that runs in that window sees an empty or partial file.

Affected writers, all reachable from user save paths:

- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js:939-943` `writePromptFile`. Called from `agents.js:479` (agent system prompt in a `{file:...}` reference) and `commands.js:296` (command template file).
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js:1254-1260` `writeSkillSupportingFile`. Called from `skill-routes.js:826` and `skills.js:601/675`.
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/plugins.js:466` plugin-directory file write (`fs.writeFileSync(absolutePath, content, 'utf8')`).
- `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/snippets.js:94` snippet file write.

Related but distinct: #887/#889/#891/#892/#897/#898/#899 (JSON stores, all fixed), #2375 (rename race), #2330 (session-goal atomic writes), #2120 (run-history compaction).

## Why it matters

Agent and command prompt files are the content OpenCode loads on each run. A save that is interrupted, or a read that lands mid-write, can produce an empty or truncated agent prompt or command template with no error reported.

## Fix shape

Route all four writers through `writeFileAtomic` (or the same temp+rename helper), keeping each caller's existing validation (`assertSkillSupportingFileWithinCap`, the plugin size check, the snippet byte limit) before the write. Keep the existing `mkdirSync` calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `writePromptFile`, `writeSkillSupportingFile`, the plugin file write and the snippet file write use `writeFileAtomic`.
- [ ] A symlinked target keeps the symlink, as `writeFileAtomic` already does.
- [ ] A test or probe shows a reader never observes an empty or partial file during a save. For example, a concurrent `readFileSync` loop during `writePromptFile` never sees a length below the old or new length.
- [ ] Existing validation and size-cap errors still fire before any write.

labels.name: effort/xs

body:
## Evidence
`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js:1879-1890` checks the destination with `lstat`, then calls `fsPromises.rename`. On POSIX, `rename(2)` replaces an existing destination file. If another process creates the destination after `lstat` returns `ENOENT` but before `rename`, the route returns success and destroys the concurrent file, despite the explicit 409 guard for existing destinations.

I reproduced this deterministically on current `origin/main` (`a0580d5e4a7c8e7aafd53edd1923a609fe0340d5`) with a temporary workspace and an injected `lstat` wrapper that creates `dest.txt` immediately after the destination lookup observes `ENOENT`: the endpoint returned 200, `dest.txt` contained the source bytes instead of the concurrent bytes, and the source disappeared. The fixture was removed after the probe.

## Acceptance criteria
- Make destination creation/replacement race-safe: if a distinct destination appears after the check, the rename returns the existing-destination conflict and preserves both the source and destination contents (use a no-replace primitive or an equivalent platform-aware strategy).
- Add a regression test that injects destination creation between the lookup and commit, and retain coverage for same-file case-only renames.
- Verify behavior on supported platforms, including Windows.

title: fix(web): /api/fs/write drops file mode on editor save — 0755 scripts become 0644

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/web
labels.description: Package: web (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: area/web
labels.description: Web app

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`POST /api/fs/write` (the editor save path) drops a file's permission bits on every save. It writes the new content to a temp file and renames it over the target, and the temp file gets the process umask default (typically 0644). An executable script saved from the editor (0755) therefore comes back as 0644 and stops running.

PR #2350 (closing #2249) fixed the same loss for `POST /api/fs/upload` with `overwrite=true`, by stat-ing the existing file and chmod-ing the temp file before rename. The `/api/fs/write` path was not covered.

## Where

`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.js` on `origin/main` (`a4384ad9bb`):

- `/api/fs/write` handler starts around line 1552.
- Temp write and rename at lines 1643-1644 (`fsPromises.writeFile(tmp, ...)`, then `renameWithRetry(...)`). No stat of the existing file and no `chmod` on the temp file.
- The upload path (around lines 1719-1749) does stat, `existingMode = stats.mode & 0o7777`, then `chmod(tmp, existingMode)` before rename.

## Reproduce

1. `chmod 755 script.sh` inside a workspace.
2. Save new content through the editor, which calls `/api/fs/write`.
3. `stat -c %a script.sh` returns `644`, not `755`.

## Expected

The existing file's mode (`& 0o7777`) is kept across an editor save, the same as the upload path.

## Fix shape

Stat the existing file before the temp write. If it exists, `chmod` the temp file to its mode before `renameWithRetry`. Add a regression test in `packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.test.js` that writes a 0755 file via `/api/fs/write` and asserts the mode is still 0755.

## Searched

- #2249 (closed) and PR #2350 (merged): upload path only.
- #1127 (closed): identical-content size gate, a different defect.
- Open issues and PRs for `fs/write` and file mode: none.

body:
## Evidence

`packages/web/server/lib/dictation/local/model-downloader.js:124-142` streams a pinned archive to `${outputPath}.tmp-${Date.now()}`. Pipeline failures and size/checksum mismatches remove that temp path, but the final `await rename(tmpPath, outputPath)` is outside those cleanup handlers.

Reproduced on `origin/main` (`d3c78bc4`): download a valid pinned fixture while the destination path is an existing directory. `rename` throws `EISDIR`, and the full verified temp file remains in the download directory (`archive.tar.bz2.tmp-<timestamp>`). The catalog contains archives up to 482,468,385 bytes (`packages/web/server/lib/dictation/local/model-catalog.js:23`). `ensureLocalSttModel` removes the canonical archive on retries but does not sweep these timestamped temp files, so repeated rename failures can accumulate disk usage.

This is distinct from closed #417 (archive pinning) and #814 (download stall timeout).

## Why it matters

A filesystem error during the final promotion can leave a large, already-downloaded archive behind. Retrying does not clean the prior `.tmp-*` path. This is an uncommon failure path, but the leaked files can be hundreds of MiB each.

## Acceptance criteria

- If the final rename fails, attempt to remove `tmpPath` before rethrowing the original error.
- Add a regression test that makes the destination a directory, verifies `downloadToFile` rejects, and asserts no `.tmp-*` file remains.
- Existing successful download, size, checksum, and stall tests remain green.

title: fix(electron): remote-safe desktop_hosts_get leaks URL-embedded basic-auth credentials — redact strips clientToken/requestHeaders but not user:pass@ in url/apiUrl

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/electron
labels.description: Package: electron (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Symptom

A remote (non-local-origin) page can read URL-embedded credentials (`https://user:password@host`) for every saved host through the remote-safe `desktop_hosts_get` IPC command. `redactHostsConfigForRemote` strips `clientToken` and `requestHeaders` but passes `url`/`apiUrl` through untouched, and the storage normalizer preserves userinfo — so the "redacted" config handed to an untrusted origin still contains the password.

## Evidence

- `packages/electron/remote-page-policy.mjs:15-18` — the redact allowlist is two keys only:
  `hosts: config.hosts.map(({ clientToken, requestHeaders, ...host }) => host)`.
  The existing test (`remote-page-policy.test.mjs:29-56`) pins exactly this shape with credential-free URLs, so the gap is locked in.
- `packages/electron/main.mjs:725-737` — `normalizeHostUrl` strips only the hash (`parsed.hash = ''`); `new URL('https://admin:s3cret@192.168.1.10:3000').toString()` keeps `admin:s3cret@`. `buildStoredHostEntry` (`:840-861`) stores that string as `url`/`apiUrl` verbatim.
- `packages/electron/main.mjs:5157-5165` — `desktop_hosts_get` returns `readDesktopHostsConfig()` (stored URLs included); `:6032-6066` marks the command remote-safe and applies the redact for non-local senders — the only credential boundary, and it misses userinfo.
- The embedded credentials are live secrets, not inert strings: probing/connecting uses native `fetch` (`:620`, `:995`), which sends `Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)>` derived from URL userinfo automatically.

Probe (real `remote-page-policy.mjs` + exact `normalizeHostUrl` body, node):

```
stored url: https://admin:s3cret@192.168.1.10:3000/
remote sees: {"id":"nas","label":"NAS","url":"https://admin:s3cret@192.168.1.10:3000/"}
LEAK: userinfo survives redact
```

## Why it matters

The redact exists precisely so "one server must not read the tokens or auth headers the user saved for another" (`remote-page-policy.mjs:12-14`). A LAN host protected by basic-auth-via-URL (a plausible setup for a home NAS when no client-token auth is configured) has that password exposed to any remote page that calls one allowed IPC command. `relay` descriptors are safe (public JWK only, `main.mjs:814-838`), and `desktopLocalClientToken` is not in the returned shape — userinfo is the remaining hole.

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed issues for `redactHosts`, `hosts_get`, `userinfo`, embedded-credential leaks: only the web `redactSensitiveText` family (#1920, #2074, #2128 — different module, text scrubbing) and #1073 (agent value-mismatch, different surface). No open PR touches `remote-page-policy.mjs` or the `desktop_hosts_get` path.

## Acceptance

- `desktop_hosts_get` responses to non-local senders contain no `user:password@` in any `url`/`apiUrl` (strip userinfo at redact time, or at storage time in `normalizeHostUrl`/`buildStoredHostEntry` — pick one and state which).
- Regression test mirroring the existing redact test with a `https://user:pass@host` URL asserting the credential is gone while host/id/label/routing still pass through.
- Local callers unaffected: direct connections keep working (if stripped at storage, probing must still authenticate — e.g. convert to an Authorization header at use time rather than dropping the credential silently).

body:
## Evidence

Verified on fresh `origin/main` (`072ba8c8e1c2db95897878554d4c544dd5294c7c`). `packages/web/server/lib/skills-catalog/cache.js:5,10-11,118-135,145-173` limits active scans to two, but `acquireScanSlot()` pushes every waiter into the unbounded `scanQueue`; each distinct key also remains in `inFlight` until its loader eventually runs and settles. Same-key requests coalesce, but distinct catalog keys do not.

The route can generate distinct keys for configured sources: `skill-routes.js:432-448,463-488` accepts each valid `sourceId` and calls `scanWithCache`; `settings-normalization-runtime.js:503-533` deduplicates custom source IDs but has no count limit. Thus a burst of concurrent requests for many configured sources can accumulate pending promises and retained request/loader state even though only two Git scans run at once.

Reproduced with the exact cache module and dependencies archived from current `origin/main`: submitted 10,000 unique keys with the first two loaders held open. Only 2 loaders started; 9,998 unique requests remained pending, and heap usage grew by about 10.7 MB. This exercised `scanWithCache` directly (not the HTTP route); no external repositories were cloned and the temporary data directory was removed. Existing `cache.test.js` asserts the active-loader concurrency limit with six keys, but does not bound queued work or test overload behavior.

## Why it matters

The active-scan limit protects subprocess concurrency but not memory or outstanding HTTP work. A large burst of distinct configured scans (or a slow/unavailable Git host) can grow the pending queue and `inFlight` map without a bound, then continue launching queued clones as slots free.

## Related work and dedupe

Closed #968 bounds completed scan-cache retention; it does not bound pending scans or the waiter queue. Fresh all-state issue searches for skills-catalog pending queues, scan concurrency, and in-flight refresh found no matching issue. The refreshed open-PR inventory has no skills-catalog queue implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bound pending distinct scans (and corresponding in-flight state) in addition to the two active scans.
- Define an explicit overload result for excess requests (for example, a typed busy response); do not silently drop accepted requests or create unbounded waiters. Preserve same-key request coalescing.
- Add deterministic tests that hold both active loaders, fill the pending allowance, verify excess is refused, then release the gate and confirm accepted work drains and all in-flight state is cleaned up.

title: fix(web): keep the passkey store empty-file recheck bounded

body:
## Problem

`createUiPasskeys()` reads `ui-passkeys.json` through `readDurableJsonFileSync()` in `readStoredValue()`, but then `loadStore()` calls `storeFileIsEmpty()` for an existing store. That helper (`packages/web/server/lib/ui-auth/ui-passkeys.js:202-208`) directly calls `storeFs.readFileSync(storeFile, 'utf8')`, bypassing the shared durable-store's 32 MiB cap and regular-file-checked read. This check runs synchronously on passkey status/list operations.

## Evidence

On current `origin/main` `158baff0c4af4f3b630e3f6dbcafe5fae8997fd3`, the `loadStore()` flow at `ui-passkeys.js:211-245` first reads through `readDurableJsonFileSync()` and then reaches `storeFileIsEmpty()` for a valid existing store with a matching password binding.

A focused `createUiPasskeys()` probe used the existing injected-`fs` seam to replace the file after the bounded read but before the empty-file recheck. `listPasskeys()` then performed a second synchronous read of 33,554,433 bytes, exceeding `DEFAULT_DURABLE_JSON_MAX_BYTES` (33,554,432), and returned normally. This models a concurrent replacement/growth of the store between the two reads. The existing `ui-passkeys.test.js` covers empty-file user-ID stability and durable-store errors, but not this second-read path.

The prior durable-store issue #1649 fixed bounds inside the shared primitive; this direct caller read is outside that primitive. All-state issue search for `storeFileIsEmpty` and passkey empty-file recheck found no specific tracked item; open-PR search found no implementation.

## Why it matters

The helper's bounded, regular-file-checked contract does not bound every read on this request path. A concurrent replacement can make passkey operations synchronously buffer an arbitrarily large file on the web server's event loop, causing avoidable memory and latency pressure.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove the direct whole-file `readFileSync` from `storeFileIsEmpty()`; use a bounded, regular-file-checked read or carry the missing/empty distinction forward from the durable-store read without introducing a second unbounded read.
- Preserve the existing empty-file initialization behavior and stable `userID` across subsequent loads.
- Add a regression test using the injected filesystem seam that replaces/grows the file between the initial read and the empty-file decision, proving the second read remains bounded (and does not bypass non-regular-file refusal).
- Run the focused `ui-passkeys` and `durable-json-store` tests.

## Finding (PR consolidation / superseded open PR)

PR #1967 is still OPEN, but the test fix it carries was landed by PR #1974 and its issue #1796 is CLOSED. #1967 should be closed as superseded — it must not be merged.

## Evidence

- PR #1967 — `test(web): fix host-shutdown replacement test hanging on a dead store-read spy`, head `queue/13557-1796-guest-shutdown-timeout`, commit `177d0b02a5cf`. Verified OPEN and unmerged twice on 2026-11-10 (`gh pr view` and `gh api .../pulls/1967`: state open, merged_at null). It also carries the `merge-conflict:true` label.
- PR #1974 — `test(web): re-point the host-shutdown store spy at the bounded reader open (#1796)`, MERGED 2026-11-08T15:29:35Z as `fa4ce1a9926f` (ancestor of main verified via compare API: `main...fa4ce1a9926f` ahead=0). Issue #1796 is CLOSED.
- Same queue task: #1967's branch is `queue/13557-1796-guest-shutdown-timeout` and #1974's is `queue/13557-1796-service-hang` — two heads of task 13557 for the same fix. Both PRs touch exactly the same single file, `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.test.js`, with the same change (8 additions / 4 deletions): re-pointing the dead `fs.readFile` spy at the bounded reader's `fs.open`.
- Current main `e895968ba30b` already contains the landed version verbatim: the host-shutdown test in `service.test.js` spies on `fs.open` with the bounded-reader comment from #1974 (contents API, 2026-11-10).
- Sole delta in #1967 not in the twin: a `30_000` test-timeout bump. It is not needed once the gate actually resolves — #1974's body records the same flow completing in 0.7s without the dead spy — so nothing is lost by closing #1967 whole.

## Why it matters

A stale duplicate of a landed test fix is a standing hazard: a sweep that merges it would stack a second spy re-point (plus an unneeded 30s timeout that masks real hangs) onto the landed one for a closed issue. The four-repo PR pile is being burned down deliberately; this one is a clean close-as-superseded.

## Acceptance criteria

- PR #1967 is closed (not merged) with a comment naming PR #1974 (`fa4ce1a9926f`) as the landed implementation and #1796 as closed, noting the 30s timeout bump is deliberately not carried over.
- No code change is merged from #1967; main's single `fs.open` spy in `packages/web/server/lib/guests/service.test.js` remains the only one.
- The `queue/13557-1796-*` task family is confirmed fully done in the queue (no live task still points at PR #1967).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PRs #1960–#1974 (batch above watermark 1958, main `e895968ba30b`).

body:
Every request and side thread from one working session (2026-10-20), with where each one stands. Checked boxes are done; unchecked ones are open work. Updated as threads move.

## Asked directly

- [x] **Why a question did not show under Questions.** `sidebarLayout.otherAttention` defaulted to `off`; fixed by the user from the sidebar menu "Needs attention".
- [x] **Is all OpenChamber config in files?** Mostly: `~/.config/openchamber/settings.json` and `preferences.json` (per-surface values under `surfaces`), `projects/`. Not in files: browser-only settings (sidebar width, message limit and about 25 more) and live state.
- [ ] **Agent tooling to view and change everything in the UI and in OpenCode config, global, project and session.** PR #145 merged (per-surface settings, project settings); PR #179 merged (`projects.setup`). Open gaps:
  - [x] browser-only settings (`registry.ts` `LOCAL_DEVICE_KEYS`) are unreadable to agents: PR #272, merged (read only: each window reports its device settings; `settings.devices`)
  - [x] project setup can be read: `projects.setup`, PR #179. Environment variables: `environment.get/set`, PR #167.
  - [ ] **Decision needed:** may agents write setup commands and project actions? They run outside OpenCode's permission rules, so #179 is read only.
  - [ ] `hiddenFromWork` lives on the unmerged `hide-project-from-work-sessions` branch; another session merged it into a local, unpushed `integration-2026-10-21` branch on 2026-10-21. Left to that session.
  - [x] OpenCode's custom config file is read-only to agents: PR #198, merged. Review added: config writes refused in enterprise mode; OpenChamber's merged config view now follows OpenCode's order (user, custom, project).
  - [x] `projects.add`, `projects.update` and `projects.remove` read the project list outside the save lock: PR #194, merged; it also fixed one failed settings save making every later save fail until a restart
  - [x] uppercase hex colours refused (#146), fixed on the PR #145 branch
- [x] **Goal editor** (PR #150, merged): background save with a card, message with the change (steer or queue), resizing, length limit setting plus a per-goal switch, a separate check-length setting, writer model and effort per run, Remember plus a Settings switch. Live run was partial: Settings only.
- [x] **Does the spec writer or a fork share the prompt cache?** Answered in the session: the writer (`generate.text`) does not; a fork does up to the fork point; `session.generate` does up to the last message.
- [ ] **Learn from manual model choices; Settings proposals** (#147).
- [ ] **Route pool descriptions for the classifier** (#148).
- [ ] **Do tool, MCP and skill toggles break the cache? A search-only tool surface through mcpx** (#149). Answered in part: tools come first in every request, so a mid-session change loses the whole cache; skills and MCP are unverified.
- [ ] **Integrations (GitHub, GitLab, Linear, source-control bindings, extension catalog) readable and editable by agents, like providers.** PR #169 merged: 21 actions. Decided: read everything, edit everything except raw secrets. Open questions, defaults in force:
    - [ ] Extension capability approval, install and removal stay user-only (default)
    - [ ] Linear session comments, which post a session link to Linear, are not gated by enterprise mode (default, same as the Settings switch)
    - [ ] `binding.set provider` needs no `confirm` (default)
    - [ ] An extension setting whose id ends in token, key or the like is refused (default)
- [ ] **Vault references for secrets** (`op://Vertex SRE/github_token`) in integrations, OpenCode and OpenChamber config, and MCP environment variables. Decided: OpenChamber reads `op://` with `op read`, memory only; it reaches OpenCode and MCP servers as environment variables used through `{env:NAME}`; in enterprise mode OpenCode gets none of these variables (unchanged).
  - [x] Environment variables (user and project) accept `op://…`; read at OpenCode launch, on user actions for Git, the terminal and project actions; Settings shows the reference and why a read failed; agent actions `environment.get`/`environment.set` (references only). PR #167, merged.
  - [x] GitHub and GitLab credentials from a vault reference: PR #176, merged.
  - [ ] Linear credentials from a vault reference: not built. Linear signs in through OAuth only; a personal API key would need the Linear client to send it without `Bearer`.
- [x] **Track every thread and read the session's own log.** This issue; the log was read with the `openchamber` tool's `session.messages` (`role: user`).

## Found along the way

- [x] `session.messages` with `limit` 50 or more failed with OpenCode's page-size error: PR #151, merged.
- [x] `lifecycle-process.test.js` shutdown-during-startup flake: PR #206, merged (1 s poll to 10 s; under load 2/5 failed before, 10/10 passed after).
- [x] Dead code "failing on `main`" was the checkout path: Knip matched the `.gitignore` line `*.local` against the `~/.local` folder above every OpenCode worktree. `main` and every PR branch pass from a dot-free path. Fix: PR #177, merged; PR descriptions #145, #150, #151, #167, #169, #176 corrected.
- [x] `git/service.test.js` failures were a product bug: hunk staging broke for anyone with `diff.mnemonicPrefix`/`diff.noprefix`/`diff.srcPrefix` (this machine's `/etc/gitconfig` sets mnemonicPrefix). PR #195, merged. The buffer-limit test also depended on `core.bigFileThreshold`; pinned in the test.
- [x] `markdownCore.test.ts` timing failures were a real freeze in older JavaScriptCore (Bun 1.3.11; Safari and iOS WebKit before macOS 27.0.1 — **corrected 2026-10-22: current Safari is fast without the fix**, see PR #273): marked's `^`-anchored rules scan the whole remainder in JavaScriptCore (quadratic). PR #196, merged: 4,000 paragraphs 3.9 s to 16 ms in the system JavaScriptCore.
- [ ] Goal ideas from review, not built — dispositioned in #1815 (splits #1828, #1829, #1830, #1831; idea 5 folded into #1573): diff of old and rewritten spec, rewrite one section, goal version history, a token estimate next to the length counter, writer through `session.generate` when its model and effort match the session's (shares the cache and sees the conversation; needs usage from OpenCode to show it).








- [x] **Upstream sync** (openchamber/openchamber `main`, 218 commits, 107 conflicted files): PR #203, merged. Fixed during it: the merged server did not start (a moved constant), and a handoff successor started a second OpenCode (per-server instance folders; now claimed by the adopting server). Kept the fork's flake; upstream's `nix-eval` and `nix-hashes` workflows run only upstream. aarch64-darwin `nodeModules` hash: PR #269, merged (measured, full build passes). **The x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux hashes are stale and need a Linux machine.**
- [x] PR #205 and follow-up PR #270, both merged (review findings: edit/retry/forced-queue flag loss, inline objective cap restored over #207): Queued goals drop the fork's goal flags: upstream's `QueuedMessageGoal` carries only `objective` and `tokenBudget`, so a goal queued while armed as settled, with "brief the agent", or ignoring the length limit loses those, and the server's queue delivery never briefs the agent with a rewritten spec (scheduled tasks do). Follow-up PR after the sync.

- [x] PR #197, merged: `scripts/bump-version.test.mjs` failed here: this machine's Bun is 1.3.11, the repo pins 1.4.3, and 1.3.11's lockfile refresh keeps old workspace versions, so a release bumped with it would publish `@openchamber/web` pinned to the previous `@openchamber/sdk` (upstream #3633 again). PR #197 makes the bump script refuse an older Bun.
- [ ] `packages/vscode/src/opencodeConfig.entity-v2.test.ts` "web search locks follow OpenCode config precedence" fails when `TMPDIR` is under a home folder that has `~/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` (the walk-up reaches it). Passes with `TMPDIR=/private/tmp`. Test environment only.

- [x] Agent-tool text and docs said a new session gets a worktree only when asked and that projects can't be registered: PR #204, merged (12 locales; review added the Git-only, fork and pull-request exceptions).

### Defaults adopted on 2026-10-22 (asked, not answered; the user said "continue")
- Agents' access to setup commands and project actions stays read only.
- In enterprise mode, all agent config writes stay closed (no allowlist).
- The four #169 integration defaults stay as they are.
- Sidebar: sorting sessions by time wins over the List layout when both are on.
- Browser-only settings: build read-only reporting (each window reports its device settings; agents read them per device).


- [ ] Open product questions raised by reviews, defaults kept:
  - Isolated spaces don't see the host windows' device settings (`settings.devices` is empty inside a space); forwarding them would widen the space boundary.
  - Re-arming a queued goal that has `briefAgent` without an objective (only non-UI producers can create it) drops `briefAgent`.
- [ ] Linear credentials from a vault reference: issue #304 (needs a Settings field; not built).
- [ ] #147 model-choice notes: in progress on `feat/model-choice-notes` (no PR yet).
- [ ] Upstream sync 2026-10-26 (271 upstream commits, 302 conflict hunks in 154 files): in progress on `sync/upstream-2026-10-26`. Upstream's Streamdown rewrite and source-control provider registries replace files the fork changed; the fork's Markdown anchored-rules fix is re-wired into Streamdown, and 1Password vault-ref accounts are being ported to the new provider modules.
- [x] #148 pool descriptions: PR #305, merged.
- [x] #149 tool/MCP cache notes: PR #306, merged (measured: direct tool changes break the cache, skills and code-mode MCP do not; evaluation on #149).

- [ ] Chat windows interrupted twice an hour ("OpenCode restarted while a response was still running"): the desktop app and an `openchamber serve` on one data dir retired each other's OpenCode through the shared `state.json`/`draining.json`. PR #293, merged (owner check through the managed-process registry, exclusive orphan claims, shared draining list kept, port-checked readiness; tests no longer write to the real registry). Both servers need it; the running 2.3.3 serve does not have it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every still-open checkbox thread either links a live issue/PR or records the decision that closes it.
- [ ] The open decision — may agents write setup commands and project actions (PR #179 is read-only because they run outside OpenCode's permission rules) — is recorded with Drew's answer.
